gd_topics_tips:
11 people for the GD | 5 cases | 5 Minutes each | One person was made the moderator by the company people

Case 1: Prod Manager at a Battery Factory, came to know of a night watchman who sleeps at duty. Turns out he had another job elsewhere and when asked says that he need to support a big family and had to look for income sources. Shall we continue with Him or terminate him?

Case 2: Sales Head at an Automobile Company. Their market share fell from 89% to 57%. The reason was the overloading of trucks. The consumers used to put 22 tons on an 11-ton truck which resulted in damages. Consumers asking for compensation. What will you do? Pay or not Pay

Case 3: Principal at a School. You want to introduce Sex Education in the curriculum from class 5 onwards. A certain section of parents is against it. How will you go about planning and tackling it?

Case 4: CEO, an E-commerce company. You offered a promo coupon for Rs. 1000 on purchase of Rs. 10000. But on the sale day, a technical glitch made the coupon available for sales above Rs. 1000. Resulted in a 9 times overbudget and 20% loss in net sales. Tech and the legal team says that you can revoke the offer as it was mentioned in T&C. What will you do?

Case 5: CEO of 2-Year-Old Startup in Soap and Beauty products industry. USP: Natural and Organic with Handcrafted products. Primarily B2B model of Luxury Hotels. But now wanna venture to B2C market. How will you position yourself and the plan of action for the same?

Experience: 
We had a huge problem as time was less and people were many. Having the position of the moderator was a huge advantage as you will get a sure shot chance at speaking minimum two times, once at the start and other at the end.
The opener was the one who got the most peaceful time, as anyone who followed had trouble in making points as for about 20 secs minimum of 3 people will be talking simultaneously. I spoke in only 4 of the 5 times. In the last 2 cases, I had to fight my way to speak a minimum 2 times each which allowed me to go forward. Overall it was a fish market and no one focussed on the overall case objective given to all of us.

Tips:
1. Focus on the objective of the Case and it was very clearly reminded by the HR at the end of the cases. That can really help in moving forward.
2. In a GD with so many people don't try to counter anyone as it will waste your precious time.
3. When multiple people talk, DO NOT STOP speaking, as at one point people will stop. This helped me as I was speaking only random words for the last 2 cases as the people simultaneously talked. I was saying the phrase "Negative PR for the Company" and "Expansion by B2B2C" continuously till everyone stopped speaking, this allowed me to make my point started the moment people stopped. ( A trick which can only work on Online mode)
4. BE ON POINT and DO NOT GLOBE
5. Fancy words are good, but it is better to have your points in a language as simple as possible. Ultimately you have to deal with normal consumers and hence your speaking skill will matter and need to accommodate common people
6. The number of times you speak does matter as ultimately you want them to notice you!

Result: 
Only 2 Members from my GD made through, the other guy had made 7 points in 5 cases. I did 6 points in 4 cases. There was one participant with 6 Points in 3, but had actually countered a few points of others and hence did not add per se.
interview_outline:
Pre-Interview:
The call was connected and I had a random casual conversation with an HR rep. He saw my resume and asked me about sports as it was mentioned. He asked me my opinion on the Match the last day. I mentioned Man U v Fulham game the previous night, but he meant India's win at the Gabba. So I went back to him giving my opinion on the game and talked like a person who may not have technical knowledge of the game but did follow, in order to make a connection to him. I was pretty comprehensive on my answer as I detailed him about Pujara's performance and even mentioned how Aussies Approached the game from a simple bystander POV. The detailed did display that I knew what I was talking about and had a real interest in Sports and Tactics Which I guess I was able to and have an impact on him!

During:
Two members took my interview. It started with "Brief Introduction". There I mentioned about my CIS in Insurance Modelling and my general interest in Sports and Academics. I was very particular to mention both of my CIS projects. I also gave one-liner descriptions of both my Social and Summer Internships. Panellist straight away asked about the Insurance CIS, which was a comfortable question for me and I told him everything about it, and even giving a disclaimer that it was not an Actuarial level study and only for an introduction into the vast world of Insurance premium stats. Then from there, The interview moved into some HR based questions based on my experiences. And it went on for some time.
After this, the main panellist, who was a doctor asked me a question about Sports and Stress release, which I talked about while explaining HR answers. Then a general question about the Life Insurance industry, which explained a lot of detail. I used my previous knowledge and intuition to answer the question by explaining the Insurance market in deep detail and a great focus on Term Life Insurance and why it is not famous. 
His response to my answer was, "You gave me more than I expected from you".
This gave me a positive impression that I am surely going to the next round.
domain_questions:
1. The CIS on Insurance came as bliss as I was asked to explain what exactly I did in that. I was directly honest by telling that it is not something at an actuarial level but only a basic statistical study which a faculty and I did. I did explain the process of my CIS and what all were my understanding from a purely logical perspective when we come into calculating Utility, Premium and Random events in the real world. I followed up by explaining more of how different discrete and continuous distributions work with the intuition behind each of them. I also accepted that if they ask a direct premium calculation, I may not be able to do that without opening R or Excel
2. Another question was about my own understanding of the Life Insurance Industry and my opinion on the future of it.
This I believe to be the low full toss I had in the interview. I told them about an Edelweiss Tokio Live project I applied to. That project helped me in understanding a bit more about Term Insurance. I explained all of my understanding in detail. I also mentioned some industry reports by Max Life Insurance and Insurance penetration. I discussed newer markets and possibilities for the Life Insurance industry given the COVID 19 situation
All of it was also backed by HDFC Life getting a 20% upside Buy rating from ICICI direct in a recent report. This displayed my market awareness for them.
hr_gk_questions:
Disclaimer: My HR questions were very specific to my experiences in Sports. Hence the answers are at a very personal level.

The following questions related to HR were asked:
1. How did I cope with my left-hand injury?
My answer to this established my interest in sports even more as I told them that I was planning on playing games which require only the right hand, like TT and Chess. And explained why it was so important for me.
2. I have played as a Captain and as a team member(follower), what do I like more?
Answer to this was a bit tricky, I explained how as a Follower and having a good mentor actually helps one in developing themselves as I myself have improved only when I was learning as a follower. While as a leader, it was a responsibility for me to teach and pass on the knowledge to the new members of the community who were coming and playing the sport for the first time. This answer drew experiences I have had on the field while playing and hence added to the genuineness of the answers. My insights about the role of a leader and a follower along with the things which I experienced did explain the order of my development as a team player and as an individual.
3. Why Volleyball?
The answer to this was a bit funny which I did tell them beforehand. I told them directly that how IPM PT had Football, Basketball and Volleyball as the only options. Football and Basketball were having a lot of contacts hence I chose Volleyball due to my injury.
looking_for:
1. Have a general knowledge of the Insurance Industry. Including markets, general trends and Market reports
2. I guess they wanted a person who had a genuine interest in the Insurance industry
3. They wanted to a person to know what they say they have an interest in, for me it was Sports and Statistics
4. Honesty was a necessary trait and one needs to be themselves and not fake anything.
right_wrong:
Went Wrong: Nothing in my opinion, as we had a very genuine conversation with each other about things. So from my perspective, I don't think anything went wrong

Went Right: My knowledge about the Insurance sector from both theoretical and statistical standpoint helped me create a positive impression. Apart from that, my responses to sports questions and the association with my day to day life also helped as I was fully honest about the questions they asked me and was able to leverage my experiences to answer the questions. The answers were such which did not create any suspicion of them being false. That also helped in a good overall image of mine. I used my leadership experiences to give real insights than something one reads on the internet one day before.

Result: Converted and Selected in just 1 interview!
tips:
1. My main approach was to use my existing CIS and research done in the live project to display that I have the sector knowledge.
2. Understanding of the industry and the market as a whole will actually help in answering questions. You don't need to muck up the Key measures but the knowledge of such measures and the inference of their value will help you seems genuinely interested in the role
3. General knowledge of current affairs and market awareness can never hurt as you can try to be as creative to use a given piece of news to infer anything in the business world.
4. Mock GDs were good as in online mode it is way different than an offline mode of communication. Hence practice is needed before you go for a GD.

interview_outline:
I was shortlisted for the GRID(Government Reforms and Infrastructure Development)- Infrastructure  vertical of PwC India. The interviewer for the first round was a director working with this division. The interview was done in two phases - Resume-based and Case-based. The verbatim of which is as below
I - Interviewer , Me - Interviewee 

Phase - 1 (Resume-Based)

I : Tell me about yourself 
Me: Covered the most important aspects of my professional and educational life, while also stressing more on the achievements during these two phases. Personal aspects were not talked about much in detail, but, a brief elaboration of my interests and hobbies was given while answering this question. 
I: Tell me more about your Internship
M: I did my internship in CRISIL and my project revolved around valuation of real estate and Infrastructure assets in India and estimate the potential of REIT(Real estate Investment Trust) and InVIT(Infrastructure Investment trust). The project required the application of concepts that we learn in Finance(Valuation, Beta analysis etc). Since I had done a thorough preperation of the same, this part could be done really well.
I: What is a discount rate, what discount rate was used for the purpose of valuation during your project?
M : Answered this on the basis of my project and the research that I had done during my time at CRISIL. 
I: What are the different techniques of valuation and what is the valuation techniques that you followed for your project ?
M: Talked about DCF, Price Earnings and CAP rate method and also explained the valuation technique that was used by me for my project. 
I: What is a Beta and what is it's significance ?
M: Here he was particular about distancing from the formula and explaining him the true meaning of Beta in Laymans' language ( No globing and No beating around the bush) 

Phase - 2 (Case Interview)
I: I am the CEO of an airline company. I would like to know if I should start operation between two cities A and B ? The suggestion should be a Yes or a No, but substantiated with data. 
(I asked him for some time so that I could structure in my mind, the right questions that can be asked in order to solve this and he gave me 5 minutes to think through it)
M: Could you please tell me if these cities are Tier-1 or Tier-2 ?
I: Tier- 2 cities.
M: How are these cities connected at present, what are the available modes of transport and the average time taken for these modes of transport ?
I: Road and Rail and he made up some numbers to represent the time taken for these modes. ( It was 8 hours by road and 24 hours by train(no direct train). Now I am making this up) 
M: If we start a flight, what is the expected time of travel between these two cities?
I: 1.5 - 2 hours
M: Since this being a tier-2 city, there will be a potential market for this.But, in order to understand the segment, the number of target customers and the willingness to pay for air tickets I would like to do a survey among the consumers. Do we have the budget for doing a market survey?
I: No. A consumer survey would be expensive and hence the company wouldn't want to do it. Suggest something much cheaper.
M: How about conducting a survey among travel agencies and mobile applications through which bookings are currently done? Is that feasible in terms of numbers and budget?
I: Yes. The company has collected a list of travel agencies in both the cities.The number is not that huge and hence surveying wouldn't be infeasible.
M: Do we have the number of bookings done for buses, trains and taxis and also the average price of these bookings?
I: Buses : normal bus - Rs.500 , Volvo - Rs.2000 , Trains - 250-300, Taxis: Shared - 1200 per person, Single- INR 5000 per person)
(He gave some random number for the number of travellers that use these modes between these two cities during one year. The idea was to understand the target customers. The target customers are the ones who are willing to pay a premium for the convenience. Here, in this case they are the ones that travel by Volvo and the ones who take a non-shared taxi are the target. He also said that the travellers who take trains are highly price sensitive and would never take a flight to travel). 
M: Do we have some number for the number of personal cars that travel between these cities during an year? What is the cost per person during a one way journey?
(A random number was again given for this. The cost figure pointed out that it was somewhere between 2000-3000 per person. I assumed this as a target group for flight with a penetration of 2-5 % during the initial year. The number of target customers were estimated by adding all the potential targets.)
M: I would like to understand the fixed and variable cost of operating a flight between these two cities?
I: 2 Million USD fixed cost for an year and another 2 Million USD as variable cost if the flight travels to and fro, one time between these two cities on a daily basis. This is assuming that on an average the flight is 75% occupied.
M: What is the average ticket price and the seasonal variablity during a year?
I: The average ticket price is Rs.5000 and the variability is +/- Rs.2000. 
M: Is it safe to assume Rs.5000 to calculate the break-even quantity of tickets that should be sold during an year ?
I: Yes, you can assume so.
( With this I could calculate the breakeven quantity . The earlier calculated target customer figure and the breakeven quanity was used to calculate the penetration required to break-even.)
M: Sir, based on the penetration figure I would recommend you to go ahead with starting a flight between the two cities A and B.
I: Ok. thanks for the recommendation, but I would also want you to design a strategy to achieve break even and profitability.
M: We can approach the travel agents and apps and use them as channel partners for selling tickets. Advertising in traditional media by emphasising the cost part and the convenience in terms of time reduction can be a first step. 
I: Thank you for your recommendations. 


Phase-3
I: Do You have some questions for me ?
Me: The HAM projects in roads were introduced to reduce the stress of high leverage on private players and yet these kinds of projects had no takers in 2019, could you please tell me the reasons for this?
I: Talked about the faults in the model and also about the general trends in the infra domain.
Me: How is Governement looking forward to PPP model transformation of 6 airports in the country that are currently operated by AAI?
I: Since he works mainly on airports, He could explain very well in detail about the strategies Government can adopt for a smooth transaction. 
I: Is there something else to ask, regarding the kind of work or about the company?
Me: No sir, Thank you for clearing my doubts on the questions. 
I: Ok. Thank You.
domain_questions:
Finance:
1) what are the different methods of valuation?
Ans: Discounted cash flow, Price-earnings multiple, Cap Rate method. Be very clear with Fin-1 and Fin-2 concepts discussed in the class. 
2) what is beta and what is it's significance
Ans: I started off by discussing the formula but the interviewer wanted me to explain it in layman terms. I explained this with an example in simpler terms. He wanted to check if I was clear with the concept of beta and did not want to get into the nitty-gritty. 
3) what is discount rate? What is the discount rate used for valuation of real estate assets?
Ans: Again, this was a pure revision of the concepts that were discussed during Fin-2 classes. 

I was asked a lot of questions from internship because it revolved around valuation of infrastructure assets in the country and estimation of their potential for being listed as InvITS. The most important aspect is to be clear with everything that is written down in the resume and also being able reproduce the concepts studied in class in the right context.
hr_gk_questions:
HR questions:
1) Tell me about yourself?
Ans: Explained about the approach in detail in the interview outline 
2) Why consulting as a career?
Ans: 1) it provides a platform to study in detail and provide solution to a business problem. 2) The challenge associated with consulting and the learning is massive as the problems are real and the solutions and recommendations has huge impact- financial and strategic.
3) A good place to use the concepts and learnings in class. For instance, marketing concepts can be used in a business problem around new product introduction or entry into a potential market, Financial concepts can be used in valuation of projects and understanding it's viability.
looking_for:
1)The most important aspect that was looked for was the capability to bring out solution to a problem. In consulting, the recommendation that is given by has major impact and hence we need to have a holistic approach towards solving the problem and putting forward solutions. 
2) Another aspect that was looked for was clarity of thought and communication skills. 
3) It was essential to think out of the box. In the case that I was given to solve, market research could'nt be done in the conventional way by going to the population and then doing a sample analysis. In that case, the sample to be gone to was, the tour operators. 
4) Confidence- Exude confidence in the way that you answer and approach the case. But, over-confidence will spoil the mood.
right_wrong:
Right 
1) One of the strong point of the interview was my clarity of Fin concepts because this really kept the discussion alive during phase-1 
2) I had the right questions for the interviewer during the case analysis
3) When asked if I had any questions I could come with relevant questions relating to the infra projects

Wrong
1) Took a lot of time to solve the case as I did not practice case interviews earlier 
2) I couldn't guide the interviewer into asking me questions relating to my work experience. This could have been done by framing a much better 'tell me about yourself' answer
tips:
1) Company deck and HR questions by Prepcom 
2) Previous year interview experience - By prepcom and consulting club 
3) Mock case interviews and general interviews on youtube
dos_and_donts:
1) Go through the website of the company properly ( If not, atleast through the company deck shared by Prepcom- they are wonderful last minute preparatory material)
2) Do case studies and guesstimates - A lot of them!

pre_process_tips:
1. Apply on Reculta
2. DB conducts a Workshop where they solve a case study and seek participation from the applicants. It is evaluative in nature. 
3. They shortlist based on the Profile of the candidate and the performance in the workshop.
4. The shortlisted candidates then have evaluative buddy calls. Most of the candidates had 2 rounds, with an Analyst/Senior Analyst and then an Associate/VP.
5. Candidates offered soft offers/selected also had a 3rd round with the Director.
6. All the candidates shortlisted after the Workshop also have a networking dinner, which again is evaluative. Its basically a hygiene check to see if their soft offer candidates can behave decently and communicate effectively. They are rolled offers the day after the dinner.
no_interviews_duration: No interview - But 3 budyy calls (20mins, 45 mins, 20 mins)

Buddy Round 3 -

2. Asked me if I had any true passions or I just try everything and get bored - Told him about how my passion for chess got me selected as a Team Leader at FIDE Chess Olympiad and how I am still pursuing my passion for Geography trivia and quizzing in IIM Indore as well

5. Gave me a scenario - if I had a task due tomorrow, and another manager comes and gives me another task due tomorrow and says its urgent and would need only a day to complete, what would you do? I asked if the earlier task was urgent and he said yes, both are equally important, and the first task would take 2 days and the second would take only 1. I also did not have anyone to delegate it to. I then clarified what did he mean by days work - to which he said 8 hours, so I told him if its that important I will work late night for 4 hours both days and get it done. He was impressed that I asked the definition of the work day and liked my solution.
looking_for:
Most Importantly - how willing and eager you are to join them and do you have a positive attitude to learning new things? If they take you, will you eagerly learn and deliver? Are you
the right fit for the role - will you be okay working long hours and weekends? - This is where they judge how passionate you are towards this. 
What they want you to have
1. Passion towards finance/IB
2. It really helps if you have done something relevant in that field that shows your passion towards it. Certifications like CFA, NISM help to demonstrate that atleast you have taken some steps
3. Basic awareness of whats going on, and knowledge about atleast 2 sectors and its happenings.
4. Basic understanding of Financial Statements, Ratios, Valuation Multiples.
right_wrong:
I did convert and land an offer. 
Good parts - My background of CA and CFA helped me sail through a lot of questions. My passion was evident by the way I spoke about Finance and IB and DB. They were also able to sense my passion for my hobbies which meant that I actually pursue my passions and dont give up easily. What also went well was I was able to strike a very good conversation with the interviewer and she became very comfortable and also spoke about her personal memories. My confidence and smiling throughout and showing them I am excited also helped.
Bad - I lied about the ethical dilemma at workplace question and they were able to sense that. So you should be honest and not give made up fake answers. It didnt affect the interview but it could have. Also, be confident in any case.
tips: Basic understanding of Financial Ratios, Valuation Multiples and knowledge of 2 sectors

interview_outline:
Interview 1 - Technical Heavy
The interview started with the interviewer introducing himself and then asking for my introduction. He then went ahead to ask questions based on customer lifetime value and a guestimate. There was a limited discussion on resume and HR based questions towards the end. In the end I asked him one question about the role.
Interview 2 - HR Heavy
The interview introduced himself but didn't ask for my introduction. The interview primarily based on HR questions and towards the end I asked him three questions about the role.
There were no company based questions in either of the interviews.
domain_questions:
In interview 1, I was asked to estimate the customer lifetime value of a fitness center. I asked him whether I have to estimate for any specific brand or in general. he told me any would do. I told him I was a member of cult.fit and therefore would like to estimate the lifetime value for it. I analyzed it for 3 customer profiles - the fitness freak, a person who would continue for 1-2 years and a person who would just take a membership once and never renew. Based in this, I calculated lifetime values for each of them and then took the average. He was happy with my approach, but suggested I could have taken the route of churn rates as well (I used very few technical terms).
In the second question, he asked me to guess the average revenue of any Starbucks outlet in Delhi. I told we can calculate it as avg cost of one order * no of orders. He was satisfied with this and then I told that the average cost of an order can be taken as Rs 200. Then, to calculate average no of orders, I told for Starbucks, the takeaway orders would be limited, so we'll consider only the dine-in orders. For no of dine-in orders, I considered the operating hours, capacity, average occupancy and no of people/seat in an hour. I took some time to arrive at this number, though I kept interacting with him about this approach. He told me I could have taken a guess for no of orders instead of calculating it this way. He then asked me to guestimate the number of outlets of Starbucks that should be opened in Delhi. I told him we can consider area of Delhi and then base our calculation on it. He told that instead we should look into population density as in Delhi sometimes two Starbucks are present in one road, based on the population density of the locality.
In interview 2, there were no technical questions.
hr_gk_questions:
In interview 1, he asked me why I wanted to be a consultant. I told him that it would allow me to work in all domains and since I want to be a CXO in the future, it would help me as I would have basic knowledge about all domains of the organization. He told me that this would not be possible as a consultant, CEOs are hardly ex-consultants because consultants are more used to using their minds for solving problems instead of managing people. I was also briefly asked about my previous work experience and my work as an infrastructure committee member.
In interview 2, I was first asked to tell my 3 most significant achievements in life and why I consider them significant. I told him about being the school topper in board exams, getting site level quarterly award in my 1st quarter of employment and securing admission in IIM Indore. He seemed satisfied with my answer. He then asked me what was the biggest failure in my life. I told him my biggest failure was to not secure an internship offer in my UG. A lot of discussion took place around this. Why I consider this as the biggest failure? Why do I think I failed? What steps have I taken to improve? How is this Saral 2.0 different from the first Saral? Basically, I told him that it was a big failure because I was able to clear the coding round of all companies but couldn't convert the interview rounds for any. The reason for failure was my lack of self confidence, which arised due to comparison with others based on coding platform ratings and led to nervousness during interviews. Saral 2.0 is different because he has stopped this comparison and bagged offer from 4th company on campus during placements and 4 PORs in IIM Indore.
He then asked me which specific domains I think I would be good at while working as a consultant I told him IT(because of my UG and WorkEx) and Operations(because of inclination towards quantitative domains). He then asked me to list any 3 business problems which I think I would be able to solve. I listed them on IT and operations.
Towards the end he asked me about my hobbies.
There were no questions on current affairs in either of the interviews.
looking_for: They were looking primarily for candidates with Work Experience. Other than that they were looking for a good problem solving approach and how well does one can respond to feedback. Since psychometric test was the first step of the process, they were looking for candidates who were culturally fit for KPMG.
right_wrong:
Things which went right - 
My introduction was well rehearsed.
My approach for Customer Lifetime Value calculation - I didn't use any specific terms but came to the answer in a structured manner.
My resume was quite balanced and I answered all questions on it well.
NPAD came in handy as I was prepared for the HR questions and gave good answers, without making up fake situations.
There was a lot of discussion around my biggest failure and I was able to cover it all with the STAR approach, showing progress within the 1st year of failure.

Things which went wrong - 
The guestimate took some time and the estimation for no of Starbucks should have been based on population density.
The answer for Why Consulting was not according to what the interviewer was expecting.
tips:
I referred only to the material shared by Prepcom. Most participants go for IIMA casebooks, so to create a differentiating factor I focused on IIMC casebooks. We had formed a case prep group and used to practice cases in it. Guestimates should be practiced as much as possible because cases have similar structures, guestimates tend to be rather unique.
Mock PIs/GDs conducted by institute in partnership with REC were hardly of any use. However Mock PIs and GDs by seniors were useful, especially my NPAD mentor. Try to have as many mocks with seniors or your batchmates for both technical and HR questions.
dos_and_donts:
Do(s)
Prepare NPAD and have as many mocks as possible
Show good listening skills.

Don't(s)
Taking too much time to answer/solve. There shouldn't be more than 5 seconds of silence at any point. Keep discussing your approach and if required, take max 1 minute to frame your thoughts for solving a case, after informing the interviewer.

pre_process_tips: Direct resume shortlisting. Having anything related to finance in resume is a plus. Work experience or internship is not necessary. Added tip: Have a top heavy resume.
interview_outline:
Round 1: Telephonic Interview which was a surprise one. The interview was a pure HR based resume grinding since I had only 5 month experience in TCS. Started with introduction, Went into grilling each and every detail of my resume. No role related or finance related question but asked a simple puzzle to solve. Interview ended with if any questions to be asked by me.

Round 2: A quick 10min online face to face interview which too is surprised. Directly asked questions related to basic finance, A small simple situation based finance question. Interview ended by asking my feedback on previous round PI experience and role preference.

Round 3: A short HR interview based on my resume again. Started on a brief introduction, went into technical aspect of my resume, basic HR questions related to finance and interview ended with a question on my future plans.
domain_questions:
Round 1: Interview started with tell me about yourself for which I had a prepared answer. Technical questions came from my resume on SQL as I had work experience in IT BFSI in TCS for 5 months in which I worked on Oracle DB which included SQL. The questions were basic concepts on SQL for which I was prepared. The other technical question came from python as I had mentioned a certification in my resume. Questions were similar to previous ones on basic concepts of python and asked my weakness in python. My answers were direct, honest by using the STAR approach and admitted I didn't know some concepts but eventually came to the answer. The panel was an American and seemed pretty convinced that I was aware of my resume.

Round 2: The interview was completely technical on finance and based on derivatives, options, futures and forwards. Gave brief answers of each concept confidently with necessary examples. Panel pretty convinced, gave me a situation question on options and hedging for which I was well prepared and provided the solution with examples which easily convinced the panel. Interview ended with a question about the role and asked my preference for other roles for which I was honest on giving answer for the desired role and showcased my flexible attitude.

Round 3: This round was HR again and was similar to round 1. Asked about my work experience for which I honestly answered it as a IT based and not finance based job. Then grilled into the same by asking questions on SQL. I answered some questions accurately but admitted I don't remember to one question. Interview ended with questions on why finance, why GS and what's my future plans in finance as my career. The panel was completely convinced on my genuine answers.
hr_gk_questions:
Round 1: Questions were basic HR type such as tell me about yourself, why GS, Why finance for which I was well prepared with the help of my NPAD. Questions were totally from my resume based on SQL from my work experience, Python from my certifications, My PoR on social service and initiatives, my extra curriculars on chess and questions on that. I was thoroughly prepared on my resume with brief answers on technical questions and STAR approach for non-technical ones. The interview ended without asking any questions related to the role or current affairs. Hence I asked questions on current affairs related to the company and related to the roles to when the panel asked if I had any questions.

Round 2: After all the finance questions answered, the panel asked about my round 1 PI experience and feedback for it for which I was honest and genuine on what happened and how the round went which they already knew.

Round 3: Basic HR questions on Why GS, Why finance, Why should we hire you and what are your future plans in finance. As expected, I was well prepared with my NPAD and gave structured answers to each question using STAR approach with some added elements of personal connect in answering. The panel were well convinced of my answers.
looking_for: Honesty, Confidence, Genuineness was the three mantra for this role. The panel repeatedly tested my honesty and genuineness in each round by asking feedbacks of previous rounds. The confidence in delivering answers and being honest of admitting if we don't know a solution to a question were key elements of the interview. Work experience was not a priority but panel expected some IT based technical knowledge as the role demanded it. Readily prepared attitude is another expectation and that is why PIs were surprised with timing window between 5pm to 10pm any day and expected candidates to be spontaneous.
right_wrong:
Matched their expectations on being genuine, honest and confident while answering. Provided structured answering to HR questions and brief answers to technical which was a plus. Finishing the interview on time is a big brownie. Well prepared with NPAD and technical questions. 
Stumbled with a technical question on python which I could have prepared even better but was honest in admitting I don't know.
tips: Since interview was surprised, I had to be prepared for the whole week and anticipate the call. Thorough knowledge on Job Description and role is a big plus. Knowledge of company's current reports can be added advantage (to ask questions to panel). Concepts for Risk governance can be found in Investopedia (Derivatives and its models), ICWAI business online material, Equit-I and prepcomm preparatory material.
dos_and_donts:
1) If you get a shortlist, don't be casual and start preparing till you complete the interviews as Risk Governance in GS is a jackpot role for freshers who have zero finance knowledge or background. 
2) Interviews would be by international panel, so be in a place where you get good mobile signal. And never ever postpone your PI to a later time if you get a call. Take maximum 5 min as buffer.
3) Always have your mobile in hand for the whole week (even if it takes to take it to bathroom).
4) Prepare your answers in a crisp and brief fashion with each answer not exceeding the the 1-2min mark. Finishing your interview on time (usually 20min) is a very big Brownie. 
5) Never bluff your answers. Panel are well aware of the technical IT concepts that you mention in your resume. So its better to admit than to bluff. 
6) Keep track of the answers that you say in PI rounds. Panel are aware of your answers in previous rounds and ask feedback to test your honesty. 
7) Last but not the least, Be well prepared with your resume and NPAD. Use STAR framework for HR based questions and keep it short.

pre_process_tips:
1) Capgemini ELITE's application submission happens in two stages - first on Reculta and the second on a platform called SuperSet. The Superset Application is quite extensive and must be given at least an hour and a half of time to fill and make sure that all information submitted is optimal. It would be advisable to fill the details regarding internships and PoRs in the SuperSet application diligently. 

2) (14th Sep) After application submission and shortlisting (which happens on the basis of your profile as given on your resume and SuperSet application), candidates were invited to take an ADEPT-15 personality test. While mandatory, this is NOT an elimination round - however, it may have some bearing on your overall application as far as "cultural fit" is concerned.

3) (14th Sep 5:00 p.m.) Post the ADEPT-15 assessment, we were asked to join for a GD. (Details in the successive question.)

4) Immediately after the GD, we were asked to solve a fairly easy guesstimate. (Details in the successive question.)

5) After these two assessments, we were made to wait in a Zoom room and told the PlaceComm would intimate shortlists for the interview. After a while, I was asked to log into SuperSet and join the meeting from the same platform.

6) The interview lasted for approximately 25 mins. Equal parts HR and Case Interview. The selection was intimated shortly after the interview.
gd_topics_tips:
Case Based GD. For us, the GD was about a quick commerce start-up which has recently started selling luxury perfume on its platform. However, the sales of this product aren't good enough compared to the industry average of other quick commerce companies selling the same product. We were required to discuss the pros and cons of selling the luxury perfume on the quick commerce platform and come up with recommendations on how the start-up can increase the sales of this luxury perfume. We were given multiple data points and facts but were only allowed a limited amount of time to read the case (5 mins approx) after which we were thrown headfirst into the GD. It is advisable to start making notes IMMEDIATELY after the case is viewed. 

As for tips, I am genuinely not an expert xD, but it's always a good idea to: 

1) identify constraints, parameters and important variables
2) identify why the aforementioned variables and constraints are not optimal. You may use one of the frameworks to do so if it fits however don't try to force fit it. 
3) brainstorm ideas to bring it to optimal levels through the GD

I started the GD and contributed around 5 times within the given 12 minute timeframe. I made a conscious effort to take notes during the GD, helping me keep track of the discussion's direction and the topics that were covered.
interview_outline:
The interview started with introductions, followed by the quintessential 'Tell us a bit more about yourself' question. After a brief discussion about the topics I mentioned in my introduction, the interview transitioned to a case. I was tasked with devising a Gen AI model for a retail company aiming to reduce its operational costs and enhance transactional efficiency.

After the unconventional case mentioned earlier, they presented a pricing case related to the GD topic. I was asked to determine the price of the bag in which the luxury perfume would be sold.

Following these two cases, the interview shifted towards more of an HR-type discussion. In my introduction, I had highlighted my entrepreneurial mindset, which prompted them to ask why I was interested in Capgemini while having an interest in entrepreneurship. This led to further questions regarding my profile.

I was able to answer these questions reasonably well and link them to what I hope to achieve with Capgemini in the future, if given the opportunity to work within the organization.

Subsequently, they asked me, 'Why Capgemini?' I also mentioned one of their customer experience projects in partnership with Adobe, which intrigued me, especially considering my experience with Adobe software. Following that, they asked about Capgemini's revenue model. They also posed a situation-based question.

Naturally, at the end of the interview I was asked whether I have any questions for them. I said I did and we had a conversation of approximately 3 mins on the same.
domain_questions: As mentioned above, they asked me about Capgemini's revenue model. I didn't know the exact model, however knowing that it is a tech consulting firm I came up with 3 ways the company might earn revenue. I also explained 2 of these 3 ways citing examples which I read on the company's website.
hr_gk_questions: As mentioned in the outline of Interview question.
looking_for: They were looking for creative and out-of-the-box thinking, particularly because there's a vast scope for innovation with technology. However, it should also be practical and feasible. They were interested in individuals who are inquisitive, capable of critically analyzing reasonably complex situations, and are a good cultural fit for the organization.
right_wrong:
I began with an introduction that focused on my experiences and interests, which included entrepreneurship, marketing, video editing and meditation. This led to follow-up questions from the interviewers, and I believe these discussions went well. I also managed to connect these interests to what I hope to achieve with Capgemini in the future, if I get the opportunity to work with the organization. One of my interests is marketing, and I talked about a project that Capgemini is involved in with a company that is indirectly related to marketing. Also, for the first case, I was able to come up with a few creative recommendations and involve my knowledge of technology in the same.

During the second case, which involved pricing, I initially struggled to provide the answer one of the interviewers was looking for. She had to repeat the question 3 times, but I eventually conducted an in-depth analysis and was able to come up with the explanation.
tips:
Naturally, Case Books are a great source to build structured thinking and problem-solving ability. I would highly recommend going through a few and memorizing a few frameworks for ease of analysis.

It is also advisable to closely follow tech developments as this can help in coming up with recommendations for the cases. Before the interview, it will be helpful to go through the company's website and thoroughly review it.

Mock GDs and PIs are incredibly important to understand where you falter and to begin improving upon any deficiencies in preparation.

NPAD is, as always, a useful tool for HR questions.
dos_and_donts:
Do's:
1. Case preparation and guesstimates.
2. Review the company's website.

Don't:
1. Avoid repeating the same answer. Understand what the interviewer is asking and provide an answer specific to the question.

pre_process_tips: For Deloitte S&O, it was only your CV and the shortlists were made based on that
no_interviews_duration: two interview rounds [1st: 20-25 mins approx., 2nd: 20 mins approx]
interview_outline:
[Interviews were on zoom platform]
Round 1: started with introduction, interviewer introduced herself to me (her background was in cloud solutions) and I followed after that. she briefly explained me the process for this round. started with a guesstimate. guesstimate was around demand of orders on an app. post that one more person joined the call. Then we proceeded with a case. Case type was unconventional, related to cloud and product I worked upon during my work experience (Note: I have work ex of around 2 yrs as a software engineer in a financial services firm). domain_questions:

hr_gk_questions:
No current affair questions;
HR based questions: 
(Round 1) not a HR question as such but....
they asked me if I had any questions and I asked them what sort of projects they are working on and if they have only strategy or implementation function as well.
I am mentioning this because they replied it with utmost enthusiasm and went on to explain me their work for next 3-5 mins.

(Round 2):
next 5 year goals
understanding of consulting

right_wrong:

tips:
