For interview: Just be relaxed, think of it as an opportunity of conveying your perspective/thought process, and for HR related questions an opportunity to tell your story. Do not complicate it to make it more appealing or sell it. Let it become a coherent story (read "structured approach" for guesstimate and cases) and a genuine one.

role_offered: Global Leadership Cadre - Sales, Consulting & HR
pre_process_tips: 1 minute video on "Why I am a leader & why should I be selected for the GLC?" next round was a Psychometric Test of about 30 mins
interview_outline:
Interview 1 - started with tell me about yourself. Follow up questions on what I had done for my latest internship which was in Sales. What did I learn from it? Why do I want to join Tech Mahindra - wherein I stressed upon the importance of digital transformation which was further accelerated post-pandemic. Around 4/5 panelists including a senior/alum. Was also asked about role or industry type preference - if FMCG sales, IT sales etc. Alum asked a resume based point - case competition details, how we had approached and what as the solution. Final question was from HR who asked where do I see myself in 2 years from now.

Interview 2- CPO round. Asked if I knew which role I was in consideration for? I said Sales and they reconfirmed, yes. Asked if it was my preference or not. Candidate can be honest while answering this since the next questions would be based on this question. Given a case/situation based question on B2B Sales (mock sales call). This round was more grilling, but I maintained my composure and tried to convince the panelists and kept going on with answers and reasons.
domain_questions: Not so domain specific. But the final interview had a sales mock call. Situational question - so basic knowledge about B2B Sales will help. Also, about the services etc. Check the company deck by PrepComm.
situational_questions:
Mock Sales (in CPO round) - Sell IIM Indore as a service. I did not understand the question carefully, and thought of trying to sell an IIM Indore service that can be taken up by Tech Mahindra. Went with TCS Ion, and gave them solutions and kept speaking for 1-2 mins. One of the panelists then mentioned that I have not really understood the question and asked the questioner to repeat. Only when he repeated - I clarified the understanding with him and then took a minute to answer. My answer was the Jigsaw Academy IIM Indore course can be taken over or sold to TechMahindra. I was the salesperson for IIM Indore (the organisation) trying to sell the online analytics course of IIM Indore to TechM (the client). Gave basic details about the course, pros and cons in the sense - no extra work needed to be done, as the videos were already recorded by IIM Indore faculty and this is a MOOC course(did not use this term in the interview and kept it very simple and in layman terms). Said that the only expense will be in evaluation for the participants in the MOOC which can be outsourced back to IIM Indore or we can hire other evaluators. Follow up questions  - We (TechM) already have a Learning & Development System, why should we buy from IIM Indore. I answered with a clarifying question - who teaches are they academia or industry experts. Very tough answer - said academics that move to industry. Used a different pivot saying that IIM Indore researches in all fields and industries and has experts from various fields are in the institute. So, since TechM is working and looking for clients across the domains and industries, this acquisition/collaboration can help. Final question - Why should they (client) not go with IIM Ahmedabad and go with IIM Indore? I answered that there are obvious differences since IIMA was set up in the 60s and IIMI in 1997, however, the student & faculty body is large and diverse and even being a younger institute the quality of our research is top notch etc etc. 

Note: Be jovial, happy and do not let the nervousness show even when it's a stress interview. Confidence is the key. And keep going at it, attack the problem from multiple POVs. In situational question, following the case method helps, but do it sparingly, this was not a case interview and the interviews went along only for 20 mins, so there are only so many questions you can ask. In this case, clarifying the initial question / case should have been done, and understanding the exact question they are asking (in this case which service or what type of product of IIM Indore to sell) would have wasted less time.
hr_gk_questions: No, but I used various contemporary examples in some of my answers. In Interview 1 when asked about what is your primary interest area in the past 5 years. I mentioned that it was startups since I had worked at startups and researched about startups etc. Used examples from my Internship experiences.
looking_for: Some sales or IT experience, but not necessarily since most people interviewed were freshers. Ability to handle tough questions, glide through situations. Also, a well balanced resume with leadership positions or good projects.
right_wrong: The first interview went well with the panelists and me maintaining a jovial attitude, In the second interview - approach to the case could have been much better as explained before. First thing to do in  situational question or case should be to re-iterate and make sure you have gotten the question or the case. In my case the question was ambiguous and became simpler only when we went along, Similarly when suggesting answers, questions can be asked. Why I suggested the online analytics course can be taken over by TechM (the client) should have asked if this was the kind of service offered by IIM Indore that they want as an answer (question was which IIM Indore service they can take over.)
tips: Previous case practices for Consulting Interviews helped. Company deck, and other material including industry reports.
dos_and_donts: Start prep early maybe in around November/early December irrespective of the kind of shortlists you have or will have. Consulting/case prep helps a lot in even other domain interviews (GenMan, IT, Analytics etc.) Having some knowledge or even a little experience in any sales & marketing domain - say internships or live projects will help.

pre_process_tips: Case submission (product-related): In short, redefine the wishlist experience of an imaginary e-comm platform. We had to submit a deck within 30-35 hours. Shortlists for interviews were issued after that.
interview_outline:
Both interviews started with Tell me about yourself. The interviewers meanwhile, go through the resume. Both the interviews then delved into product cases. They began with generic and non-specific product-oriented questions. 

Both the interviewers were directors of products for the Merchants and Customer acquisition pods within PhonePe. 

Interview 1: Last Big Billion days, Flipkart did not meet its expected sales targets. As a product manager, solve this issue. 
I utilised the CIRCLES framework to solve this case. After identifying the core problem, the interviewer guided me to design a product and marketing-focused solution for the next Big Billion Days and the general Flipkart application. Post that, 25 minutes were exclusively dedicated to discussing KPIs, monetary vs customer-oriented feature focus and feedback on the case. The interview ended with the interviewer asking if I had any questions. I asked two questions, and the interviewer answered them in much detail. 

The 2nd interview happened immediately after the first. 

Interview 2: What is your favourite product, why? And mention two favourite features of this product, from prodman's perspective. 
I proceeded to clarify which product he talked about. Whether a mobile application, PC and laptop software, physical product or proprietary product. The interviewer gave me a choice to choose but expressed interest in a mobile application. I explained that N26, a German neobank's product is my present mobile product and how it helped me as a user when I was attending my forex semester. I chose and explained my two favourite features as spending analytics reports and transaction-oriented spaces, and how these could be implemented within PhonePe as new product features. The interviewer then asked me to explain the features for PhonePe, how the app should be redefined to implement these features and make a customer acquisition and rollout model for these new features. Post that, 15 minutes were exclusively dedicated to discussing KPIs. The interview ended with the interviewer asking if I had any questions. I asked two questions, and the interviewer answered them in much detail. 

Both interviews were very conversational, and the interviewers helped me throughout the way. The interviews were low pressure and medium paced. They felt like general discussions and not interviews. 

Verdict: Selected.
domain_questions:
All domain-specific questions were included within the cases. Notable topics include KPIs, customer vs monetary focus and rollout. 
The interviewers did not want the theoretical concepts for KPIs but feature and use specific KPIs that aren't traditionally used. 
For customer vs monetary focus, after choosing the features and their uses, using a theoretical basis for both, justify these features' focus and why. 
Once a focus is established for rollout, I needed to explain to which users these features are rolled out first, which incentives to use, how to make a self-sustaining model, and how the decided KPIs help the rollout plan.
situational_questions: NA, there were no questions except the cases.
hr_gk_questions: The cases expected specific ideas of general awareness and current affairs. The Flipkart case led to the COVID pandemic, and the interviewer led me to use the social situation to model the solution. The favourite product case had points about the Indian Financial system and understanding of UPI and Indian fintech regulations.
looking_for:
They were looking for structure and quick thinking on the feet. Understanding business and general clarity on PhonePe, its operations and product were required. 
Further, they expected us not just to think like PMs but also as users at the same time. Both interviewers expected simple and practical solutions and features. 
They did not expect technical knowledge other than product knowledge or any specific work-ex. Many non-work ex and non-tech peers were shortlisted for the interviews.
right_wrong:
What went right: 
The pre-process submission: I chose a complete remodelling of the wishlist and based it on the Flipkart experience. I made sure to choose practical features and created basic UX designs. 
Interviews: Both interviews had lots of preparation. Using the CIRCLES framework and making extensive notes helped me structure my interview how I liked. Making certain decisions about handling cases before the interviews helped me gain some much needed time for analysis and clarification. Further, the questions I asked at the end were specific and hoped to communicate a deep understanding and research of the company's role and impact.  

What could have gone better: 
KPIs. Both interviews had an extensive focus on KPIs. I could have chosen KPIs to better link my rollout idea with the target users and product focus. 
In both cases, I missed some fairly obvious points. The interviewers pointed them out and led me in the direction they wanted. I could have done a better job of highlighting all points of interest.
tips:
Prepcom preparatory material on product management and Prodlab's product management casebook were very focal and vital in my prep. Although not very relevant to my interviews, the PM primer by prepcom was helpful to learn the language of product management. 
Product frameworks were important to structure approaches to case questions. An in-depth google reading will suffice to learn the frameworks. 
Practice, practice and practice. This is the only way to learn how to talk in a product case interview. I used videos on product interview experiences and mock product interviews by Exponent and The Product Folks to understand the concepts, structures and language. 
Having a small case group is very beneficial. Practising all the different product cases and preparing answers for many such cases helps save time in the interview. 
Although I did not face these questions in my interviews, situational questions are generally asked in many product interviews. Preparing the NPAD and going beyond these questions to make specific product-related answers can be beneficial. 
Learn about the company that you're interviewing for. Helps specify solutions and be relatable in interviews. Read the JD welland understand the expectations of the company.

pre_process_tips: Applied on portal and the initial shortlist was resume based. No submission or tests, shortlist was released the day before the company was scheduled.
gd_topics_tips:
Topic: Deadlines destroy creativity
Group strength: 5 to 6 members

Moderator was friendly and urged everyone to introduce themselves before the GD began. Since I was alright with speaking for and against the topic and could not decide which, I waited to enter after listening to 2 entries. Gave an opinion that was contrasting to the ongoing discussion and explained with some examples to justify. Tried to summarise the discussion at the end and conclude that the topic is true in certain cases while the opposite is true in other cases.

GD was overall amicable and did not turn into fish market (probably because the moderator was chill and put us at ease with the short intros).

I made 3 entries and spoke for max 30 to 40 seconds in each, also politely stepped back a couple of times when I started talking at the same time as others.
no_interviews_duration: 1. Group Engagement aka GE (Group Interview with 7-8 panel members and 10 candidates)  2. Personal Interview ( Panel members from GE and myself alone)
interview_outline:
1. GE (Overall 30 to 45 minutes)
7-8 members from the company were present comprising of the practice leaders of the roles they offered and HR team. The senior most HR person posed the questions, others chipped in whenever it was relevant. Namely, 3 questions were asked:
a) Introduce yourself and the role of your interest (they were offering 3 roles- Finpro, PE M&A, Employee Health & Benefits Consulting).
b) Why Marsh?
c) Why this role?

Each question was posed in a round robin fashion to all candidates and was a bit formal and serious.

For introduction it helps to give the common linear response (UG, MBA PoRs, Competition, Internships, Hobbies) but extremely crisp. Have to understand the roles they offer and select the one you are most aligned with (interest/knowledge wise or qualifications wise).
Why Marsh question can be dealt with talking about the points they discussed in their PPT. I talked about their legacy and how the company rode the waves of industrialization way back in the 18th century. Also talked about their model of insurance broking they apply and that it is interesting. Please take care not to talk much about the role here or how you are aligned with it. It is all about what you know about the company. Can take one of their values and say how it is important to you and how you thrive in such an environment.
Why this role question needs proper understanding of the JD pointers. Take 1 or 2 and explain why it interests you (travelling, client facing role etc). For the rest of the pointers, translate it to how it matches your existing skillsets or your enthusiasm to learn/do similar things.

All of this was said in an extremely crisp way since it was a group round.

2. Personal Interview
I was asked to remain on call post the GE to start my PI. Having to suddenly face all of the panel alone was a bit intimidating, but they shifted to a amicable tone and put me at ease. Questions asked were pretty much the same, just phrased differently.
a) So tell us your story.
b) Why this role, what do you understand about it.
c) Any questions for us?

Here the answer is same as the intro question from GE, but one can be a bit more elaborate and informal. Talk about why you took up certain PoRs, competitions, what each of them taught you, internship project- difficulties, how you overcame it, key learnings etc, also maybe a couple of things not in your resume.
For the role, I took each point of the JD, stated my understanding of it and related it to my skills and interests. Also said how it is a nice thing to help companies devise benefits strategies to attract best talent and help them grow their human capital.
Asked how a day in the life of a consultant looks like, what I will have to learn etc.
domain_questions: No case questions or guesstimates were asked. Understanding of company and role was tested at length.
situational_questions: No specific situations were asked. Was asked to tell my story.
hr_gk_questions: No current affairs were asked.
looking_for:
I think they were looking for candidates who have understood the job profile and was willing to put in efforts to learn.
Communication skills were also key, most questions they asked required talking about oneself, understanding of company and role at length.
right_wrong:
Good part is that since I had many points to talk about the company(from PPT points friends has noted down) and job profile (from JD), I was comfortable speaking about it in detail.
I had also maintained a detailed note of what to speak about each line in my resume- that helped to pick points when I had to be crisp and to elaborate with as many points as needed.

Bad part is that I got a little nervous when the GE switched to PI and I suddenly had to face the entire panel alone, I stammered for a few seconds. I was also not prepared with 'stellar' questions to ask the panel and had to make do with mediocre ones
tips: Domain specific materials gave confidence. So did mock case interviews with friends. Mock GD/PIs highlighted the areas I need to improve and gave the much needed push.
dos_and_donts:
I have always dreaded GDs. Please try and get comfortable with them. Devise strategies for number of entries, how to deal with fish market GD or when you are not familiar with the topic.
Be prepared to speak at length about anything on resume. Sitting down and noting all possible points about each POR/Project can help. Order it using STAR framework. A lot of answers for situational based and other HR questions can be derived from this exercise.

pre_process_tips:
It would be helpful if you try to make some notes of this. It's long and some points are repeated so not to miss any important point please make notes. I got selected if it helps you in making notes and giving this long essay some credibility..

First round was to give an online test after filling your application on superset. It requires you to download an app on your desktop and then proceed. Downloading the app was fairly easy but it asked for several alphanumeric codes (it asked the codes 2 times) for logging in. Make sure to put the codes in right place they have similar and confusing names. Otherwise you will be logged in but won't be able to start the test (happened with me)Don't worry close the app and log in again correctly. Questions were typical hirepro type questions (gap challenge, motion challenge, grid challange) It had an additional section of remembering a position of a dot and then identify whether 2 patterns are similar or not. Repeat this process 3,4 and 5 times and at the end you need to put the dots in order. It's test was similar but harder than the external hiring test of PnG.
interview_outline:
Interview happened on superset. You get mail from superset before Pcom informs you about it. Morning slot 10 AM. Make sure to log in to superset and sit not only in your 1 hour slot but if there are any candidates before you make sure to log in at the start time of 1st candidate. They will go in order but if someone finished early they will call you next. Even if your slot hasn't started. There was no need to join a zoom meet. Be vigilant on the screen you will receive a video call from the panel at the start and simultaneously get a mail and a message by superset. 

I enter the call. One male panelist was They didn't even ask me my name. (Ig they had good enough information from superset). We tested the mic and camera with an informal hi hello. And then repeated the same when formal interview started. They were looking for interactive communication from the start ( I failed a bit by giving binary response to informal questions). Interview was totally driven by you. They started with a resume question (most pertinent to the JD). And then interview was flowing freely on the basis of what you say. Reading the JD is a must and try to link the company's work in your answers.
domain_questions:
JD was to do waste minimisation in consumer product group (CPG) in Capgemini or generally known as FMCG goods at each and every point in value chain. 

The questions and my answers fully revolved around it. 

Know about major players in the industry and what they do to solve the problem as well as emerging trends related to core hard technology.
looking_for:
A well versed person with a lot of knowledge about the domain, international advancements in techniques and general practice in the industry by the major players. Most importantly being aware of JD. Read JD before researching.

 It was not mandatory but having some work and knowledge of FMCG and waste management in FMCG was very useful. 

Don't stick to your resume try to tell about any other things not included in it. Don't lie as you will discuss about anything you say in detail.
right_wrong:
Take time to speak, speak slowly but cover all the aspects. Break down things in small chunks and then take up smaller chunks and explain it. Try to be MESE in answers ( never thought will be writing this) 

If you get selected for interview round you have a very high chance of making it through. 

I did not know international practices for very niche type of wastages in the sector.
tips:
3-4 hour research on value chain how food is wasted at each and every step and a elaborate current and probable wate management and reduction. 

Try writing it down on a piece of paper to have a better recallability and revision. Try to search Google scholar for recent research papers in allied field. 

I had a long offline "internship" as inventory manger or FMCG goods. That was the anchor point of our discussion and it let me make myself credible while saying anything out of the box solution. 

Doing thorough research on Capgemini and its current initiatives and partnerships in the sector. Capgemini website is very important and sufficient for this.

I also had a research paper on reducing food wastage not included in the version of resume I sent. We also talked about that. 

Being interested in the conversation and trying to learn something from it Instead of seeing it an a win loss interview.

Practicing the questions for the aptitude tests with my friends. Try innovative ways to solve them. And if you have experience to solve these type of questions via previous pre processes its a plus.

The interviewer was very helpful he told  the answers to the questions I did not know. It was kind of a KT session instead of interview.
dos_and_donts:
Do prepare hard they will go into nook and crannies of your answers. 

Don't say anything you can't explain till last point.

It's okay to say that I don't know. But try giving a best guess after saying that.

Learn about Capgemini it's vertical you are applying for and the job description.

Most important was JD it will give you all the questions that will be asked in the interview. 

Link somethings you say to the values and Capgemini's actual work being done. It helped but don't overdo it.

If you made it this far without getting bored I hope you get selected. If you are here by random do read fully.

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlist, Non-evaluative Case Workshop, Non-evaluative Buddy Call
interview_outline:
Round 1 - Manager - 35 mins - Mergers & Acquisitions Case + Guesstimate 
Interview started with a couple of questions asking about myself and my work experience in detail. Interviewer gave an M&A case (PepsiCo wants to acquire Paper Boat; how should they go ahead?) Deloitte case interviews are not typical MBB interviews. It is more of a question-answer type, interviewer driven discussion. We discussed the case. Interviewer gave a guesstimate related to this case (Estimate the number of cold drink bottles sold by any one outlet in IIM Indore campus in a month). I solved the guesstimate. Towards the end I asked a question to interviewer. Interviewer told me that I have cleared the first round and second round will be continued in the same room in 5 mins.

Round 2 - Sr. Manager - 20 mins - Business case on promotional strategy 
One more interviewer joined the room. He did not ask any profile-based questions. He gave me a case. (Your client is a fast-food restaurant chain in the United States. The revenue earned has been stagnant for the past year. They want to introduce a promotional offer where customers get a movie ticket when they spend $50. Should they launch this offer?) We discussed the case. Again, this was an interviewer driven discussion where he provided many data points upon asking and asked me to calculate the required numbers. Towards the end I asked a question to interviewer. Both interviewers answered.

Round 3 - India head, Strategy practice - 10 mins - HR + Fit Interview 
This round was more like a casual discussion where he asked me questions based on my background, work experience and checked willingness to work for offered profile. Towards the end I asked a question to interviewer.
domain_questions:
What do you mean by the term synergy?
What are the different types of synergies in an M&A deal?
What are different types of due diligence?

My approach to answer these questions was to be very precise and short in giving answers which I think showed clarity of concepts.
hr_gk_questions:
Round 1
Tell me about yourself and Tell me about your work experience at Reliance in detail
- For both of these questions, I had my answer prepared. I tried to present the answer in the structured way such that I could highlight the important pointers.

Round 3

Your academic record has been excellent and consistent. I think you are a boring person. What do you want to say?
-I had faced this question earlier also. I presented my other hobbies and talked about other non-academic achievements.

Where are you from? What is the specialty of the Konkan region? Which Konkan region is more important – Kerala, Karnataka, Goa or Maharashtra?
-This was easy to answer as I was generally aware about my native region. I tried to bring in personal as well as business perspective while answering the last part.

Have you got chance to meet Mr. Mukesh Ambani while working at RIL? Tell me Mr. Ambani's two qualities that you like the most.
-Answered with sharing personal examples of working at RIL 

From your profile it looks like you have done a good job in manufacturing sector like work experience at RIL and summer internship at JSW. Why do you want to join consulting?
-I had my answer prepared

Your practice preferences include Supply Chain Practice and Operations Excellence Practice. But we are not hiring for these roles from your campus. Would you like to work in our Strategy practice?
-This was unexpected question. I gave genuine answer about why supply chain and operations excellence were my first preferences. Also, answered how I am interested in strategy practice too. It is important here to not sound desperate while saying yes to this question.
looking_for: In case interviews, they were looking for clarity and structure in thought process, good communication and domain knowledge in whichever field you have worked in (either workex or internship). It is also important to explain your work experience clearly since interviewer in round 1/2 decides whether your work experience is relevant or not (CTC offered differs according to years of relevant workex).
right_wrong:
Went Right
I both case interviews, I structured the discussion very well. For first, followed the M&A framework and answered the questions to the interviewer's satisfaction. In second case discussion, before solving the case, I touched upon various internal and external factors by asking the right preliminary questions. I displayed clarity in concepts like market research, profit margins, CLV etc.  The last interview went more like a conversation. I was able to maintain the flow of discussion.

Went wrong
In round 1, I could have stated more assumptions like seasonal variation, consumer behavior etc., while starting the guesstimate solution. In round 2, I could have been better in communication while solving numerical problem. That way, I could have avoided the mistake in calculation too.
tips: Be extremely thorough with your resume and personal background. Case practice is a must for consulting interviews. Solve different types of cases. Do not refer only one casebook. Form a group of individuals who genuinely want to  practice cases and give honest feedbacks to each other. I have experienced how case practice helped me to structure my thoughts and make better presentation. For HR questions, NPAD is a sufficient document. Please go through NPAD once before an interview.
dos_and_donts: For Deloitte USI Consulting, the type of case discussion happened during the interview was similar to the discussion in case workshop. So, participate in the workshop and make use of it.

pre_process_tips:
There were 2 test conducted before GD and interview. One was Aptitude test and on qualifying the aptitude test, you go for Psychometric test. On further qualification, you are called for GD.
Both the tests were not difficult. In psychometric test, be yourself and take decisions in context of the workplace, rather than a general context.
gd_topics_tips:
Topic of GD:
National companies vs MNCs- Which would you choose as a career choice and how would you like to end your career in anyone of them.

Structure of GD: 
We had to raise hands in Microsoft teams and we would be given 2 minutes to speak our points. There was no fish market discussion as the moderator was allowing the participants to speak after they raised their hands. So you will get ample time to speak without interruption, but that also gives rise to expectations of well structured answers and distinct points. 

Tips:
1.  The GD topic was straightforward, but as NPCI was a Govt. company, I was in favor of National companies and I structured my answers with the reasons to join national companies.
2. Moreover you should have 3-4 different reasons to support the same. Try to find new reasons and related your career choice in context of the nation, if possible (that's what I did)..
3. Even if you support the other side you should have 3-4 distinct reasons and that should make sense.
4. Write your points on paper (as there was ample time to think), and then give them a rough structure.
interview_outline:
The interview was based on the resume and was balanced. There were 3 members in the panel, one technical and 2 HRs. The technical guy was taking the interview and the other two were silent and had their videos off.
1. It started with introduction about me. It had to be in brief as it was instructed by the interviewer.
2. My internship was mildly related to product management in IoT, so there were two questions on the same. One was on, what was my internship about, and the other was "challenges related to IoT device management platforms"(which was essentially the outcome of my internship).
3. Then I had questions on design thinking, as I had mentioned that in the elective & academic achievements and it is very much relevant to prodman profile.
4. Then there were questions on "Why Product management and why NPCI?"
4. Then there were questions on the family background and some funny questions to lighten the interview.
5. At the end of the interview there was "Do you have any questions for us?"(Please ask 1 or 2 questions, I did ask 1)
domain_questions:
Design Thinking: 
1. Why did you take this subject?
Answer: I related that to my interest in Prodman and the importance of DT in designing any solution or product.
2. State just one and the most critical aspect of design thinking?
Answer: Whenever you design a solution or the product, you should always do that by keeping the extreme user in mind because the solution or product that is made for extreme user, can be easily extended to average or normal users.
Response from the panel: "This is one of the best description of DT that I have heard"( I think I cracked the interview at this moment)

After this there were no technical questions and the interview drifted towards HR and some light & funny questions.
hr_gk_questions:
1. What's your family background?
2. Why NPCI?
Answer: I answered this in 4 points.
a) The first one was related to Prod man profile and my interest.
b) The second point is what I related to the JD and my previous extracurricular and co-curricular activities. I also pointed out the advantages(like the full ownership of the product etc.) that was mentioned in the JD.
c)Third point was related to the impact that NPCI creates by deploying its payment solutions(Eg: The impact of UPI and RUPAY card in the payments domain and also the appreciation and recommendation of UPI by Google in their letter to Federal reserve systems of USA ).
d) The last point I related to my personal choice of working in a national company and creating indigenous solutions to indigenous problems.(Remember the GD, it was on the same topic and the panel in both were the same individuals, so by doing this there was uniformity established).
looking_for:
They were looking for two things:
 1. Some genuine interest in Prodman:  You should not be expert in this or well versed with the subjects, just that you should know some basics and can articulate your answers well.
2. Those who would stay in the same company for years: They repeatedly asked questions about my family background and why NPCI? Your answers should project the same..
right_wrong:
Right: 
1. My crisp way of answering his questions(especially the DT part).
2. Relating my profile and interests to their JD and prodman.
3. Smiling and keeping the interview on the lighter side.
Wrong:
I suppose, Nothing.
tips:
1. Product managements sessions were helpful.
2. Reading the JD thoroughly.
3. General knowledge about NPCI and its products.
4. Visiting NPCI website.
dos_and_donts:
1. Be thorough with the JD and the basics about product management.
2. Design Thinking is used at one of the stages of product development, so be well versed with the subject(it's an easy task to do this).
3. Keep smiling throughout the interview.
4. Structure your answers well.
5. Listen to prepcomm and use the materials.

pre_process_tips: The process comprised of shortlisting on the basis of resumes, Assignment of buddy, 1 telephonic interview with a senior associate, On campus interviews with Manager, Director, HR
interview_outline:
All interviews started with, "Tell me about yourself", "I have your CV right before me, please walk me through it". The interviews with the senior associate and the manager were very technical heavy. The interview with Director was more behavioral and situational. That round is mostly to check your fitment for the firm and their team. HR round was not very elaborate.
(Tip: I had multiple questions regarding the firm, the role, personal development ready to ask each interviewer - Shows you are eager to join the firm. Also don't repeat the questions, they have the data of what you have spoken in your previous interviews)
domain_questions:
Senior Associate: After Introduction, asked about my internship, workex and questions like what do you know about US healthcare, Then gave me 2 cases, "Devise the data management strategy for an insurance company", "Devise a market entry strategy into China for Apollo". These cases were a combination of both my workex and internship.
(Tip: Since this was a telephonic round, kept it more conversational. I had thoroughly prepared my workex, US healthcare and the PrepCom Materials, so it went breezy for me)

Manager: After Introduction, directly jumped to my workex and asked about it in "nth" detail, Gave me 2 cases, "You are a private insurance company, which country will you choose to enter, and how will you enter", "Devise the health analytics strategy of a payer". Describe the value chain of US healthcare, What all competencies should a payer have? What is value-based care, what is in it for all the stakeholders involved? How will you incentivize the providers to be a part of it?
(Tip: Since this is a consulting profile, kept it a serious conversation)

Director: Asked me about my workex and behavioral questions to which I answered very technically citing examples from my workex.
hr_gk_questions:
Senior Associate: Why PwC, Why this role, What do you want to do in your life in the next 5, 10, 15 years, What are your aspirations?

Manager: What will your manager/ mentor say about you in your previous organization? What will your colleagues say? What will your friends over here say? What will people who don't like you here say ? Are you aggressive?

Director: Tell me something that is not there in your resume, tell me where you come from? tell me about your family?
Tell me a time when something was going fine and your intervention actually made it worse? what did you learn from it.
Tell me a time when something was going bad and your intervention actually made it better?
Are you willing to relocate? Why PwC? Why this domain?
(Tip: Give all examples for the situational questions from your workex)

HR: Walk me through your CV? What are your subjects? What all certifications have you done? What are your aspirations? She spoke less, So I asked her multiple questions about the firm, about personal development, about one's growth in the firm, how does the firm help in that.
looking_for: Cultural fitment is what every firm looks for, be earnest, show them that you are eager to learn. Since this role is very domain specific, my prior experience at United Health Group helped me. Even though it was a very technical role back then, the interviewers expected me to know all of US health care. They were certainly happy when they saw I had AHM 250 certification.
right_wrong:
Right: My interviews were very technical heavy because I played my strength and drove them towards it. I even answered the behavioral questions technically citing examples from my prior work experience. Preparation helped me a lot. I knew my stuff. I didn't bluff.
Wrong: In the manager interview round, I was asked what will people say about you to which I had replied "Brutally Honest" to which he immediately asked what are the issues because of it to which I had replied, "I end up hurting people". This exactly is a big no no in interviews certainly can be answered in a more diplomatic manner.
tips:
Prep Com material is a must do. In addition to their consulting material, I had covered their IT, Marketing, Sector Reports, Recent News Materials. I had 
also prepared from Mckinsey insights and PwC reports. I had watched several videos on YouTube pertaining to my domain.  Had also read about recent trends, digital transformation in healthcare which gave me points to speak about in the interviews.
dos_and_donts:
Dos: Whatever you read, make notes/pointers of it. It is humanly not possible to remember everything. So the notes help right before the interviews and give you ample time to prep for the company specific questions. For behavioral questions, I had prepared the answers in STAR format. Telephonic interviews and usual interviews are pretty different, so I had practiced a mock one with a friend prior to my telephonic round.
Don'ts: Don't bluff in your CV, speak only those parts where you can go to the nth detail. Don't let panic get the better off you. Nobody knows you better than yourself. So stay confident.

pre_process_tips: There was initially just a google form where we had to put in our domain preferences. After the shortlists came for the individual domains, there were different processes for different domains and one person could get multiple shortlists. I got a shortlist for Operations and DDV. In Operations, there were two rounds of telephonic interviews before the main on campus interview. In DDV, there was an excel round and then an interview.
gd_topics_tips: No
interview_outline:
In the two telephonic interviews of Operations, both initially started with an introduction, then resume details, and then the interviewer started asking technical ( knowledge based ) questions - mostly basic Operation terms but if someone has done a six sigma certification (which I had done), they specifically drill you on its contents, so one needs to be thorough with that. Also, it helped me drive the interview towards my interest in Operations. One thing that is very important is they specifically ask "Why Operations Consulting and not any other domain in consulting" - so it is helpful if you have something on your resume that connects to your interest in Operations, for eg. any live project during MBA, a previous internship during your undergraduation, workex in operations or elective subjects that you can talk about. Now, in the first interview, there was a guesstimate and a case, after all the above mentioned things. The problem statement in the guesstimate asked was, "How many orders Zomato approximately delivers in Delhi on a normal weekday" (Delhi because I had done my internship there) 
In the second interview also, the order was similar and there was only one case (operations specific) that was pretty long and had follow up questions, specifically related to supply chain. 
There were no HR questions asked as such, except why Consulting, or "why Operations Consulting when you have cleared CFA L2",  "why not finance" , etc
domain_questions: Technical questions - leadtime, strategic sourcing, DMAIC vs DMADV, 5S, Pokayoke, lean methodolgy, value stream mapping. Many questions were asked during the case also as follow up questions, which I do not remember exactly, but on average you can expect to be asked about 15-20 concepts in each interview, so be thorough with all operations related terms - go through the shorter version of operations related terms provided by Prepcom, it helps.
hr_gk_questions:
Resume based questions mainly focussed on my Six Sigma certification, a previous internship I had done in Schneider that was related to Operations, live market research project of Volvo-Eicher and my summer internship experience and learnings in Synergy Consulting. I kept my answers short and crisp and always tried to link them to my interest in operations or consulting, which the interviewer liked. 
There were no Current Affairs based questions. There was a separate HR round after three personal interview rounds. Basic HR questions were asked like why I preferred operations over DDV, where do I see myself in next 5 years, what was the most difficult experience during my MBA and how I overcame it, what would be that one thing that would force me to resign a company, etc.
looking_for: At the end of each interview, the interviewer provides a feedback so that you can perform better in your next interview - in the first interview, mainly communication skills and clarity of thought process(checked through guesstimate) is important. Anything else is a plus point.But in the second one, they grill you more on technical questions and having your concepts clear is important. I think they look for people with good problem solving skills (hence multiple case interviews) along with a good technical knowledge and good communication skills.
right_wrong: What went right was that I had already prepared for all types of resume related questions, so I could handle them very well. What went wrong was that in my final interview, I got an operations case in automotive industry and I was not very familiar with it, so I had to ask many basic questions, before I could come up with a proper solution - so the case went on longer and I could not perform as well as I had done in previous rounds. But, then again, I had practised so many cases, that I could ask the right questions even though I did not know the industry properly, so I could solve the case. So, I would say a good case practice is the key to cracking the PWC interviews
tips: The casebook material repository provided by Prepcom helped me the most.
dos_and_donts: Be very thorough with Operations Subjects and practice as many cases as you can. In the first round, they can give any generic case also. So go through all the case books that you can. For specific Operations case tips ( go through ISB case book - how to reduce costs and increase profits). Also, read about topics like Warehouse Management, latest trends in Logistics sector, etc. Try to do a six sigma certification as it helps you with your operations knowledge.

role_offered: Vendor Manager and In-stock Manager (Same interview, profile allowed to be chosen in the end, although preference given in the preference form can tilt the interview slightly towards one profile)
pre_process_tips: Resume based shortlisting
no_interviews_duration: 4 rounds (1st round: 1 hour 30 minutes, 2nd: 1 hour 20 minutes, 3rd: 50 minutes, 4th: 30 minutes of CEO round, each round was an elimination round, but all who cleared 3rd round, also cleared 4th round)
interview_outline:
1st round: Started with any random point on the resume, deep down on it for 30-40 minutes, then another point.
Another 2 points chosen one after another, mostly work ex and other academic achievements, continued for a total 90 minutes. A few leadership questions on 14 principles of Amazon. 

2nd round: Started with work ex, continued with situation based questions, gauging fit with 14 leadership principles of Amazon. Nearly 5-6 situation based questions were asked (Eg. Tell me a time when.....) and went deep in to each situation asking 3-4 Cross questions. Then a case on my work ex in Hero MotoCorp - you are the owner of a start up that is in to automotives. You have been given 100 Crore rupees. You must gain a revenue of 10 by the end of 5th year. Which sector to enter - 2wheeler, 3 Wheeler, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles? Which technology - conventional fuel or hybrid or EV? How will you go about using the money? Justify all your spends in different parts of the automobile value chain. Estimate the market sizing of 2wheeler EVs in Bangalore in 2023. 

2nd round ended with Why Cloudtail? Why eCommerce? 

3rd round: Started randomly asking me about which city I belong to. Which part of India I worked in, the geography of that area, type of people that I worked with. Asked about recent achievements, small, big, academic, non academic, personal or professional - any achievements. (ice breaker only)

Asked a case: Imagine you are handling a product category sports shoes, you have to negotiate with Skechers brand for a better deal. Skechers has some constraints such as it will never agree to a price discount of its products on Amazon or any other site for that matter. It won't give you a margin more than 30 % while others like Adidas, Puma etc. Give you 35% margin. You also can't force Skechers for a bulk purchase deal, to bring down its price as you buy in lakhs.

How will you go about the deal? What is your BATNA? How will you leverage short deals to increase sells? Note that Skechers allow short deal sales on Amazon. List down all different aspects of such a negotiation. 

4th round  : 5-6 Amazon leadership skills based situation questions, and a case.  How will you launch Paint products through Amazon eCommerce (Asian Paints internship)?  Thoroughly about internship.
domain_questions:
Past work experience, bringing about 14 Amazon Leadership principles through examples from work ex, internship, live projects, clubs and committees - just anywhere. There could be any number of counter questions. Eg. I was the team manager for my institute Formula SAE team (a national level competition in which undergraduate Btech students design and build a racing car). To a question of what major challenges I faced during my tenure, I spoke about how our engine was imported from the US, got stuck at Kolkata port due to mismatch in import duties expected and what we have filed. Questions like why was there a mismatch? I answered the question by saying, non commercial imports are charged at a lower rate as compared to commercial imports. We filed as per the lower bracket of non commercial import tariff. I was asked what was tariff rate difference and what percentage of your total vehicle manufacture budget did it account for? How did you solve the problem? (checking frugality as a part of 14 leadership questions of Amazon). Name the authority in a port who can decide/waive off how much tariff to be levied for an import? What would have happened if it was not released? (after 2 months it would have been sold as scrap). What back up plans did you have? Did you exercise your back up plan? When do you exercise a back up plan? In your case what we're the risks involved?

A number of questions around my automobile work experience, live projects were also asked.
hr_gk_questions: Not specifically asked about current affairs, but resume related companies/industries and their related current news would help enrich your answers while solving cases. For example if a new regulatory barrier has been created by the govt. In a particular industry you have mentioned that you have done a live project /academic project in, it will be helpful if you can name drop the same during a discussion.
looking_for: Amazon's 14 leadership skills, authenticity of real life examples to questions like Tell me a time when....
right_wrong: Whenever I could not answer a question right away, I would discuss the same by saying, I might not be able to correctly answer it but I will think loudly. Please correct me when I am going sideways. Especially in the 3rd round while solving the unconventional Negotiation case, the panel gave a lot of inputs.
tips: Prepare a set of real life examples, preferably from work experience around the 14 Amazon Leadership principles. Practice them.

pre_process_tips: 3 rounds - First an aptitude test consisting of questions across finance, fixed income, accounting, Logical reasoning, corporate finance etc.. Then, case-based GD. Case would be on the lines of credit-analysis, and must be done under a time-crunch (20-30 mins for prep + 30 minutes discussion). Numbers are very important, and the ability to take out ratios will make you standout. Last round will be interviews. One will be technical, one will be general (anything under the sun), one will be technical + HR
gd_topics_tips: Credit analysis of the telecom sector of India. They looked for both a quantitative analysis as well as a qualitative take on the sector. Clarity with ratio formulas + quick excel calculations + balance sheet/income statement interpretations is the key here.
interview_outline:
First Interview - Started with intro. They picked up a couple of points from my intro and delved deeper into it, like which is your most significant achievement and why? Do you get time to play sports in college (had mentioned volleyball and badminton) etc. Then went into technical stuff such as what are the ratios you will look into to decide whether to give loan to a company or not, followed by a detailed discussion on why certain ratios would be better suited. This was more of a conversation, than a question and answer. He kept asking me the formulas for some ratios in between. Then we discussed why some ratios have this formula, its interpretations and implications etc. Then it went on the qualitative side, with questions on the Indian economy, whats happening in a sector of your choice etc. Then he focussed on a couple of my internships, which I explained in detail. Then he asked me if I had any questions for him, I asked 2, and that also went on for long.

Second Interview - This was very generic, and very current affairs based. Asked me resume related stuff, and basic accounting formulas (free-cash flow, operating income etc.). Then went on to global events and Indian economy. A bit of sports as well. Ended with a detailed discussion about the Evergrande crisis.

Third Interview - I guess this was supposed to be HR based, but turned technical. She asked me certain formulas (repeated from the first interview), then which are the top-3 sectors in trouble due to Covid, and why. Then top-3 sectors doing better because of Covid, and why. Then resume based questions, about my hometown and EBITDA VS EBIT etc.
domain_questions: Stated a lot of them above. Be thorough with your ratios and their details (especially Credit Ratios - Coverage + Leverage), accounting formulas (Term 1 FAC would be enough). I prepared from the corporate finance institute's website + Prepcom material. Prepcom material is good starting point, and then you can go over the CFI website for details.
hr_gk_questions: Intro, best thing about you etc. Nothing that NPAD didn't already cover. Current affairs was very much on the economic and financial end of things, with both domestic and global topics. Have stated the questions above. Be clear with all RBI rates, international events (Evergrande, Archegos etc.)
looking_for: Firstly, they were looking for a sound knowledge and understanding of Credit analysis and balance sheet interpretation. Then, I think communication skills and general awareness would be next. Nothing like work-ex preference, but commerce and arts students do have an edge. Anyone with accounting knowledge (CA, CFA) can nail the technical part without any effort.
right_wrong:
CTC + WCS was the best interview I gave (after messing up two before JPMC). Everything went right from the questions they asked me, to the discussions we had on global issues (Like ranting about China), to my current affairs knowledge. Nothing went wrong except that by the third interview, I had begun to falter as that was the 5th interview in 2 hours. I could have been a bit calmer and more composed in that, apart from that, I don't think anything went wrong. 

Converted :p
tips: I found the Prepcom finance material to be very comprehensive. I did everything from there, and then went on to CFI, Investopedia for further details and finer interpretations, exceptions etc. Equit-i primer was also helpful. GD was qualifying in nature, so being in the top - 2 of your group is paramount. In the PIs, you have to come across as someone who is energetic, knows their stuff, can talk professionally and has an understanding of what's happening in the world
dos_and_donts: Reach out to as many as people as you can, well in advance cause they won't give you time to prepare. Ensure that your Resume + NPAD prep is done well in advance of the placement week, so that in these crucial days, you can focus on technical prep. Company specific to would be generic about their values, learning opportunities etc.

pre_process_tips: The company asked us to fill a form on the placement portal -Reculta. It included the normal registrations and a google form where we need to select 3 roles out of 5 roles came for placement. There was no aptitude/ psychometric tests or any submissions for the eligibility.
interview_outline: So the interview started with the introduction of the panelists and then mine. Introduction included a set of academics related information with more emphasis on qualities I have. Then we deep dived for 10 mins on the work experience I had of 24 months as a data scientist. They talked  about the projects and the output you were able to get in terms of monetary value. pre_process_tips: Reculta -> Kearney Portal -> Resume Shortlisting -> Case Workshop -> Dinner -> Hotlist
no_interviews_duration: 4 (3 Buddy Calls +1 Final Interview). On an average, the buddy calls lasted for about 20-30 minutes, whereas the final interview lasted around 15-20 minutes.
interview_outline:
1st Buddy Call: Asked me to introduce myself, explain my background, interest in consulting, why did I want to join consulting when my interest was clearly finance, greatest achievement, failure, etc. It mostly seemed like my buddy was asking me random questions to gauge if I can keep him engaged and if I'm really interested in consulting+Kearney. 

2nd & 3rd Buddy Calls: Case based. Asked 1 check-up question like how I was doing and then went into the case. All three buddy calls were over a phone call so initially I found it hard to explain myself. In the 1st case, even though I had come to the right solution but still he did not understand the same and the interview went on for 5 more minutes after which he ended it in disappointment. The 3rd buddy call/2nd buddy case went well. It was a very short one, the case in itself last only 10 minutes. He was mostly looking for communication skills and approach to the case. 

Final Interview (with a Partner): In the final interview, I was asked to answer why Kearney and I had no specific answer for it. I globed this one and luckily made something up but would definitely recommend having that answer for all the companies. The partner gave me a market sizing problem statement for a company they were actually working with. Although it was supposed to be a guesstimate, I went like a proper case. I asked the 3CPI clarifying questions and took time to structure my guesstimate. So even though my final guesstimate was very simple, the partner was impressed with the fact that I took time to understand the context to come up with better assumptions. I made a mistake in the guesstimate which grossly overestimated the number, but what helped me was being cool about it, taking the partner's cue and immediately correcting it with rationale. Post the guesstimate, the floor was open for questions. I asked the partner about their ongoing cases and since the partner worked in Fintech/Insurance space, I asked them a very specific doubt I had about the implications of CBDC on the banking sector. I was told later by my buddy that the partner was impressed with the interview.
hr_gk_questions:
1. Tell me about your background/ Take me through your resume/ Introduce yourelf
2. Greatest Achievement & Failure
3. Why Consulting? 
4. Why Kearney?
looking_for:
1. Communication skills
2. Ability to hold a conversation and make it interesting.
3. Case-solving skills of course
3a. Ability to break down the problem as much as possible. 
3b. Ability to incorporate your awareness of business models/ current affairs/ understanding of the business world into your analysis.
right_wrong:
The Bad Parts: 
1. I wasn't prepared to answer why Kearney?
2. I couldn't explain myself very well over the phone during buddy calls as I could not see their expressions or show my workings. 

Good Parts: 
1. I started case practice early on and practiced a lot of cases of each type, which is why in my last buddy call when I was given an unconventional case, I could handle it well. 
2. I knew the partner who was taking my final interview as I took down the names and intro of all the people who introduced themselves during the PPT as well as the Case Workshop. I knew exactly what I would ask her, asking her what are the current cases that she's working on was just customary.
tips:
1. CASES, CASES, CASES. I did cases from A, B & FMS book. Not just practices cases, but after each case analyze what went right and what went wrong. QUALITY >>> QUANTITY. Take feedback very very seriously, from your batchmates as well as from your seniors. 
2. Since communication skills and HR questions are very important, fill the NPAD extremely diligently. You won't know what exact HR question will be asked, but if you have taken time to fill your NPAD, you will be able to make answers to any curveball questions.
dos_and_donts:
-> Don't lose hope at any stage in the process. My buddy was visibly disappointed in me after my first buddy call, but he was also really impressed after the second one. Everything will work out if you keep learning from your mistakes and don't make the same mistake twice. 
-> Don't ignore other domain prep. I was constantly in touch with finance prep along with case prep. In case Kearney wouldn't have panned out, I would have to instantly switch to prepare for finance interviews and that wouldn't be feasible. 
-> Do prepare guesstimates. I didn't expect my final interview to be based entirely on a guesstimate.

pre_process_tips:
Online Assessment Round: The test was of 40 min. and had 4 sections: Financial Accounting, 
Corporate Finance, Market Awareness, Financial Derivatives
gd_topics_tips: Case-based GD. Case would be on the lines of credit-analysis, and must be done under a time-crunch (20-30 mins for prep + 30 minutes discussion). Numbers are very important, and the ability to take out ratios will make you standout. At the end of the case, 5 questions were asked. The test was to observe the candidate's knowledge in different areas like industry awareness, calculations accuracy, credit analysis (very important), strategic solution to the problem given in the case etc.
interview_outline:
First interview was technical heavy and some resume based questions. Major part of the interview was about 3 financial statements. Interviewer (a chartered accountant) asked me about some line items and their impact on each statement. Some basic questions based on ratio analysis like how will you analyze the efficiency of a company based on the financial statements. EBIT v/s EBITDA v/s PAT: which numerator is better to calculate interest coverage ratio and why. Why is depreciation recorded even if there is no cash outflow. 
Second interview was started with my basic introduction, the work I did in my summer internship and why WCS. Other than this, it was technical heavy. The interviewer asked me about any any specific industry I follow and most of the subsequent questions were around that industry (I choose telecom industry). Some questions were about the financial statements of the companies in that industry. If there are is any unique features in their financial statements. Some questions on financial ratios of those companies. How would you measure the performance of the companies in that industry (basically the KPIs) etc. Then some basic FAC questions (operating lease v/s finance lease, depreciation accounting and how it will affect each financial statement). Then some questions on credit risk like how will you analyze the client from credit risk perspective before lending him the loan etc. One basic OFD question was about how will you hedge against falling prices of inventory material and vice versa. Then one question about derivatives accounting.
domain_questions: Pretty much mentioned above. Be very thorough with your ratios and know exactly why that particular figure is used in that ratio especially efficiency ratios, leverage ratios, coverage ratios. Be thorough with term 1 FAC. Prepcom material and corporate finance institute's website are useful sources. Also, know the in depth analysis of all 3 financial statements.
hr_gk_questions: Basic HR questions like basic introduction, work done during the internship, why credit risk etc. There were not many HR questions.
looking_for: They were looking for someone who knows the financial statements in depth. Also, who knows how to use various ratios to find out information about the company. In the second interview, the interviewer was looking for how in depth I know the industry I was following. Also, they were judging how confident I was of my answers. Both the interviewers asked numerous time whether I was sure of my answer.
right_wrong:
Apart from my introduction, I wasn't well prepared for other HR questions. I didn't answer 'why credit question' adequately and stuttered during that question. I didn't know the industry I choose in too much depth. So, I had to rely on the general knowledge to answer the industry related questions which could have gone either way.
The good part of my interview was I knew the answers to a lot of 'why' questions about ratios, financial statements, FAC questions etc. and I was confident in my answers.
The industry related questions could have been answered more precisely.
tips: I found prepcom material, CFI, Investopedia websites very helpful. In the GD you have to be in the top 2-3 to get to the next round. For the interviews, my background in the accounting was very helpful. During your introduction, try to steer the conversation towards the subject you are very comfortable in as there will be some questions on you intro. and the work you have done in the internship. Have some general sense of what is happening in the world (macroeconomic) and be confident in you answers.
dos_and_donts:
Prepare all the HR questions well in advance as you won't have much time just before the placements. Be very thorough with your resume. For tackling questions like why this company or why this role, try to match your answers with the values of that company and the opportunities mentioned in the job description.
Never bluff about anything in the interview. If you are not sure about the answer, ask the interviewer whether you can take a guess and then answer. Reach out to the seniors well in advance so that you have some time to prepare.

pre_process_tips: Resume based shortlist

Asked me about economy post-Covid. (3-4 counter questions on my answers) How the debt-equity market is doing, the reason for the same. Questions related to different sectors were asked, what is happening and why. 
Credit Risk related questions- What is your understanding of the role, how do we decide whether to extend credit to a party or not. 2-3 cross questions on the factors I stated.
