Was asked about options and its graph (for long put and short call). Then he gave me few examples to understand the gain/loss of option holder and seller.
Asked me about the CAPM model, what is beta, how we calculate it. What is a risk-free rate, how do we select it? 
Detailed discussion on markets and banking sector. Asked me why despite covid Sensex is doing so good. Many counter questions on my answer. How is Covid crisis as compared to 2008 crisis? (1-2 counter question on my answer). I mentioned some facts about the FMCG industry, he picked it and asked me what is happening in FMCG, asked me to explain whether it is a good time to invest in it or not. What factors should we consider before extending credit to them?

3rd round- It was a mix of tech and HR. Asked me many questions related to why I want to join the Credit Risk team. Why am I fit for this role, what challenges will I face if I get slected? My internship experience, projects, learning from the same. 
Asked about options, credit risk in Options, how to mitigate it. Gave me few examples and asked me what will happen in each of those situations. Asked me my opinion of the government stimulus provided. Was it a good move?

4th round- It was only HR questions.
domain_questions:
Different types of bonds, Bond pricing (foreign bonds). Asked me about options and different option strategies (Straddle, etc) I was not very aware of the same, he explained it to me and then asked me 2-3 questions on the same.
A lot of questions on markets (he was more interested in why something is happening rather than what is happening). Economic recovery, fiscal/monetary policies by govt and its impact
hr_gk_questions: Was asked a lot about markets, economy, recovery post Covid
looking_for:
Someone who is very curious (and eager/quick to learn) and is able to think on their feet.
For eg. I was not aware of a topic, he explained it to me and then asked me 3-4 questions on the same.
right_wrong:
Right- I kept on asking questions (clarifying as well as role-related) to make it more like a conversation and keep him engaged. Gave structured answers for all HR questions. Was able to answer most of the technical questions correctly.

Wrong- In the 2nd round I made a mistake of adding premium as I panicked. Could have given better answers for Covid recovery in banking sector.
tips:
Read the JD as many times as you can to understand the role. This will give you an idea of what to prepare. (Talk to someone in similar roles). 
In terms of where to prepare from- PrepCom repository (Fin + current affairs), fin-1 course, YouTube videos (IFT).
Invest good time for HR answers. If asked initially, they set the tone for the whole interview. If asked at a later stage, can give your interview a good closure.
Also, smile and try to make the interview engaging, ask questions. 
In the end when you are asking questions make sure you are not asking random questions, try to pick up something from the interview, and then ask about it. Even if you have pre-prepared questions, try to frame them in a way that it doesn't look rehearsed and contextually irrelevant.
dos_and_donts:
Don't globe, even in HR questions. Have very very structured (and personalized) answers. Especially for questions like Why GS, why Credit Risk, why you, etc.
For technical questions, if you don't know anything, tell them clearly. They will explain it to you (But be ready for many questions on it after they are done explaining :p)

pre_process_tips: There were 2 aptitude tests (with questions from quants, verbal, finance and a case), followed by a GD, followed by 2 interviews
gd_topics_tips:
There were 2 panelist, one of them was on a good senior postilion. GD was in a group of 5, and lasted roughly about 20 to 25 minutes was around the Case from the test. Started off with short intros from each of the candidate. It was open at the beginning and we were all giving our insights from the financial data of the case. Followed opinion based questions and on inferences. Followed by some cross questioning and justification requests. Lastly any questions from our end.

Be prepared with ratios, valuation, some bit of stock market movement and financial analysis and what any of that could mean for a company. If the analysis and implications of every aspect of financial statements are thorough, then you'll be able to present good inferences. The panel was looking for clarity of concepts, ability to deeply analyze and understand the  financial statements and any unique perspective that you were able to bring to discussion. Also being passionate and up to date with Current Affairs may help you understand things better.
interview_outline:
1) Basic Intro, Fav subjects and some concepts from that subject, internship experience and your learnings from that, why Finance, what do you know about finance, questions and deep analysis of various concepts, situation based questions, why DE Shaw and not DESRI, any questions from my end.

35% HR, 55% technical, 10% academics - Slightly technical  

2) Basic Intro, questions around internship, some around pors and my interests, questions about the current affairs in the field (about stock market), more questions about "what if" then how will it affect the market, if I knew what DE Shaw does, why DE Shaw and my expectations from the internship

50% HR, 50% technical - Balanced
domain_questions:
Valuation methods - deep analysis (Why of everything), Ratio analysis, stock prices movement, repo rate and its effects
Questions decided to explain DCF method and briefly about the multiples method. Was asked to define every element of DCF and often asked about why this and why not this. Eg about why we use WACC instead of market rate. Even if I didn't know the exact answer, talked about my thought process and told them this is how/why I believe something like that might have happened. Similarly for another question about change in inflation and how that would affect the stock market. To answer that I told them what I think moves the stock market and thus my perspective about how that would affect the market. 
Some more basic questions like what should be an optimal number for various ratios. The most systematic approach was not just giving the number directly but rather assuming a context, industry and then based on that coming up with no.s.
hr_gk_questions:
Asked about my life story, who am I and what are my interests, then some questions about why finance, why the company and how will I use my skill once a part of the org.
I tried to create a story around me that would keep them interested in knowing more about me. Tried to display my passion and newly found drive towards finance, justified that with how I plan to undertake activities to keep this passion growing. Backed my claims about my skills with the right instances from various projects/pors or even internships.
looking_for: A Passionate individual, with strong inclination towards finance. Some basic knowledge about the field, and logic enough to deduce implications. And some knowledge about the financial environment and current affairs. No hard requirements for workex or any certification, but maybe a project/internship towards finance will give a direction to your story and journey
right_wrong:
Converted. 
Good - applying logic to come to a conclusion, even if I didn't know a particular concept. Showing my drive towards the company and my zeal to learn.
Bad - Messed a bit about concepts from my favorite subject. So I would recommend to know bits of your resume in and out, be it even a couple of academic subjects.
tips:
Mock GD not so much, but PIs did help, because they covered a lot of the technical aspects that were somewhat also reflected in the actual interview. 
One of the best prep-com sessions was for Advance Finance and that did help a lot.
Materials shared by Equiti and prepcom were good for preliminary study and knowledge. But did a lot of research by my own using youtube, moneycontrol and investopedia.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlist for the case based GD round after which there were interviews.
gd_topics_tips:
Case:
Federal Reserve plans to wind down its asset purchase program and as a rates trader, one has to point out the risks and benefits of the following alternatives : interest rate swap, options (interest rate caplet), futures contract, swaptions. We were also asked to discuss how the portfolio valuation would change under each of the four alternatives in the event of an earlier-than-expected interest rate hike. Relevant data (US Treasury yield, anticipated increase in rates, cap rate) were given. 
I think they were looking to test our understanding of various derivative instruments and our ability to apply them in a real world context. 

Tips: 
1. Try your best to begin the GD as it sets the rhythm. 
2. Highly recommend to follow ET Prime diligently or atleast make a prep group of 3-4 people and discuss the latest happenings everyday. I talked about the Taper Tantrum event in the GD as it was pertinent to the given case. 
3. Please be civil. Don't be boisterous by cutting people off. Try being the bigger person and include people by asking them to speak (that is, after you are done speaking, of course :P)
interview_outline:
Interview 1 (55 mins)
1. Introduction and walk me through your resume which was followed by resume based questions. 
2. Technical questions.

Interview 2 (5 mins) 
1. Introduction and technical questions.
2. Current Affairs and my knowledge about the role. 

Interview 3 (10 mins) 
1. Introduction and HR questions.
domain_questions:
1. There was an extensive discussion on option greeks. I was asked to list down the greeks that I know of and then I was asked the sign of delta for a short call and value of delta for an at the money call option which was followed by a question on naming an option combination (with the maturity periods) that has a negative gamma and positive vega. 

2. Questions on At the money option, forwards, volatility. 

3. Basic Probability and Statistics questions. For e.g. why take squared deviation in variance (and not raise it to any even power) 

4. Questions on VaR, Conditional VaR.
hr_gk_questions:
Current Affairs:
1. How have the markets performed?
2. Semiconductor shortage and the reasons for the same. 

HR:
1. Questions on my ability to work in teams and substantiating them with examples from my life. 
2. How do you deal with criticism and settle disagreements?
3. Why Credit Suisse?
looking_for:
1. Strong logical thinking skills. 
2. Knowledge about derivatives. 
3. Application-oriented approach. 
Certification : CFA L1 Candidate. 
Work-ex: Fresher (IPMer)
right_wrong:
Outcome: Converted. 

Good: 
1. Decent understanding of derivatives helped in the interview as I had done a couple of related courses and an academic project in IPM which helped me drive the interview in the direction I wanted to a certain extent. 
2. Kept it conversational. 

Bad:
1. Should have been a little more patient and could have thought well instead of answering the questions in a hasty manner. Always remember that the interview is not a sprint and points won't be deducted just because you took a few more seconds to arrive at the right answer.
tips: Prepcom materials, Equit-I's material on derivatives, Investopedia.
dos_and_donts:
Do(s):
1. Pay keen attention in the interview when the interviewer tries to teach you something as there might be follow up questions based on what the interviewer taught you. Try to add value by letting them know what your views are/asking relevant doubts. That way, it will look good on your part as it shows you had paid attention and that you actually understood the concept. 
2. Be absolutely thorough with each and every word that you've mentioned in your resume, especially if you have written something that is related to the role being offered. 
3. Participate actively in the pre placement talk as it gets you positive attention and helps you understand the company better.
4. Go through the JD and have a good understanding of the role being offered (talking to seniors will surely help in this regard, we are always there to help! )  

Don't(s):
1. Never globe. The scope is limited anyway in such interviews and it becomes obvious that you are trying to beat around the bush which is certainly not a good thing. 
2.  Don't panic. Summer Internship is not the end of the world. Stay as calm as possible and enjoy the process, it will definitely help you in bringing your A game in the interview. 

All the best! :)

pre_process_tips: Resume Based shortlisting
no_interviews_duration: 1st round(1 hour), 2nd Round(1 hour), 3rd round(1 hour), HR(10-15 mins)
interview_outline:
1st Interview - First 5-10 mins were spent on normal HR questions about me, Work-Exp, and SIP. Was given two unconventional cases and no guesstimates. The premise of both the cases was from my work-exp domain( IT automation) and SIP project( GTM for a digital solution). I was taken off-guard when I was given an unconventional case and the interviewer asked me not to force-fit any frameworks. I was thinking out loud and expressed clearly whatever I had in my mind. She rectified me in the approach. Once I suggested something, she said I am thinking in the right direction and then I took it from there. In the second case, after my initial evaluation, I clearly said this isn't a feasible business opportunity. She had counter questions but I justified my arguments.
2nd Interview - First 5-10 mins were spent on normal HR questions about me, Work-Exp, and SIP. Started with a Growth case. Once I was able to arrive at the expected strategy, we moved to the market sizing for the new market entry that I proposed. This involved the guesstimate. This was a conventional case and hence I was able to drive it better. I used the question to derive insights that helped me eliminate options early on. There were times when I was going the wrong way and the interviewer was giving subtle cues about that. I picked those up and rectified my approach where needed. Did ask me to do the calculations and I tried to do them out loud so that on a call there is more clarity. 
3rd Interview - Started with normal HR questions. Did ask questions about Leadership traits. Started with a guesstimate and then moved to a new market entry case. He started with setting the premise about the guesstimate. I drove some insights from that to build my logic for the guesstimate. In the case I had to devise marketing strategies for the customer segments identified. 
HR Round - Normal questions about why PwC, why Strategy competency( a lot of whys here), how my summers exp would help in Strategy role, any PORs that I held at IIM Indore
domain_questions: None. Few were related to SIP experience but nothing technical
situational_questions:
Q- What according to me is the one must-have trait and one trait not required in a Leadership position. Similar question for a team member position.
Ans - Took a minute to think and used my past work exp to answer this. Based on how I have seen my leaders and team members, answered these questions. Had a conversation around this answer at the end since the interviewer had a similar experience at his position.
looking_for:
For Cases - They were checking if I was able to structure my thoughts and how was I using them to solve the problem at hand. Structuring doesn't necessarily mean fitting any framework but how you use the data/ information provided to arrive at a solution. They don't expect flawless approach. But it is important that you are able to realize that you are going wrong, acknowledging that and taking the right step. 
For HR - They just check how comfortable you are in holding a conversation. Nervousness cannot be avoided but try not to show it to them. Smile and keep a cheerful stance all throughout. Don't let stress overshadow your performance.
right_wrong: My ability to think out loud helped me in all of the cases. That way my interviewers were able to show where I was going wrong and I was able to take the correct steps. Also, I made sure I asked questions at the end. These questions helped me establish a connection with each of them and maybe also showed them that I was genuinely interested in this role.
tips: The case preparation materials by PrepCom and Consulting Club are exhaustive enough for the preparation. I made sure that I practiced cases with friends from all possible domains and sectors( special emphasis on the ones which were mentioned in my resume). Also, read about the sectors in my resume( especially the cost and revenue drivers). Make sure that you time your practice cases too since in actual scenarios they don't spend more than 20-25 mins on a case. The domain sector sessions were really helpful, especially the Consulting session.
dos_and_donts: Practice cases early on. That can help you face the interviews more confidently

pre_process_tips: Company directly shortlisted based on resume
no_interviews_duration: 4 interviews: 1st PI (40 mins), 2nd PI (20 mins), 3rd (15 mins) and 4th PI (20 mins) were on Day 0.
interview_outline:
First PI : It was a telephonic interview. It started off with small greetings and then a 2 mins run through of the resume. Then he asked about one of my internships in index construction. Gave me a situation and asked me to walk through the steps of index construction and what the various ways are to test liquidity of stocks. Then there was a brief discussion about futures and forwards. At the end of the interview, he asked me for any questions on my part.
Second PI : It was a telephonic interview. Again asked a brief introduction on resume. He asked few HR questions like why finance, why credit risk. I had derivatives in my electives, so we had a brief discussion on that and what type of credit risks derivatives can have. 
Third PI : It was the first zoom interview with a member from Hong Kong team. He asked me again for a brief run of my resume. He then asked me some case based questions.
Fourth PI : It was again a zoom interview. Started with an introduction from the interviewer on his background. Then my introduction followed by a case. He asked to compare two companies in different sectors and what are the key metrics to use to evaluate them. He asked HR questions too like what I like about credit risk, why Goldman Sachs. Then the interview ended with some questions on my part.
domain_questions:
Domain specific questions were:
1. What is credit risk?
2. What are the key metrics to evaluate credit risk of different sectors
3. Derivative related -  what instrument to use to hedge against some particular risk
Always try to walk through your logic and explain why you said some particular approach. If there is a flaw in your approach, the interviewer gently nudges you into the right direction. Take the hint and be willing to rethink your answer. If I didn't know the answer, I tried finding a similar situation and what I would do in that situation and extrapolate that to the question asked.
hr_gk_questions:
Some HR questions included:
Why finance? I talked about my background and what inspired me to take on finance as a career. Spoke about my engineering days and what made me give CFA. Try relating the answer to some situation in your life.
 Why credit risk? I talked about what I like about credit risk and how it helps me analyze a particular sector. Here try talking about what part of the job excites you and a new idea you want to implement for the role.
Why Goldman Sachs? I spoke about the culture and the feedback I received from my alums about their experience in the company. I said I liked networking with some of the brightest people in the industry and the great learning curve there.
What are your strengths? My interviewer kept on making me list my strengths. So I had to talk about 4 strengths. Always give an example as to how it justifies you strength.
looking_for:
They wanted people who are genuinely interested in the role and want to learn it. You need to show some excitement for working and give ideas the company can implement. If not, have questions to ask about the team. 
I am a fresher, so there wasn't any work-ex expectations. It is preferable to have CFA or FRM on your resume. A project or internship in finance will give you some edge.
right_wrong: The good part was that it was a discussion on my resume. They gave me situations based on that only. In case I didn't know the answer to some question, I tried finding a parallel to it from the stock market or any industry. The bad part was that I was not that thorough with few HR questions, and so had to think about it in the interview. I converted the interview.
tips: Prepcom's sector reports was useful. Their sheet with the current affairs will help keep you updated with current news. External resources I used were ibef reprts and crisil research reports. Also, I did a revision of CFA level-1.
dos_and_donts: Be thorough with your resume and be ready with how to introduce yourself in 2 mins. Always be prepared with at least 2 role specific questions to ask the interviewer. For finance particularly, ensure that you cover 2 sectors.

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlisting
interview_outline:
The First interview started with interviewer giving brief info about himself, followed by my intro. Basic questions like why operations, why consulting, why PwC, followed by a short case based on the "value chain of a biscuit manufacturer". Further discussions on the value chain part and follow up questions like When should we outsource production, what factors would you look for in the supplier etc. This was then followed by a short guesstimate of "number of tyres sold in a year in India". Lasted about 50 min.
2nd interview, started on similar lines with the introductions, followed by a case of "Heavy vehicle manufacturer based in US, who were suffering decreased profits since last 2 years" and we had to find the issue and possible solutions. The case covered all the basics of operations management like cycle times, bottlenecks etc combined with the complete supply chain development. The interviewer went in depth of every part of the supply chain i mentioned discussing the possible issues and solutions. Lasted about 45 min.
3rd Interview( the director round), again started with brief introductions and a bit more on why operations consulting? She asked a bit about my work experience and asked to choose between inventory management or sourcing related topics for a short case. Told that i had no experience with either and had more interest in production/manufacturing part but was still given a case on sourcing. The interviewer was helpful and it felt more like a discussion with 50% of ideas coming from her. Lasted about 25 min.
4th Interview- HR round- Was more of a formality round (might not be true for other competencies or candidates, This was NOT a non-evaluative round for the DDV-IT folks). HR asked if i was willing to accept the offer. Lasted 2 min.
domain_questions: There were no specific technical questions. Somewhat basic technical questions were asked in line with the case .The basic knowledge of the First year courses of OM-1,2 and SCM should be enough for answering them. Eg. what is bottleneck, how to identify it, what are the causes, how to rectify them etc.
situational_questions: No situational questions
hr_gk_questions: No HR questions
looking_for: They kept emphasizing that the most important criteria of judgement would be the structured thinking process. This i feel is not only related to the Cases they ask, but also to the other questions that you answer like why ops, why consulting, why PwC etc. Follow MECE approach to ensure you are always methodical and never miss a point.
right_wrong: As i had practiced many case interviews with my friends, the first 2 interviews were a breeze. In them i ensured that the interviewers were feeling engaged (as it was online) and i made a point to confirm my approach with them and take into account their feedback. The 3rd round was challenging as i had no knowledge of the domain of the case being asked. I openly mentioned this fact and even apologized for the same. The interviewer didn't mind the lack of knowledge and mentioned that my attempt was good and well structured.
tips:
Practice, Practice and Practice!!! Case interviews and guesstimates are all about practice. Form a group of 3 to 4 people and distribute cases among yourself. Each prepare one and interview the other. Using this our group was able to cover many cases(quantity and variety both are important) in a short time.
YouTube channel i used extensively : https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCmUIX2KvSSsztvD-ldjkcuQ
His videos especially for Ops based cases are the best i came across.
Prep com Mock PIs were good for initial start to get rid of those early jitters we face and basic ops material will help you revise your subject knowledge.
dos_and_donts: The interview season can tend to be very hectic, especially the consulting ones with multiple rounds. There is no need to stress or panic. Just practice a lot and stick to the structured way of thinking and presenting your solutions. Give a good attempt and there won't be much issue even if you lack some particular factual knowledge. Keep the interviewer involved, and ask for guidance if you are stuck. Case interviews are all about discussion and generally not a one way street, make sure to remember that. And in the end, a smile can go a long way. Nod and smile and enjoy the process. All the best!!! :-)

no_interviews_duration: 1. Introduction Round (30 mins), 2. Case Interview Round (1 hr), 3. Director's Round (45 mins), 4. HR Round (30 mins)
interview_outline:
Introduction Round:
Almost every interview started with "Tell me about yourself". I structured my answer briefly in terms of Educational background, work-ex, internships, live projects, certifications and Biz competitions. 
I was asked more about my internship viz. my roles and responsibilities, nature of my project and its strategic objective, challenges I faced, recommendations I made.
Later,I was asked domain specific (IT) questions like Enterprise software solutions, PaaS, data security, etc. not technically heavy though.

Guesstimate Question: 
You are the CMO of Apple iPad division. You need to design an Ad campaign for your new product - iPad Pro. Determine how many people inspired by your campaign would buy your product in India?

Case study Round
Question: You are a PwC Consultant. You need to handle IT dept in an acquisition setup of a 'veterinary management company' by a private equity firm. Structure your answer as a due diligence process you shall be conducting for the private equity firm.
domain_questions:
1. What are primary considerations from an IT systems' perspective in M&A - divestiture setup?
Ans. Intensive due diligence; identification of synergies and process improvements; post M&A - divestiture integration and implementation. 

2. What is Legal Entity Rationalization?
Ans. Legal Entity - Customer facing (Go To Market) entity that acts as a profit center for an organisation.
Rationalization - reduction or simplification of LEs via mergers, acquisitions or divestitures to realize cost and revenue synergies.
situational_questions:
1. If you are a PwC consultant, what specific questions will you ask the CIO of any company to get an overall picture of the IT systems they hold?
2. If given a chance to invest all your money into either cloud computing or ML technologies, where would you invest and why?

Guesstimate question: 
You are the CMO of Apple iPad division. You need to design an Ad campaign for your new product - iPad Pro. Determine how many people inspired by your campaign would buy your product in India?
hr_gk_questions:
HR questions that I was asked:
1. Did you ever receive constructive criticism? How did you react to it? Did you find it useful? Did you work upon it and brought the improvements in practice?
2. Have you ever taken up any responsibility, proactively, which made an impact to your project/group/organisation? 
3. Why PwC? Why not any other consulting firm?
looking_for: The interviewers were mainly looking for candidates who can provide comprehensive and structured solutions to various business problems. Chances of getting shortlisted increases if one has relevant work-ex/summer internship as required for DDV IT role.
right_wrong:
In case interview round I was supposed to structure out the process of IT system migration. While my answer tend to have deflected more towards technical implications, the interviewer expected my response from a financial point of view (like potential cost headers the migration process would generate). I was interrupted and was asked to re-frame the structure from a finance angle. It got me confused at the time and I asked the interviewer for few minutes to think upon. Although I couldn't give a comprehensive response but the interviewer 
seemed satisfied. 
Learning: Don't try to overstate things and frequently validate the flow of your answer with your interviewer. They will happily guide you in the right direction if in case you get lost/stuck/deflected.

I converted the interview.
tips:
Approach: 1. Be thorough with your resume 2. Have a basic level understanding of the industry/domain you are targeting for 3. Be aware of current affairs/trends in the industry 4. Practice guesstimates and case interviews regularly

PrepCom material that helped me the most: ISB casebook, IT and Product Management Deck

Yes, the domain-specific sessions were extremely useful.
The mock GD-PI makes you aware of any shortcomings and scope of improvements in your lateral, final preparations. It builds up sufficient confidence to take on real interviews.
dos_and_donts:
General:
1. Start working on your resume at least 3 months before your laterals/final. Be thorough with it and continuously improve upon it.
2. Keep yourself updated with industry trends and challenges.
3. Practice guesstimates and case study interviews regularly.

Company Specific:
1. Understand the role the company is offering viz. Projects, responsibilities, challenges faced, work culture, etc. (Make best use of the Buddy Connect)
2. Always try to exemplify your interview answers either with your past experiences or hypothetical scenarios.

pre_process_tips: Application forms need to be filled apart from Portal .The aptitude test consists of CAT type questions (70 mins) in all & coding questions relating to R & SQL . Need to manage time in the Aptitude part and need to at least solve 1 or 2 coding questions out of 8.
no_interviews_duration: There were 2 rounds of interview the first one being Technical Round and the Second one being HR Round ,  Round 1(40 minutes)   Round 2 (45 minutes)
interview_outline: Both the Interviews were Balanced with Resume and HR based Questions. First Round Started with Introduction , Some puzzles to be solved ,Guesstimates .Second round consisted of Mainly resume project based and HR cum Situational based Questions.
domain_questions:
Guesstimates
Estimate the Toll Revenue of the Bandra Worli Sea Link . I tried to make it clear the assumptions I was taking one-by One .Be very precise in the segmenting step. And then performed calculations . The panel was mainly interested in the approach and till how depth you can make correct assumptions. The panel was impressed when I did not include bikes and also included Monthly passes revenue in the calculation.
Asked to Explain my Summer Internship and 1 Academic Project: I Gave the scenario of my internship in Half a Minute and then Proceeded with STAR Framework to describe the Project. The way I explained the project and Internship the Panel didn't ask me further Questions.
Direct General Knowledge Questions on YOGA as I had mentioned it on my Resume. Why YOGA ? When is YOGA day? How will you continue Practicing YOGA after joining Office?
situational_questions: Share an Instance where you could Avoid/Resolve conflicts in the Group? Focused on Why these conflicts arise .How to know the group Dynamics Beforehand and how to tackle it by Good communication and Team coordination. Gave an Example using STAR Approach.
hr_gk_questions:
What is Unique about IIM Indore that other TOP B-Schools don't Have?
I thought at the moment for around a minute and mentioned about being socially Conscious Institute. Mentioned about REP, Utsaha and IRIS  records .Also spoke about Spiritual Garden.

What have you Achieved after 2 Years of MBA?
Focused on while giving Examples on each of the following points.
Team work ,Being customer oriented ,Networking ,Peer to Peer Learning and the Brand of IIM will help me a lot in future Life.

What is one point you Feel company needs to improve?
Took Half a minute to think and Mentioned them about their website Jargons ie Number of Jargons should be less. The Panel felt Happy with the Answer
looking_for: I think they Were Looking for Clarity of Thought and How can you break each Answer into Simple Logic . They wanted the Candidate to think well before answering any Unconventional Question thrown at you and not answer in a Hurry. Be consistent in your talking and Explanation. Need to know Resume and basic HR questions Thoroughly.
right_wrong:
Good Part: I handled the assumptions well and Always had a two Way Conversation while speaking anything. I was prepared at the basic HR questions and could answer them Keeping in their JD in mind. I always thought before answering any unstandard question.

Things could have handled Better : I should have been prepared for the questions like Why IIM Indore earlier.
I converted the Interview and got Placed
tips: According to me what helped me was to focus only on the Resources of Prep Com.Prepcom Preparatory material was more than Enough to guide me throughout the preparation and also gave me important framework on How to answer the questions. The Mock GD/PI helped me but I continued to Take MOCK PI and feedback from all my Placed friends everyday when I didn't have any process. I started my Preparation Early when Prepcom had given the Domain sessions. Prepcom's HR question material and Sector Reports were the best and the Excel sheet where current affairs was updated regularly.
dos_and_donts:
Do's Whenever Any Club or committee is organizing any event Like Sharing or experiences or Making Available domain sessions always attend them and focus and improve upon the topics. Different Clubs would share you Casebook. Keep referring to that only.  Read  the JD carefully.

pre_process_tips:
1. Resume Shortlisting
2. Interview 1
3. Interview 2
4. Presentation (no submission)
5. HR round
no_interviews_duration: Initial two interviews were scheduled for 20 minutes each but went on for roughly 40 minutes. Presentation went for 20-25 minutes and HR round was roughly 10-15 minutes if not lesser
interview_outline:
1. Interview 1 (Videocall scheduled for 20 minutes))- They called it a buddy call but be prepared for it as it is just like a normal interview. 
Started off with tell me about yourself, asked why I wanted this role considering I had significant number of finance-related resume points. If I was the CEO of my startup company, what two things I will change about it. (15 minutes). 
This interview was to check cultural fit, even if they go technical, you have to make sure that you show them that you are a personality fit. 
Ended with my questions (20 minutes)
2. Interview 2 - Same format as the previous interview. Not everyone had this round. Started off with my questions (15-20 minutes). Questions about what I thought the role was, why I worked in a startup, why this role. Lastly asked if I would take a product management role over the role offered (my internship was in prodman and I talked about how much I enjoyed that) - This question was a recurring theme in all my interviews in some form or another. Make sure you convince them.
3. Presentation (no submission) - Gave a mostly researched-based presentation question. They had mentioned 8-10 points that they wanted covered like what industries to venture in, competitor analysis, Indian Market outlook, key use cases, major roadblocks etc. The presentation should have minimal text, be presentable, and should have a flow. Be ready for some basic follow up questions. 
4. HR round - Started with tell me about yourself and some conversational follow-up. Very relaxed and fun interview.
domain_questions: Hardly any technical question in any of the interviews. They just wanted to check your knowledge of the company, understanding of the role, your interest in the role and cultural fit.
situational_questions: No such question asked specifically but I had included such situations in other answers to prove that I was a cultural fit
hr_gk_questions:
Tell me about yourself (and then a few follow up questions from this)
Why did you choose a startup for your internship? (Since I interned at a startup)
Grilling on the fact that I had a lot of finance related points in my resume but applied for a sales strategy role (Common question asked throughout every single one of my interviews. Have a bulletproof answer ready for this)
Question on my interest (Basically to see if you can hold a water cooler conversation)
looking_for: They don't care much about the technical knowledge. Their focus is the cultural fit and your enthusiasm for the role and the company
right_wrong:
1. Well-researched about the company and the role and my expectations of the role were very clear.
2. They love to hear about themselves and the company. Focus on this. Talk about what the company did, their different products, their CEO (yes! Marc Benioff is really admired in the company. Look at some of his videos and get a gist of the values and things he focuses on) and try to incorporate their customer success stories (available on their website)
3. Had a long list of Salesforce-specific questions (helped in driving the first two interviews as they were supposed to clear our queries in them; also helpful to show that you have researched about the company). The questions can range from being conversational (asking the interviewer about his role and projects), about company CEO and values (the things they did in the past like the CEO wanting to pay more taxes to help homelessness in San Francisco), about the role (challenges in the role, expectations, responsibilities) to about recent company M&As
4. Be enthusiastic. Look positive. Smile. Be polite (even if they try to take a stress interview)
5. Answers aligned to the company values
6. Consistency in your answers (Don't lie. Like in my case, I did CFA and was the candidate for level 2, so I owned it. Told them I liked it but then followed up with a convincing argument about how I wanted to take up the role they offered)

Selected for the role.
dos_and_donts: Thoroughly go through their website like Investor relations PPT, their product offerings, customer success stories, blogs.

pre_process_tips: No pre-process as such. Profile was shortlisted and had a telephonic round before face to face interview. Moderate round for telephonic interview based on profile and knowledge about mergers and acquisitions.
no_interviews_duration: 3 rounds of Face to face interview including HR. First interview of around 75 minutes, others 15-20 minutes.
interview_outline:
First round- Started with about yourself, then understanding DDV(Deal Delivery Value)- IT and process of mergers and acquisitions. Role of IT due diligence in M&A. Case related to M&A and IT due diligence. Case was focused on how to deal with obsolete and legacy software of the target  company when you aim to acquire it and increase growth by 3 times in 1 year. Broad categories of IT due diligence checklist to cover risk in M&A and further delving deep into each category. Finding one time cost factor and recurring costs in terms of IT in M&A. Checklist  for data migration and lastly identifying if the objective of growth in 1 year will be met.
Second round- It was a director round. Was asked why DDV IT and why consultant. Profile based questions and a pricing case to be solved in 2-3 minutes. Case was to  come up with a price for gmail service if Google wants to monetize it.
Third round- It was an HR round. Questions based on profile and preferences. Walking through your resume, why pwc and similar other.
domain_questions: First round was most crucial. Past work experience was relevant and I could come up with suggestions from my experience. I tried to tell them  that I know about the M&A process and concepts like TSA, due diligence, integration, separation, SLA, Day 0, Day 1, Day 2. This gave him an idea that I have a basic understanding of M&A and IT part of it. He was noting them down in his laptop. Further  during case I tried to cover my answer following MECE approach and kept taking his feedback about whether I need to  cover any other aspect. It helped me as in some situations he said I have almost covered all points and sometimes he helped me to consider some points that I missed. I wrote every point and detail he provided in a structured way as he was looking and reading them all. Clarifying case situations and asking  for feedback at every analysis helped. In one or two situations he was not convinced with some points, instead of neglecting them I tried giving logical reasons behind them and he seemed to like that. Also asking a relevant question to him at the end of the interview was important. He was very much willing to answer.
hr_gk_questions: Questions like something about you, how your internship or work experience align with the role, why DDV IT, why consulting, why pwc. I had worked in two companies before MBA, so I was asked the reason to switch. The most important thing was  to come up with a different and innovative answer for why DDV  IT. The HR asked me not to come up with any generic answer like I have an IT experience so DDV IT. I tried to come up with three defining words for DDV IT , which were innovative, challenging and impactful and explain my reasons behind each by relating to importance of  IT in M&A and importance of technology in every sector. This worked and HR told me that she was impressed with the answer.
looking_for: IT knowledge, not the technical part but business part and SDLC awareness. Basic understanding of mergers and acquisition whole process and IT role in IT.  Communication and analyzing skills.
right_wrong:
Good part was that I told them what I know about process of M&A.I also tried to make the interview conversational and come up with logic for whatever I said.
One point that went wrong was that I missed one case fact told to me in the beginning since the case was very detailed. The interviewer ignored that mistake but it could have gone wrong.
tips: Reading about the JD and taking guidance from the buddy assigned by pwc helped a lot. Before interview I read 5-6 documents of Delloite, PWC, KPMG about M&A and IT role in it. Some important topics were due-diligence, integration, separation, Day 1 and digital transformation.
dos_and_donts: Be calm and confident, try to drive the interview in your direction.

gd_topics_tips:
Topics were abstract and general (eg. Live in vs. marrige, one night stand, etc.)
Value addition is important. Try to add new and valuable points even if you make few entries. Be calm and confident.
interview_outline:
2 people were there in the panel. It was a balanced interview. Started with introduction. Then they asked about my interest and future plans ( expect a lot of cross-questioning). Then they started with my resume. It was more of a discussion. They ended with the extensive travel requirements and how I perceive it. 
2nd interview was totally HR based. It was a Skype interview with the 2 directors of the company. They started with asking about the last interview, what happened and what I disliked about it. Then they started with my resume. At last, when asked for my questions, I said I already clarified them with the previous panel. It ended with them telling me about extensive travel required in the job and checking my willingness.
domain_questions:
PI1: I had done six sigma certification and taken TOC. They asked to explain what my understanding of these was. Then they asked me to apply TOC to Tata Steel ( previous work ex) and questioned every point I made. Then they gave a case - ' There a 2 machined in a plant - A and B. How will you improve their efficiency?' They just needed whether I ask all the necessary and relevant questions or not. 
They also checked knowledge of some basic concepts like efficiency and utilization. They looked satisfied with my answers. I forgot 1 important point during the case and they corrected me. I did not panic there and accepted my mistake by remaining calm.
hr_gk_questions:
PI1: They were checking my willingness to join the company and asked repeated questions on that. Eg. Why TOC, why consulting, etc.
PI2: I had a 999 profile and average profile here. There the asked reasons for this. Then they went on to ask if I had any disagreements or major arguments in my undergraduate college. I had no such incidence, but I said I can tell you such stories from my work ex and told them that incident. Same question was asked on my MBA college incidents.
Then they asked if I am a liked of hated person on campus, I gave a balanced answer with examples. 
They also asked if I have ever stood up for something or had any confrontations with my arthritis. I narrated the incidence.
Next questions were - how did I come to know about TOC? Learning and liking about the course? Why didn't you go to your other operations faculty to tell them about TOC and that they are wrong? I said that such things take time and we need to be patient with the people with conventional wisdom. That knowledge of the concepts is also important. The change needs to take place gradually. I explained by giving examples and they looked satisfied.
Next qu- What all I did to know more about the company after attending their PPT? What did I find out in my research? Etc. I had gone through their website and connected with them on LinkedIn, so it helped.
looking_for: They were looking for a genuine interest in the company and assertiveness. They check if you are a fit for the company. They need leadership qualities and managerial skills of handling people.
right_wrong:
I was honest and accepted my mistakes if I made any. I knew all the details of my projects and work ex. I was confident and calm and didn't panic at any situation. I don't think they disliked anything.
In the 1st interview I asked them- What do you think is the 'constraint' for your company? They looked impressed.
tips: They will go deeper in every question they ask. Know your resume in and out. Don't try to lie, they can sense it. Their website has huge resources and case studies, they are very helpful. Prepare NPAD questions thoroughly. Be calm and confident. If you stress, they will give you more.
dos_and_donts: Don't try to defend yourself too much. Accept your mistakes and go ahead. Be clear and precise.

pre_process_tips: Filling the form in the Reculta portal and another site which they will provide. No written test No GDs. Direct interview after resume shortlisting. 2 interviews
domain_questions: As I mentioned that I worked in Operations and in the Quality department, they asked me various questions relating to it. I had done  Greenbelt in six sigma so they asked me precisely on what is Kaizen, Six Sigma, an instance when you implemented Six Sigma, How you helped solve issues in the shopfloor using the theories you have read in operations.
hr_gk_questions: Prepare the NPAD questions well and know everything about the hobby you have mentioned. Questions like, Why MBA, Why you left the previous job if it was good and you liked it, What motivates you to be in Consulting. Prepare the JD well. One of the question asked to me was, " DID YOU READ THE JD, IF YES, HOW DO YOU THINK IT SUITS YOUR PROFILE" Scenario based question was asked to me, quoted as" there are 5 members in the team and all are having different views of a problem, you have to come to consensus in 5 min, how will you do so?
looking_for: As the role was of customers and operations consulting, they asked a lot of question related to the operations, how shopfloor works, how you have implemented what you learn, when it comes to working in a business setup. They look for the communication skills, ability to think with diverse perspective and the practical understanding of the subject matter.
right_wrong: They wanted me to answer my questions based on data and then take a decision on all activities and not just bluntly choosing options. Ability to interpret graphs and understanding the importance of data, speaking of instances when I interacted with customers were the things that impressed the interviewer. Converted both the rounds of Interview.
tips: Practice at least 30 to 40 cases and don't just read the case. Have the frameworks in mind but don't just memorize them blindly. As there were 2 unconventional cases, personally, I could not use any framework, Its just the knowledge that you have and your approach is being checked. I did not reach the solution to the 1st interview but yet selected for the 2nd one, as the preliminary questions and approach was being judged.
dos_and_donts:
Don't read the casebooks, solve them. 30 to 40 is enough, but don't just solve the case and close it, go through it again and analyze what went right and wrong and how it could have been better, focus on your thinking patterns and styles when ever you get a case.
ASK MORE AND MORE RELEVENT PRILIMINARY QUESTIONS. IT REALLY HELPS IN UNCONVENTIONAL CASES, FOR UNDERSTANDING AS WELL AS SOLVING THE CASE.

pre_process_tips: Filling Application form in PwC portal followed by shortlisting based on resume
no_interviews_duration: Three rounds of interview with 50 mins, 45 mins and 25 mins duration respectively
interview_outline: First round consisted of resume based questions, situational questions, domain knowledge questions and case interviews. Since I worked in Health domain before I was asked about my work experience in detail. Also, since I interned with PwC India, projects I did there were asked in detail along with the learnings. Few academic projects done in R were asked too. US health insurance sector knowledge was tested and case was also based on that. The case was to devise a strategy for selecting provider network for an insurance firm in US. It was followed by few situational questions which had to be answered related to experiences I had during my work experience. The second round was taken by Director at PwC. It was more of analysing your fit to the role and to the company. It had questions related to technical capabilities. I was asked about programming languages I am comfortable with. It had also situational questions to assess how well I fit to the role and organisation.  Third round was HR round where I was asked about my internship and work experience in detail followed by situational questions.
domain_questions: They expected me to know the industry I worked in. Also, it was expected to have some knowledge on US health insurance sector. It is not necessary that we need to know everything in detail. They help when we are unfamiliar with some technical terms. During the case interview,  I was asked the type of insurances, insurance sources, changes in the health insurance sector, value based health care, etc. Also, terminologies like providers, insured, co pay, co insurance, deductibles are expected to be known. Keeping on asking questions and getting clarification are the main things. Also, thinking out loud and in all possible directions would help
situational_questions: I had many situational questions across the rounds. Some of them were: 1) Share an instance where things were going wrong and you stepped in and you actually made it worse. What have you done wrong? What would you do now if you face a similar situation now? 2) Share an instance where things were going wrong and you stepped in and you actually improved it 3) Tell a situation during any phase of your life where you actually motivated someone to realise their potential and reach their dream
hr_gk_questions: 1) What would someone who likes you tell about you? 2) What would someone who hates you tell about you 3) Describe yourself in one sentence 4) Are you a team player or do you like to work Individually 5) What are your strengths and weaknesses 6) What are weak areas and how are you trying to improve those 7) Where do you see yourself in 5 years  8) What is your short and long term plans
looking_for: They were looking for someone who is fit for the role and the organisation. They had shortlisted those who had some previous experience in the health industry. They were looking at how effectively and structured I was able to communicate. Articulating thoughts clearly was important. Also, asking important questions and showing that you are genuinely interested in the work they are doing is important
right_wrong: Good part was that they were really helpful when I had been stuck at few points. Panicking is not at all desired. Talk freely and communicate effectively. Make the interview like a conversation rather than question answer session. Ask about the work they are doing and what do they expect us to do along with questions about US healthcare industry. Read about changes happening due to Presidency change or otherwise. Bad part was that I should have looked more into case frameworks. Cases can be combination of too much things. So solving some of the cases related to insurance sector would have been good
tips: Victor Cheng, ISB case book by prep com, experiences shared by previous batches, practicing guesstimates from external sources, studying and practising in friends’ circle helps in covering a lot in minimum time
dos_and_donts: Don’t panic at any time. Keep on asking questions and make the interview as interactive as possible

pre_process_tips: Application Form(You have fill your preference order of all the COEs floated along with the normal biodata. Recommend to go through the COEs and what the roles are about, dont want to work for a COE you dont want to. Talk with seniors), Round 1 - Aptitude Test (Strong LIDR calculation based questions), Round 2 - Mandatory Workshop (Not an eliminatory round. Just a session to give participants an idea about the case interview), Interview Round (Only one round, 20-40minutes, Senior Manager of the COE you chose in the preference would be taking the interview).
interview_outline:
First 20min HR Questions. Next 20min Case driven.
Greeting and some casual conversation, Introduction about himself-company-role, My Introduction, Some follow questions on Work-Life Balance based on my introduction, Case, Analysis, Recommendation, Nice meeting you-thank you.

Very Balanced with technical and HR.
domain_questions:
Why Consulting and Why Bain? (Align your interest, values to the company's values)
I spoke about how I aspire to be an individual who's versatile with his knowledge of various  industries and diverse sectors and how I put a lot of emphasis on making an impact with the work I do. This aligns with different types of consulting services provided by bain in different industries to businesses and governments and making substantial impact. Hence I want to be at bain. 

Market Entry Case -
An established personal care products company based in India for over 60+ years is looking for growth opportunities. Asked me what to do.

Started off with throwing some ideas like apparel industry, Food products etc. And asked if the client has any specific market in his mind. He told me to look into Baby Food. Put down some qualitative elements. Dived into numbers and market sizing. Showed him its an attractive market to enter. He grilled me about how baby food will suit the company's image of a personal care product company and the operational feasibility for a few minutes and took my recommendations
hr_gk_questions:
Introduce Yourselves - Add details about experience, graduation, social activities but also a personal tough, something that can be related to your core value system to make it more authentic. Every single answer should be structured but authentic. 

How would you manage work-life balance - Gave an honest answer by saying that I am a 21 year old with a premature understanding of it and what I think of it and what I understood about it from my peers and social circles and parents.

What is Work life balance for you - Gave an answer that goes along with my quality of having a proportionate amount social and work life.
looking_for: Someone who's interactive and keep the person engaged in a conversation. It was evident that he's looking for crisp and clear points but also a casual afternoon conversation. Did not really get into my resume. Just stuck to few standalone HR questions and dived right into a case.
right_wrong:
Right - The whole interview was a light casual conversation with no awkward pauses. I think The HR part went great and I could see a positive impact on him from the answers. 

Wrong - The ending part of the case went a little off and I had to take his help a couple of times when I got stuck. Could have been even more structured.
tips: I think being honest and having a casual conversation with him helped. It set a vibe for the interview. Always keep your answers structured. And be free in the interview. Dont be too uptight
dos_and_donts:
Do(s)
1) Prepare your NPAD well. 
2) Prepare answers to HR Questions and run them through peers, seniors. 
3) Take as many Mock PIs from seniors and friends as possible apart from the case prep.
4) Go through the company website, check their values and results and align your answers accordingly
5) Go through prepcom's guesstimate fact sheet and skim industry sector reports. Will e very handy if asked a question about an unaware industry

Dont(s)
1) Dont do cases on your own. Reading Casebooks wont help. You have to do cases with friends or peers in a one to one or group scenario.

pre_process_tips: Application
interview_outline: Intro, simple banking questions, general questions, asked me to ask a question
domain_questions: None, just stuff like "what do you like about finance"
hr_gk_questions: There weren't many questions like this. It was easy and I simply answered based on my NPAD and brain.
looking_for: Not being a complete degenerate I guess? They were easy on me and were basically just making sure that I wasn't a fraud and had some semblance of interest in their job.
right_wrong: Honestly it was as perfect as it gets. And I converted; this was the only interview I had.
tips: Having my NPAD prepared properly and reviewing a few other HR questions specific to me that weren't in the NPAD helped a lot. Anybody can do technical questions after studying, but the HR stuff is pretty personal and scary so I would recommend people to focus more on that than on remembering what the heck deferred tax is.
dos_and_donts:
Don't half-ass anything. And don't give up hope: if you're doing the rights you'll eventually get placed, and probably get something you like even if you are picky. PlaceCom knows what they're doing and have your back so relax and apply to everything you're eligible for.

Also make sure your resume is top-notch and ready ASAP. Also collect proofs for ALL POINTS ASAP and in their proper format: PlaceCom is super strict about this and even a 100% legitimate valid proof which does not meet their exact specifications WILL BE REJECTED AND YOU WILL NOT BE ABLE TO ADD YOUR POINT. 1-2 points that you know are true might get rejected for this reason and that's ok: they have to do this to make sure that lies don't creep into people's resumes. And make sure you fill a page and 70-80% of each line otherwise getting shortlists is hard (Resume plays a huge role in getting shortlists). And try to do some easy, short online certificate courses and such before arriving on campus so you have a few points and proofs to add to your resume (Believe me, filling 1 page is pretty damn hard - even for those whom IIM Indore deemed good enough to admit - so don't be at all overconfident about this).

And don't half-ass the NPAD either, as long, difficult, and potentially useless as it may seem at first. It is easy to slack off on it as it isn't checked as much and obviously isn't submitted during applications, but trust me, without it you will get destroyed during HR questions, which in my view are far more nerve-wracking than technical questions. But if you sit down for a while and do it sincerely, properly and thoughtfully, your interviews (and even some applications) will be far less painful as you WILL NOT have time to do your NPAD during placement week. Just make sure to review your NPAD before interviews - even a quick skim can help a lot if you've made it well and right.

Oh, and a lot of what PlaceCom does will irritate you but don't act on it. You're here to get placed, not irritated, and getting on their wrong side will only hurt your chances of achieving your goal. Don't be afraid of them and simply do as they say. PlaceCom people are way nicer than they might seem at first so if you're good them they'll reciprocate it, trust me. It's easy to forget but they're also students and humans just like you (and they don't get thanked enough for all their hard work I might add). Also keep checking your email as much as you possibly can during Term I. You'll also have 11 PM meets and stuff so know that it will hurt and balancing that with so much academics and 9 AM classes will be a massive challenge. But DO NOT SKIP CLASSES because you'll barely get time to study this term so if you don't pay attention in class then you're beyond screwed. Brace yourself, live one day at a time, and just know that when you finally get placed, it will all be worth it.

pre_process_tips:
1. Resume Shortlist:There was first a resume shortlist. My profile was very media and socially driven- two social internships and 4 PORs mostly dealing with media (social media strategy, content management, engagement strategies etc). 
2. Psychometric Fit/ Expectations : A short was to be filled with preferences and basic details. Try to stay open to options in rural India and working longer days 
3. Virtual Interview : This round was consisted of more general and HR related questions, which needed to be presented creatively. They were timed to be one minute long. Tip: Try to follow the STAR methodology to make answers crisp, go through NPAD
gd_topics_tips:
The GD topic for my process was as follows : Is the banning of Chinese apps the right step or not. 
I took a stance against the topic. Tip : It is best to try and stand out in some way. For instance, whilst going against the topic I mentioned the need to recognize the biases that come from our own government by highlighting the extensive use of WhatsApp campaigns in the 2014 and 19 elections. This prompted the interviewers to ask if I was passionate about politics in my Personal Interview.
interview_outline:
The interview was HR and Resume heavy. 
It started out with questions such as what am I passionate about, details of projects in my resume and the courses that I had taken during my under graduation. They also asked me a few technical questions, such as the difference between sales and marketing, and a  favorite campaign and why. 
The interview was fairly conversational and one needs to present points that are not directly asked to keep the conversation going.
domain_questions:
Not very technical questions were asked directly. 
When they asked me anything campaign or brand related I tried to use some marketing jargon whist justifying the points. 
I went through Kotler's summary or the Marketing Compendium besides noting a favorite campaign (and even picking a favorite campaign in a particular genre of campaigns). I went through a lot of campaign examples to see what really goes into making a successful campaign- more nuanced understanding of market research, whether it be direct or indirect. I also extensively went through the company's work, including future prospective/ plans and CSR
hr_gk_questions:
I was asked the following questions that were HR based : 
1. What are you passionate about 
2. What is your dream company 
3. Why marketing 

These formed the crux of all the HR questions. My approach was basically to introduce a new thing I did with every questions asked, to keep the conversation going. So when asked about what I am passionate about, I mentioned my internships (which were consequently asked about). When answering "why marketing", I highlighted my POR experiences. 

My approach was to be candid and frank, and not too frigid. The interview was not extremely formal, as they are looking for a cultural fit mostly and hence I believe they wanted to make it as conversational as possible. I even cracked a few jokes (they laughed, so I am guessing the jokes were good? Fingers crossed :P)
looking_for: They were looking for someone who had good communications skills and was enthusiastic. I do not think they were looking for prior experience or even knowledge, they wanted someone who made an effort with things they were interested in. Having said that, if that "interest" is somewhere in the circle of marketing- that's obviously a plus.
right_wrong:
What went wrong : 
I was not clear on one of my answers. I was asked why I wanted to do marketing since I had a very socially driven profile. I was asked the question again, after answering it once, when the interviewer said he was not convinced with my answer. 

What went right : 
I was myself. I think the interviewers gave me the space to respond and talk in a very candid way, and I think that made me more comfortable and hence confident.
tips:
- Marketing Compendium 
- Kotler Summary 
- Real life examples of different marketing strategies 
- Favorite brand, why, best campaigns, their impact

pre_process_tips:
Stage 1- 
Psychometric Test- Behavioral and Situational (Leadership and Personality related) questions

Stage-2- (Only after passing stage 1)
Gamification Test-  Various kinds of games related to aptitude, situations, reasoning etc. were asked. It had 3 sets as below-
a) Grid Challenge- Memory based puzzles that check short-term memory. For eg. you will be shown a grid of dots with one dot highlighted, it will disappear immediately and you have to recall it quickly. You have to remember 2-5 dots positions and the order of their appearances. Difficulty increases with the level. 
b) Switch Challenge- It checks logical reasoning. You will be presented with two rows of symbols with an operator between them changing their order. Your goal is to choose which operator will match the upper row with the lower row.
c) Digit Challenge- You will be presented with a basic numeric equation containing a predefined answer, empty spaces, and operators. Your task is to find the combination of digits that will correct the equation. Difficulty increases with the level.

Note:- You won't be able to apply for any role offered by P&G for 1 year if you fail in stage-1
interview_outline:
Round-1 (35 min.)-
1 interviewer (Female)
The interviewer gave her introduction and then asked for mine.
Then it went into behavioral NPAD-related questions. Total 8-9 questions were asked. Some of them are mentioned below-
Interviewer- Describe an instance where you wanted something and went out of your comfort zone to achieve it.
Interviewer- Describe an incident where you suggested an out-of-the-box solution and were appreciated for the results.
Interviewer- Explain a situation where you took up something beyond your primary area of responsibility 
Me- Related all answer with work experience.
Finally, she asked me if I had any question.

Round-2 (45 min.)-
2 interviewers (both male)
The interviewer gave their introduction and then asked for mine.
Behavioral questions were asked. For e.g. Describe a conflict (situation) at your workplace, Share the details of one of your key projects, Describe an instance when you gave a unique solution for a problem etc. Total 6-7 behavioral questions were asked.
Heavy cross-questioning in every question, like how did you came up with this idea, what were the implications, why it was not done before etc.
Then 3-4 situational questions were asked. For e.g. You have recently joined an organization and everyone in your team is experienced. What will you do if you got an idea which will benefit the whole organization but nobody is interested in listening to you? etc.
Cross questioning in situational questions also.
Then few marketing-related questions related to STP, Type of distribution channels, favorite Ad etc. were asked.
Finally, they asked me if I had any question. So I asked that weather projects in internship would be given by my choice or as per the company requirements.
domain_questions:
Marketing-related questions related to STP, Type of distribution channels, favorite Ad were asked.

right_wrong:

pre_process_tips:
After the shortlisting process, a buddy was assigned to us and they conducted a workshop across B-schools. (I don't think either of these was evaluative). 
Post that we had a timed simulation game, which included puzzles.
interview_outline:
The first two interviews were purely case interviews. 
The last two interviews, which were partner rounds, were HR heavy and the questions revolved mostly around my workex. They asked a lot of behavioral questions and asked me to solve a case on how would I give consultancy to my previous company to help my former company double their market share. 
The partner rounds were more like a conversation than an interview.
situational_questions:
1. Instance where you had to make a tough decision or choice: 
I talked about a situation where I had to handle my company's multiple initiatives and decided to prioritize one over others to which my boss had some reservations. 
(They were looking for a candidate who can evaluate what would be the best for the company/client and take decisions, kind of like focussing on 80/20 ) 

2. Instance where you took some initiative: 
I described a time where I came with a new business idea for a potential client (Cement manufacturer) that involved signing an MoU with our company (HPCL) and getting their hundreds of transporters on board with us. The interviewer asked me to elucidate on how I executed the idea and what results I could get.
(They were looking for an instance where you thought something out of the box and then owned up the initiative to ensure final execution. They were as much interested in results as the idea.)

3. Did you ever deal with an unsatisfied client: 
(They were looking for how would you handle clients who disagree with you) 

4. Instance where you had a disagreement with your superiors: 
Described an instance where I and my boss wanted me to pursue different clients and how I convinced my boss that my idea was for the betterment of the region in the long run. 
(They were looking for your skills to reason with a superior and how did you manage to convince them) 

5. Something you did differently in any existing project: Narrated on how I managed to boost our market share by understanding what exactly our customers wanted. 
(They were looking for how did you bring new perspective, which helped in improving results.)
hr_gk_questions:
Tell me about yourself : 
(Try to keep it under 90 seconds and insinuate a particular interesting skill or incident so that they ask follow-up questions on that. Narrating education, work experience, internship in chronological order is a strict NO.)
looking_for:
How well can you handle different stakeholders (leadership)
Unique/ Creative ideas (Entrepreneurial skills)
Ability to structure and communicate things effectively
An eye for identifying problems and suggesting solutions
right_wrong:
I think my client-facing role and my experience in implementing new initiatives helped in having a conversation.
Other than that, trying to think of different possibilities while solving each case went right for me. Interviewer also liked how I linked the case at hand with the present trends going on in the industry. 

What I could have done better : I missed considering the HR aspects of the firm in a case.

Result : Selected
tips: Solving different types of cases across multiple industries will help a lot. For prep, casebooks and materials sent by the prepcom would suffice.
dos_and_donts:
McKinsey focuses more on quantitative skills, so it would be better to practice cases which are quantitatively based. (Foreign case books like NYU Stern and Darden might be useful)

General Dos: 
Keep the interviewer included in your thought process, so that in case you are stuck, he/she might be able to help you.
Keep the structure as MECE as possible. Always check with the interviewer if you have missed anything.
It is always good if you can throw in some qualitative insights in addition to the data-driven inferences.

Don'ts: 
You can ask for a minute to gather your thoughts but don't ask for time too frequently and keep it limited to 60 seconds.

pre_process_tips:
(1) Filling application form on Reculta and website
(2) Nautics assessment - game based simulation assessment wherein they check if your values match to that of theirs. Various situations are given in form of a story and you have to give solutions like what you would do if you were put in the situation. Its basically a psychometric test, so no answer is right or wrong, but choose wisely because they see the fitment of yours in their company.
(3) PI - Very few shortlisted candidates from the Nautics round. If you make it through that, which I did, then interviews are pretty good if you are thorough and prepared with your NPAD. Simple questions and also a case given to solve at the moment, to analyze and provide marketing solutions to the same, basically providing strategy as solution since the role was strategy related. I got selected and final offer.
interview_outline: Started with introduction, questions about why to join this company and why are you interested in the role, questions about self and HR based, Case analysis (20 mins), some more questions about self. It was more of a HR heavy interview. Case analysis part was bit technical.
domain_questions: Question asked as to why interested for this strategy and marketing role in the company. So, my approach was to first introduce personal aspects to the answer like what motivated me to apply for this role, then the short-term goals with example. Some background knowledge about self and company which would be suitable for the role. Then how can I bring new ideas to the table. Explained for about 10 minutes. The 2 panelists were thoroughly impressed with the answers, so no cross-questioning.
hr_gk_questions: HR questions basically revolved around the similar NPAD questions, out of box thinking situations, overcoming challenges examples, strengths and weaknesses. Basically my approach to strength and weakness question was not directly jumping to one liners, rather describing a situation in my life, so that the panelists can draw insights so what are my strengths and weaknesses. I must say that approach did help a lot to convert into the final offer. No current affairs.
looking_for: They were looking for a individual who can work efficiently under stressful situation, who can handle things without panic, and has some knowledge regarding marketing. Also importantly they were looking for ones who perfectly blends with company core values so that there is a synergy between the individual and working in the company. The basic concepts should be clear and they pay a great deal of attention to the approach of solving a case. Even though you don't reach a solution, approach is what matters, like your thinking process and direction of moving forward. That helped me sail through and convert this interview.
right_wrong: The best part of the interview was that I spoke very confidently of whatever I knew with all honesty. When you tell lies, you stammer, but it was not in my case. They liked my answers and my approach to answer their questions. It was more interactive than a interview perspective. There was no drawback in the interview process. The panelists were cheerful and supportive as well, as one would want their interviewers to be.
tips: Your honest approach to answer questions with full confidence is what matters and helped me. Nervousness kills your confidence and that clearly is seen when you are not sure of what to tell. So, always take some moments to think before you speak. Also, do a bit of self-introspection before the PI, so that you know what are you good at and always be confident. I was really happy to convert the first process itself. This PI was my first PI in summers and I converted in the first attempt only. So, one good PI and you are done.
dos_and_donts: No specific preparation. Be thorough in NPAD and as mentioned earlier, boost your confidence levels, for that practice speaking. Communication is a very important aspect in any PI, and if you deliver the better, the better results you get.

pre_process_tips: We had the usual reculta application. After that we had a 25-30 min online assessment which mostly was aptitude and puzzle solving.
