No structure for GD but the panelists stepped in and made sure everyone got to speak. 

I think my coherent, simple points and clarity of thought helped clear the GD round.
interview_outline: Interview was largely HR based. They asked a few questions from my resume to start off, but then it quickly moved into my interests, strengths, and possible company fit. I was asked multiple questions about handling stressful scenarios and new situations. Being practiced with NPAD helped a lot. We often went on tangents. The main point was how someone like me (from a science background) could contribute to a marketing role.
domain_questions: They asked me a bit about what I expected to do at Titan. I answered honestly based on my interests. They corrected some misconceptions I had about the role, and helped me understand different possible marketing related roles. They mainly wanted to understand if my strengths/weaknesses were a good fit for my dream role.
hr_gk_questions: A lot of questions on my interests were asked, I was pretty confident about these. Can't remember any current affairs questions, they were more interested in how I would deal with new situations and handle sticky problems. NPAD prep I can't reiterate enough.
looking_for: My clarity of thought and role fit were the main things they were looking for, from what I could see. They barely asked technical questions, but wanted to see my readiness to adapt. Marketing knowledge basics were useful, but mostly to shape my answers to best show my skills. My repeated focus on being a problem solver (science background) helped solidify my case.
right_wrong:
Converted the interview. What worked: My sense of humor and confident answers were key to me making it through. I managed to convey my belief and clarity of thought in my answers. The humor worked for this panel because I got the vibe that they were friendly.

What could have been better: I could have answered with more fluency on the sticky question of why marketing and not consulting. I improvised on the spot, but prior NPAD thinking would have helped.
tips:
Marketing Compendium shared by Mercur-I plus some YT videos from IITs helped gain solid grasp of basics. Mock GDs and PIs gave me a sense of confidence that I could pull this off. The NPAD preparation was one of the largest factors.

Talk with your seniors, they are the best source of help and guidance. I spoke with the seniors I met at the advanced Domain Session, of Marketing. Their first-person information about where to spend my energies and what worked for them helped a lot! They helped me gain mastery of interview-relevant skills in a short span of time, and focus on the important bits of marketing knowledge.
dos_and_donts:
Dos: 1. Know marketing basic terms early on. 2. Talk with seniors who have worked at your preferred role. There are no stupid questions to ask them (I've done that). 3. "Know Thy NPAD". 4. Stay up to date with latest trends in industry/ the world, at least on a surface level.

Don'ts: Over-prepare/go too deep in one rabbithole of marketing knowledge. Better to cover more ground and know its IRL applications, than to go deep into one niche.

Company specific prep: Wasn't very required except at a surface level in my case. All cramming done on the day of the interview, with the help of slides shared by Titan from PPT. Google searches, of course, did the rest of the prep. Learnt as much as I could about their recent developments + business trends.

pre_process_tips: The process consists of a workshop (around 200+ people attended, wasn't evaluative), applying on their JPMC portal, aptitude test (finance, logical reasoning, basic math, verbal). Shortlist was released and then GD and interviews (can be technical, HR or mixed)
gd_topics_tips: GD was conducted for all the candidates shortlisted. Our topic was: "Which sectors are more resilient through the business cycle and why". They were looking for example-backed arguments and using financial terms as part of the discussion. While GD was ongoing, they were scanning through the resumes.
no_interviews_duration: 1 or 2 (Depends upon candidate). The 1st interview was typically technical and could last for 20-40 mins
interview_outline: The technical interview was brief for me. Started off with a 1 min personal introduction, why finance, what roles are you looking for in the finance domain. I was asked what did I learn from the workshop and what WCR analysts do. Then they had a look at my CV, picked a company (it was in the IT sector) and asked how will you analyse credit-worthiness of this company? They asked about key differences between IT sector and heavy manufacturing sector, as well as my opinions on the GD topic. Then I was asked about 2 key economic events that are plaguing the world (I explained the effects of Russia-Ukraine conflict and global inflation hikes). They went deep into the inflation issue: asked what is inflation, what is repo rate, implications of high repo rate, why is India having high inflation. Lastly they asked how banks make money and is high repo rate good or bad for banks. At the end, they asked if I had any questions for them. This was my only interview. Some other candidates had an additional short HR interview, some candidates were asked more technical finance questions in their interviews.
domain_questions:
1. The finance technical questions for my PI was very limited. A basic understanding of credit analysis (revise workshop notes) should be sufficient. Do current affairs well and if possible, push some hot credit topics into your answers. 

2. They were expecting us to know about the role expectations in detail. Be very prepared with the role position in the firm and have the JD at your fingertips. Since my PI was just after the GD, I didn't have much time to prepare for the JD related questions, so that could have been a setback. Normally, don't say anything completely off-putting or wrong about the JD. If you don't know about a specific thing about the role, don't make it up, just say you'll look into it, and if possible ask the interviewers that point when they expect questions from your side.
hr_gk_questions:
1. HR Questions: why finance? (this is an underrated question, but this question can be a trendsetter for how your entire PI will progress) Prepare template answers and tweak them as required. Have convincing backing. Don't be under-confident to prove you are a good fit. 

2. Current affairs included Major macroeconomic events and other bank specific happenings. Follow one business newspaper closely.
looking_for: If your profile is good, they weren't asking tough finance questions if your background isn't in eco/fin. For Eco/fin students, you can expect deep questions. Confidence, way of speaking, attitude towards the role and being candid mattered a lot. Don't have long pauses in between answers, be spontaneous and direct. Don't push random finance terms just to globe or appear knowledgeable. The PI would go very differently based on your profile.
right_wrong: Converted JPMorgan (WCR) after the 1st interview. I could have prepared for the role specific questions better. Nothing went wrong during the interview. They were quite lenient if I looked lost after a question. Be confident throughout and own your CV. PLEASE craft your 1 min introduction well (from your childhood to MBA chronologically, not vice versa).
tips: Confidence, being short and crisp in answers, being candid on what I didn't know
dos_and_donts: Prepare 'Why Finance' and '1 min intro' VERY WELL. They can change the entire PI. Follow one business newspaper closely (both global and Indian happenings)

pre_process_tips: No pre-process, direct resume shortlisting
gd_topics_tips:
Topic: Amazon vs Flipkart
Pattern: Everyone was given a minute to first express their points and then the stage was open for discussion. Around 10 minutes was the discussion time and one person was asked to summarize the GD. The entire GD lasted for about 25 minutes.
Key Selection Criteria: It was a very open ended discussion. Multiple viewpoints were put. Selection criteria was mostly the uniqueness of the points (as points became repetitive after sometime ) and the quality rather than the quantity.
interview_outline:
Interview 1: Started with the introduction of the interviewer. 
Asked questions about the points I had mentioned in the GD. Asked me questions about the profitability of Flipkart pre and post Walmart. How Amazon was turning into a much bigger umbrella than e-commerce and why or why could not Flipkart replicate the same. 
The second part of the interview was mostly internship related. I had interned at HSBC in the digital products division. Asked me questions on the products, target audience, market share of those products, KPIs and other parameters I had used during internship.
Questioned me about product management. What idea I had about the role, what other responsibilities a project manager might have, the type of costs a product person should have in mind and some questions about lifetime value of a customer (what it means and why/ why not a product manager should be concerned about it). 
Question to the interviewer: Horizontal structure in products in MMT

Interview 2: Started with basic introduction. What my family does, how do people know me, my hobbies and so on. Then I was asked some mini cases on new product development, for e.g., what would you design to keep your team enagaged in CSR activities throughout the year, what are the current gaps in the travel industry and what changes can be done to the existing products to stop the gap. 
Question to the Interviewer: What aspects of product development would we be working on rightaway?

Overall, both the interviews were balanced. Even though I had practiced guesstimates and cases, the interviews were more conversational and they wanted to understand how the interviewee was thinking or answering even basic questions.
domain_questions:
1. What is product Management and what are the responsibilities of a product manager. (try not to give definitions but what you actually understand from it. I had answered that a product is a product manager's baby and everything starting from the inception to revenue generation to re-inventing the product is the product manager's responsibility)
2. How to evaluate user experience of an app
I had mentioned several parameters including UI, fonts, alignment, no. of clicks, attention ratio, time spent on each page, no. of pages needed to navigate, etc.
hr_gk_questions:
HR questions:
1. What do people know you as? (in school, undergrad and at IIM Indore)
2. How did Undergrad change you?
3. Tell us something about your family
looking_for: Ingenuity, Interest, Knowledge of the profile and what work is to be done
right_wrong: I think my eagerness and interest in the role was clearly visible to the interviewers which worked in my favour. My entire resume is full of digital and creative internships so my interviews were more like conversations rather than proper interviews. Even when I could not answer a couple of questions, I promptly let them know that I was out of my depth and they appreciated it.
tips: I did not attend mock PIs or GDs but the mocks during my summer placements time did help. Mock PIs are important. Make sure to practice in front of your friends so that your thoughts get some structure and you do not get lost while speaking.
dos_and_donts:
1. Make sure you have done your homework about the company. 
2. Always remember the names of the people you are interviewing with.
3. Don't fake or beat around the bush. They did appreciate honest answers.

pre_process_tips: Resume screening, Two telephonic interviews followed by final in-person interview.
no_interviews_duration: 2 telephonic interviews (20 minutes and 40 minutes) and final interview (25 minutes)
interview_outline:
Both telephonic interviews were extremely technical heavy. Began with tell me about yourself and dig deeper into finance related questions. Heavy focus on derivatives and risk mitigation strategies. Lots of questions related to financial ratios and their interpretations. Case study based questions to test my apporach. Why the company, Why credit risk, what did I understand from the company PPT. Do you have any questions for us? 

Final interview was focused on my resume. I had to explain my academic projects in depth (my projects were from the economics domain so seemed relevant to the interviwer), skills in R software MS Excel, whether I can do a similar project for the automobile industry in APAC and what variables would I consider. There were lot of questions as follow-ups to what i said. About the company, about my understanding of what the role entails, explain some financial ratios for credit risk analysis, explain DCF valuation.
domain_questions: Lot of questions were finance domain specific. Derivatives and Financial ratios were asked in great depth. Company related questions were on the surface level to gague genuine interest in the role and company.
hr_gk_questions: None. Just self introduction at the start of each interview round. Make the introduction engaging, show academic merit as well as initiatives you took to apply concepts in the real world (via projects/internships). Portray your financial and technical skills well. Stay calm and confident and pitch your profile as if you're having a conversation with them. Follow-up questions will be based on what you say. Then they will move on to core finance. Current affairs questions were minimal for me but it is heavily dependent on fate as some of my friends were grilled on current news and financial gk.
looking_for: Someone who understands both the quantitative as well as qualitative risk well and can connect different aspects of credit risk with financial markets. They were mainly looking for people with sound financial knowledge and confidence to answer the questions clearly and comprehensively.
right_wrong:
Converted the interviews. 

Right - Prior CFA L1 certification - Brushed up CFA concepts before the interview which helped me cover the technical questions well. Confidence was key. Quick on the spot thinking and a very good all rounded profile with extra curriculars like data analytics also helped. The final interview went extremely well as I was able to build a rapport with the interviewer and have an engaging discussion where he also pitched in different perspectives. I was calm and took few minutes whenever I needed to frame my thoughts coherently. 

Wrong - since the telephonic interviews were an absolute surprise I didn’t have time to look up the company beforehand so my answers to “why GS” were quite generic. However it didn’t impact the overall flow of the interview, since i was able to convince them. It is advisable to be specific and give particular examples/company policies/names mentioned during the PPT to frame your answers better and show genuine interest in the company and role.
tips:
Prepcom fin materials, basic CFA knowledge (read through derivatives, fixed income, equity related concepts from Kaplan Schweser secret sauce or IFT notes). There is absolutely no way you can globe in GS interviews. 
Vendor mock GD/PIs helped to show me my shortcomings and boosted my prep due to panic of under-preparedness.
dos_and_donts: Since the phone calls are unpredictable and random, be prepared with core finance early on. Prepare questions to ask them beforehand (especially for the telephonic interviews). Keep your answers short and clear. Do not try to globe, but rather let them know that you are unsure of the answer but would apporach the case in XYZ manner. They are not looking for hard and fast formulae to be memorised, rather an overall understanding of credit risk. Support your answers with examples from current affairs in the macro-economic or business environment.

pre_process_tips: It was a resume based shortlisting, followed by Aptitude test of 75 Min. . First round was the case presentation which was given to me the previous day. Next round was resume based/technical interview. Final round
interview_outline: After getting shortlist for the PI round, I was given a case the night before my interview and I had to send the solution within 3hrs. (Case: Build a strategy for opening a data science training institute like Jigsaw academy, or coursera etc). Sent the solution within 3 hrs. Appeared for interview next day. First round was case interview, more inclined towards the case and went on for 1+ hr. It started with short introduction and there was a lot of discussion involved about each point I mentioned in solution. Second round was resume based interview where a lot of technical questions was asked related to machine learning(because I had put machine learning courses in resume),  marketing and few questions on my undergrad project based on Machine Learning.
domain_questions: First question was What is Machine Learning and how it is impacting the world. I answered as it is something in which machine is trained to learn and recognise something next time when it encounter the same. I tried to explain with an example. Amazon echo when first launched had a small dictionary of words. it could not understand various words but when people started talking to it it learnt that words itself by constantly updating it's dictionary. This is called machine learning. How is
situational_questions: I was asked about how will you communicate the insights you get from data to the clients. Give an example
hr_gk_questions: After that I appeared for Hr interview. I was asked questions like Why do you want a firm which operates i quite niche segment like pharma?. Why Axtria and not other firms?. Are you comfortable in coding? where do you see yourself in next few years?
looking_for: They were looking for people who could solve a case with the data. The case that was given to me was to open a company and do financial projections. The interviewer grilled me on the data and whether the data was making any sense. On the general note they looked for confident people because it is a client side role
right_wrong:
I solved the case very judiciously and it worked in. my favor. I made a good impression by attaching the google sheet link of financials in the Appendix and the interviewer was impressed by my efforts. 
One thing which went wrong was a point in my presentation which did not seem reasonable. I was grilled on the single point for 10 min
tips: I started with the first year courses. I revised every course in 2-3 hours. I did only basics of those courses. Then for my electives in my second year i did a thorough study and for few courses from them I did very deep preparation ( this was to answer the question, which is your fav subject?) . We made a group of 15 people to do the GDs. Everyday 10 people would turn up and we would discuss the recent topics. Also we took mock interviews of each other among our friends( believe me it helps a lot)
dos_and_donts: In the case write each and every point with justification in your mind. Dont just write anything. since only 3 hrs is given for case you can take help of friends. Practice presentation 2-3 times. Since time was very less it is suggested to keep a template for ppt and just fill in the data in that template. Building ppt from scratch would take a lot of time. Be confident in interview. If asked about can you do coding? it is advisable to say yes if you have coding background and if not you can say I can learn it and then can do it. All the best!

role_offered: Summer Intern - Management Consulting in Financial Services
pre_process_tips: There was an application form on Superset. It only asked for personal details, education details, work experience, etc., and no HR questions. There were no screening tests and no pre-submissions.
interview_outline:
First interview - The Panelist gave his introduction and asked me about my Introduction (Tell me about yourself). Some follow-up questions were asked based on my answer. After this, I was given a case (Your client is Govt. of Nepal and wants to increase digital transactions in the country) and after completing the case, sir asked a guestimate to solve (No. of cars currently plying on roads of Delhi). After this, sir asked, "Why do I want to join this role coming from a chemistry background and how would I rate my knowledge about the banking and Insurance industry on a scale of 1-10 (told about my interest in consulting and finance and how the role is fulfilling both of them, rated my self as 8/10 for banking and 6/10 for Insurance). The link for case and guestimate transcript - https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1--S6lYEHn15b9HoLu4biNqgaw-xHngLh/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=102516412535754103693&rtpof=true&sd=true
Second Interview - The panelist gave her introduction and asked me about my Introduction (Tell me about yourself). Some follow-up questions were asked based on my answer and family business like will I join my business or not, if not why, etc. Post this, ma'am asked an ethical dilemma question - 5 companies have approached PwC India for advice and we have identified 5 factors causing the problem for them. There are two approaches to solve. However, if the first approach is followed, 3 out of 5 companies would benefit but 2 will suffer a loss, while on the other hand, if the second approach is followed, those 2 companies would benefit but the other 3 would suffer a loss. You (me) are leading a team for the second approach and another team of PwC India is working on the first approach. What will you do as if you work well, the other team will tend to lose. My answer - I will diligently fulfill my responsibilities since I have the responsibility of my team members. I must perform effectively, as any shortcomings on my part would have adverse consequences for the collective performance of the team. Additionally, I believe that the second team will likewise make their utmost effort, as both teams are dedicated to the organization and undoubtedly aspire to contribute to its success. Therefore, I shall diligently undertake the assigned task, utilizing my utmost abilities.
Third Interview - The panelist gave her introduction and asked me about my Introduction (Tell me about yourself). It was mainly a conversation to ask some hygiene questions, e.g., whether I have any problem with relocation and others that were asked in the application form.
domain_questions: During my interview, Panelist asked, "Why do I want to work with PwC India". I answered this question based on my understanding of the firm with insights from their website. No major domain-specific question was asked apart from the case and guestimate.
hr_gk_questions: No major questions were asked from the resume. In both interviews, panelists asked only follow-up questions on Tell me about yourself.
looking_for: I myself being a fresher can say that there was not any expectation related to work ex and for certifications also. Be as true as you can in your responses. Apart from this, having good problem-solving skills is more than sufficient.
right_wrong: My Introduction answer was well framed and it helped me set a launch pad for a good interview. I tried my best to remain true to myself and responded in a way that I believed was right. I could have solved the guestimate in a slightly better way.
tips: If you are looking for a consulting job, it is essential to practice solving case studies and guestimates. These skills are crucial for success in consulting roles. The consulting casebooks helped me along with the PrepCom domain sessions.

gd_topics_tips: GD started by asking us to introduce our name and passion. Topic was "Whether work from home is blurring the line between work and life". The panel was looking for relatable points and they also expected candidates to listen to others too. I was asked in between GD to contradict another person's view. In the end of GD they asked each male candidates to say, how work from home had made females life easier and vice versa
interview_outline: It was mostly HR based. They didnt even ask about anything about my resume except my top 5 percentile in SM part. I wasnt even asked tell me about yourself question, they directly began the interview by asking what went wrong in my GD performance (I had extended shortlist from GD group as all previous 3 candidates from my GD were rejected)
domain_questions:
How will you strategise the way forward for Indian IT industry? (Since I mentioned put top 5 percentile in SM-1 and SM-2);
I mentioned how Indian IT industry is service based and should shift to product based or consulting based to get high margin. I also mentioned how all service based projects are at a risk of being replaced by AI/ML and high skill projects are need of the hour

How comfortable are you in Excel and powerpoint on a scale of 10? 
I answered 6 or 7 score only, and answered how I improved my presentation skills through my internships and live projects

How will you sell Wipro's digital solutions to your college admission assuming they don't have any IT knowledge? Factors you will ask them as a consultant?
I was able to link the knowledge gained from digital transformation and inbound sales course I did and used CGP TCP BA framework to list down the factors
situational_questions:
If you want to leave Wipro now but asked to wait 6 more months what will you do? 
I explained how I will stay if I have a project at hand and I am needed in that. I also explained I will leave if I had set my mind after fulfulling my commitments, since staying would not be fair to myself as well as to Wipro

Favorite football club? Favorite player? What characters you like in Messi? Is Messi a team player, why does good players underperform when messi is in the team? Is it right for him to foul a player and get that red card? Is it right for Barca to hold him back when he wanted to leave? Is board right not to allow him leave? Is messi reacting violently due to the frustrations on Barca board?
(I had mentioned football in interest section of resume and had said it as passion during my GD)
I was able to link all the above questions with an organizational perspective
hr_gk_questions:
How you handled free riders in my groups in college life? How will I handle the same in Wipro?

You always seem serious? Do you have any funny moments in your life?
looking_for: They were looking for someone who they can easily make an intellectual conversation with. They also expected simple honest answers and didn't want any structured or exaggerated answers
right_wrong:
Right:
Honesty in saying to interviewers about how I became a bit aggressive in my GD and exposing my weakness in my Excel skills and showing an intent to learn
Knowledge of Indian IT industry landscape by following current affairs and through CTC course discussion

Wrong:
Being a bit aggressive in GD and not listening properly to others
tips: HR questions preparations helped to handle the behavioral questions. Thorough resume preparation helped me link my 2 certifications in inbound sales and digital transformation to what was asked in interview
dos_and_donts:
Do' s - Be honest, treat PI it as a two way interaction 
Don't s - Too much structured and templated answers

pre_process_tips: Initial shortlist and two back to back interviews
interview_outline: First interview was almost like LRDI round and questions were just puzzles and some personal background questions, second interview was case study like where they asked me to think about factors to consider while launching or designing a product and how to measure its success.
domain_questions:
How to access a product's financial feasibility. I was asked to list down all the benefits and costs of launching or developing a product. 

I listed the benefits as primary revenue, secondary effect on other product lines, publicity and increased customer lifecycle. 

Costs were RnD, manufacturing, marketing with HR costs considered inside each vertical. 

Another question was about how to measure success of such project and I had to use knowledge of the app traffic analytics like interactions, clicks and all that.
hr_gk_questions: I was asked to tell something about myself and I explained my life choices very confidently and was unapologetic about field changes. 'Why MBA?' is always going to be present in these interviews and you should be absolutely ready for that.
looking_for: Thinking outside the box, someone able to manage all aspects of launching new products and think critically.
right_wrong:
I was little confused over one of the puzzle and it went in wrong direction. I was able to salvage the situation by explaining my reasoning and ultimately saying I was constrained by some of terms of the problem.

In first interview, I was constantly asking for more clarification about puzzles and giving trivial outside the box answers, so he would have to explicitly state the conditions to make the puzzle actually a challenge. That also allowed me to think about the particular puzzle for longer time.

In second interview, I was not explaining my answers very well in some instances, but I answered 80/90% right. When she revealed aspects of the problems I missed, I tried to explain how I covered them in other categories, but did not make excuses for things I clearly missed.
tips: I was down with corona and couldn't prepare at all. What helped me was a lot of interview practice in summers and internship learnings. I have a lot of interest in puzzles and other product management related issues, so outside reading and general awareness of tech product launches and their failures helped out.
dos_and_donts:
General tips :

Shut up and never cut off the interviewer. You do not know what they are going to say, so just listen.

Second, be confident and unapologetic about your life choices and why MBA questions.

Third, take your time in answering case based or puzzle based questions, keep water with you and drink it to get some time if needed. Don't hesitate in HR questions.

Fourth, express accurate uncertainty about your answers in case based questions. If you are 100% sure about the answer, say that with confidence. If you are having doubts, say you're almost sure. If you are guessing, explain your initial logic and explicitly say that you are guessing.

Specific tips :

If you are given a puzzle or case, do not auto assume common sense conditions that are not mentioned. Confirm them with interview and explain that you'd arrive at a trivial answer if those conditions are not present. 

This will ensure a) you do not limit your solution scope b) You will have a lot of time to think about solution and understand the complete problem and c) Interviewer will appreciate that you are looking for outside the box solutions.

e.g. I was asked if you had a lot of money and you had to start a venture, what would you do. I just said I'll start installing a lot of machines to capture carbon from atmosphere because he didn't tell me I had to be profitable.

Lastly, embrace MECE. It is always needed.

pre_process_tips: Resume Based Shortlisting
no_interviews_duration: 4 Interviews - 1 With Manager (30-40 Min), 1 with Director (20-30 Min), 1 with HR (5-10 Min), 1 with Partner (5-10 Min)
interview_outline:
I did not get a single case to solve unlike my peers who got a case or two in the process
Interview 1 - Manager Level - 30-40 Min (CV Based in Depth Questioning)
Started with About Me type, Went to rigorous CV Based Questioning with in Depth on Work Ex and Summer Intern. Asked about favorite Subjects and why, Since I had grown up abroad got asked why come back to India, Why Consulting, Fine with Travel type question.
Interview 2 - Director (Pass-out of IIM Indore) - 20-30 Min (CV Based with slightly less rigorous than previous) 
Similar Questions as in Round 1 basis Work Ex and Summer Internship, Learnings from Internship, Why Consulting, Are you fine with Travel, Explain about PoRs, Slightly Behavioural questions basis how handled communication issues and leadership at work
Interview 3 - HR - 5-10 Min, Asked on recent Farm Bills since I had mentioned I follow politics etc. and how Govt can resolve conundrum.
Behavioural Questions on what annoys me and type of people I don't like to work with and how I handle it, Politics interest, Social Initiatives, Why Consulting.
Interview 4 - Partner Round (My B.Tech Institution Super Senior) - 5-10 Min
How different experiences have shaped my view, Given I grew up abroad some questions on that, Industry Choice, Do I want to continue in the domain I interned in, Questions about B.Tech Experience, Why Consulting and Travel, Location Preferences
domain_questions: Had no Cases unlike others in the process
situational_questions: What annoys me at work, Type of people I am annoyed by, Handling Freeriders, Learnings from experiences, Social Initiatives, Leadership Positions issues, Handling Communication Issues at work
hr_gk_questions: Since I mentioned Farm Bills I got asked on that my views, Everything covered in outline of Interviews
looking_for:
Communication Skills, Leadership Positions, Initiative Taking. 
In my case based on a remark made by the Partner, I think they were also looking for some background/work ex in Tech
right_wrong:
Could have been more Top-down at points in answering, STAR Format for Behavioural stuff. 
Converted
tips:
Preparation Wise - Prepped a lot on Cases and Problem Solving using Casebooks like Case Interviews Cracked, IIMA Case Books, IIML Books & Videos, Foreign Casebooks for Math Prep. Had got an excellent Case Partner and more committed than me to push me (He got placed in "The Firm" as well); Prepared my CV inside out - RAC Format in the CV, More details for the Interview, use cases, Benefits of the work; Prepared subjects mentioned in my resume; General Reading on Current Affairs (Not only for Interview Prep but otherwise also an interest); Looked at Last Year's EY Interview Experience; Linkedin Stalking of the type of work 
PPT Day - Interacted a lot with the person who came in - asked a lot of questions on what the work entailed, experiences etc.
Interview Day - Tried to Keep calm during the interview, tried to be articulate, Smiling always, Showing the passion, asked the Director level about their experience over the decade in working, Found common passions to connect with each interviewer.
dos_and_donts:
Try to know the company inside out - very useful when you want to make a conversation. 
Know yourself and why you want that company and that domain and that role - Not just a prepared answer but you should really mean it (In my case this was one of my dream companies in life and among this year's Placements the topmost on my priority list and I explained why every time) - Even if it isn't your dream - make it sound like.  
Helpful to find common passions/experiences with the interviewer - Helped me with HR who had worked at my previous company long back. You get to learn about a person more.

pre_process_tips: Just reculta application with preferences (Choose preferences wisely; if they like you for a role but you did not put it as your preference, you might not get it)
no_interviews_duration: 2 telephonic interviews (25-35 minutes each) + 1 video interview (30 minutes)
interview_outline:
1st call (About 9 days before day 1 of finals placement) - Technical heavy. Started with introduction. Then I was asked questions about my summer internship which was at an insurance company (How do the financial statements of insurance companies look like? What financial metrics used to test financial strength of an insurance company? Explain the ratios? Explain what you did for internship, mention some key findings). I had mentioned valuation on my resume so asked me about types of valuation and when to use which one. Then I was asked what was 'leverage' in financial leverage. I was then asked about what my favourite subject was and why? The next set of questions were from what I mentioned. (I mentioned options & derivatives so I was asked to explain some option strategies and when an investor uses them, how to hedge against foreign currency exposure and interest rate fluctuations). The call ended with the interviewer answering my questions. 

2nd call (About 7 days before day 1 of final placements) - Technical heavy. Introduction; why credit risk specifically? How to analyse credit risk for banks (Both qualitative and quantitative measures)? What is the typical capital structure of a bank? How to look at asset quality of their loan book? (Be thorough with CAMELS approach). Then I was given a specific situation: SBI wants to enter into a swap agreement to hedge against rise of oil prices and GS has to facilitate this swap. What are the risks that GS faces? How to hedge against this risk? Types of collaterals? How will you know how much collateral is good (Concept of haircut) Then interview moved on to 1-2 HR questions (Biggest failure?) and ended with interviewer answering my questions. 

3rd call (Day 0) - Mix of HR and technical. Started with introduction. Why credit risk? What do you know about GS? What are the types of divisions? Give an example of a type of work that GS does? Then based on my example he asked further technical questions. Whats a financial or economic news that you've recently read? Asked technical questions from there in depth (about inflation, monetary policy, effect on GDP, measures taken by RBI, etc). I had come to IPM after a year of finishing 12th so I was grilled about my gap year after that. You basically have to really convince them that you're long term goals are to stick with GS. Was asked about my short-term, medium-term and long-term career goals. Interview ended with interviewer answering my questions. 

4th call (Day 1) - No "interview", just chit-chat and offer made.
domain_questions: Mentioned in previous answer. Be structured, articulate and confident.
situational_questions: Mentioned in previous answer
hr_gk_questions: Mentioned in previous answer
looking_for: Strong technical knowledge of derivatives, valuation, and workings of different financial institutions.
right_wrong: Good understanding of the role and finance topics.
tips:
Be thorough with resume. (Internships, work ex and projects). Read the JD properly and learn about every technical word that is mentioned. Fully understand the role offered and learn financial topics that come to use in the role (derivatives). 
I specifically did 2 courses on credit risk on udemy. Googled about every word mentioned in the JD and had answers prepared for every sector mentioned on my resume. Sector knowledge will include (current news, pre-covid to post-covid changes, financial metrics for that industry, understanding its costs and revenue structures, etc). Prepcom material on risk was helpful but go to CFI institute or investopedia for more details. Learn about what GS really does and how credit risk division plays a role.

interview_outline:
Automated video interview: 3 questions - Tell me about yourself, HR situational question, current affairs for ex: impact of russia-ukraine war on global financial markets etc
Buddy Round: Started with introduction, covered major points of the resume, went in detail in one of the internships, asked about the company, etc.
Offline Interviews: 3 rounds; 1st room - completely resume based, talked about internships, projects, data analysis projects, these conversations segued into insurance industry since projects involved the same, also questions like why DE Shaw, what makes it different, why this role, etc.
2nd room - HR Heavy, Multiple situational questions on working in teams, being a leader of a diverse group, etc. Couple of technical questions on Fundamental Analysis and Financial Ratios
3rd Room - Technical heavy, asked to choose one finance topic, dived deeper into it, for ex: derivatives - what are options, futures, forwards, payoffs, their applications, etc.
domain_questions:
Company Related Question: Every interview round, from the buddy call to the last offline interview round had one common question: What do you know about DE Shaw? All the interviewers really wanted to know how much you know about the role, the company, and want to understand why you want to join them. PrepCom Company PPTs helped me a lot to frame my answers about what exactly the company does. Reading the JD thoroughly and multiple times helped me understand the role in detail. Paying attention in the company pre-placement talk helped me a lot in answering questions like "Why DE Shaw". I was able to give examples from the pre-placement talk in multiple interviews which impressed them.
Technical Questions: Any technical terms on your resume, make sure you know them well. For ex, if your projects are on 1 particular industry, make sure you know the industry in-n-out. Financial Ratios are quite important for almost all finance interviews, not just DE Shaw. Know the ratios, their interpretations, and some particular industry averages, and ratios unique to that particular industry. Know basic financial concepts on fundamental analysis.
hr_gk_questions:
Tell me about yourself, what did your projects involve, what is it that you did, etc. Dived quite deep in the projects/achievements. 
HR: Situational questions - you are the leader of a diverse team, how will you ensure the minority group wells welcomed, etc.
looking_for: Genuine interest, curiosity and love for the company and the role
right_wrong:
Good Part: I answered the situational questions quite well. Used the STAR framework which made my responses look quite structured. Knew well about the company and the role. Asked them a lot of questions about their work and the teams. Knew my resume quite well.
Bad: During my technical round, I was in a hurry to give the answers due to which I misunderstood a couple of questions and ended up giving the wrong answers. Be calm and listen to the questions completely to understand what is being asked.
tips: Know your resume very well. Even if you do not have a finance background, brush up basic financial concepts of FAC course and prepcom material and ratios for finance roles and interviews. Read up on current affairs. Give structured, to-the-point responses. Refer company ppts and the JD to know about the company and role. Do ask genuine questions, if you have any, after the interviews.
dos_and_donts: DO read up very well on the company and the role. Cannot stress this enough. Simplify your answers for questions like what the company does and what the role is, rather than learning and repeating prepcom slides' language or the JD in the interview.

pre_process_tips: Attend Case workshop organised by company,  take notes during pre placement presentation to know the department and respective employees better
interview_outline:
Round 1 : Guesstimate 

Round 2 : Case on Supply chain - specifically about reducing cost - use principals like kaizen. highly technical

Round 3 : taken by Senior Management - Looked at the over all profile. Asked me about my R1 and R2,  asked 1 case and 1 guesstimate, it was more personal than the previous 2 rounds, was asked why I wanted to join consulting and why PWC in specific. 

Round 4 : HR round, was asked about any situation where I have shown leadership, and was also asked to mention a situation where I had faced conflict, and what I did to handle it.
domain_questions:
Automobile Industry (Was employed here previously) : was asked to estimate the EV market size for India. Was asked to list factors that would be essential to consider before and after venturing  into the EV Market, specifically factors that would differentiate my company from competitors. Was asked about Market share and trends of competitors and entry of new players. Was asked to compare products among competitors and within own company. Was asked to forecast sales for a particular month for my Ex Employer which was Hyundai; along with mentioning the qualitative aspects that need to be taken care of, was also asked to apply a forecasting technique to get a quantitative result. 

Domain Related questions - A new US based commercial vehicle company has entered the Indian Market. It has a small demand in market and issues pertaining to high costs. Its products are not competitively priced, help them solve this issue.

Apply the Value Chain approach - Take individual element to identify costs attached with them. Eg: Raw material procurement is not cost effective as supplier awards manufacturers with volume demand with discounts. One solution could be to leverage the Supplier Relations of MNCs based in the US who have a presence in Indian market too. You could also think about other solutions.

Cost reduction in Manufacturing - Use concepts of Lean manufacturing and 7 principles of Kaizen. Revise OM1 for this. Also revise the 6 sigma concept.
situational_questions:
What will you do when the client is reluctant to work with you stating that you do not have the expertise in the industry?

State one example where you had to Manage Crisis during a conflict.
hr_gk_questions: New Car launches, EV in India.
looking_for:
Communication, Logic, and structuring of problem.
Also, they were looking for the candidate's ability to grasp, think out of the box, and the willingness to learn. 
Be calm even if you are struggling to give a recommendation; the communication and though process behind reaching the end solution matters the most, rest can be managed.
right_wrong: What went right : Showing that you are sincere, eager and ready to learn is something that they liked.
tips:
IIM I casebook, IIM A casebook, Sector specific Sessions organized by Prep com  
If you have work ex - it would be best if you get updated about the recent happenings in the industry you have worked in. if you are asked a question from this sector, and you are unable to give an appropriate answer, it would cut out a very sorry figure, and chances of getting rejected are high. 
Most of the times, the questions revolve around the industry you have worked in. Especially if its an automobile industry, most panelists will be interested in knowing about your opinion.
dos_and_donts: It is best to state everything while you are solving the case, rather than feeling it might be inappropriate and then realizing in the end that it was an important piece in your solution.

pre_process_tips: We had to fill a google form with our basic info like previous education, internships, workex, etc. DB is one of the few companies which asked for our CG so I feel that contributes to getting the shortlist. Lastly, relevant finance certifications obviously help a lot.
no_interviews_duration: 4 interviews (first one was a buddy call and last was an HR call), buddy call went for 40 minutes, round 2 and 3 went for 30 minutes and lastly, HR call was for 10 minutes.
interview_outline: I first had a buddy call which was a short interview of 20 to 30 minutes and then I had a round two which was with the head of the trade finance team and that also went on for 30 minutes and then I had the final round which went for 40 minutes and lastly I had a very brief HR call. I think the results were probably decided by then, but HR just asked me a few questions to see my communication and my understanding of DB and then I was given the result.
domain_questions: From what I understood about the corporate banking role and the interviews that happened for that is that they don't really expect us to know a lot of core finance. I got asked - how do you choose an industry, how to analyze an industry, how to analyze a company. In my round two with the head of the trade finance team she went a bit deep into these things before lending or before taking part in any transactions, what all steps do you check… So it's more about having a good understanding of the role and the JD.
hr_gk_questions: I got asked a lot of HR questions because here the role is really heavily dependent on client interactions and stakeholder management so they went to every single past experience of mine where I could have shown or done any amount of client interactions and they asked what I did there, how I was able to manage the stakeholders. They also asked me a lot about my past decisions i.e. why did you leave a previous company, why did you do an MBA, why exactly do you want to join DB, why this role, etc.
prep_resources: I referred to the red book and the PrepCom slidedecks for my core finance prep and then I just revised my resume and whatever I had mentioned there to be prepared for all these HR and open ended questions.
looking_for: I think in the corporate banking role they look for a very confident individual who they feel will be able to deal with clients. Obviously they want you to have a good finance background but they don't really look for deep finance knowledge. What they value more is confidence and experience with client interactions and stakeholder management in your past so if you can highlight that, I think that makes your profile really good for the role.
right_wrong: So what went right, I would say in the buddy call I asked every single question that I could think of and my buddy was also very friendly so she gave me a lot of suggestions which I was able to use in my further interview rounds and I think that is why my rounds two and three went very smoothly. My buddy suggested that you should emphasize your client interaction part. Something that could have been better I guess is that my finance prep was a bit lacking, so when I had my first round with the buddy I was really panicking on whether I am prepared well for finance or not. So, I would say if you're targeting companies like DB then have a really good finance prep so that when the interview is nearing you focus more on parts like your resume and HR questions.
tips: Staying confident, communicating smoothly and knowing my resume inside out.

pre_process_tips: There were no pre-processes. After applying for the company's role, we got a shortlist
interview_outline:
More HR based questions
Round 1 - Group interview
Group interviews are generally uncommon. Here, we had 5 candidates in each panel and had to answer questions asked by the panelist one by one. It started off by a brief introduction, followed by dream job and dream company (barring PWC). Then there were questions around strength and ideal traits of a consultant. He further asked us to rate ourselves on 3 parameters - relationships, communication and problem solving skills and what is the one most important skill a consultant should have.

Round 2 - Personal Interview
Went for about 15min, it started with an introduction, followed by changing trends in the energy and utilities sector. He went on to ask about why consulting and if I had any questions for him.

There was no round 3 but before rolling out the offer there was a last HR round where I was asked if I'd be willing to travel or not and which part of the country do I come from?
domain_questions: This was part of the second round of interview, where trends in the energy and utilities sector was asked. No specific details were asked but it was to gauge an understanding that the candidate had regarding the role and sector at the macro level. Since it was pertaining to energy, I spoke about a general global shift towards renewable sources of energy, relating it my UG internship. I also talked about the impact on allied industries and sectors.
situational_questions:
During the group interview, we were asked about our strengths. 
As consulting requires one to listen and understand the problem thoroughly, so based on this, I aligned my strength of listening more and observing with this trait of a consultant.

 The technical one started with my introduction, then he asked me questions from the things I mentioned. Then it went to the technical part. Since I had my certifications( CFA Actuaries etc) he asked me few questions then he was convinced on that part. Then it went to CV based questions from my internship, academic and love projects. Discussion about the events happening in the BFSI industry. And a few other things.

domain_questions:
I was asked less technical questions than other people because he saw that I already had quite a few certifications.
It’s started with me being asked about valuations. I was asked about Entertprise Value. So I answered it but I also mentioned all the possible ways, like how I would calculate it if I were to start with FCF or FCFE. Then how I would value the equity part of it, as in all the there valuation methods( DDM, DCF and relative valuation). And in what case I would use each of them, like DDM I would use only when i’m Valuing from an retail investor POV and not from an acquirer POV for that I would go for DCF, and etc.
So at this point they were conveniencd about my valuation concepts and they mentioned that I see you’ve done your certification. So the thing is don’t say everything you know, but keep your answer around the question that has been asked but mention all the nuances and details in a systematic way. 
Then they asked about my statistics project. So I mentioned about the regression methods I used and they asked me further questions on that about the inferences etc. But from all my interview experiences I understood that all the corporate people have their knowledge about stats and regression limited to P value or maybe a little further. So if you talk about Poisson distributions and GLM then they don’t ask further questions.
Then questions about my internship and my learning’s from there. So I mentioned something about non cash expenses so they asked me about it, wasn’t very difficult.

They didn’t ask me anything company related but when they asked me if I wanted to ask anything. so I asked what was the wholesale Banking’s division to the rising NPA at that time.

pre_process_tips: You have to create a resume in the format provided from the company for the role. You have to be a Chief ___ Officer. You have to explain your idea behind choosing the role. I chose tot be Chief Impact Officer, as I firmly believe in creating impact and provided anecdotes from my life (1 liner) supporting the same. Use the space wisely.
interview_outline:
The interview started with the interviewers introduction. It tells you a little about the exact role you are being interviewed for. My role is most probably Life Sciences Consulting.

I was asked to introduce myself in a minute. Some questions regarding my previous job, and then we quickly moved to the Case Study Part. As soon as it got completed, another interviewer joined the same call to continue the discussions.

I was asked a few questions (1-2) and we again did a case related to the healthcare sector. It ended with both qualitative and quantitative analysis.

After 2-3 hours, I had my 2nd round, which lasted for a few mins (3-4).
domain_questions: No technical questions were asked
hr_gk_questions: I was asked the reason behind my interest in Consulting Role. I was also asked the reason behind choosing Deloitte.
looking_for:
They were very interested in my work at ZS, where I worked on a merger project in healthcare sector. They were also interested in my Graduation Stream (Pharmaceutical Engineering).

They were looking for someone who can break down the problem and analyze it to grater depths. For some questions, I was specifically asked to provide some qualitative points apart from the solution supported by the data to examine the depth of knowledge and my creativity.
right_wrong:
I was not able to understand two columns in the data provided. I couldn't proceed to the calculations based on the data provided. I asked them to explain me the data thrice until I understood the exact meaning of it. I never hesitated to ask them questions and extra relevant data. (Always back your questions with logic otherwise you won't get any answer to them).

I was not able to calculate very fast. One must practice speed math. I was also not aware of the population of US.
tips:
I remembered the cases taught in the classes well and used terms like Lead Time, a few marketing concepts and customized them for the healthcare sector.

Always read some basic facts about the native place of the company too.

Always take your time before asking questions. Once you start talking, talk for a minute, and take pauses of 15 secs, saying "Let me think now". They happily allow you to do so. Always remember to get the case done in 20 mins. (max 25)
dos_and_donts:
Always keep an excel open. I hadn't. They asked me whether I was communicated regarding that or not, then, allowed me to make the data on my notebook. I struggled with calculation in the data. Should have had excel.

Strike a conversation in the beginning of the interview to take control. The interviewer asks you some general questions in the beginning like How's the day? How's the whether? How's your family?
Reply to them and ask at least one questions and keep giving some visible responses to them. Interviewers are not ready to answer those and, you get the courage to drive the interview on your own.

If the interviewer says that he doesn't have enough time (less than 10 mins), then ask very questions. Keep progressing just by making assumptions and not even verifying them. Use all probable decision trees, so that they are convinced about your holistic and can measure you abilities quickly.

pre_process_tips: Google form based shortlist with basic background details and an essay ("WFH is the future of workplace" was our topic for summers and finals as well) | Two case-basd rounds and a final partner round
no_interviews_duration: First interview- case based, about 35 minutes, second interview - case based, went for about 20 minutes, third interiview - partner round that went for about 20 minutes
interview_outline:
First interview was a profitability case - The interviewer started with a brief introduction and my idea of what Everest group does. Then jumped to the case right away, which was lengthy; each aspect of the problem (number of units sold/ cost of each unit/ inbound and outbound logistics. to name a few) everything had a problem and I had to ask questions and make calculated guesses as well (based on current affairs). Please note that no number crunching was involved. The interview ended with case summary and solutions. 

Second interview was an unconventional case (while others had market entry or growth cases) - it was a DILR problem. I was clueless in the beginning but started with asking questions and doing some number crunching. I could not arrive at the correct answer but my answer was close to it. The interviewer made me conduct a top-down approach as compared to the bottom-up approach I had chosen initially. 

Third interview - This was the partner round. I was on STEP during my interview so he asked me about the place and whether I learnt French. Then the interviewer asked me about the exchange rate scenario and how it affects Indian service providers like TCS (I did not know much in this regard and I told him the same honestly). I was then asked to describe my hometown and IPM as a program. I asked two questions to the partner regarding the work he has done (not something about the company per se, but about himself). The interview ended with a sly question about whether I have further placement processes lined up which I tackled with a witty answer.
hr_gk_questions:
Why Everest (Great work culture, much greater accountability right from the entry-level position; related it with similar work I had done previously and thus, I would thrive at a place like Everest)
As a fresher why do you want to enter this line?
looking_for:
- A strong command of case frameworks
- Decent current affairs knowledge
- A structure and sound reasoning; my answer in the second interview was not correct but my explanation made sense to the interviewer (which is also why my answer was close to the correct answer). 
- Whether you can engage in a conversation and your presence of mind (especially during the Partner round)
right_wrong:
What went right:
- Knowing the case frameworks almost by heart.
- Having a little idea about current affairs 
- Following a structured approach even while answering questions not related to the case (HR questions, opinion questions; it always helps if you answer in points)
- Maintaining my composure even when the case felt daunting or when I did not have any clue about how to proceed

What could have gone better:
- Knowing when to choose between bottom-up and top-down approaches (even though the first is used way more than the other, I arrived at the correct answer using the second, and only because my interviewer gave me a second chance by asking me to do so).
tips:
Know a bit about what's happening in the world
Hold several (as many, no number is enough) mock case interviews with colleagues
Make sure you think (and think out loud) through the guesstimate before arriving at an answer, they do not want to know your answer but how you arrive at the answer.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlisting
interview_outline:
1st interview started with an introduction, a few questions on work-ex, questions about company and finally a case to solve.
2nd interview was more like a stress interview round. Started with an introduction, a lot of cross-questions (I said solving puzzles as my hobby and the interviewer immediately gave me a puzzle to solve) and finally a case.
domain_questions:
Case-based Questions:
1) Paytm has started a referral system to increase its customer base. How can we make this system viral?
Approach: Started by asking preliminary questions like what the referral system is, how it works, objective of launching it, the geography that we want to target etc. Then moved on to divide the present customer base into several segments based on age, income and usage of the app. Finally, suggested various marketing techniques that can be employed for each of the customer segment.
Tip: Be aware of various digital marketing techniques.
2) The no. of subscribers in the Paytm mutual funds segment have decreased in last few years. How would you go about it?
Approach: Asked questions on what the business is, types of customers, types of subscriptions, trends in the last few years in each type of subscription. Also, shed some light on overall economy and mutual fund business as a whole. The interviewer asked me to stop in between, hence, no recommendations were given.
Tip: Ask as many questions as you can in a structured manner to understand the root cause of the problem. Don't jump to the recommendation part directly.
hr_gk_questions:
"Why Paytm?" was asked in the 1st interview.
Approach: Spoke about the various business segments within Paytm, the segment that I am more interested in and the sense of entrepreneurship (freedom/ownership) that can be obtained to work for a business which is in its nascent phase and at the same time being backed by the huge brand name of the organization.
Tip: Know well about the company.
In the 2nd interview, some stressful questions were asked like:
1) Why was PPO not being offered by the organization that you interned in? Did you under-perform? Did you reject the PPO?
Approach: Told all the good things about the organization and the project. Told him honestly that I have no clue as to why PPO wasn't offered.
Tip: Don't make any negative remarks on your past organization.
2) You interned in a fin role, your resume is more tilted towards fin, then why did you apply for this role (S&M)? Do you know where your interests lie?
Approach: Said that I don't have a specific domain interest. Just like to play with numbers. We are here to understand business as a whole.
3) What electives have you taken in 2nd year? (Asked questions on luxury retail management)
Tip: Name a few electives from every domain.
looking_for: A person who can approach problems in a structured way and does not falter when put under pressure.
right_wrong: Kept my calm and answered all questions with a smile. Asked a good question at the end and cross-questioned as well (shows that you are good listener and aren't asking a question for just the sake of it).
tips: IIM-A and IIM-L casebook (solve in groups of two), Digital Marketing (read about some of the digital marketing techniques and when to use them).
dos_and_donts: Stay calm and highly motivated, have a smile on your face even if a question catches you off-guard, Know about the company.

pre_process_tips: Pyschometric Test + GD
gd_topics_tips:

Two questions were asked 1) if I were the CEO of the company, how would I drive the growth and sustainability of the company  2) what were would the bank need to look into before sanctioning the loan. 
Basic knowledge of the financial markets and terms were good enough to pass the GD. The panel was looking at how efficiently we could link up the theory in finance with the actual problem given in the case study. Good knowledge of credit cycle, working capital, and the functioning of a bank is required to be known.
interview_outline: Asked me why finance? Then asked me about the BFSI sector in the country. Told me to relate my work in the summer internships to the role which the company offered. Finally, HR questions.
domain_questions: Why finance? Then what was my perception of the BFSI sector and what changes would come in the sector in the post-Covid era. My perceptions of the Indian stock market? Why did India have record FII inflows during the Covid pandemic? What factors do investors look for before investing in a country? How is ESG important in the current scheme of things in the Indian banking industry? How will you convince a company to undertake more ESG related sustainable measures?

1) Are you willing to relocate anywhere in India?
2) If you had to do a bit of a S&M job alongside the major finance work, would you be willing to do it?
3) Wont there be any objections from your family if you are relocated anywhere in the country?
hr_gk_questions:
1) What are your strengths (Why you?)
2) What makes you think that you will work well in a client facing role?
looking_for:
1) Knowledge of the BFSI Sector
2) Changes in the BFSI sector after the pandemic
3) Indian stock market
4) How I could relate the summer internship work with the role offered
5) Cultural fit with the organisation
right_wrong:
I was prepared about the impacts of Covid 19 pandemic on the BFSI sector and outlined in great detail as to how the sector would be impacted and how it would look in the future. Although the interviewer kept on disagreeing with me, I stuck to my points with confidence (kind of a stress interview to see whether I was confident enough in what I knew and in my own abilities). I was ready with whatever they would ask me about the summer internship experience. Good Knowledge of FAC, Fin 1 and 2 is a must. As previously mentioned, current affairs was the most important factor which helped me in this interview.
Result" Converted.
tips: 1) Prepcom sessions were extremely important. I thoroughly studied the PPTs shared by prepcom on the various sectors (especially BFSI). The live lectures and the PPT helped me to gain immense knowledge about the current affairs. 1) Always show that you are willing learner who is always ready to learn
2) Show that you are a very flexible and adaptive individual who is always willing to relocate, do S&M jobs, take on increased leadership responsibilities, etc. whenever possible
