interview_outline:
Round 1(R1): Started with random chit chats for around 2 minutes and then moved on to introduction. Thereafter, I was explained about the process that round 1 is going to be an eliminator and another colleague will join for Round 2 (A case interview), If I do well in R1. R1 started with a Guesstimate. I was asked couple of HR questions after that. Successfully cleared the round.

Round 2(R2): Started with a case study. The whole interview revolved around that. R2 did require some IT knowledge to conquer the case.

Round 3: Started with an Introduction and then a few HR questions.This round was HR heavy.
domain_questions:
No technical questions were asked in the interview. The major focus was on my work experience.
Questions: 
Q1) Run me through your work experience.
Q2) (Picked something from what I said) Explain your contribution and role in this project.
Q3) Explain a situation where you worked on a new technology and how did you go about it?
Q4) What was the product that you developed in the last organization.

Approach: I tried to emphasise more on what was the overall objective, the pain points and the reason behind doing that project ( Business aspect of it) and then I moved on to my contribution in resolving the pain points/issues.

Note: The Panel never wants you to go into technical details. They just gauge your confidence through your contributions. Try to be calm and composed while you answer and keep it very concise. And the most important thing : "SMILE"
hr_gk_questions:
Few HR questions like:
Q1) Explain a situation where you worked on a new technology and how did you go about it?
Q2) Why Deloitte?
Q3) Where do you see yourself in 5 years?
Q4) Why Consulting?
looking_for:
Qualities/Traits to portray:
1) Genuine: Please try to be who you are. " Globe at your own risk :P"
2) Decent Communication Skills: This is one of the most important part when it comes to consulting. Please take your interviewer as your client and make him/her comfortable to share the details with you.
3) You must know what you do not know:  Be very clear about what you know and what you don't. It is perfectly okay to not know something.
4) Calmness: Try to maintain your composure even in stress situations. This really makes a good impression.
right_wrong:
I held a very good conversation. Tried to be humorous (This was instinctive). 
Situation: I cleared the R1 and was conveyed that the other person will join in few minutes for R2. Then, followed an awkward silence.
I grabbed that opportunity to talk to the interviewer. (Please avoid silence, They want you to talk)

I converted the offer. This was my first interview on campus.
tips: The consulting case domain sessions along with the materials provided were helpful. Also, I had a second round of PI by REC which proved to be very helpful.
dos_and_donts:
Be well prepared about a few things before the interview.
1) Introduction
2) Why a particular company?
3) Where do you see yourself in 5/10/15 years?
4) Your Short term / long term goals.
5) Why this role?

Although these answers shall be thought of, but still while you answer, it shall sound candid and not mugged up.

pre_process_tips:
Resume based shortlisting.
No written/psychometric assessment. No GDs.
interview_outline:
Both interviews were a mix of Domain/company specific as well as HR and situational questions.
Round 1: Started with introduction/walking through the resume. What ideas do you have for growth of paytm (they will be expecting details and granularity)? Questions about key takeaways from past workex/internship. HR questions
Round 2: Intro followed by grilling on the career gaps. Multiple Domain related questions. One Puzzle, one guestimate (number of people watching netflix in India this very moment). Some HR questions.
domain_questions:
What's your Growth strategy for Paytm: Keep asking questions since the company offers so many verticals. Get the interviewer to narrow down the question. This will show you like specifics. 
The questions I asked:
Which group are we talking about, users or merchants? which users, payments or billing/insurance/paytm mall or payment bank? He said payments.
Then I went ahead with the STP and Different plans for different segments based on the age/demography and media they are exposed/influenced by. The details left a good impression. 


Multiple questions regarding the electives in the resume.
7Cs, Porter's 5. Which force is the most dominant  for paytm/fintech companies. Arrange them in descending order.
situational_questions: How do you deal with deadlines? What if the time and resources are scarce? How will you still deliver?
hr_gk_questions:
Why did you jump into MBA? If you had stayed, you would be doing very well in the industry without spending 18L for the MBA. 
What's your biggest achievement?
Why do you want to change your industry?
Answered with utmost clarity and justified your career decisions point-wise and systematically. Explained my drive towards emerging industries like fintech/edtech/platform businesses, followed by how I'd be useful given the JD.
looking_for:
Clarity of thought and total understanding of the paytm business model, which is not a straightforward one.
Behavioral traits which fit well in a fast growing, startup environment. The culture fit and 'energy' fit.
Relevant internship/Live projects seemed would be a plus, provided you bring it up in the interview.
right_wrong:
Concluding each answer by connecting to my abilities to the JD. Drawing parallels between internship experiences and the JD. The constant reinforcing of why am I useful and a good fit worked.
The clarity about paytm's model gave a good impression. Multiple follow up questions when asked about my plan for paytm's growth made them think i care about specifics and am not into giving globe answers. 

Wasnt able to crack the puzzle, but he didn't mind much. Worst part was when I wasnt able to finish the guesstimate in time since I took the longer (if not the wrong) approach. Sensing he's losing the patience, I just gave him the next steps showing i was on the right path atleast. I conceded and suggested saving some precious time. Seemed like a good damage control (but may differ from person to person).
tips:
Multiple mock interviews with friends were they key. It gave me a lot of practice and comfort in speaking continuously with clarity for long stretches of time. Go through the prepcom material. It helps.
Keep track of the current events in the business world, especially the big happenings in the Indian startup ecosystem (unicorns, M&A, IPOs, etc)
dos_and_donts:
Study the model well. Keep track of current events in the fintech industry.
Dont mug up intro answers. Keep it super chatty. Have a story to tell for every resume point. All the best.

pre_process_tips: Application forms -> CAT type test with heavy focus on LRDI oriented questions -> GD -> Interviews
gd_topics_tips:
Topic: Are gold prices rally an indicator of macroeconomic uncertainty or bubble build-up?

Tips:
1. Was thorough with numbers like the current gold prices, the price movement over the last 5 years, 2 years & 1 year horizon
2. Knowing all the major macroeconomic indicators and asset classes & connecting them with gold price rally was useful
3. Quoting research reports I had read on this topic along with the sources was useful
4. Knowing some more enhanced indicators like gold/silver relative price movement and its implications was very useful
5. Connecting it with past instances of gold price rally, like the 2008 GFC was a good indicator of knowledge and helped enrich the discussion
interview_outline:
First two interviews were with Analysts operating out of the Mumbai office, highly technical in nature - one focused on corporate finance theory & the other was more focused on global macros and industry knowledge. Past internships & work done was talked about here.

The third round was an ED round which was rapid fire corporate finance followed by a series of questions where I was asked about my opinion on AI valuations, rate cuts, etc. as well as a few HR oriented questions. Wasn't massively resume based, but I was asked about a specific internship, which wasn't particularly significant on my resume, since my ED knew about the company herself.

Last round was with HR which was just a chill conversation.
domain_questions:
1. Questions on the three financial statements and treatment of different scenarios/transactions
2. In-depth questioning on ratios, connecting it with different industries and how they behave
3. Valuations - DCF based, LBO, multiples based
4. Determining cost of capital, CAPM model, etc.
5. A lot of questioning on valuation and analysis of private companies
6. Questions related to accretion dilution, synergy analysis, etc.
7. Macro factors & their connection with industry prep, which was thoroughly tested again
8. Questions on M&A transaction that I have tracked and my analysis of it
hr_gk_questions: I was asked extensively on why I wanted to work on IB since I had all prior experience in private equity investing, what were my goals, why Nomura specifically, what team I will like to work for within the IBD division
prep_resources: Red book, 250 IB questions, IBEF & reports by investment banks/equity research houses (industry prep), Economic Times, general reading/podcasts/youtube videos on finance & macroeconmics
looking_for: Looked for solid technical foundations, in-depth understanding of macro factors and our own opinions/perspective/outlook. Basically, they were looking for people who had solid foundations in the technicals, were abreast of recent happenings, and could connect theory with practical understanding to develop opinion and carry out the tasks required of an analyst.
right_wrong: Everything went right except one specific accounting question, where I stumbled a little but solved with help of the interviewer.
tips: Specifically, it definitely helped being confident, being very well prepared, being warm and smiling, having conversation with them where I also asked them questions/made comments to engage them in the middle of the interview, asked them for feedback, etc.
tech_skills: Accounting, valuations, macroeconomics, financial markets/news, M&As, LBOs, etc.
dos_and_donts: Study up on M&As, LBOs. Be thorough with recent news, market updates, and policy decisions (particularly by the central banks). Thorough preparation on industry aside from the Red Book & 250 IB prep.

pre_process_tips:
1st round- Aptitude test
2nd round- Psychometric test
3rd round- GD(more like group interview)
4th round- Personal Interview
gd_topics_tips: Should startups invest heavily in traditional media or social media?
no_interviews_duration: One round of interview for around 30 minutes
interview_outline: It started with introduction with a touch over to your family background. After that it went on to major HR questions and a few technical questions in the sense how one principle or concept can be applied in real life.
domain_questions:
Marketing of a certain product in the rural market was one specific question that was asked.
I structured it in the way that there are some influential people in the village and then there are some people who follow these influential people and then there are slabs in village in which the people are divided so we can target people from the slab who can be important in making our product reach a better number of people.
situational_questions:
A situation was given where you have worked really hard on a project but then your boss straight away rejects it then what will be my approach to make him/her believe that the proposal should go through.
I approached the question first in the way that nobody will reject any proposal if they don't have a reason to so i will try to find out the reason as to why it was rejected at the first place, if she is not ready to give me the insights then i will approach other people in the same rank and try to gather as much information as i can and improve the report to the level best and then again approach the boss but this time i will present it rather than give the report in simple manner and also try to know what is wrong or what went wrong the last time.
hr_gk_questions: If a product has been researched enough and all the team were confident that the product is going to be successful but still it flops then why do you think it was flop?
looking_for: I think they were looking for people who can easily gel up with the current association and is cheerful in nature. Basically they were trying to avoid a (potential) bad apple in the lot.
right_wrong: I guess the constant smile on face was a huge hit and the last question which i asked to them regarding their company really gave them the feel that i am genuinely interested (which i was) in the company. They asked twice in the interview in different versions that if i was actually interested and why? And i did convert the interview :)
tips:
You should be thorough with two things for sure. 
1st- Your resume
2nd- The company/organization you are a part of the process
Mocks are important in the sense that you know they are going to happen but the variety and the questions and the way in which they are asked is always different so they could have been better. I asked many of my seniors outside IIM Indore to take my mock interviews and that's how my pool of questions increased and the confidence had a big boost.
dos_and_donts: Never globe around. When you are at the other side of the table it is very clearly visible  that you are trying to bluff your way out. If you are not sure just accept it and try to make up for it in the next part.

pre_process_tips: We were supposed to fill out the company application form and were shortlisted based on profile
interview_outline:
Interview 1: The first interview lasted around 25–30 minutes and was largely centered on my profile. The discussion covered the usual introductory questions—my background, my understanding of the role, why I’m interested in it, why I want to join the firm, and what expectations I have. They also asked for my views on AI, including how I think it will evolve and recent trends. I was asked to elaborate on the projects I’ve worked on in data analysis and share details about my internship, especially the projects I handled and their outcomes. Toward the end, they gave me a guesstimate: estimating the average monthly revenue of cab aggregators in my city.

Interview 2: The second interview lasted around 30 minutes and focused more on technical concepts in AI and data analysis. I was asked basic questions on topics such as p-values, regression, my projects, and general real-world applications of data analysis in organizations—nothing too detailed, just to gauge my foundational understanding. They also gave me a guesstimate: estimating the average monthly food and beverage revenue of multiplexes in India. Overall, the interview followed a similar pattern to the first one, but with slightly more depth.
domain_questions: The domain-specific questions focused on my understanding of AI and basic analytics concepts, such as p-values, regression, and real-world applications of data analysis. They also asked me to explain the projects I had worked on and relate them to practical business use cases. Additionally, both interviews included guesstimates to test my analytical thinking.
hr_gk_questions:
The HR questions were straightforward and focused on understanding my motivation and fit for the role. I was asked to introduce myself, explain why I was interested in this particular role, why I wanted to join their firm, and what my long-term career aspirations are.

There were no current affairs questions in particular.
prep_resources: The resources I used included the casebooks and preparation material provided by the preparation committee. I also made it a point to read the newspaper daily and reviewed my resume thoroughly to ensure I could justify every line.
looking_for: I believe they were looking for someone who was eager to learn and contribute, someone who had a clear understanding of the role and was well-aware of their surroundings and overall business context.
right_wrong: I had read extensively about the company and their recent projects, which helped me feel genuinely excited about the role—and I was able to reflect that enthusiasm during the interviews. The conversations were quite natural and engaging. I didn’t memorize any answers; instead, I prepared key pointers so I could improvise and keep the discussion authentic and conversational.
tips: Having a clear, in-depth understanding of the role, along with a good grasp of the basic technical skills associated with it, will definitely help.
tech_skills: Data Analytics, Artificial Intelligence, Python (not tested, but asked if I was familiar with it)
dos_and_donts: For preparation, ensure you have a clear understanding of the role, revise fundamental technical concepts, and stay updated on relevant industry developments. Review your resume thoroughly and prepare concise pointers rather than memorised answers, allowing you to communicate naturally and confidently. Avoid overcomplicating explanations and ensure your responses remain structured and precise. Additionally, conducting solid research on the firm and its recent projects is essential, as it demonstrates genuine interest and strengthens your overall preparation.

pre_process_tips: Only application on Reculta. A google form was floated for the role preference.
gd_topics_tips: Discuss the challenges and growth prospects of start-up ecosystem in India. The GD was an unstructured GD. No instructions were given regarding bifurcation of time for thinking and discussion. The panel was looking for candidates who tried to structure the GD, allowed others to speak, built upon points presented by others and ensured participation from each candidate.
no_interviews_duration: 1 technical interview (20 minutes) and 1 HR interview (10 minutes)
interview_outline:
Technical: Started with introduction and a walk through of resume, questions regarding internships, went into why sales, situational questions like how would you overcome language barriers, how is sales different from marketing, a few NPAD questions.
HR: Introduction, major life decisions and rationale behind them, questions about family, major personality traits and what incidents shaped them, a few NPAD questions, why Haleon and why would you be a good fit.
domain_questions: What is the difference between sales and marketing? Talked about the basic differences of push and pull strategy. The panel was not convinced and wanted to hear more technical terms. Mentioned the Sales process, Sales funnel stages and 4Ts of Sales from the internship starter deck. The panel sought explanations of a couple of terms mentioned.
hr_gk_questions: HR questions about resume were about the education trajectory I undertook and what were the factors I considered to make the decisions at each stage, for instance, why MBA after MSc? The panel just wanted to understand if those decisions were carefully thought out decisions or not. Another question was about internships where the panel wanted to understand my learnings from them. Lastly, they were looking for a link between extracurriculars and hobbies.
looking_for: I think they were looking for clear and concise answers. Also they were looking for someone who had a clear understanding of the role they had applied for, whether they had an understanding of the kind of challenges they might face and how would they try to resolve them. Also, given that this was a sales role, they were looking for someone who's willing to travel and would be comfortable talking to people.
right_wrong:
During the GD, the group collectively decided to take a minute to structure our thoughts and allowed others to speak. I think that led to a constructive discussion and was looked upon favorably by the panelist.
The good part of the interview was that after every answer I gave, the interviewer also put forward their point of view and then allowed me to explain my answer. They also maintained a very formal yet conversational tone. I had prepared for all questions and the answers were drawn from personal experiences, so I was able to justify them well.
The only bad part was some technical glitch on their end for a few minutes during which I couldn't hear them and that broke the flow of the conversation.
tips: I think the most helpful were the NPAD questions and the Marketing repository (Both starter decks and domain sessions). Also the consulting repository cases helped. The mock GD and PIs helped in understanding how to structure your thoughts and answer in precise manner.
dos_and_donts: It's okay to ask for a minute to structure your thoughts. Try to speak concisely and to the point. Listen to the view point of the interviewer. Read about company's vision and values and justify through examples how you and your actions align with theirs.

pre_process_tips: They wanted us to submit a presentation on either of the topics: E-wallets, Telecom sector, Banking sector shifting from offline to online.
interview_outline: Interviewer asked about my city , why I chose to do MBA, about the company comviva and about the role, then interviewer asked questions based on my resume on summer internship and projects. He then went on to discuss about the presentation that I submitted in the previous round on E wallets and wanted me to compare different wallets and come up with new use cases for them. He also asked me to suggest ways to increase revenue from those wallets and also identify the costs and reduce them .Then he asked some technical questions of the mobile wallet industry . And then went on to HR questions. The interview was balanced
domain_questions: As I am a fresher, he knew that I am not aware of technicalities of telecom sector so he was not expecting any technical jargon and wanted to check whether I am very of the current industrial trends. He asked me about E wallets and much of the interview was around it because I submitted a presentation on it. He wanted me to come up with uses cases for E wallets, and how can they increase customers. I went on to identify the customers for differeng E wallets and segregated them based on their usage of the wallet .Then suggested ways to ensure that their is less churn.
hr_gk_questions:
Tell me about yourself, wanted to know about my city , the kind of organisation I want to work with , the kind with which I absolutely won't work, where do I see myself in 5 years. Which is my dream company (not comviva)? What do I do in my past time, asked me about the last novel I read and its plotline, asked me about my family background , my strengths and weaknesses with examples, I have done few case competitions so he asked me what my role was and how my strengths helped me there.He asked me how many interviews have I given before and how was my experience over there and why I was not selected. 
I had more or less prepared for these questions , I had a story to support each answer, they were looking for company fit, so even though I had no experience they guaged that I was willing to learn.
looking_for: Company fit- aligned with the company values, willingness to learn and just checked my common sense and communication skills. Work -ex was not mandatory.
right_wrong: I wanted to talk about my case competitions because they were on B2B sales and the role I was interviewing for was also revolving around it so I mentioned about the competitions when I was giving examples of my strengths and the next question they asked me was to tell me more about it and I think they got impressed with the work I did there and it played a huge role in my selection. I was struggling with the uses cases for e wallets , but I suggested 2 , one was personalised wallets and other was wallet for B2B customers and then tried to justify it with scenarios and examples which helped my case.
tips: Mock PI's helped with the HR questions
dos_and_donts: Read about the company and telecom sector

gd_topics_tips:
Topic: Automotive sector is on a downturn but the Government is enforcing new vehicle norms like BS6 which will further stress the companies with respect to rising costs. Is this the right time to enforce such norms or the Government can take take other steps to de-stress the sector?

Time: 3-5 minutes for structuring your thoughts & 15-20 minutes for GD

Key Selection Criteria: It was important to make the right points. The panel was looking for the quality rather than quantity. As a matter of fact, I spoke the least in the whole GD (2 entries) amongst the group of 7.
interview_outline:
The interviews were more of a conversation rather than the conventional interviews per se.
Interview 1 - HR, Situational, Resume, Case
The first interview itself had all the elements of the type of questions one can think of.  It started with the normal introduction and then went on to discuss the internships which were in the Consumer Home durables sector. Based on my internship I was asked to list down the key drivers that influence consumer's purchase. I was then asked to solve a case which was based on the same industry that was facing issues with its cost structure. The interviewer added key facts to the case as I went through it. Then She asked about one of the PORs in my resume & asked about How I would handle a 'freeRider' in a team. 

Interviewer 2 - HR, Resume
The interviewer asked about my resume and then went on to ask the HR questions like What is the biggest learning of your life, Your hobbies, what is that one quality that differentiates you from others.

Interview 3 - Resume, Case
The interviewer asked me to walk him through the resume and then went on to the case. The case was regarding identifying key parameters that should be considered while analyzing cost synergies due to centralization of value chain elements with the advent of GST in the FMCG sector.

Interview 4 - Resume, HR
This was the partner round where the person asked me to walk him through the resume and then asked me the reason why am I opting for consulting as a career option. He asked me about my strengths and how have they helped me through different phases of my life.

Interview 5 - Resume
The final round was just an introduction about me with few resume points and then I was made the offer.
domain_questions: The cases were based on my internships. Rest already mentioned in the above answer.
hr_gk_questions: Already mentioned in the previous question
looking_for: They were looking for a person who would have worked in various fields and was ready to continue the same. They were looking for someone who adapts to new environment pretty quickly and has a rational though process.
right_wrong: I was not able to solve the first case properly and thus was not confident about getting through the first round. The good thing was even if I missed few things here and there, I didn't allow the flow of the conversation go interrupted.
tips: Being calm and understanding the fact that IT IS A CONVERSATION AND NOT AN INTERVIEW. The interviewer
dos_and_donts: Read the JD and the company report provided by prepCom thouroughly. Think about few GOOD questions to ask the interviewer.

pre_process_tips: Application > shortlist > preprocess (this preprocess is not a shortlisting criteria for further process. It is just for reference during pi. Few candidates were not even asked on this) > GD > PI (some people had second round of PI too)
gd_topics_tips:
Topic: Should Gd be compulsory in selection process

Guidelines: They ask everyone to introduce themselves for 30s before GD. State your internship here and this 30s is a chance to make an impression. Then GD. Then they ask everyone to summarize in 30s.
gd_duration: 10 mins of GD (excluding intro and summary)
no_interviews_duration: Mine was around 30 min and just one round. Few people had two rounds of PI.
interview_outline: 3-4 hrs for GD. Then they shortlisted around 30 people for PI. The PI was almost hr based. Currently the company is in growing face so most of the questions were what I want to do in future and which kind of life I expect from future. This aligns their goals with yours. Just one technical question that too practical related to their company.
domain_questions:
Currently the company wants to expand. We talked about Rebel Foods. The question was "If I ask you to launch a brand, will you expand it with cash flow positive or acquire customers at company's cost"


The answer I gave " Depends on few factors. One of them being the amount of funding I have and the brand perception from customer. If perception is not good and I dont see a good future, I ll go cash positive. If I see the brand has a lot of potential and I also funding to sustain, I ll acquire customers. This is a tradeoff."

He said yeah that's good. Sounded he was satisfied.
situational_questions: There were no situational questions for me.
hr_gk_questions:
1. Where do you see yourself 5 years down the line?
2. When wilk you be satisfied?
3. What do you want from life?
4. What is your ambition?
5. Don't you think you have already achieved alot?
6. Will you join Rebel Foods after 6 months ?

The answers were related to the introduction I gave.
looking_for: What I felt (just my view)is that they wanted to see if you are ambitious like them. They were set to grow and wanted the same enthusiasm but with a clear rationale .
right_wrong: I clearly stated that I was following a Rebel Foods and we talked about. At one point he asked me if I am joining their company just to switch to Rebel Foods later. I did explain that I am interest in their company because it has growth opportunities and Rebel Foods might give me just a stagnant role. So I won't switch. The way you put this argument matters. This can go wrong if not explained well.
tips: What I think helped for me is the knowledge and interest for their industry. The interest I have in my life for my career path aligned with theirs. Goal alignment worked for me.
dos_and_donts:
Do state upfront what you want from company. Detailed conversation of what exactly you want. This shows that you are really interested and you are very clear with what you want. Helps in aligning the interests. 

Also, ask questions, this will make them know that you know about the industry and really look forward to them.

While greeti g us for selections they said "you guys really pitched yourself well" What they look for is a pitch of yours.


All the best :)

pre_process_tips: After applying with the resume on reculta and filling up basic profile details on their website, there were 3 more rounds. 1 buddy round, 1 networking round, 2 interviews (both CV based for me- engg background).
interview_outline: Intro, followed by detailed discussion on the basis of what was said in the intro. Then why do you want to join the company, why this role, why interest in finance. Asked for my opinion on some recent trends in the industry- no explicit prior knowledge was required ( not expected as I am from engineering background). HR heavy (owing to non finance background)
domain_questions: 2 questions from ratio analysis studied in fac course.
hr_gk_questions: Started with 1 major project and interests, discussion on the project, followup HR questions like what were the problems faced, how did you solve, etc. Brief discussion on interests. Then asked why do you want to join DB, why this role, why interest in finance. Then brief discussion about recent trends in banking- what do you think would be the role of banks now that fintechs are coming up? Then some discussion around work hours, work life balance, culture at the bank (as a response to when I asked about it - they had asked if I had any questions). The second interview was also CV based mostly. Then there was discussion about the role of banks in the economy, some questions same as the first interview, 1 or 2 easy questions based on ratio analysis studied in fac.
looking_for: They were looking for genuine, hardworking and logical/analytical people. No extra knowledge was expected apart from the fac course.
right_wrong:
Good parts- my genuine interest in the projects and interests that I had mentioned, honest answers, trying to answer the questions which I was unaware of as best as I could, some knowledge about the recent trends in the industry helped in answering questions. The interviewers were nice.
Bad parts- think your answers through before answering, keep your cool
tips: Apart from properly preparing CV and NPAD, go through the JD and understand the role, company website - especially role related parts, recent news about the company, upcoming trends in the industry (for example, use of AI and ML in banking) to have something to talk about in the interview if asked and it shows your interest in the role. Prepare general questions related to the industry such as what is the functions performed, how is it beneficial to the economy, and definitely prepare questions related to why this company, role and interest in finance.
dos_and_donts: For non finance background people, they do not expect you to know much details about finance, only limited to the scope of FAC course. Make sure to neccesarily participate properly in Buddy round, and Networking round. The same people will be taking the interviews, so it's best to ask good and meaningful questions and make a good impression in networking round. My networking round was held at 9 pm and I had my interviews with the same people at 6 am. A good impression will definitely help there. ABSOLUTELY DO NOT GLOBE. They will point it out if you do, and will not get you a shortlist. Be genuine and honest. Talk about things/work that you did and you're proud of and have faith in yourself. All the best!

pre_process_tips: Online test consisting of questions from Quant, logical reasoning and 2 sets of data interpretation. Data interpretation question were moderately difficult others were easy.
interview_outline:
First round of interview started with introduction and walking them through my resume. 3 member panel including one HR.They asked in detail about my live project in market research and internship in NBFC sector. No questions about Kotak was asked. Then they asked to explain the JD in my words. Then asked about which are the marketing electives opted in the second year. But no concepts where asked. It was a balanced interview. 

Case 1: Kotak Mahindra bank mobile app at present is used by 20% of the total customers. How will you increase it to 30%? Design a campaign for the same?( 5 minutes where given to prepare)

Case 2: Currently you are the campaign manager for the bank. You are sending email to 5 lakh customers about the interest rate of fixed deposit which got revised currently to 10.50% from 10%. Instead of writing 10.50% you wrote 1.50%. You learned about the mistake after it was sent. What will you do at this moment? How will you handle the situation?

Second round of interview  was video interview. Asked to explain the JD completely. Asked about the family background. Asked to explain the work ex in detail.
domain_questions:
1) How will you handle an irate customer?( This was asked because I worked as a customer care executive)

Answered first try to empathize with the customer.Don't cut in while he is speaking. Give multiple solutions. If he/she is not satisfied ask them what are the resolution they are looking for.

2) Any data analysis tool used during MBA in any project or course?

Explained about Anova, Regression and Cross tabulation.
hr_gk_questions:
1) Explain about your leadership skills?

Explained I was the group leader during HOP and I used to take the lead in my friends circle. Interview was diverted to HOP since they were eager to Knew about the program. Answered about all the learning and difficulties faced during HOP.

2) Which will you prefer the most: Brand Name, Role offered and CTC?

Initially explained if the company is a good brand like Kotak hope they will be flexible enough with the role. Informed I never focused on a particular domain and my resume is the proof for that. But will be more happy with the current role offered since analytics has a great potential and future. Also answered Learning is important now and money can be earned enough if I can showcase my potential completely now. But they wanted a specific answer. Then informed Preference : 1) Brand: 50% 2) Role: 25% 3) CTC: 25%.
looking_for: People with marketing knowledge and customer facing work ex. They were very keen in asking about the details of the JD.
right_wrong: Mentioning HOP went well because I diverted the interview towards that. Talked for about 10 minutes about the same. Answering with confidence was important. Took time to prepare and answer both the cases asked. Didn't ask much questions during solving the campaign related case.
tips: Studied about data analysis methods from friends who learned market research. Also went through all the preparatory materials once and prepared notes from that.
dos_and_donts: Went through the company deck before the interview.  Study the JD completely.

pre_process_tips: Application form--> Gamified Psychometric test --> Shortlist for GD
gd_topics_tips:
1-Chairman GD: 8 candidates, 8 rounds, with each candidate being the chairman in one of the rounds.
2. Each round will have a case-based GD, mostly on a company scenario:
Theme of cases asked to our panel: declining profits, new market exploration, ad campaigns for a new or existing product, conflict management, and organization restructuring.
3. As chairman, remember that your main job is to facilitate the GD process (you can put in 1-2 points) and be cognizant of not overpowering other candidates in the panel. >>Also, the chairman summarizes the GD, so please note down the key points discussed during the round.
4. In other rounds, when you are not the chairman, perform as you do in normal GD and add actionable and tangible points to the case problem (the panel judged quality over quantity).
gd_duration: 1 hr. 12 mins, 8 rounds (8 mins per round + 1 min per case reading by coordinator)
interview_outline:
1. The interview was mostly focused on resume points and past work experience. Questions were asked about projects undertaken and the impact of the projects on customers and the company.
2. The interview was HR-balanced, and questions were asked on goals (both personal and professional), interests, and "why we should consider you over other candidates?".
domain_questions:
1. Quantum and Impact of Projects Handled; Process undertaken during project planning, development, testing, and execution; Monetary and non-monetary benefits of the project to the company and the customers
2. Questions were also asked on current market trends prevalent in the work-related industry (for me, questions were asked on new trends and tech in auto sector, i.e., EVs and FFVs, Scrappage policy)
hr_gk_questions:
1. What are your personal goals, and how will your professional life help you fulfill them?
Approach: Personal goals are mostly long-term goals. For a quick response, you can consider your personal goal as a second career or priority you want to pursue and excel at after you are in a settled position career-wise.
2. Why should we consider you over other candidates?
Approach: Basic NPAD question; going through your prepared NPAD at least once helps a lot in most HR questions
looking_for:
Almost all (if not all) candidates waiting for interviews had work experience. No questions on certifications were asked in my interview.
Qualities scoped: clarity of thought, diligence, and some social and current awareness
right_wrong: You might be called in the morning, but your interview might happen in the evening, so one important and understated aspect is to present yourself as an energetic and motivated candidate during the initial interaction with the interview panel.
tips: Mock GD and PI are helpful; use them as a dry run for your technical and NPAD preparation.
dos_and_donts:
1. For the Gen Man role, resume prep (i.e., being thorough with every point (whether true or exaggerated) on the resume) should be the foremost priority.
2. NPAD prep
3. Interest prep: pick one area/skill/interest and know it inside-out (you can actually use the "Tell me about yourself?" answer to guide your interview to this point); one of the interviewees, apart from a few HR and work-ex questions, had an interview primarily based on Moto GP.
4. Company-specific preparation is expected and does help, but don't spend excessive time on it (the panel assumes you might have prepared for the company and rarely asks questions about it; none were asked in mine).

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlisting followed by a case-based GD and 2 rounds of interview
gd_topics_tips:
Topic: The GD was about frauds related to credit card transactions.
pattern: We were asked to read a small write up on a topic related to fraudulent transactions through credit cards and hold discussions on 3 questions - how to understand whether a fraud has occurred or not?, how to use big data analytics to curb such frauds? and how to improve customer experience in such cases?
Time for discussion: 45 mins (15 mins for each topic). The moderator had explicitly mentioned that every one will get a chance to speak and the GD was very decent and went on smoothly.
Key selection criteria: Knowledge about big data analytics (brief knowledge will do), ability to structure your thoughts and articulate them well. They were looking for good points which were practically executable.
interview_outline:
First interview: Basic HR questions, questions on competitions won, my internship project and why Amex. Then I was asked if I had any questions. This was kind of a stress interview.
Second interview: Purely technical.
domain_questions: I was asked whether I had any experience in analytics or anything close to it. I talked about my internship project which was about analysis of data for segmentation and targeting doctors. I had taken up a course "Advanced Marketing Analytics" and was asked on linear and logistic regression, multicollinearity and variance inflation factor, p- value and machine learning basics. In relation to my academic project, which was about analysing financial ratios of Crompton Greaves, I was asking what ratios would I consider if a company approaches Amex for credit. Regarding my term paper in the course "Pricing", I was asked to explain the premise of the paper, t-test, f-test and the concept of ANOVA. Lastly, I was asked why I wanted to join Amex. This question can be answered well if one has done thorough research about the company and has gone into all possible details. It shows that you are really interested in what the company is doing.
hr_gk_questions: HR questions- run me through your resume, internship projects, competitions won, why did you do MBA and didn't take up a job after engineering? and why Amex?
looking_for: They were looking for people with either some kind of experience or a very keen interest in the field of data analytics. I don't have any work-ex in this domain but I think I was able to demonstrate the great amount of interest which I have in this area. Certifications on R/Python/Machine learning would definitely help.
right_wrong:
Good part: I was sure about whatever I said, for example, when I spoke about the course "Advanced Marketing Analytics", I was thorough with all the concepts taught. Speak about your interests and make sure you talk about topics which you are really well prepared with.

Bad part: I was not very well prepared with why Amex? Could have handled it better. A constant smile during stressful interviews always helps.
tips: Since I am really interested in analytics, I had done some online courses related to it.Mock GDs helped.
dos_and_donts: Try to read up as much as possible about the company, practice GDs on a regular basis, be thorough with your resume, go through the domain material shared by Prepcom.

pre_process_tips:
1. Application form on the company website
2. Written Test: Fundamentals based questions + Basic Excel Modelling
3. 1 Telephonic Interview, 2 Zoom Interviews
no_interviews_duration: 1 Telephonic Interview with VP: 20 minutes ; 1st zoom interview with GIR India Head: 15 minutes; 2nd zoom call Interview with VP: 30 minutes
interview_outline:
1. Telephonic Interview with VP-1 (1st Interview): Technical Heavy
Started with a brief introduction (I talked about my background: both family and academics, summer internship, a finance project on bank mergers, how I have been following markets and bitcoin); followed by a 10 minute long discussion on bitcoin: What's your opinion, is it overvalued or undervalued? how does it derive it's value? Do you see a herd mentality? (I talked about the why the value is soaring, movement of hedge funds and FIIs into crypto and retail investors, esp. Robinhood investors, looking for alternatives with better returns, what was my mindset when I put money in crypto, what have been the regulatory changes, growth of crypto in emerging nations specifically India); moved to a discussion on the markets: Why are the market indexes soaring? What's my take on it? ( I talked about record FII inflow, fiscal stimuluses across the globe, accommodative MP to support the excess liquidity and how it is being channelized, India's performance amongst the emerging nations and growth opportunities, also the movement of retail investors); finally I asked 2 questions: 1 was about the interviewer's journey in the firm and 2nd about bitcoin which turned into a small discussion)  


2. Zoom Interview with GIR India Head (2nd Interview): HR Heavy
Started with a brief introduction (same as above), Why I want to make a career in GS? What did I do different from my batchmates do get a good rank (5/590)?, Where do I come from? Basic questions about my family. Are you comfortable coming to Bangalore? My experience with coding languages (I knew R and showed willingness to learn new languages), 2 things I want to change about myself. I got to ask her about the GIR India unit: how it has transformed over years and how her responsibilities have changed, what markets do we cover and a follow up question on regulatory changes in EU & as analysts do we get to attend earnings calls.     

3. Zoom Interview with VP-2  (3rd Interview): Technical Heavy
Started with a brief Introduction (same again), what attracts my interest in the GIR role? Lot of questions on Bitcoin (a majority mentioned above in Interview 1, adding only new topics of discussions)- intrinsic value, speculative investments, drawing parallels/contrasts between Crypto and other alternative investments like gold, holding trends.
We moved to markets with discussion on Banking (the interviewer asked for my preference), some stocks recommendations, performance of banking recently. 
This was followed by questions on valuation: How do you value banks specifically retail banks? (both absolute and relative terms, which ratios to use, what's the FCFF). Finally, he asked some HR questions: Situations where I faced conflict-management issues, where I come from and my interests.
domain_questions: Try to make your answers more conversational, add examples from current affairs.
situational_questions: Answered above
hr_gk_questions: Answered above
looking_for: Sound technical knowledge backed by good logic and evidence
right_wrong: If you follow a trend, mention it. Elaborate on it with the right logic, the more you can support with current affairs, the better.
tips: Smile and stay confident, that's the most important

pre_process_tips: Application on Reculta, GD, Interviews
gd_topics_tips:
E-commerce vs small stores
The panel wanted everyone to speak, so everyone was given a chance to speak. The logical points and building on to other's points were appreciated. Having a different opinion wasn't necessary but new points even when everyone is agreeing on the topic was helpful.
no_interviews_duration: 2 interviews, about 15 mins technical, and 20 mins HR
interview_outline:
Technical Interview:
Started with introduction. Then talked about internships and the learnings from my projects. They asked about why I wanted to join the company and the career trajectory here, why I wanted the Sales & Marketing role when I've already done a similar internship before and would I be open to working in different locations. The interview was mainly resume/ HR based.

HR Interview:
Started with a personal introduction, asked to talk about family. Why MBA and Why Marketing were asked. They asked about my internship experience and wanted to know how I would handle different situations with regards to internship location- a completely new place or if I don't know the language. Was looking for personal stories etc

Both the interviews were very NPAD based, and since I had an internship with a FMCG company, they focussed on that.
domain_questions: No technical questions. One question about the company was the expected career trajectory post the internship. Doing some research and being specific with the roles and timeline here would have been helpful.
hr_gk_questions:
I was asked about my internship, my addition to the projects and my learnings. Knowing about all this, and about the company and its operations was useful.
Both interviews were HR heavy. I was asked about why MBA (IPM), why S&M, why FMCG and why Haleon. There were situational questions as to what I would do if I was assigned a role in a new place. I was asked of a time that I overcame a language barrier/ if not, how would I approach the situation. Personalising all the answers based on past experience/ stories was helpful. I tried to talk about internships/ PORs whenever possible.
No current affair questions.
looking_for: Knowledge and understanding of the FMCG industry along with dedication to work (there were many questions on how willing would I be to work given a particular location/ situation).
right_wrong:
Being thorough with my resume and NPAD helped immensely as the interviews were primarily based on that. I could have been more prepared with company specific questions- why Haleon, the career trajectory and basic research.
Converted.
tips: Researching on the company and being familiar with what they do, how they were formed, values etc. Since technical questions weren't asked- preparatory material was not needed. The mock GD was helpful as you get to know how to enter and how to structure your points. The PIs were helpful as you get to know the wide range of questions an interviewer can ask. The most helpful was the preparation of NPAD and its iteration- I got to know what all to focus on while answering the questions based on my profile.
dos_and_donts: Alongside resume and NPAD, being prepared with how the things you've done/ courses you have studied can help you in your internship. Also knowing about some unique S&M concept which you can talk about or include in your answers

pre_process_tips: Aptitude Assessment Test (around 1 hour) on AMCAT.
gd_topics_tips: Future of EV in India
interview_outline: Interview was very much balanced. There were 2 interviewer. One was the senior sales manager and other one was the HR manager. The interview started with introduction and then 2-3 question on family background which has been asked to specify during introduction. Then, one situation based question on the values which company incorporate. Interviewer also asked about the Job Description and about my preference among different roles offered in S&M. After that most of the question was related to my internship. The interview asked me technical question on my internship experience. It was stress interview and they will grilled me on my internship experience.
domain_questions: I did data analysis in my internship. So they asked me about the process which I followed while doing data analysis. They also asked me what type of analysis which I have performed (prescriptive, descriptive or predictive) on the data and what kind of challenges which I have faced while doing that work. Else, there were no cross questioning from the interviewer. Also no domain question further.
situational_questions:
HR specified the values which company believes in and then asked me which value I felt most connected with. I told him one of the value. Then he gave me one situation where I have to show that character.
Value which I told: Courage
Situation: You are the manager. You have to achieve overall sales target. Company is pushing new bike in the market but it failed to gain popularity. You are responsible to invest your total resources either on new bike or on the core products so as to achieve your overall sales target. What will you do?
Interviewer response on my answer: He grilled me on my decisions. And then he sighed and moved on to next question.
hr_gk_questions: HR questions were related to family background and my hobbies. Not very much has been asked from HR perspective.
looking_for: They were looking for Resilience, good communication, etiquettes. Also your internship experience. They were also looking at how you can handle stressful situation.
right_wrong: Overall Interview went good. I felt my communication fell short while dealing with questions where he was putting stress on me. I could have taken more time to structure my answers. But as the interview proceeded, most of the things went right.
tips: I was thorough with my introduction. I used STAR approach for preparing my resume points. I focused on basics of the sales and marketing. I also solved cases based on profitability, market growth, GTM strategy.  I also created one document where I wrote all the major learning which I got from subjects so that I can discuss for more than 5 minutes in the interview on each subjects. Primer from prepcom were really helpful. Gave mock interview to my friends.
dos_and_donts: Be strong and defend your answers no matter how much they will ridicule your answers. Don't let your previous answers affect your next answers as it will be stress interview. Be thorough with your resume and especially with your internships, live projects and electives. Do read the job description before the interview. Keep smiling and be positive.

pre_process_tips: Direct PI if shortlisted
interview_outline: There were 3 panelist. The interview had a mix of Technical (Electrical + Finance), Power Sector Industry, HR Questions, Hobbies, bit of General Knowledge and questions about the company. So, it was a balanced Interview.
domain_questions:
Tell what you know of  the power sector of India
What is the power consumption in India? Why is it low ?
Which has more losses among Power generation, transmission and distribution ? And why ? What can you do to improve that power system ?
What do you see in a company when they approach you for funds ?
Questions on ratios.
How will you devise your project execution plan from the DPR ?
What is the business model of PFC ?
What do you know about PFC ?
In depth questions on Workex and Internship.
situational_questions:
Do you think short term or long term ? 
Being a south Indian why do you want to shift to North India (since the posting would be in Delhi). Isnt it too cold here in the North ?
I had mentioned that my hobby was to read Bhagavad Gita, and they were impressed by it. So, they started asking pragmatic questions about it like tell which shloka you connect to deeply? etc.
hr_gk_questions:
Since my hobby had about playing a musical instrument, they asked the famous musician of that instrument from my home state.
CSR activities done by PFC
Why should we hire you ?
Why do you want to be a part of PFC ?
Present Solar Power generation of India?
Do you read newspaper? Which one? Tell me two recent news that you read about Power sector of India.
looking_for: Someone who understand the Power Sector, Project Financing and who is reliable.
right_wrong:
I had another final interview of a foreign company post this, so I was literally chilled out as I had a backup even if I don't convert this. So, this boosted my confidence and we ended up having a very friendly conversation during the due course of interview. Post half my interview and getting through the technical part, they started shooting some stress questions in Hindi, to see how I answer them back. I was infact enjoying these questions more and gave witty answers, that probably helped. I knew that my interview was last, so they would have been exhausted by the time they came to my slot, which as at 8:30 pm, so I tried to keep it a joyful conversation to raise my chances of conversion.
Yes, I converted PFC.
tips: Just be yourself. Unlike a private firm, these folks are government heads, so they want people with strong ethics and sincere lads. So, dont globe around and just say what you are at the core.
dos_and_donts: I went through their entire website. Also being from Electrical background , I could answer their technical questions related to it with more details. Also, my work ex involved working on the ground level in some of their projects funded by them, so I could give clear picture of where their projects could have improved. I revised my electrical engineering knowledge and delved into the insights of my workex.

pre_process_tips: Video Based Interview; about 7 questions ranging from your understanding of the role, the domain, the skills you have. The expected duration of each answer was supposed to be 3 mins, but I only spoke till I felt I was adding something relevant, typically for 1.5 mins.
interview_outline: The first round was taken by a panel of two people working in the same role. They asked me about my resume, one PoR, my summer internship and anything else that I'd like to speak about that I hadn't mentioned till then. They tried to focus more on roles that had communication or market research involved.  Second round was HR, it was more of a confirmatory interview after their final shortlist. Mostly asked about my understanding of the role.
domain_questions: I was shortlisted for the life sciences role, so they asked me about my understanding of the domain; I had an internship in the related field so it helped. They asked me about possible applications of the domain that I could think of, and what were the current products being offered. Then they asked me about the role of tech and internet in the growth of startups(mentioned actual examples like some startups in the Edtech and Retail domain, etc.), and then asked me to list out the shortcomings of using tech and internet for startups. I talked about the growth of startups using tech and IT such as Byju's, Classplus or Teachmint, which had made a niche in a saturated market. Same with the advent of online shopping. Mentioned Covid as a catalyst in their growth and how companies established in the domain are now following their footprint (Online shopping platforms by HUL, etc. and Byju's acquiring coaching institutes). For shortcomings I mentioned lesser focus being paid on the actual product, while promotions and development is only continued on building the platform. Mentioned complaints by parents, or a lack of one-to-one teaching like in offline tuition without taking any names.
situational_questions: Listed a situation where people had been arguing in a group and did not listen to each other, and my role as a moderator in order to make them cooperate. Listed out the possible reasons for the conflict, such as frustration out of not being understood, opposing views presented, underestimating the ideas of the participants, etc. For a solution I proposed each member getting the opportunity to present his ideas while the others in the team are tasked with paraphrasing what he said till the speaker is satisfied. This will ensure a sound understanding of every member's points, after which they can continue their discussion.
looking_for: Domain knowledge, thinking and problem solving skills
right_wrong: Didn't stress during difficult questions, took my time in forming an answer, mentioned my thinking when I wasn't ready with an answer.
tips: Be very through with the resume, think of possible questions that can be asked for each point in the resume, have a strong intro ready, and be prepared to speak for about 2 minutes for every point mentioned in the resume. Be aware of recent developments in the market, like any IPOs released, possible acquisitions, etc.
dos_and_donts: Don't get nervous I guess

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlisting and then personal interviews
interview_outline:
Started with introduction, went into resume details, focusseed on work ex, questions about self and HR based. Situational questions related to the role offered to gauge ability of thinking on the feet, past experiences to judge the candidates on their leadership principles. Focus on the result part and use numbers to show impact.

They will note down everything that you tell them and that is cross checked across interviews.

One simple puzzle was asked to test your ability to think on your feet.
domain_questions:
No technical question related to any course at all. Overall work ex and projects done without delving into technical details but focus on behavioural aspects.

Situational questions to check your overall understanding of the role and sector.
hr_gk_questions:
Describe your work ex. What was your internship about. Your roles in the various projects mentioned on your resume.

What do you understand about the role? How do you think you fit in the role? 

Then experiences from past where you showed leadership skills, went beyond your call of duty, manged time, worked independently and as a group, influenced someone, biggest achievement, biggest failure, what did you learn from those experiences and how you used those or will use those in the future?

Approach: Don't panic, don't be in a hurry to answer, articulate properly, use numbers to show the impact. By numbers you don't necessarily have to impact the bottom line or top line of a company. Simple improvements or optimization in your work like reducing the time required for something by 30%. Helped or managed a group of 4 or 5 people etc.
looking_for: People having qualities that match their leadership principles and who can think on their feet, good negotiators, people good in communicating their thoughts
right_wrong: You are fine as long as you are discussing and interacting things with them. They don't generally put you under pressure unless they want to check your composure. Interviews were steered by them mostly as they had questions in mind already based on your resume.
tips:
Basic domain knowledge would help as the interviews are not technical. Remain calm and composed as they are judging you mostly on your traits. 

Remember you are in an interview, not a question and answer viva. So converse with the interviewer, clarify your doubts, take your time to gather your thoughts, smile, before you answer any question.

Have some mock interviews with friends to understand how effectively you are able to communicate your thoughts
dos_and_donts:
Go through their leadership principles (14). Have situations prepared from your past work ex or MBA life where you can link the leadership principles. As many examples as you can since this is the main focus of the interviews. Be as detailed as possible since they would dig deep into every answer. 

Having numbers and result oriented situations is an advantage.

Don't create situations/numbers out of thin air unless you are sure that you can manage it. Cross checking of your answers are done across rounds by various means.

Defend your answers as you will be grilled but don't argue with the interviewer.

pre_process_tips:

hr_gk_questions: HR question were there in the video submission and not much in interviews
