pre_process_tips: The pre-process for Capgemini Chrysalis is a Psychometric test. This test is around 45 minutes long and consists of a few memory games to test deductive and inductive reasoning abilities. Along with that, there are about 100 questions related to your personality and work ethic. If you are not good at GDs and want to bypass them, take this test very seriously.
no_interviews_duration: There were 2 interviews. The first interview was about 15 minutes and the second interview was less than 10 minutes.
interview_outline:
There were two interviews.
Interview 1 - Technical heavy (15 minutes)
Q1 What do you know about this role?
Q2 What are your value proposition
Q3 Any experience in market research
Q4 What were the challenges that you faced and how did you handle them?
Q5 How different is it to conduct a market research for College students with that of Companies and Businesses?
Q6 You have to conduct a market research for a company. Take us through the process and how you will go about it.
Q7 What do you know about Capgemini?
Q8 Any IT related experience?
Q9 Rate your presentation and designing skills
Q10 Any Questions for us?

Interview 2 - HR heavy (8-10 minutes)
Q1 Tell me about yourself.
Q2 You mentioned you have good leadership skills. Can you give me an example of this from your past experience?
Q3 Where do you see yourself in 10 years?
Q4 What is your area of improvement?
Q5 How will your strengths help you in this role?
domain_questions: To answer such questions, I took help from the Research Methodology classes and also from the experience I had of conducting a market research for an organization.
hr_gk_questions: No CA questions. HR questions are same as mentioned above.
looking_for: They were looking for candidates who are enthusiastic about the role and have enough practical knowledge about it. They prefer people with good presentation & designing skills and thus your PORs can be very helpful here.
right_wrong: Before entering the interview round, I wasn't aware of the role and the first question they asked me was about the role. So I guessed the role and ended with a question. Most of my answers were ending with the question to make the interview more like a conversation/discussion. I thought this would lead to a bad impression but I was still able to convert the interview. I think this was because I didn't pretend to know the answer to it and was honest about not knowing it.
tips: The Company Deck was my go-to material for every interview to research about the company. It has enough information for you to be able to speak about the company in the interview. NPAD helped me the most during my HR interview. Through my Mock PI, I was able to refine my HR answers which was very important.
dos_and_donts: An important tip from my side. Just writing the answers for NPAD is not enough. Tell a story, video record your answers, re-watch and look for improvements. Do this as frequently as possible. This should help you come out as natural during the interview. Also, learn about the values of the company and use them in your answers whenever possible but don't over do it.

pre_process_tips: First, resume shortlist. Initially a video recorded assessment was scheduled to happen, but got cancelled due to technical issues. Later, we were asked to submit a 1 minute introduction video. You can be a little creative so as to stand out from others.
interview_outline: Started with basic introduction. Asked if I keep myself updated with ongoing news, if yes then how, what platforms, newspaper, online, etc. Asked what type of news you read, and what type does your father read? Is there any difference? What things you would want your father to know, and what does your father want you to know. How do you act in stressful situations, give examples. Asked questions about my POR, and asked me how the work I did there is related to what HT media does. What do I know about HT media? I'm I a paid subscriber of mint news? How many students in your college are paid subscribers? How can you increase with number, come up with a marketing strategy. Give proper numbers keeping in mind HT Media is present nationally. Why do you want to join HT media? Why do you think you are a correct fit? Which city you prefer working in?
domain_questions:
What do you know about HT media? Different types of new platforms. Why do you want to join, are you the right fit for the organization? 
I did full thorough research about the company before itself, website, social media. I was also prepared with answers for these questions, since these were the basic ones. For the question why I want to join and if I'm the correct fit, I first told why HT media. I was always curious to know the working of the media industry, and how a typical day is at the workplace. Mentioned what kind of people work there according to their values and linked my characteristics to that. They were satisfied with all my answers and didn't cross question. 
About the technical question regarding marketing strategy, they asked many follow up questions and wanted me to mention the specific stats.
hr_gk_questions: Asked me if I was aware of any ongoing news, how did I come across that news
looking_for: They were looking for an enthusiastic person who had knowledge about their organization and the domain. There were 3 panel members. It was a very conservational interview, and I always had a smile while answering.
right_wrong: I was not confident with my numbers, couldn't estimate them properly, as I was not prepared  for a guesstimate question at all. But with some basic population knowledge, I gave them some stats, they didn't question me though. More than the stats, I focused on the strategy and its result. So, they were convinced by it, and I successfully converted the interview.
tips: Prepcom materials were very useful, sector reports, domain sessions and ppts, and company decks. Go through the current affairs sheet also. Mock GD/PI were very important, I got to know where I stand, and how much more should I prepare to crack the interview
dos_and_donts: Just be confident, be you and keep smiling.

pre_process_tips: Case Submission: Problem Statement was "Imagine you are running a new team at a major ecommerce company tasked with dramatically increasing the number of customers creating a wishlist." Case submission was first screening round. I followed CIRCLES framework for case submission. Make a good presentation as it will have impression in the interview.
interview_outline: Both interviews were technical. They started with introduction & then had 3 questions in both interviews. From resume they only asked about my engineering project. They asked "Why Phone Pe" as well.
domain_questions:
First Interview: 
Tell me about yourself.
Guesstimate (How many ACs sold in India in a year?)
As a product manager of WhatsApp what will you do to stop spamming of fake news
Root Cause Analysis: As a product manager at Phone Pe you go in the office on Tuesday to find out that app visitors declined by 40% yesterday. What would be possible reasons? (I approached the problem from external factors including economic factors, then went to internal factors like problems with app, upgrades, etc. He was satisfied with my answer. Interviewer asked me to think from another approach. I threw problems at him by considering customer journey on Phone Pe & what problems might have happened at each stage.)
Second Interview:
Tell me about yourself.
What is your favorite product & why? (I talked about Myntra.) 
If you have to design a competitive app for Myntra how you will go about it? (I talked about delays in delivery, competition with brick & mortar stores- suggested going hyperlocal. I did Myntra Competition where problem statement was about going hyperlocal. I told this to interviewer. He was impressed with same.)
As a product manager, what will you do to reduce order cancellations on Myntra? (Identified reasons why there are order cancellations & then recommended solutions)
Asked about cryptography project from engineering.
hr_gk_questions: Why Phone Pe. I was prepared for this question beforehand & had 4-5 solid reasons which I spoke in interview. Look for these reasons in JD, PPT & company deck.
looking_for: They definitely were looking for critical thinking. They were more interested in breadth than depth. Interviewer saying anything else you can think of was constant throughout interviews.
right_wrong:
I think in both interviews I took time for structuring my thoughts and involved interviewers. They many times helped as well when I couldn't think of answers. 
Knowing about Phone Pe was crucial. When I was solving RCA question in 1st interview about Phone Pe I described 3 verticals in Phone Pe operate. That showed my interest & knowledge about company. 
I would have prepared for guesstimate better by practicing.
tips: The material shared by Prep Com is really useful. Seek A Mentor session on prod man was good. It really helped to understand what kind of questions are asked in the interview. Other than this there are many YouTube Videos which can help in the preparation. You can look to recent interview experiences of the companies you are applying & competitive companies. I found these 2 interviews useful for prod man interviews : https://youtu.be/DSV-vuvmIro, https://youtu.be/ZoCOzFSDrxY)

pre_process_tips:
Interview
Round 1: Guesstimate cum case round
Round 2: Questions related to workex followed by case
Round 3: HR questions and profile based questions as to why the candidate is the right fit for the role
no_interviews_duration: 3 (Round 1 - 40 minutes, Round 2 - 45 minutes and Round 3 - 20 minutes)
interview_outline: All the three rounds of interview started off with quick rounds of introduction followed by questions based on resume and work experience (technical heavy). This was followed by a guesstimate and case rounds for round 1 and and round 2. Round 3 was purely based on HR questions and assessing how the candidate is a right fit for the job role.
domain_questions: One of the technical questions asked in the interview was from my work experience - What are some of the changes that you'd make to the GeM platform (Govt. e-marketplace). So, here they are basically testing how much in depth knowledge you have when it comes to the projects that you have worked on. I framed my answer in a structured manner and stated as many relevant points as possible.
hr_gk_questions: HR questions - Why Deloitte? What are some of the things that you'd want Deloitte to make? What do you bring to the table having worked in an oil and gas company (answered it with a real life situation - like what I'd bring to the table in case of an M&A project)
looking_for: Someone who is able to strike a conversation and take control of the interview, shows genuine curiosity and enthusiasm about what they do and is able to think on their feet and communicate the same effectively
right_wrong: I answered the questions asked from the resume well, I had prepared the technical details well. I answered the HR based questions about the company and the role were answered well. I converted the interview
tips: Prep com preparatory materials like the decks, NPAD, Mock PI, various casebooks (IIM I, FMS and IIM A); Consulting prep sessions with consulting club mentors, seniors and batch mates helped me crack this interview
dos_and_donts:
Express your genuine enthusiasm for the role and the company. Use positive language, such as "I'm really excited about the opportunity to work here because..." or "I'm impressed with the company's recent accomplishments, and I'd love to be a part of that."
When you're asked a question, don't just give a brief answer and wait for the next question. Instead, engage in a back-and-forth discussion. You can say something like, "That's a great question. In my previous role, I faced a similar situation, and here's how I approached it. Does that align with what you're looking for in this position?"
Instead of saving your questions for the end of the interview, ask questions throughout the conversation. These can be clarifying questions about the role or company, questions about the interviewer's experience, or questions related to the discussion. This demonstrates your interest and helps keep the conversation flowing.
Pay close attention to what the interviewer is saying. React to their comments with nods, smiles, and verbal cues like "I see" or "That's interesting." This shows that you're engaged and interested in the conversation.

pre_process_tips:
Screening test consisting of 2 sections.
1. Aptitude Test (Critical thinking, Logical Reasoning) 25 mins for 25 questions
2. Data Interpretation (3 small caselets with 3 questions each) 25 mins for 9 questions
gd_topics_tips:
GD Topic: Is India ready for Electrical Vehicles?
GD Structure: 8-10 participants in one panel. The panel instructed that no one would cut each other and everyone would get a chance to speak. So, the GD went on pretty smoothly.
Tips: Speak twice/thrice (would be enough). Give others a chance to speak as well; don't impose yourself. Speak comprehensive points when you get a chance (2-4 minutes) that add value to the discussion.
interview_outline:
The interview started with a discussion about the GD. I initiated the conversation by telling them how I liked the GD style of the panel and how it reflects the company's culture. The next question entailed any mistakes that I made during the GD, and went towards a discussion of the company's culture. (I was able to show my interest and the fact that I know alot about the company, this reflected positively on my performance). Rest of the questions were mostly based on my experiences, along with a few HR questions. The interview ended on a light-hearted note with us sharing a few personal stories. 
Overall, the interview was mostly HR-based. No technical questions were asked. And the panel (of 2 members) made the interview really chill & comfortable.
domain_questions: No specific domain/ industry related questions.
situational_questions:
1. Tell us about a project that you worked on, but you regret doing.
2. Tell us about a project that you're proud of.
hr_gk_questions:
1. Which companies value do you admire the most? (I had set the context regarding values of the company)
- Tried to initiate discussion about the company myself. It showed my interest in the company.
2. Strengths (at least 4-5)
3. Weaknesses (at least 3)
- Be prepared with these many strengths and weaknesses. Make sure the strengths are something that help your role at the job. The weaknesses should be reflected such that you're trying to improve those.
looking_for:
Cultural fit for the company! 
There were no technical questions at all. They just wanted to make sure that the candidate fits into the culture of the company. (Which is very informal and focuses a lot on people; customers, employees alike)
right_wrong:
I kept the discussion very light-hearted, tried to include instances about my life myself; sharing stories. Tried to initiate conversation about the company culture and values and what I like about it. 
Converted the interview!
tips:
1. Have thorough knowledge about the company and try to bring it into conversations.  Company decks can be helpful. 
2. Be aware of the industry trends and news about the domains affecting the company you're sitting for. 
3. Prepare thoroughly for the domain you're applying for. Even if there are no technical questions, you would feel much more confident.
4. For marketing prep, refer to preparatory material shared by Mercuri as well apart from material shared by Prepcom.

pre_process_tips: No forms or pre-processes. CV based shortlisting and then direct interviews (2).
no_interviews_duration: 2 (10-15 minutes each), and one final interview for providing offer letter
interview_outline:
Interview 1: Started with saying something about yourself. Asked a bit about 2 hobbies I mentioned (acting and t-shirt painting). Professional aspirations (I mentioned IT and then moving into Operations as it was my 2nd preference). Give a scenario where IoT can be implemented and what potential threats can you see in an IoT based system (I mentioned APT - Advanced Persistent Threat and they asked me to elaborate about it). Are you willing to travel pan India? Any questions for us? (I asked if they are working on any Blockchain projects in India).
Interview 2: Mostly HR questions. General aspirations and career aspirations. Why PwC, and not, say, Infosys Consulting? How flexible are you when it comes to learning something entirely new? Your strength (give some examples)? What is the meaning of career to you?

Both interviews, not too technical. Will ask a bit about the jargons you throw around.
domain_questions: What kind of an organization can implement IoT? What is APT (Advanced Persistent Threat)?
hr_gk_questions:
Most HR questions were about flexibility with new projects/domains/technologies. I gave an example talking about my internship and how it was a completely alien industry and still, I learnt and eventually solved a business problem for the organization.
Asked about hobbies. Just wanted to gauge interest in the hobby and how passionate you are about it. 
Career aspirations - mentioned IT and then move to Operations
Why PwC - said that it gives me a platform to stay challenged all the time and also gives me an opportunity to move to some other domain/industry if I want; they get repeat clients and have a big name and so, would be a great place to start my career.
Meaning of career: as long as I stay challenged in whatever I am doing, I have a career. If I start getting bored, it's time to switch.
Any questions for us? - Are you currently working on any blockchain projects? Which industry in India is more likely to be taking this up faster? Are there any barriers to its adoption?
looking_for: Someone with a general idea about the profile, looking forward to learn. They didn't have a problem with my limited knowledge about IoT or Blockchain. But they were happy that I was very keen to learn.
right_wrong: I put in some IT jargons that I could talk for a bit about, when they asked about my career aspirations. The interview pretty much went in the direction of whatever I was talking about. Nothing out of the blue.
tips: Read up the Prepcom material on Cybersecurity and IoT, and a few articles on PwC India website and that helped me talk about those topics in the interview.
dos_and_donts: Both interviews were pretty chill and they wanted to take people. So there's no need to be anxious or nervous. They are simply looking for people who have a fair idea about the job, and are willing to learn.

pre_process_tips: We had a 45 min screening test based on Data Interpretation and Logical reasoning.
interview_outline: There were two members in the panel. One was a senior associate and one was manager of the team. Interview started with tell me about yourself. I was asked questions regarding my work experience and internship only. Then we went into a guesstimate which lasted for about 20 min. Then we went on to a case study on new product introduction. It was completely interviewer guided.  I started with a basic framework to check viability of introduction in terms of breakeven. The interviewer asked me to find out market size and consider competition to see how much of market share can be captured. The case also went into pricing later. Towards the end they also asked me solutions to enter the market. Overall, it depends on the interviewer in which direction the case would go into be ready to improvise. Post the case study just some situtation based questions were asked. Post that they asked one question on permutation and combination nothing difficult just easy peasy to through you off guard. Something related to indian economy and its performance. Once the interview was done they asked me whether I had any questions for them. I asked them questions regarding  what kind of projects do they deal with and also what kind of projects they were dealing with in online retail banking.
domain_questions: Be prepared for questions related to technical terms in your resume also some people were asked questions from the electives they have mentioned.
situational_questions: A situation where you were criticised and how did you deal with it?
hr_gk_questions: What do you think of the economy? Comment on inflation in India.
looking_for: Be humble. Then will put you under stress just stay calm and composed throughout the interview. Since it is consulting they are looking for problem solving, problem structuring and good communication skills.
right_wrong: I think I took time solving cases and guesstimates and did not give proper recommendations in the end but I improvised well when the interviewer asked me to change the direction. Just handle your stress well and don't give up till the end. Have a fresh mind before interview it will help a lot.
tips: Practice cases and guesstimates. IIM C casebook is good to start with easy cases will give you confidence. For challenging cases solve IIM A and SPJMR case book. Some detailed case experiences are given in ISB case book you can go through it to understand what cases are generally asked in different companies. Know the value chains, growth drives, important performance metrics of each industry. Be thorough with current affairs especially for finance interviews try to understand the broader implications. Practice cases in interviewer interviewee mode it is better than just solving on your own.
dos_and_donts: It is good to have understanding of basic data analytics(R)  and data visualization tools (Tableau) from what I have seen a lot of companies are interesed in them these days.

pre_process_tips: No pre-process
interview_outline:
Interview 1 - Balanced interview. Started with a self introduction and then moved on to questions about work experience and internship. Asked a number or questions on where cybersecurity was most required in my previous work experience, importance given to cybersecurity in India and general  questions about Cyber threats. Asked about current political state in India. Finished off by asking about a extra-curricular resume points and HR questions(Why do you want to switch fields, biggest learning from MBA) 
Interview 2- Deeper questioning on past work experience+HR(biggest strength and weakness, why consulting) 
Interview 3- HR interview(why pwc, why consulting, what do you bring to the table)
domain_questions: Where cybersecurity was most required in my previous work experience, importance given to cybersecurity in India and general  questions about Cyber threats( types, how to control, which was most common, examples). Having worked in an IT field, I was able to find ways to link it with the qns.
hr_gk_questions: Current state of Indian politics(Did not want to bring politics into the discussion, so explained the general state of India right now and that I would not like to comment on the political aspect, that seemed to be the answer panel was looking for). Compare Indian's technological advancement with the rest of the world( spoke about state of IT sector, lack of implementation 9f cybersecurity, large skilled workforce)
looking_for: They seemed to be looking for synergies in previous work exp with the current role. They tried to pick up seemingly less important points in the resume and ask deeply about that. They seemed to appreciate the fact that I had a smile and remained composed through the interview even when the questions were a bit difficult.
right_wrong: I could tie a lot of my previous work to the current role. Some of the questions about filler points in my resume threw me off a bit, but managed to stay composed and gave convincing answers. I also had a few good questions prepared to ask the interviewer at the end which started a conversation. However more preparation on technical knowledge of cybersecurity may have given me a bit more of an edge. But tried to show my interest in the the topic even if I didn't know every answer
tips: Reading articles and reports by HBR, Mckinsey, Deloitte etc gave me certain facts and figures I could use to make answers not sound like globe. The prepcom repository gives you a base knowledge of IT so you have a general idea. Used it to identify keywords to Google for good reports
dos_and_donts:
Do :- 
Know every single line on your resume inside out.
Read up on your industry and know recent developments
Read the job description and try to link past experience to that.
Have an example or experience to back points you mention
Have a smile or pleasant expression throughout the interview 
Don't
Get flustered in case you don't get the answer. 
Try to answer questions you know nothing about.

pre_process_tips: Filling Application Form, Shortlist, PI
interview_outline:
Started with introduction (make sure to make at least one point which makes you different from others), asked some general question from the sector, why this sector, went into resume details and asked question from UG projects, your career will start from WFH are you sure you are okay with it, which role you would prefer with customer facing or back office (some grilling here), any question for us, Converted
It was a Balanced interview, you just need to be confident and ready with your answers.
domain_questions:
Some basic concepts about bank, like How many types of banking are there, what is the difference between public and private bank, explain bank in simple language, GDP.
Just read a little about banking sector.
hr_gk_questions:
There were 3 interviewers, one asked me about the sector, other one asked me questions from the academic projects I did in my UG and last one was observer.

Tip : When asked about projects, remember that you have worked on it for months, now you'll have to explain it to someone who has no idea about it, prevent using technical jargons and explain the interviewer in the most amazing way possible, they'll appreciate it, cuz that is exactly what a marketer needs to know, use stories to explain the toughest of concepts in simplest way possible. 

They asked me why banking sector and about different types of banking.

Tip: You need to justify how Banking sector provides you a wholesome understanding of different customer insights and how you can put it to use. Also, make sure you have some basic understanding of this sector this will be helping you to make story

Finally ASK them something interesting based on your the research on the company. And make sure one question should be from the role and other about the bank.
looking_for:
They did not have a bar on workex, since I was a fresher straight out of college. 
I could say they expected an all round balanced resume. Also someone who look at a problem differently and come up with some new ideas to solve them.
right_wrong:
There were three Good things-
- I gave a very satisfactory reason behind why banking sector
- I was confident and enthusiastic about the interview, which helped me alot during interview
-I asked relevant questions in the end. That showed that I had read the JD and was keen on trying to be the best fit for the role
tips:
-Be thorough with the NPAD questions. 
-Make sure you know everything about your resume, like if you have written that in an academic project you researched and analyzed about something than you should know what you researched and what you analyzed and how. Also, some of its finding 
-Be super confident and super enthusiastic with stories ready for every point of your resume.
-Most important- You should know how to communicate difficult ideas in simple words without jargons

interview_outline:
There were two rounds of interviews—

1. Case Round + Management Experience (Summer Internship for freshers)

The interview began with my introduction.

I was asked about my summer internship, including why I did it, how I did it, and its impact. 
I was asked some basic domain questions about what companies I am aiming for and what their client bases are. What are the skills required for consulting?

The second half of the interview involved a profitability case that a restaurant chain in Mumbai is currently facing. 

2. Case Round + Consulting Domain Knowledge

Focus on how genuinely I wanted to get into consulting. Questions involved what companies I was aiming for other than the Big 4. Leaving consulting aside, what are the other domains I was preparing for in my placements? Why as a fresher I should be hired, and how will I cope with the work that is required at KPMG?

The second half involved a case in which a Chinese automobile manufacturer wants to enter the Indian market; I had to help him decide whether he should. It was an interviewee-led discussion. I asked to tell what questions I'll be asking the interviewer, and I had to apply the framework to come to a conclusion on my own for market entry.
domain_questions:
1. Why do you want to pursue consulting?
2. Tell me about the other consulting firms, other than the "Big Four"?
3. What are the consulting companies working in the field of healthcare (my summer internship industry)? 
4. Leaving consulting out, what are the other domains that you were targeting in your placement prep?
hr_gk_questions:
You are a fresher with no experience; why should we hire you? 
The role at this company is consulting, yet you have CFA-L1 in your profile. Are you going to pursue the CFA-L2 exam or will you pursue additional finance certifications?
prep_resources: 1. Solve ample cases from all IIM casebooks 2. Prepare HR questions of Why 3. Go through industry awareness section in Casebooks 4. Read a lot of case study articles online.
looking_for:
They were looking for candidates 
1. Genuinely interested in consulting
2. Good at problem-solving
3. Who can communicate well with the stakeholders and understand their problems and requirements well
right_wrong:
1. In the first round I got their attention after talking about the summer internship project. I also gave the best answers, according to me, for why consulting.
2. In the second round, I successfully addressed questions about why I wanted to pursue consulting and performed the case to the best of my ability.
tips:
1. Went through a lot of cases of various consulting casebooks
2. Went through case studies given on consulting club websites
tech_skills: Consult Domain Knowledge; How well you tell your summer internship project or your work experience;
dos_and_donts:
1. Solve an ample amount of consulting cases before the interview 
2. Prepare your consulting domain knowledge to the best you can 
3. Be thorough with your summer internship project

pre_process_tips:
After resume shortlist, shortlisted candidates were sent a preprocess.

The preprocess contained the following questions:
1) What unique thing about yourself have you discovered recently? 
2) Describe an experience where you failed and share your reflections
3) Describe a time when you took on something significant outside your area of responsibility. Why was it important? What was the outcome? 
4) Why would you like to join Rebel?

(Each answer should be below 500 words)

Answer the questions in simple sentences but make sure you align your answers according to the company's values, goals, and orientations. Back up your every answer using examples (stories from your life).
no_interviews_duration: 2 Interviews. (1st interview was 20-25 minutes and 2nd interview lasted ~ 1 Hour)
interview_outline:
Started with introduction, went into resume details briefly (internship project). Abstract questions like "If I had two sets of problems, one which you like to solve and one which you don't enjoy solving, what would you do?" were asked. It was mostly HR heavy, Interview was mainly centered around "Why Rebel Foods", and the values I possess which should be backed up by examples. 

2nd Interview:
Started off with introduction, and then went into resume details. Interviewer tested on my LeadR Program knowledge, and asked questions on my values, and what I can bring to the table. First half was HR heavy, 2nd half was technical. Questions like GTM strategy for establishing a new kitchen in my home town was asked. Follow-up questions were asked on that.
domain_questions:
According to my hometown, biryani was most consumed my demographic there. Therefore, questions were asked about Biryani Brands of Rebel Foods, how to tweak them to suit the demographic, problems with the tweaking, what they are doing correct with the biryani brands, and questions related to that.

GTM strategy of establishing a new kitchen was asked. (From market research, to starting operations). Use GTM strategy framework discussed in Marketing Domain session. Tailor your answer according to the interests of your demographic. Be as simple & direct as possible in your answers.
hr_gk_questions: Pick the values that Rebel Foods is aligned to, and tailor your values accordingly and prepare examples from your personal and professional life to back them up.
looking_for: They are looking for a long term investment in their employee because LeadR spans over 3 years as a program. Since Rebel Foods is expanding rapidly (IPO in next 2-3 years), the operational load will be heavy. Therefore, they are looking for hardworking, problem-solving, entrepreneurially oriented mind set people.
right_wrong: If you are confused about the questions asked in the interview, always ask for clarification of the question.
tips: Company deck, basic domain sessions of marketing, finance, and operations, and latest news related to the company.
dos_and_donts: Ask questions back to the interviewers as the end of the interview. Questions related to the company, and about the interviewer as well. (Example(s): Why did Fasoos subscription model scrapped, what was the drive behind the rebranding of EatSure, and questions like 'Why did you join Rebel Foods')

pre_process_tips: A Google form was circulated. It asked all details about our profie]le. Additionally they had two rows where we had to explain our previous role and what weere our roles and responsibilities
gd_topics_tips: We had a Group Case discussion. The discussion was amongst random groups of 8. They would give a case and the team as a whole had to discuss and arrive at a solution. The case given to my group was to develop an app/website for students planning to go abroad for studies
interview_outline: purely technical. the interview was also a case-based interview. The case was a one-one interview . the case is technically assume you are a technical prod man at walmart and solve a problem. the problem given to me was to reduce return rates
domain_questions: I was asked how to implement my solution in the case-based interview using technology
looking_for: Leadership, Communication, Technical Expertise, whether can work as a team, overall domain knowledge
right_wrong: Let me start with the Group Case discussion. This was not your conventional GD. Here you needed to work together as a team. You needed a structure to be followed to arrive at a solution. You need someone who can assume the role of a leader and guide the group and prevent it from self-destruction. I was able to assume the leadership role very easily and the team went along with it. I was able to get the team to cooperate under the circumstances which made the discussion equally good. Moving on to the Case Discussion interview I knew my technical stuff and was able to use it but my approach was aggressive. Though I got selected i would advise against using an aggressive approach until you are sure you can pull it off
tips: Go for mock GDs and PIs as much as you can. Even if it is within your friend circle. The benefit of this being even if your mock experience goes bad you get to meet new people with whom you can bond and learn. This will prove helpful. Hold your nerves in the interview. Try going with a calm mindset. Always smile. Regarding the technical aspect, I would say learn the frameworks, but cases usually can be solved using common sense, so there is no need to worry about that.  Before the summers start go on a socializing spree across the campus. This will allow people and yourself to know the person competing against you in a better fashion. This will also allow you to take the leadership role more seamlessly and since people know you they will work with you
dos_and_donts: Don't fight with your team. You are also a potential candidate same as them. Avoid turning the discussion into a fish market because this will result in everyone failing.  Remember your core values and stay true to them. Dont try to oversell yourself as this will be clearly reflected in the way you speak.

pre_process_tips:
Stage 1: Psychometric Test and Games
At this stage we were required to play same logic and memory based games. It is recommended that the games be played with best capability of the individual without trying to find some hack or work around for them. There will be an option to do a practice assessment before the actual thing so make sure you do that sincerely as well.
Stage 2: Video Recorded Interview
Here a few situational questions are displayed on the screen and participants are expected to answer them while the website records the same through your webcam. Practice questions are given here as well, so make sure you try those out a couple of times to get the confidence. Dress as you would for a regular interview and ensure you know your NPAD well to answer the questions flawlessly.
gd_topics_tips:
Topic - Technology makes us less human
Pattern - About 12 people were in for a GD of about 20 minutes. People in the GD were mixed (from both the IT and Finance profiles), and each were expected to bring in points from the perspective of their respective profiles. 
Selection Criteria - People advanced to the next staged seemed to be the ones who put forward logical & innovative points and the ones who were polite to others as well (rather than the ones who spoke the most or were trying to control the decorum of the GD). 2 people were advanced from a group of 12 people.
interview_outline: First interview was purely HR based and seemed more like a conversation rather than an interview. Ensure that you are polite and show interest in the organisation, profile through relevant questions. Do not go too domain specific. In the second round your interest in the profile (rather than your specific knowledge) will be gauged. Try highlighting your interests through the resume points that demonstrate your achievements in the profile (IT in my case).
domain_questions:
What is your exposure to IT as a function? - Highlight relevant resume points. If you don't have work ex or internships in the field, you make do some online courses or competition to highlight your interest in the field.
What are the latest trends in Cyber-security? - Reading first 2 or 3 articles that come up on searching this article on google should be enough prep. This is done just to see your interest  rather than testing your knowledge.
hr_gk_questions:
Tell me about yourself
Why IT?
What conditions bring out the best in you?
looking_for: Interest in IT and a desire to learn. Doing a few online courses and certifications should be helpful.
right_wrong: Enthusiasm, Interest and a Positive outlook helped me.
tips: Prepcom IT prep material, a bit of extra preparation through online reading. I never attended a mock GD or PI but I would certainly recommend the same to develop confidence.
dos_and_donts: Be polite, show enthusiasm, have basic knowledge of the domain

pre_process_tips: Case study focused on credit risk evaluation, loan pricing & haircut calculation. Post this we also had to appear for a preliminary test with three sections: Logical Reasoning, Finance, Coding. The coding section was logical and less focused on coding jargons, a basic understanding of how loops, functions and iterations work in C would be sufficient for that section, Finance focused on derivatives.
gd_topics_tips: Case study winners were invited to a GD with the organizing VP, in order to elaborate on their approach and field questions
no_interviews_duration: Buddy round 1 (30 mins), Buddy round 2 (30 mins), HR Interview (10 mins)
interview_outline: Buddy round/ Interview 1 was heavy on credit risk concepts with a focus on using derivatives for hedging (probably because I used these concepts in my case study discussion), Buddy round/ Interview 2 was a test of aptitude with one question from probability, one from economics and two credit-related case questions, HR interview focused more on the projects on my resume and how I could use the learnings from those projects in my internship with the company.
domain_questions: Before asking technical questions, the interviews made sure you were comfortable with the topic/subject, so be thorough with what you know. Vocalize your thoughts as it will help the interviewer nudge you in the right direction. Nobody expects you to know everything, they just want to test your logical thinking and problem solving skills.
hr_gk_questions: They did not ask me any current affairs based or typical HR based questions (Aside from why IPM and why Barclays). However, knowledge of current affairs will never hurt, as I had an engaging discussion with one of the panelists about the Evergrande crisis. It helps showcase your awareness and interest. For HR: always prepare four answers - Why this company, Why this domain, Why this role and Why you.
looking_for: Someone with a genuine interest in Finance and a willingness to learn new concepts like programming to augment this interest. No prior workex, certifications or coding knowledge was mandated.
right_wrong: Barclays was my top preference for summer internships and it showed in the interviews as I was genuinely excited to have the opportunity to appear for these. I was well-versed with each aspect of my resume and motivations for the role. The mistakes I primarily made was because of rushed problem solving so I advice you to take your time with the technical questions. And yes, I converted the interview.
tips: Primarily be clear about your resume and goals, knowledge of derivatives and credit instruments is a big plus. Mock GD/PIs did not emulate the actual process as the Barclays process is more of a test of interest and aptitude rather than a test of existing prowess.
dos_and_donts: I went through the case route and there were learning opportunities in every step of the process. it is best to have one primary takeaway from each step of the process and demonstrate in the next step, it gives the recruiting team concrete evidence of your curiosity and learning attitude.

pre_process_tips: Video Assessment - 5 HR questions. The questions asked are mostly to test if you are fit for the role and the company.
interview_outline: My 2 interviews were HR (My profile was completely aligned with the role. Hence, they just tested if I am a cultural fit) - HR Heavy
hr_gk_questions:
Note: Always show that you are excited to work with the company. Even if you don't know the answer to a few technical questions, it is okay to say that you don't know but ensure them that you'll definitely learn if the role requires you to. MAKE THE INTERVIEWER FEEL GOOD. Be positive and always show the excitement on your face and in your voice. 

Interview 1: 20 min - 2 interviewers
1. Tell Me About Yourself
2. Resume Based - No technical questions
3. Long term and Short Term goals
4. Why do you think you are fit for this role?
5. Why BofA?
6. Why Finance?
7. Where do you see yourself in 10 years?
8. Any Questions for us? - I believe this is what got me through the first interview. I researched about BofA and learned that they take good care of their employees and contribute majorly to CSR. I asked what measures/benefits they gave to employees during the pandemic. (before asking let them know that you researched a bit about it and appreciate their efforts before asking the question)

Interview 2: 10 min - 1 interviewer
1. You have no finance-related points on your resume then why finance? How important do you think Finance is? 
2. Will you learn finance if the role requires you to learn? 
3. Any questions for me? - Again this was on point. I had no questions in my mind and went blank for a few seconds. While I was thinking, I appreciated the measures taken by BofA for the employees during a pandemic and remembered that BofA gave a lot of priority to CSR and asked him about the CSR initiatives planned for 2021. Luckily, the interviewer turned out to be the CSR head for the Mumbai region, and he gave a vast list of initiatives they planned for the year. After the interviewer answered the question, I told him that the initiatives motivate me even more to work with BofA and contribute to society as a part of BofA.
looking_for: Cultural Fit, Willingness to learn whatever the role demands to, Know about the company.
right_wrong:
I did not prepare an answer for why no finance on resume. I could have framed the answer for where do you see yourself in 10 years better. Be thorough with your NPAD. 

Knowing about the company helped me a lot. Talking to the seniors who were placed at BofA helped.
tips: Go through the NPAD thoroughly and research about the company.
dos_and_donts: Tips and suggestions are already mentioned in the previous questions. All the best :)

pre_process_tips: Filling form on Reculta/Portal --> Shortlist --> 2 buddy calls, final interviews
no_interviews_duration: Buddy calls can be for 15-30 mins.
interview_outline:
The telephonic buddy calls were comprehensive, covering everything from HR to technical questions. They were quite detailed and were expecting me to be extremely confident about each point mentioned. 

(1) Buddy call 1 (15 mins): Why Finance? Why this role? Why Goldman Sachs? Why move from B.Tech to MBA? Explain projects, what did you learn from them? Why not workex? Why should we choose you when other candidates have better workex? Repo rate, inflation, derivatives, bonds and yields, FED and RBI monetary policy, debt/equity financing, investor rationale, which sectors are doing well and why? They also asked which programming languages I am good at, am I good at stat/quant, is buy side or sell side more interesting, why trading?

(2) Buddy call 2 (25 mins): This call was very grilling and the interviewer pushed me to the very edge. He asked me repeatedly (around 5-7 times in total) to convince him why he should take me and not some fin/eco candidate. I was asked about derivatives, forward rates, global macroeconomic events, repo rate, stock movements. Other qs: why finance, why GS, who is the CEO of GS, why shift to MBA, why not go for tech roles, am I interested in IB, why does trading interest me. I was probed upon my composure when he asked me about my JEE ranks, why not apply for GS's engineering division, how do I stand out among other CA/CFAs from other big B schools, why should he take me if I haven't completed even a basic course in Finance. He also asked some quant questions: sum of all numbers from 1 to 100 etc. 

Although the calls were very stressful, I had a feeling I was being tested so I didn't lose my calmness. At the end, the interviewer told me my profile was very good and he was just trying to assess my candidature.
domain_questions: Mentioned earlier. Be very clear about bonds and derivatives since GBM trading depends upon that.
hr_gk_questions: Recent macroeconomic events (in last 2 weeks) and financial implications
looking_for: The buddy calls were grilling, but I felt they were trying to gauge my confidence, negotiation skills and how I was staying true to my strengths.
right_wrong: I don't know if I proceeded to PI because I was already out of the placement process by then. In hindsight, I could have prepared for the derivative questions better and crafted a more logical answer to 'why trading' and 'why GS?'
tips: Defend yourself as much as you can without appearing arrogant. Be strong and sharp to take on difficult questions because they will try the very best to test your composure. Don't mention random finance jargon because it will shift the focus. Try to keep the conversation honest and candid. For derivatives, the CFA module in brief should be more than sufficient

pre_process_tips: CV based shortlist
no_interviews_duration: 5 (3 Interviews of approx. 1 hr. each, 2 interviews of about 30 min. each)
interview_outline:
* First three rounds: Introduction - Work Ex - Internship - Guestimate - Case - HR based questions - Domain specific questions - CV based questions (All 3 were balanced)
- Round 1(Telephonic):- Guestimate: Hiking shoes market in India; Case: PE firm acquiring an automobile firm (mostly focussed towards analysing operational synergies)
- Round 2 (Telephonic):- Guestimate: Market size of refurbished smartphones and recycle smartphones in India; Case: Cost reduction exercise in a Fertilizer company
- Round 3 (Campus round):- Case: Working capital management of a B2B specialty chemicals manufacturing firm (Revolved around Inventories, Accounts receivable and Accounts payable)

*Round 4 & 5: HR based questions (Elevator Pitch, Why consulting, why operations consulting, Why PwC, Background and CV related questions)
domain_questions:
- Compare Indian Manufacturing Industry with Chinese (Because I had Doing business with China as my elective)
- 7 types of waste in manufacturing
- Six sigma: Significance and application in a bottling plant
- Questions related to supply side and demand side bottleneck and how would you deal with both
- Reverse supply chain in electronics industry (Phones, Laptops, etc.)
- Environmental regulations about electronic waste and ways to tackle the issue
- Rationale behind credit in the chemicals business
- Push Pull Boundary
- Direct material cost reduction (Procurement related and process efficiency related)
- Insurance Operations: How to optimize (Basics)
- Revenue management related questions in Hotel Industry
- Questions related to clinical trials in Pharma Industry
- Analytics based questions: About Simulations in Excel
- Importance of different intermediaries in a supply chain (Basics)
hr_gk_questions:
- Details about 2 competitons I had won in Operations/ Supply Chain domain
- Overview of other competitons (Mahindra War Room, Asian Paints Canvas, Aspect Ratio) which were on my resume
- About my POR during Undergraduation
- Hobbies related questions
- Social Initiative related basic questions
- Live project (IIP) related questions
- At what point in time will you quit an organization?
- Process vs Outcome: What will you choose?
looking_for: Rationale behind why do you want to do operations consulting, Operations domain knowledge
right_wrong:
Right: Strong operations domain knowledge

Wrong: In round 1, could have done guestimate better; In round 2, could have approached the case in more methodical and structured manner
tips:
Readings from Prepcomm Operations decks and industry decks were useful.

Feedback from mock PIs: Do PIs with your friends and ask for their feedbacks, Keep each answer to the questions based on your CV crisp and interesting.
dos_and_donts:
Do(s): Be calm, Interviews will be lengthy and at times can be intimidating or stressful. Try to maintain your cool and come up with as much alternatives as you can.

Don't(s): Although the question might seem very straighforward, there might be a twist hidden; so take a moment and don't jump to the solutions. Don't directly conclude anything before briefing. Don't make any assumptions without clarifications.

pre_process_tips: No Preprocess
gd_topics_tips: The topic was "The Best strategy for Ecommerce company", talked confidently, made 4 entries, summarized the GD at the end.
no_interviews_duration: 1 interview (2 panelist of which one was HR)
interview_outline:
The interview lasted for 25min
The first question was to introduce yourself and your area of Interest (Told about Digital Marketing) also mentioned about my summer internship in Digital Marketing
The rest of the questions were related to that point
Asked to develop GTM strategy for digital marketing of Lifebuoy soap, the measurement parameters for assessing the success of the campaign, KPI’s
 The HR asked only 2 questions at the end
How will you react if you are asked to learn Automation for a project?
Gave good reply with examples about how I took initiatives to learn new things.
How would your friends describe you?
Told about the RBSE exercise done as an assignment for TAW (Thriving at Work) and gave many examples.
At the end, I asked about the recent deal between WIPRO and Metro AG (a german based wholesale company), asked how they are leveraging the use of blockchain technology. (Read on the company website in the news section)
domain_questions: Since I mentioned my interest as digital marketing, questions were related to that only. The various channels of digital marketing for reaching to rural users. The future of Digital marketing. leveraging it with the traditional methods of marketing.
situational_questions: How would your friends describe you? Gave some examples using the STAR method.
hr_gk_questions: They did not ask for any current affairs. but at the end, I asked about the recent deal between WIPRO and Metro AG (a german based wholesale company), asked how they are leveraging the use of blockchain technology.
looking_for: They were seeking confident person who would stay calm in adverse conditions. They cross questioned me about my Digital GTM strategy and tried to put pressure. Stay calm and give the rationale behind your decisions and how the ROI can be better.
right_wrong: Should have talked about the analytical skills in the Introduction as the role demanded it.
tips: The GD topics given in the PrepCom folder surely helped. The Company deck was helpful as it gave the recent updates about the company. PrepCom session on the Ecommerce was very helpful for the GD.
dos_and_donts:
Smile often and try to stay calm. The cross-questioning for the GTM strategy was a bit uncomfortable as they asked similar questions many times. Just calmly give your previous answer. 
Ask relevent question at the end. This shows your interest in the company.
Dont freak when they ask the same question more than once. Calmly give the same answer. I had a note pad and was noting the points as I said them, which helped when they cross questioned me.

At the end I said
Thank you for this awesome opportunity today, It was a pleasure talking to you. I’ve thoroughly enjoyed the process and have learnt a tremendous amount about your company.

company: Star Union Dai Ichi Life Insurance
pre_process_tips: The company had a GD round after resume shortlisting. The GD required excellent preparation as it consisted of two topics, one abstract topic and one Knowledge-Based topic. A Personal Interview followed this.
gd_topics_tips:
GD topics:
 1) Black dot outlined with a red circle
2) Your person of the millennium 
The panel expected us to be as creative as possible and expected us to deliver an answer in a structured form with pertinent facts backing our creativity. A clear answer consisting of 4-5 well-framed points is what they expected. 
The following topic had different answers from the members participating in the GD, but the main objective was to narrow down the discussion on what made us choose a person.
interview_outline: The interview started with the panel asking me to tell me briefly about myself. This followed why do I want to join this company for the summer internship. I was also asked why they should hire me and what value proposition I would bring to them. They asked me how IT will be used in Insurance ( automation). How would I implement the changes that I am proposing? Basics of Insurance and why Insurance. Panelists tried to find loops by telling me that I have an excellent resume for all the sectors yet why I chose this sector and their firm specifically. HR questions mainly were to see if I am good at communication and can keep the panelists engaged. Technical questions required going through company background and their actual work and having in-depth knowledge of IT and its implementation in various sectors.
domain_questions:
How insurance companies work?
What impact can IT create in insurance and how?
How to cater to customers through IT implementation in insurance?
hr_gk_questions:
Why this company?
Does money matter to you more or the learning curve? 
What other interests do you have?
looking_for: I believe they were looking for a candidate who had basic knowledge and understanding of Insurance and how IT implementation can impact it?. Other than this, I felt they were to see if how good can I present myself. They were also keen on do I know and can I back my answers with valuable facts.
right_wrong: As I had prepared my NPAD, I tackled the HR questions in a structured way. I had gone through the technical aspects of the role after being shortlisted. Hence I was able to frame my answer correctly and give the answers they expected out of me.
tips: I guess showing up calm and composed helped me throughout the interview. A constant smile on my face allowed me to express my eagerness and enthusiasm to join their company. I was able to back myself with proper preparation before the interview.
dos_and_donts:
Preparing NPAD is a must for all interviews. Going through job roles and responsibilities before the interview is heavily recommended. 
It's better not to come up with vague and unstructured answers.

pre_process_tips: Application on Reculta. I used the gen man variant to apply. Make sure you put in all the relevant electives you have chosen in accordance with the company JD. No pre-process other than resume shortlisting and GD.
gd_topics_tips: Managing customer experience at the time of social distancing' was the topic given. The GD lasted for approx. 15 minutes, and there were 9-10 people in the discussion panel, with one moderator who was the HR. The conversion rate was extremely low per GD, so make sure you stand out. I made 3-4 entries, but make sure you stay relevant to the topic and bring in different perspectives. They were looking for people who could bring in different points and also, it doesn't hurt to be somewhat aggressive.
no_interviews_duration: Post the GD, there was only one PI which lasted around 15-20 minutes
interview_outline: The interview started with a mini case. They did not want to give a detailed solution, just the outline of the solution, which in my case, included 5 potential solutions for the given problem. The case was: ' You are a women's sanitary products manufacturer and a particular retail chain does not wish to display your products at their shops as the owner of the retail chain was uncomfortable with the display of such products. Since this retail chain is quite extensive, it is imperative that you display & ell your products here. What will be your approach to convincing him? Describe potential solutions'. Be prepared for counter questions for each and every solution you propose.
domain_questions: In addition to the mini case, they asked the usual S&M domain questions like "Why S&M", " Are you willing to do sales stints in the first year?", "What do you think are your skills that will help you excel in S&M", etc. They also asked whether I was familiar with any Samsung products and what features of them I liked. So be prepared with a couple of products. There were no other HR or domain questions asked. The interview concluded with these questions.
situational_questions: No particular resume-based or situational questions were asked.
hr_gk_questions: Nothing in particular.
looking_for: They were looking for problem solving skills in particular, as there were no particular resume-based or HR questions asked in the interview. Just make sure you can defend whatever solution you propose for the case given and prepare something about the company's products.
right_wrong: I stumbled when I was asked to justify one particular solution, which I gave as part of the case, but I was able to convince the interviewer of my thought process. So, I guess the proposal of extensive solutions and the way I defended it were the things that helped me convert the interview. The interview was more like a conversation. So, make sure you engage them and have a friendly conversation.
tips: Presence of mind, good communication skills, not panicking when cross-questioned. Company research helped to learn more about the company's values and their products.

pre_process_tips: Screening test (Aptitude). Moderate difficulty level. Don't waste time on a particular question. Use the allotted time efficiently.
no_interviews_duration: 2 rounds of interview (Round 1: Technical -45 minutes, Round 2: HR- 30 minutes)
interview_outline:
Technical Interview: 
No Introduction. Directly started with my top percentile subjects. Since I was the top percentile scorer in the Business model they asked me to frame one such model for AmEx. 
1. Should be thorough with your subjects and projects mentioned in your resume.
2. Asked questions on regression, Cluster analysis, factor analysis, and building regression equations for AmEx and its customers.
The interviewer was building questions from my answers. So it's imperative to speak and make use of jargon only of which you are confident about. 
Asked in-depth about my subject projects done in a line similar to analytics. Like I had my project in MR- marketing domain, but they asked me how I made use of SPSS tools to perform the tests and generate results. 

HR: 
1. Tell me about yourself.
2. NPAD questions like the time when you showcased leadership skills, One thing you would have done differently during your internship, etc.
3. Impact on Financial Service institutes due to Covid-19
4. Why AmEx
5. Why Analytics
6. What makes you different from other candidates
domain_questions:
1. You can expect the interviewer to ask you to apply your analytical tools on real based situation drafted by the interviewer.
2. Difference between Cluster Analysis and Regression
3. Difference between Credit and Fraud Risk
4. Questions on the balance sheet
5. Measures to regulate risk
6. Criteria on which you will judge the level of risk for a new customer
and in-depth questions on analytical tools like regression and factor analysis.

It helps to be thorough with your analytical subjects.
situational_questions:
Be thorough with your NPAD. Mug-up answers don't make sense but it gives you an edge if you are structured in your answers.
HR questions were basic and most expected ones but they are looking more into how well you can articulate them.
Major questions: What is more important to you- work-life balance, work culture, or quality of projects. Where do you see yourself in the analytics field down the line or what do you want to gain from your corporate life?
looking_for: Clarity in your answers and how well you know your resume points. Knowledge about the role and company in-depth. Confidence level for sure and well-articulated answers.
right_wrong: Had gone through a few recent advertisements and activities of AmEx and spoke them about during my interviews. It helped me to convince them that I follow the company closely as the Ads were released a few weeks back.
tips:
I framed my answers with examples attached to them. They appreciate this effort of yours. Read about the role very well and the latest innovations the company is undergoing.
I took few minutes to build a connection with the interviewer during my HR round. It helped me throughout.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlisting, Buddy Calls (3x), MDP Dinner (followed by interaction), On Campus Buddy Connect (1 Case)
interview_outline:
Interview 1: Started with introduction. Interviewer picked a prompt from my "Tell me about yourself" and asked me to solve a guesstimate around it. (Question: Estimate the market size of Fiction Books in India)

Asked me to do a top down and bottom up approach.

Interview 2: Interviewer had my resume handy, talked about my work exp. Asked me to analyze the BFSI space. Case was given in the Retail banking space.

Complete transcript can be found in the Consulting case book.

Both the interviews had a 5-10 min "Any questions for us" section where I had elaborate discussions on the domains in which the interviewer was working and current themes in them
hr_gk_questions: On Campus buddy (pre-process) asked me about my interest in Consulting and shift from Investment Banking to Consulting. No HR based questions in the Final Process
looking_for:
Must Have: Clear Communication and Case Preparation (Practice as many cases as you can, try to complete at least 50 cases before you start refining your methodology, target every industry)
Guesstimate knowledge: Know the basic statistics but try to be MECE in your approach. Talking to the interviewer and letting them know your thought process is very important

Could Have: If your resume has different fields of internships/projects then that can be a plus (As they want a generalist). Big brands and achievements (Spikes) are needed,
right_wrong:
Good: I was driving the interviews and ensured that my approach is aligned with the interviewer before I started number crunching. I knew about the current affairs of the top 8-9 industries thus was able to ask good "Any questions for us".

Bad / Could have been better: I assumed that the interview would last 25-30 mins (Standard case round) hence was quite comprehensive and detailed with my assumptions and numbers but the interviewer was trying to drive it as a bullet case and just wanted to know my approach which made me uncomfortable in the beginning

Converted.
tips:
Consulting PPT by PrepCom
IIM Indore Casebook for the BCG transcripts
FMS Casebook (Started with this)
IIMA Casebook (Ended with this)
Cases by PGP2/Buddies

Do by heart the structure for the basic cases (till level 3 and 4) but think out of these structures in the case as the interview cases would never be straight forward
dos_and_donts:
Start as early as possible (My group started mid July)

It takes ~10-15 cases to build the case solving confidence. Another 10-15 cases to build structures and recall them. Another 10-15 to understand how an industry operates.
Although numbers do not matter while solving but you'll definitely see progress as your numbers go up.

Do not forget the other parts of the preparation (Guesstimates - try to club with cases, current affairs, what company does, why Consulting)

pre_process_tips: Applied on the portal only. Used my General resume variant.
gd_topics_tips:
There were two GDs. Total time allocated was 20 mins (approx).
Topic 1: A fintech company has presence in 20 major cities. Should they monetize or expand? -Tried to structure the GD into pros and cons for both the options.
Topic 2: Did the government take a right decision by opening the lockdown in June?
-Once again structured the GD on two fonts- Economic and Health. Analyzed it further using the lenses of various stakeholders.
interview_outline: The walked into the interview without any understanding of the role since there was no JD and I could not attend the PPT. The interviewer started with 'You must know me, so I will not introduce myself, let's start with your introduction'. I kept my introduction brief but highlighted all my achievements. He wanted to know more about my summer internship at Amazon. We discussed my internship in detail how I created the program in 8 weeks. This went on for 10 minutes. Once done, we discussed about my workex for next 2-3 minutes. He asked me my experience aligns with technology but the role is kind of S&M. I was thrown off track as there was no JD for the position and I didn't attend the talk either.  Post that he gave me a guesstimate to determine the paint required in my home state in a year. He said take 5-6 minutes and let me know. I started working on the guesstimate alone and having solved 60-70% in 3-4 minutes, I told him "I have laid down the structure and solved most of it. Let's solve the rest together so that we can save some time." I explained him my approach till now and we went on to work on the guesstimate for another 3-4 minutes. Since we were solving together, I stopped calculating exact numbers and focused on the factors. He was quite happy with my approach. He asked me 2-3 behavioral questions and asked me if I will be comfortable relocating.
domain_questions: None. Only guesstimate was asked.
situational_questions:
Tell me about a time when you resolved conflict? -Told him about an incident from my old organization. I could also highlight how in the end I worked with senior management to change the workflow to prevent any such conflicts in future.
What is my most significant achievement?- Spoke about my project from my undergrad on which I have been granted a patent recently. 
Tell me about a time when you could turn around the team?- Took an incident from my POR.
looking_for: I think they were looking at my problem solving skills and my ability to communicate.
right_wrong: I went in and steered the entire interview towards a discussion instead of waiting for Q&A.
tips: Understanding the learning from each work mentioned in my resume.

pre_process_tips: The application form included basic educational and work experience details, keep them handy before starting to fill the form. There is also a case workshop held, which is extremely useful for your preparation process. It is non-evaluative so try to make the most of it and focus on the learnings.
no_interviews_duration: 3, 30 minutes for first 2, the third was 15 minutes in my case
interview_outline: It is possible that the 1st 2 interviews take place back to back in the same room, so you need to be prepared for the same. The interview outline could be: 1. Tell me something about yourself (Introduction) 2. Work experience details 3. few resume questions 4. Analysis of an Inventory Management system 5. Guesstimate: How much would the inventory of an ice cream parlor be in Mumbai city 6. Case: An MNC and a few other analysis details were given, had to analyze how they can reduce costs and where could those costs be used instead to help grow the company
hr_gk_questions: Why consulting, why strategy, a few questions related to initiatives taken by me as per my resume
looking_for: All interviewers are really nice, friendly and extremely supportive. If you go wrong, they help you get into the right direction. The interviewers are basically looking for a structured approach, if you have a personality suitable for their firm and how well you can apply your knowledge in cases given (also helps check thinking when under stressful situation like an interview)
right_wrong:
I got a little tensed during the beginning of case, but fortunately the interviewers were extremely polite and they realized the same, they gave me a 2 minute pause to relax and think and I could really come up with good solutions post that.

What went well - I tried to analyze the questions from all perspectives for example from the operations, HR, finance, microeco perspective to get a solution and tried to give a logical explanation for each point I raised. This impressed the interviewers greatly.

For my director round, I was confident and honest which seemed to really go well for me.
tips: Be confident - I think this is a natural consequence of portraying honesty both in the interview and the resume , try not to panic - one thing that helped me here when I panicked for a bit was to not think of it as an interview and just take it as a genuine problem and use all my learnings, basic understanding and common sense to solve it, try not to fall for peer pressure or the competitive environment around you in term 1 - will surely help you a lot.
dos_and_donts:
Try to practice cases, understand concepts well, also try to have some knowledge of current affairs, can help you in some answers
Try to understand what domain you actually want to work in and give it your best!
All the best :)

pre_process_tips: Application Form, Online Assessment (Aptitude)
gd_topics_tips: Workshop - where everyone is taught topics in Finance, based on which there is a test right after the workshop.
interview_outline: Asked for my introduction. Went on to ask questions on Financial Statements, Firm Value/Enterprise Value, WACC, Mental Maths, Markets
domain_questions:
- Asked for introduction
- Where will depreciation be added in financial statements

Firm Value/ Enterprise Value - 
- New company, give 10 shares of 10 million each, and you take a debt of 100 million. What would the balance sheet look like and what is the Firm Value.
- Then you bought a land for 50 million, and are not operating anything on it, what is the firm value then?

WACC - 
- Asked what is WACC. Told them it was the weighted average of cost of capital and cost of debt. Mentioned CAPM is used to calculate cost of capital. Then the interviewer asked what CAPM is. Gave the formula
- In CAPM, what is Rm, how is it calculated - was not sure of this

Mental Math -
