interview_outline:
There were 2 rounds. 
In round 1, interview started with question about role and company. Then a case was asked. Lastly interviewer asked me one tecnical question.
In round 2, interview started with 'tell me about yourself'. Then a case was asked.
domain_questions:
Round 1:

Q1: Why this role and Why this company?

Q2: Case Questions: Profitability case: Our client is a company that rents out lighting and sound equipment for concerts and shows. Their revenues are declining. You have to identify what can be the reason. (After I identified the reason, interviewer presented a data table and the next question was based on that data) Based on data given to you - recommend a solution to increase the revenues.

Some comments: Case was numerical heavy, interviewer expected me to do calculations in detail.

Q3: In your work at 1st company you worked for after graduation, you were involved in some procurement activity. Can you tell me some statistical methods of demand forecasting?

Round 2:

Q1: Tell me about yourself.

Q2: Case Questions: Market entry case: Our client is a company that manufactures instruments for pathological laboratory. The client is thinking of entering into the glucometer market. What will you suggest to them - whether to enter or not? (Once I told him the approach, he presented 4 data tables about competitor sales in glucometer market). Based on these data tables, what can you infer and will you suggest the client to enter the market?

Some comments: This case was also numerical heavy. Interviewer expected me to find some trends in competitor sales data and give a recommendation based on the analysis.
looking_for: Whether a candidate can give data analysis based recommendations in case.
right_wrong:
Right: 
> Kept my answers precise - did not bore the interviewer with long monologues. 
> Did not get lost in details for qualitative aspects of case. 
> Took my time to analyze the data  given. Did not jump to conclusion quickly.
> Kept asking the clarifying questions while solving case. 
Wrong: 
> In technical question about 'statistical methods for demand forecasting' - instead of mentioning different methods, I just told one method that I could remember and kept explaining it in detail. (This was also because I could not recall other methods).
> Did not tell some 'obvious' insights from given data. I assumed that it might look silly of I tell these obvious insights, but I was wrong - interviewer once stopped me and asked me to tell all insights even if they are very obvious.
tips:
> Guesstimates.
> Case solving.
> Preparing answers that are tailored for a role: as this company is into analytics consulting, I prepared all analytics related pointers on my resume in-depth, and prepared some answers that will showcase my inclination for analytics.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlisting, psychometric test, interview
interview_outline: The whole interview was HR based, but some people had a technical interview instead, so I guess it depends on the panel. The HR questions which they ask are very subtly placed in the conversation, so you will have to be thorough with your NPAD to understand which answer goes where (their HR questions would not be conventionally framed like how we see them - nothing like "What are your strengths and weaknesses" or commonly heard questions). For stuff you cannot find in your NPADs, just be yourself and you should be fine.
hr_gk_questions: Started with how are the online classes going; how did you adjust to it, and some basic ice breakers. Then he asked me to introduce myself. He asked me about my strengths and weaknesses; what motivates me and frustrates me; where do I see myself two years down the line. Asked me to rank brand, money and role. There was also a question on "why me among all the candidates being interviewed". Then he also asked me what kind of a role, company, and industry would I want to work in and why. He asked me if I would prefer a role involving lots of people interaction, or a role which involves number crunching. Asked me a few questions from my projects and why were each of them related to human behaviour. Ended with asking about my hobbies.
looking_for: Someone who knows themselves well and is well aware of their strengths and weaknesses. Also, someone who is honest
right_wrong: Did not convert: I could answer all the questions he asked since I was thorough with my resume. They probably did not see me as a culture fit with their company. Moreover, in hindsight I also feel it would have been better had I connected my answers to my resume. For example - the person asked me if I prefer a job role which is people centric or number centric. I explained why I think I would do better in a people centric role (told them I am good at communicating, I liek meeting people etc). If I would have also mentioned that in one of my PORs I have had to interact with a host of people and I did that successfully, probably that would have been a better answer. Throughout the interview I answered well (I was confident, I spoke well) but there was little reference to experiences (through points on my resume).
tips: Being thorough with my NPADs definitely helped. However, you should also know how to present your answers. Do look at the company deck to align your values with theirs.
dos_and_donts: Take the psychometric test very seriously and stay consistent throughout your answers. Be thorough with your NPADs and cite examples from your experiences.

pre_process_tips:
Aptitude Test with three sections (maths, economics/general awareness, corporate finance), Workshop, GD, 1 Technical Interview, 1 HR Interview. 
Overview of workshop topics for WCR- why do corporates need banks, financial covenants, credit risk analysis framework- structural, industry, business, financial and geopolitical risk analysis, financial ratios
Overview of workshop topics for WM- begins with same content as that of WCR, heavy focus on encumbrance and verification, types of assets. liabilities and financial statements of HNIs (very different from balance sheets of general public or companies)
gd_topics_tips:
WCR: Debt Vs Equity- what should companies prefer for financing in a recession economy: The panel wasn't looking for concrete answers, there is no right or wrong, the answer could vary for different situations, industries or types of companies. The panel appreciated answers that could be backed by real life examples with names of companies and supportive figures. Even though this would be helpful for getting hotlisted, I believe as long as a person contributed to the discussion in any manner possible and made an effort to speak, they would easily clear this round.
WM: A case study based completely on the concepts taught in the workshop. You will be required to conduct an analysis of a company's financial position and whether credit should be extended to them. I would highly recommend making notes of the workshop teachings and applying the same in the GD. A ten minute reading time would be given before the case discussion begins.
no_interviews_duration: iWCR: 2 (1 Technical and 1 HR), WM: 1 Round
interview_outline:

WM: Introduction with heavy focus on family background, individual analysis of case study (same case as that of GD), resume based questions (internships, projects). There was only one interview conducted initially and no technical questions were asked in the same.
domain_questions: How are the three financial statements connected. The specific question was that id acquisition of a company takes place how would the three financial statements of the acquiring company be affected- an in depth explanation was required for this. Further line of questioning was based on financial ratios.
hr_gk_questions: The interview began with a standard introduction. They were interested to know about the candidate's interest in finance and specifically the role they were offering. A thorough understanding of the Job Description is a must. Do expect a detailed questioning based on the internships mentioned in the resume.
looking_for: Enthusiasm for the role and the company, understanding of the job description, basics of finance- financial statements, ratios, valuation methods
right_wrong:
WCR: Even though the answers I shared were correct, I was not very confident in the delivery. Not selected.
WM: The rounds went off well, not selected.
tips: NSE's NCFM Investment Analyst Pro Modules, Prepcom Advanced PPT (especially DCF Valuation)
dos_and_donts: Pay special attention to these topics in your preparation: Financial Statements, Financial Ratios, Valuation

interview_outline: The interviewer started with their introduction and talked about the CoE(domain) I applied for followed by my introduction. After a brief conversation about the CoE and why did I apply for it, we started with a guesstimate about the number of 4-wheeler EVs sold in India in 2022 which was relevant to both the CoE and my interests. This was followed by a case which I was not asked to solve due to time constraints but only involved me giving recommendations based on the initial data provided and from the preliminary questions. The final questions asked were about the role and if I'd be comfortable working with data analytics and visualisation tools.
domain_questions:
Why this CoE? Why do you want to work in this role? Do you have any experience in Data Analytics?
Obviously, have an answer ready on why you chose that particular CoE and try to back that up using previous experiences, projects or even plain interest in the domain. The role involves a lot of research and data analytics so be prepared with convincing answers for the same. I did not have any previous experience with data analytics and my answer mentioned my coding skills and my comfort with multiple softwares and applications that I have worked with in the past and assuring them I can learn what is required.
hr_gk_questions: Although no Current Affairs questions were asked to me, I'd suggest reading up on the news related to the CoE you apply for and be prepared with them.
looking_for: They were looking for good problem solving skills especially the approach, communicating your thoughts while solving the guesstimate and the case helps a lot. Other than that they were looking for any skills or experience with data analytics and visualisation.
right_wrong: I felt I made a good connect with the interviewer and we had a long discussion on the CoE and the type of work they do and what can we as interns expect from it. On what didn't go that well, I could have had a better answer for the data analytics question and in hindsight, an online course in this field would have been helpful to back myself up.
tips: 1. Be well prepared with Guesstimates which a lot of people shrug off during their SIP prep. 2. Read up on the company and the CoE you apply for to show your interest in the domain.
dos_and_donts:
1. Stay calm and try to make a connect with the interviewer, build a good conversation.
2. Communicate your approach and thoughts while solving the guesstimate and the case.
3. In my case, having some experience with data analytics would have been helpful.

pre_process_tips: Aptitude test for shortlisted candidates followed by Technical Round
interview_outline:
Started with the typical question: Run me through your resume. Had 1-2 questions based on points that were mentioned in the intro. Interview was technical heavy with almost zero component of HR in it. The interview experience for all three candidates selected for my company varied depending on which post it was. There was not much similarities between the interviews. 

Since it was an IT Consulting role, the interview was split into two parts, first being consulting and second technological. Started of with a few general questions on my awareness of the industry for which I was applying. Then moved on to give me a profitability case. Unlike most consulting interviews, the panel was not interested in back and forth conversation to zoom in on the problem. Rather he was interested in how well I cover all aspects of the research. For example he just told me to list down all the areas where I would look for the problem(Essentially the value chain) post which he asked me to list down general recommendations based on the areas I had identified. 

Post this, we moved on to the technical aspects where we discussed on different types of technologies that are driving the industry. So here I was tested on my understanding of each type of technology, depending on the answers that i gave.
domain_questions: Since it was a tech consulting role, understanding basic technologies and how they work is required. Didnt go much deep into how the technologies work. Covering content in all IT based courses in IPM would be enough to prepare for this part.
hr_gk_questions: Initially asked for industry knowledge: Size of industry, business models of top players and so on. Research as thoroughly as you can about the industry you are going to be working in before appearing for the interview
looking_for: In my opinion they were looking for someone who can think rationally, and with consulting skills to be able to analyse a problem across all aspects of the business.
right_wrong:
Based on previous interviews, I was expecting more questions on international markets, however my interviewer alone was interested in the domestic market. Hence, more research on current affairs would be of use here. 

Good parts included a good understanding of the company and different types of technologies.(Good understanding here doesn't imply coding knowledge, but your ability to gauge the basic foundation on which the technology is based)
tips: More research on the company, industry and technologies helped build confidence.
dos_and_donts: Do not limit yourself to domestic or international markets individually when you prep for the interview. Try to have a comprehensive overview of the industry, what drives the industry and basic challenges it is facing.

6. Any question for me ?

hr_gk_questions: No
prep_resources: Case books gave me an idea of how to handle different mini cases questions
looking_for: They looked for Finance knowledge + tech idea. Apart from that any creative thoughts I can generate or not.
right_wrong: I believe things went well

interview_outline:

hr_gk_questions:

looking_for:

pre_process_tips: After the company presentation, we were supposed to sit in a 20Q aptitude test, then shortlisted people got on a 1 hour zoom call with people from Bain, then the final interviews.
interview_outline: Started with what BCN is and what is does. After this went into resume details, picked my certification (Google Digital Marketing), then asked how I implemented in one of my PORs. After this asked if I had any questions for her (had prepared 2 beforehand). Then started with the case.
domain_questions: The case was, "Your client is a leading FMCG company and they're looking to launch a new product, that purifies water in a few minutes. Should they go ahead with it?" I started with asking a few preliminary questions, like more about the company, more about the product and competitive landscape, then asked her we can analyze it on basis of economic feasibility and/or operational feasibility. She asked me to go ahead with economic first, then we dived into a simple guestimate, she stopped me before I started doing final calculations, so we just worked with percentages. Once done with the guestimate the focus changed to operational feasibility. Once done with this she asked on what metrics should we decide whether to launch the product or not, then a final question was what is the formula for the profit that the product will earn. At the end she asked me again if I had any questions for her, I politely said that my queries had been answered before the start of the round and wished her a good day.
hr_gk_questions:
Q1- What did you do in your "Fundamentals of digital marketing" certifications?
Q2- How did you use it in you "Klueless - IRIS" POR? (It mentioned use of digital methods to increase reach by 500% on social media) 
I answered them as honestly as I could. First one was simple we just talked about SEO, SEM. The second one, I gave her an example of a question that usually come in Klueless, after this I said that we usually depend on reposts from friends and family's and as the event caters to a particular group of people they lookout for such opportunities, we have huge growth potential without paid marketing.
looking_for: They were looking for good communication primarily and then some focus on number of relevant factors I can mention in the case.
right_wrong: I think I had gone through my resume thoroughly and plus also went through the company deck which started the interview on a very amicable note. After that it was how much practice you had done in your cases.

pre_process_tips: We were initially asked to fill a form which contained basic details, role and location preferences, and a Statement of Purpose. This was followed by a a small video test which asked for 7 questions, similar to the ones in the NPAD.
no_interviews_duration: 2 technical rounds (25-30 minutes each) and 1 HR (10 minutes)
interview_outline: The first interview started with an introduction, followed by some technical questions based on the role. This was mostly technical The next one was similar but focused more on the resume, hobbies and understanding of the role. They asked for detailed explanation of the project undertaken in the summer internship, followed by some follow-up questions. The HR round was basic where they extended the offer. The interviews felt more like a conversation and were breezy.
domain_questions:

looking_for: From my experience, all the interviews felt like they were conversations. They were very affable in their approach and guided through the process and role understanding. And also I think I was interesting enough with my answers to let the conversation be breezy.
tips: Being thorough with the resume is of utmost importance. Preparing for domain related basics is important and PrepCom sessions really help with that. So, it gives one an edge if they attend and attentively focus on what's being taught. Knowing the role and understanding it with some background check of the company and knowing about it (revenue, products/services offered, vision, mission, values, etc.) is important and helps.
dos_and_donts: Generally speaking, be updated with Current Affairs and have a few topics, beyond academics that you're really interested and zealous about (hobbies, politics, etc.). Think of the interview as a conversation and be confident. Having a human touch to your interviews is very important for most companies.

pre_process_tips: The pre-process involved only resume shortlisting before the final interviews. Resumes were scrutinized diligently to identify spikes in the candidate's profile that suit the role offered. Spike can be in terms of academic achievements, work expeirence, internships, academic projects (publishing research paper), or even extra-curricular at state/national level
interview_outline: Started with a brief introduction and some basic questions about work experience. I had work experience in a similar field hence they asked in detail about the projects I worked on. This part took up 5-7 minutes of the interview followed by a case. All 3 interviews were case based and focused on profitability/market-entry/growth strategy related cases. The interviewer was looking for the right structure and approach towards solving the case than the final answer. However I did reach the final answer in 2 interviews, the 3rd one was an open ended case.
domain_questions: As I had work experience in consulting domain, the panelists focused towards asking about the projects I worked on and what I learnt from them. They wanted to know why I left a top consulting firm to pursue an MBA, my reply was that I am looking for a front end consulting role to which they seemed convinced. I was also asked about the industries and geographies I worked with during my work experience.
hr_gk_questions: No current affairs question. HR questions were limited to tell me about yourself. Only one interviewer asked me to describe a difficult situation and how I dealth with it. I focused more on describing how I dealt with the situation and what I learnt from it than describing the situation itself.
looking_for: The panelists were primarily looking for 1) strucuture, 2) logical flow of though, 3) good communication
right_wrong: I followed a MECE approach in all my cases which helped me structure my thoughts and convey the same to the interviewer. It is essential, specially in a virtual set up, to communicate your thoughts to the interviewer in a seamless manner. If the panelist is able to follow your thought process, they will be more interested in helping/guiding you through the case in case you are struck somewhere. I was able to convert the process.
tips: I started with watching the Victor Cheng videos to get a basic idea on how to approach case interviews. Post that, I practiced cases from IIM Ahmedabad casebook and Case Interview Cracked. More than reading the case, what helps is practicing cases in a mock interview setup (preferrably with PGP2s as they have a better idea of what interviewers are looking for). But even practicing regularly with PGP1/friends/family helps as long as you are practicing quality cases (across different industries and frameworks) regularly.

interview_outline: Introduction about myself, Resume walkthrough, Case on growth and profitability, Situation based question, Q & A.
domain_questions:
Case 1: A Domestic Steel manufacturer producing all types of flat and long products is seeing a decline in its revenue so it wants to diversify its product portfolio. I started by listing out the products for diversification. I used the usual profitability framework on the Steel industry value chain for profitability growth. I included almost all the factors that can impact profitability (MECE approach). They asked me to think of the domestic manufacturer as Bhusan Steel in Odisha, as I am from Odisha they asked me to use my general awareness of the PESTEL factors and list all internal and external factors. The transcript of the Case has been submitted to the Consulting Club. 
Case 2: The client is a chip manufacturer who is facing a backlash as its chip packets are found to be leaking at retail stores. What steps will you take to address this issue? There I answered by identifying the stores where it is leaking and finding the defect rate at the retail store end and factory exit gate by doing an inspection. Then will use the 6M approach for RCA, One by one i explained how all the 6 factors of 6M might be impacting the packaging process. 
Panel was positive.
hr_gk_questions: Q: If a client of your team misbehaved with one of your team members how will you approach the situation? Ans: I will reach out to our HR and then through our HR we will approach the HR team of the client company the Manager of that person and the accused himself. Every organization has a committee for such issues, those committees will here both the accused and victim's sides before coming to any conclusion for disciplinary action. They were satisfied with the answer.
looking_for: They were looking for my general awareness, and my case-solving skills, particularly MECE and my professional behaviour.
right_wrong:
Good parts: The questions I asked to them about ESG-related projects, they liked it as the ESG domain was directly controlled and carried out by their CEO. It was a positive impression it seems.
Bad parts: In case 2 in 2nd round, my answers were not structured initially, after some time I structured them well and I took some time to think properly, there were some long pauses. I converted the interview.
tips: The Prepcomms folder helped me a lot. Mock PI gave me a moral boost and guided me to structure a better introduction. Thanks a lot.
dos_and_donts: Practice different consulting cases and don't exclude unconventional cases. Have awareness about industries and ,macroeconomic scene in your home state.

pre_process_tips:
Case
i.	Add a new feature to Zomato, create a roadmap for it. 
ii.	A new revenue stream for zomato for which you also have to make a revenue model for three years)
interview_outline:
Interview 1
-	Tell about yourself
-	What is adtech?
-	What is cookies, cache?
-	Why do websites take time to load the first time but load faster when loaded the second time?
-	How do URLs work?
-	What is retargeting customers?
-	Prodman question: How would you design a smart stick for visually impaired people? This also included delving into technical aspects of how a feature would be implemented. (This question went on for 45 mins) (Did not require CIRCLES) (features thought of were GPS, direction sensing, battery/charging, calling facility, music, have a few buttons on the stick, sense surroundings, UPI payments through NFC, Bluetooth.) (Was also asked to draw and design a few features like charging and buttons)
-	Guesstimate: How many people use Indore airport in a month. (Did not have enough time for this question, so he asked me to rush through it in 2 mins, just the approach, numbers were not required)

Interview 2
-	Tell about yourself
-	Pricing Question: (Went on for 40mins) Flipkart wants to launch something similar to amazon prime subscription, Flipkart First (FF), what would be its monthly price?
o	Checked on the objective
o	Compared the features to be offered by First vs prime
o	Broke down the price for prime based on features
o	FF to offer only free and prioritized delivery as compared to prime.
o	Interactive decision
-	Root cause analysis: (Went on for around 20 mins) Uber revenue per ride is reducing. Find out root cause.
o	Since per ride revenue is reducing, there is no problem with cost and number of rides, there is a problem with fare.
o	Possible causes – reduction in long distance rides, reduction in promotional offers, increase in fuel prices, any updates in apps, only shorter rides possible in smaller cities, people shifting from uber cabs to uber autos
looking_for: Quick to think and varying thoughts
right_wrong:
-	Narrated my thoughts and approach while thinking of new features.
-	Involved the interviewer in my answers
-	Could have read about adtech companies in general
-	Need not fumble if unable to think of new ideas
tips:
-	Do not try and forcefully fit in frameworks
-	Clarify the problem statement. In the Uber question, I started analyzing the problem wrt decrease in revenue, but the problem was decrease in revenue PER RIDE, so there was no need to consider decrease in units (revenue = units x cost)

pre_process_tips: Need to fill in the Amex career portal followed by a cognitive test and then 2 interviews
interview_outline: 1st round was quite balanced and the 2nd round was more technical.1st round started with intro post which some discussions on my summer intern as it was analytics based.After which a few short scenario based questions regarding analytics.A couple of behavioral questions.Was asked about the revenue model of Amex.2nd round was started by an intro and more or less same manner except no HR based questions.There were more into analyzing whether this was the role I wanted and fit into.
domain_questions:
Revenue model of Amex(also how Amex is different from Visa and Mastercard)
In Amazon with available data points generally known to us, how will you find customers whose annual income is above 15 lakhs(there were looking for credit card users as banks would have verified them already)
If you had to target Amex to young people(20-30 yrs) how would you go about it(talked about cutting off the annual charges, bringing more offers like Zomato,Swiggy,)
If you need to target people who use Amazon to sell Amex cards how will you go about the STP?
Talked more about my summer intern as it was purely analytics role,Insights I gained,algorithms used for classifications,Types of tests I used for analysing in SPSS
situational_questions:
Tell 2 of your strengths and weaknesses.
Biggest achievement in life so far
Situation where you felt like your efforts did not receive due diligence
(genuine answers linking to some incident from life.For the last question I focussed a bit on the learnings and experience despite my efforts not reaching the expectations)
hr_gk_questions: Why this analytics role?(Since I had done my UG in IT, talked about how it encompassed and brought in my knowledge from both UG nd MBA)
looking_for: I had certifications in R. They asked about the analytical tools I knew. There were looking for someone with technical background and has a sound understanding of analytics.
right_wrong: Could have gone for more of a structured approach when answering the cases but the interviewer helped and made me go towards the correct approach.What went right was took time to think about the case and answered everything confidently.Knowing the working model of Amex helped a lot.In case based questions I was able to tell them confidently that Amex was using this model,targeting this set of people and hence can adopt this (say XYZ) practice.All quetsions somehow revolved around credit cards only.
tips: Last and before last year interview experience helped a lot.Session by Motiani sir was also very insightful.
dos_and_donts: Be confident in your resume and NPAD questions. See latest news regarding the company and industry before interview.

pre_process_tips: Application form, Screening Test (Accounts +Quants +Subjective Question- Fin), Group Discussion, HR Interview (5 mins) + Final Interview (2 rounds; for some it was 3 rounds- around 25 mins each)
gd_topics_tips: Topic was the subjective question they had asked during the screening test; Tips- Don't throw jargons unless absolutely necessary, try bringing in novel points, keep the discussion to the point
no_interviews_duration: 3 interviews (1 HR- 5 mins, 2 main interviews - 25 mins each)
interview_outline: Both the main interviews started with intro and basic questions about the company and what I understand of the job profile. They focused on one of my fin projects and delved deeper into my understanding of it. After that they asked a few domain questions in relation to my major in undergrad (econ). Finally, they asked if I had some questions for them.
domain_questions: Some of the technical questions were- Views on Inflation, PPP and its implication on company valuation (related to the monetary policy decisions of the gov), Views on sensex and the future of banking. While answering the questions, I tried to break down the terms in the question and then went on to explain the variables that impacted the final dependent variable. Further, a logical flow to the final answer is what they were expecting.
hr_gk_questions: Most of the technical questions revolved around the current economic scenario and a little dive into the futuristic view of the same.
looking_for: I believe they were looking for candidates that had a broader view on the topics discussed and those who could break down the topics into simple terms. They further advised me to build a deeper understanding of any topic that I worked/would work on in the future.
right_wrong:
The good part of the interview was I asked for time before answering questions. This helped me build a roadmap for the answer that I would present to them. 
Something that I should have worked on in hindsight would be to have anticipated what kind of questions they might have asked based on my resume and build answers accordingly to completely ensure that there was no scope for wrong answers from my side.
tips: Read newspapers (business standard and ET)- helps with GD and current affairs, Prep Comm Fin Prep Material and Fin Interviews Question Bank from the Internet ( n number of sources for the same)
dos_and_donts: Don't use jargons if you don't know the exact mechanism behind them; keep answers simple and to the point; smile while answering and try engaging them while answering; you could be honest if you don't know the exact answer to a particular question (I did the same); Be thorough with the JD and asks futuristic questions about the company if the conversation allows so.

pre_process_tips: Application filling (Have to select a COE domain, select the domain that interests you the most) -> Aptitude test -> PI Shortlist after that -> Workshop (Non eliminative)  ->  Personal Interview
interview_outline: Introduction (tell me about yourself) - Few questions from workex - guesstimate - Market entry case from the guesstimate topic  - few questions from the guesstimate topic ( were checking your thinking on feet ability) - asked few questions about finding insights from data - If I have any question for them .
domain_questions:
Question related to Workex - Asked me about few Digital Marketing projects ( my workex was in digital marketing analytics) I did. I did few geo holdout tests for an American bank during my workex - so she asked me about the process of the test, how to segregate data using k-mean clustering. etc ( Be very thorough with each project you mentioned in Workex/ UG project/ Internship) 

Guesstimate Question - Calculate the number of Nike Shoes sold in Amazon India, In a year.
Case Question - Nike India wants to introduce a new shoe in India, what should be its market entry strategy
Questions related to Guesstimate/Case - When we buy a shoe in Amazon, what  products does it recommends us in "users who bought this also bought this" section : Its answer was anything related to a shoe. Like socks, shoe accessories. etc - they upsell us 

She was quite happy with the response
hr_gk_questions: HR Question - Tell me about yourself question and Why do you want to shift from Digital Marketing to Consulting
looking_for: They wanted someone who is good with handling large data, gain insights from it and analyze it better. The other important quality they were looking for was how good you are in thinking on your feet
right_wrong: The part that went correct was that I was able to start a conversation in the "Ask us any question" part. I asked them about the issues they face in data management and related it with my previous workex. This conversation became quite interesting and as I was the last candidate to be interviewed, the interviewer also had the time to share her experiences about consulting and corporates in general. We talked about various data management philosophies used in the industry and How Bangalore's climate is a factor in its Success. The convo went for 20 mins extra.
tips: IIM A Casebooks should be the basic book to study for Cases. Along with that YouTube Channel of Aaditya Agarwal was very essential in understanding basics of case solving. Apart from that before interviews read about your COE very strictly

pre_process_tips: The aptitude test was quite technical. It had sections based on Corporate and Financial Accounting, Corporate Finance, Market Awareness, and Economics.
gd_topics_tips: There was a JAM round where a participant was given a topic and had to talk about it for a minute and a half. The next person had to speak on the previous person's topic for a minute before they were assigned their own topic. The topics were not technical. Example: Electrical Cars in India, Sustainability, Work-Life Balance, etc. It's a good idea to take a few seconds to organize one's thoughts before speaking and be confident and fluent while expressing one's views.
interview_outline: The first interview was quite technical, based on concepts taught in FAC-I and general financial knowledge. The interviewer might repeatedly ask you if you're sure of your answer; do not get nervous. The next interview was HR based, but also went into specific details of resume points (especially projects, subjects and internships). Prepare questions that you might want to ask the interviewer at the end.
domain_questions: Since I was not a CFA applicant, I was not expected to know very complex financial models or jargon. I was tested on basic finance and accounting concepts (refer to prepcom and equiti repository), which I was confident and clear with. It is good to be honest and made reasonable intuitive estimates.
hr_gk_questions: I was asked generic questions like strengths and weaknesses. No current affairs. It's a must to be completely thorough about every single word in one's resume.
looking_for: A person with clarity in basic financial concepts and a general interest in finance. Good communication skills, academic performance and extra curriculars are an advantage.
right_wrong: Being calm and confident throughout both interviews helps win half the battle. Revise well and do not get flustered if you do not know an answer. Answer open ended questions in a way so as to direct your interview towards your advantage. I did not expect random questions from my academic project subjects that were out of the range of the project itself. Since I had used projects from subjects that I was very comfortable with, I was able to recall and answer the questions on the spot.
tips: For a CFA applicant, complete knowledge is expected, but it is not a prerequisite for non applicants. Complete the PPTs shared by Equiti and Prepcom and pay close attention in the domain specific preparation sessions. The mock PI was a good way for me to get an idea of the kind of questions I could be asked and acclimatize to the pressure I would be under.
dos_and_donts: Covered in previous answers

pre_process_tips: Pre process comprised of filling up a form on Reculta and submitting the resume
no_interviews_duration: Had 2 interviews. Round 1 - with a senior consultant at Accenture (30 mins), Round 2-  With MD and Partner (35 mins)
interview_outline:
Round 1 interview - Asked in depth about my resume (undergrad projects, academic and extracurricular achievements). Basic questions like - Tell me about yourself, Why Consulting, Why Accenture. This was followed by a guesstimate. The interviewer asked me to calculate the % of lakes in my city which had different kind of marine life. I confirmed with him about classifying the marine life into small (fishes, snakes), medium (large fish) and large (crocodiles etc). I laid out a structure applying filters like - the location of lake, size, depth, freshwater or not, closeness to human population, closeness to industrial area etc. After confirming with him about the filters, I dived deep into explaining the rationale behind the same and details. He was satisfied and the interview ended.

Round 2 Interview -
I had 3 panelists. One was a moderator the other 2 were of MD/Partner designation. The interview started with - "Tell me about yourself", Why consulting?. This was followed with a case. The problem statement was : Your client is a network provider and is shifting from a one time payment model to subscription model. Which of the departments in the organization will be impacted and describe the level of impact (High, Medium, Low).
After confirming the problem statement and the objectives, I laid out the structure - detailing about the kind of operations happening in the current operating model viz a viz the new subscription model and the pros and cons of each. I then followed up with each division in the company (HR, Sales, Marketing, Finance, new - Customer Engagement) and tdetailed about the changes in operations needed in each along with a rationale.

The interviewers seemed satisfied and gave me the opportunity to ask a few questions after which the interview ended.
hr_gk_questions: Questions on projects mentioned in resume, Academic and Extracurricular achievements related.
looking_for: They were looking for how much variety and variability and depth can we have in the structure that we present to the interviewer for our guesstimate and cases.
right_wrong:
Converted Accenture Strategy.
Good parts - Lying out the structure in case and guesstimate beforehand to the interviewer and confirming with him
Parts that could be improved - could have added more detail and depth in the structure (couldnt think due to time pressure)
tips: The initial ice breaker questions (tell me about yourself, why consulting, why Accenture) really made a difference in setting the tone of the interview. Prepare them well in advance and revise them for each company and profile.

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlist
no_interviews_duration: 2 technical rounds - 40 mins each. After that, 1 HR round - 15 mins
interview_outline:
Round 1 - Friendly interviewer. Calmed me down as I was visibly nervous. Started with brief introduction, which transcended into resume section. I have 4 academic projects (all related to my CS background) and he went through all of them. He enquired me about the challenges me and my team faced during these projects. Ended the interview with asking me why I wanted to be into Product Management. I answered all the questions as calmly as possible at that time. At the end, I asked about the work life at MakeMyTrip and had an interesting conversation on the topic.

Round 2 - Once again, a very friendly interviewer who immediately switched to my mother tongue (Hindi) to make me comfortable. After a brief introduction, he deep dived into my UG and summer internship. Asked me as many follow up questions as possible so as to ensure I had a thorough understanding of the work I did. I answered as honestly as I could regarding the work and the knowledge I gained. After this, he gave me a pretty straightforward guesstimate to solve (number of arrivals and departures daily from Chennai airport). Then he asked me favorite app (I answered Urban Company) and we had a discussion on the business feasibility of the app. At the end, I asked about a fresher's expected career progression at MakeMyTrip.

Round 3 - A very brief formal interview wherein the interviewer asked me about my family background. He enquired about my career ambitions, long and short term plans and the reason for choosing Product Management. He asked about my comfort levels with programming lingo and jargons. Lastly, he asked me what all have I studied for Product Management.
looking_for: They were looking for the right reasons in a candidate to be a product manager. They wanted to ensure a logical and level headed approach to all problems.
right_wrong:
Thorough preparation and reading up on past interview experiences helped me a lot to familiarize myself with a ProdMan interview. 

On the downside, I could have had a more structured approach in the guesstimates and I got nervous easily whenever I felt a certain answer wasn't going the way I wished for.
tips: Stay calm. Stay confident. Make the interview conversational. Read up on past ProdMan experiences and practice cases and guesstimates. Have answers prepared for questions like favorite app, reasons for choosing Product Management and career plans in this domain. If stuck, calmly admit that you are unable to think at the moment and apologize, instead of getting nervous in the moment. All the best!

pre_process_tips: No written pre-processes
interview_outline: Started with the introduction. Focused on the projects which are done. Proceeded to the kind of work optum is doing and they also checked your inclination to analytics. Interviews were more to check your fit in the company and your openness to technical work as well. Knowledge about the company and the work they do is checked. Also, they look for what the motivation is - questions like 'why optum', 'why healthcare' are common. Any projects related to IT/Analytics that you have done could be asked in detail.
domain_questions:
1. What do you think Optum does
A basic research about Optum and Optum Advisory would be enough
2. Why do you want to work for US healthcare
Framed an answer around why its a growing industry and the scale of opportunities.
3. Why Optum
Basic answer to show your interest in the company. Apart from that, pick a unique thing about the company or role that interests you. For eg., I mentioned about their Consulting Development Programme and how it benefits new graduates (and it made them happy!)
4. Compare the Indian and US healthcare industries
Mentioned 4 points on which I would like to compare these and then gave a brief explanation on each point. For eg. the customers, the role of doctors and hospitals, govt programmes etc.
5. Evaluate the opportunities and threats in both
Identified some 3/4 factors that act as opportunities and threats. Mostly from your personal experience/knowledge. And, elaborated these.
For eg. insurance penetration, alternate modes like Ayurveda, etc.
Did not cross-question and seemed satisfied
hr_gk_questions:
1. Strength and Weaknesses
2. How would you want your typical office day to be
3. What if you are given some technical related thing to do
4. Why consulting and why healthcare
5. Where do you see yourself in 5 years
6. Are you looking for a long term career in consulting

For these questions, the approach was to identify some key points and explain it in a concise manner (1/2 lines). Also, at point should you seem to be in a unsure whether to be in healthcare/consulting. The willingness and motivation should be projected.
looking_for:
Willingness to work for healthcare consulting
Background on IT/Analytics
right_wrong:
Good part:
Convinced on my intention to be in consulting and knowledge of the role they offered.
However, the HR questions like 'strengths and weaknesses' remained a  weakness and could have been better conveyed !
tips: Case preparation will help you answer any question in any interview better. A bullet point approach to answering helped a lot
dos_and_donts: Do: Company Research, Role Description

pre_process_tips: A short audio submission of 'walk through your resume' type; A case on company restructuring to accommodate rapid expansion was given[Helps to refer to ODC notes]; CGPA above 2.25
no_interviews_duration: 1st Round - interview with directors, 20 minutes; 2nd round, interview with MD and directors from the previous round
interview_outline: The interview was balanced, they tested mainly on the skills we bring to the table. Qns: Resume, a background about us, Tell me about a situation wherein you handled a large team, faced challenges and how did you go about it; Problem-solving - How much vaccines should be produced to inoculate a portion of Indian population such that herd immunity is achieved, and how will you plan the logistics for the same -supply, distribution. They mainly asked whether I was willing to relocate to Chennai, and that they are a startup organization wherein we would be immersed into all roles, not specifically one domain, and whether I was ok with such a shift from an established organization with definite roles[TCS]
domain_questions: Knowledge on Six sigma, PERT, Lean techniques is tested. Qn on whether we have applied it in any real life problem was asked. Good to have/know about concepts in Green belt certification
situational_questions: Already answered in previous qn..MD round: Why should we select you, what are the 3 main skills you bring to the table, Appln of ops concepts in real life, extension of case from previous round
hr_gk_questions: No current affairs question
looking_for: They are looking for individuals who are go-getters, wants lots of responsibilities and carry a stake in company's development. Green belt certification added advantage, Problem solving [case solving type] approach must be structured, IT experience advantage, but knowledge of basic IT is sufficient
right_wrong: The interviewers were very clear in elucidating the type of role, and nature of job they were coming for. Listen to them genuinely, understand whether you would like to fit in such a role and answer. Structured answers [STAR approach] helps, cite examples on how you managed different things simultaneously. They were upfront about saying that MBA equips you for handling things, but its your call whether to really go for it in a role where you'll be conducting HR drives as well as working on core optimization processes, in a flat organization.
tips: Prepcom Ops material, basic idea of ops concepts works. Solve cases to get the structured approach right. Knowing yourself, and instances from NPAD to support the situation based questions works
dos_and_donts: Kindly understand the role and decide your fit for it before applying, since a lot is at stake when you signup for a startup with rapid expansion plans[Had a series D funding recently, doing well]. With Great Power comes Great Responsibility :)

pre_process_tips: Company directly shortlisted 18 candidates for Personal Interview on the basis of CV
no_interviews_duration: 2 PIs, First PI was for 8-10 min, Second PI was for 18min with VP & GM in Business Strategy unit.
interview_outline: First PI was balanced and more focused around company. It was very short as I was the last person to be interviewed out of 18 people. I started with my intro but was stopped midway and asked my work-ex, switched suddenly to questions like what do you know about the company (spoke in details about company's products & services portfolio), how does company generates revenue( issuer pay model), and don't you think there is conflict of interest between CRA like ICRA and firms whose facility rating is being done (spoke about transparency and regulations by SEBI and RBI).
domain_questions: Second PI was more around direct CV question and critical thinking questions. I was asked about my market research project that I have done during my work-ex. Then, first interviewee asked about the approaches I would take to do market research to  help increase the revenue for the company, that is, to get new clients if some data is being shared regarding service gap in the company (mentioned every possible points), what questions would you ask indirectly as a part of survey to bankers to know about their pricing (related to pricing strategies and asking questions like max, min, ideal amount, willingness to pay extra for particular assessment, etc.)
hr_gk_questions: No HR question asked but only one Current affairs question was asked. Question was "India is growing at a rapid pace and people are buying new cars but ford is exiting India. Why?" (Explained in details starting with customer mindset, how Kia entered into India, but Ford failed to understand Indian market, reasons for the 2Bn USD losses, etc.).
looking_for: I think they were looking for enthusiastic people who were using structured approach to answer questions.. No work-ex compulsory requirement was there as one of fresher was also selected in ICRA
right_wrong: Verdict: converted successfully. Good part was my profile matched with the company requirement.
tips: Go through the company website and JD and understand the role clearly. It will make a huge difference in interview in the last moment preparation. Read current affairs related to your domain or your interest area. Read about credit rating, process of doing rating, factors considered ( all available in ICRA website).
dos_and_donts: Be well prepared for Introduction part- Keep it short and concise. Do mention that you have worked as a team member and team leader ( it always creates good impression!). Try to be humble and speak slowly as if you have not crammed any answers but are actually thinking during interview.

pre_process_tips: Application on the company portal and online aptitude test (1hr) - 20 questions with RC and DI sections
interview_outline:
Interview started with introduction - Tell me a bit about yourself, then asked a few questions about my work-ex and summer internship. Further, he asked a few questions about career goals and why consulting ( while answering this question, try to include the reasons why you would be specifically interested in working with bain)
Then, we went into the case+guesstimate. Case was a market sizing problem where global financial services company wants to launch their app in Indian market for digital distribution of mutual funds, the app works on the similar lines of zerodha, groww etc. and he wanted me to find out actual number of users who will be willing to get onboard such a platform. I kept the problem structure very simple, asked clarifying questions and calculated the market size by following structured guesstimate approach. Once I came up with the final number, he asked me how would I be able to verify this number and my approach for this. At the end, he asked me if I had any questions for him and I asked what kind of projects he is working on particularly in the TMT domain.
hr_gk_questions: Asked "what are your long-term career goals and how do they align with you wanting to work in consulting?" , asked "why did you leave your previous job and what are you really looking for in your next role?".
looking_for: Good quantitative skills and a logical and structured approach. Also they look for someone who can stay calm and confident and keep smiling, keep the conversation light throughout the interview.
right_wrong:
I think keeping the tone conversational and light - one thing that worked for me is to think of the interview as if you are solving or discussing a problem with your co-worker and it can help you stay calm during the interview. 
When he asked me to come up with an approach to verify my final number, I could have been more confident with my answer, I feel I kind of doubted myself for a moment there.
tips: Staying calm, keeping a smile on your face and thinking that your interviewer is your co-worker you are just having a discussion with helped me a lot. Also, as part of the preparation, I had gone through casebooks (IIM A and IIM C casebooks are a good start) and other prepcom material, 1 on 1 mock interviews with your friends also improve your overall performance during the actual interview.

pre_process_tips:
After resume shortlisting, pre-process included:
1. Psychometric test with 2 parts; first real life situation based decision making followed by behavioural questions where you need to rank yourself from least likely to most likely. 
2. Phone call simulation with a client convincing the client to buy your service. There were a total of 5 related situations for which you had to record your responses. Time limit for each response was 2 minutes and you get only two attempts at recording the response.
no_interviews_duration: 2 interviews; first one was for 30 minutes; second one was for 20 minutes
interview_outline:
(1) The questions in first interview heavily revolved around my work experience, including some technical details on the projects I had done. Towards the end of first interview a couple of situational questions were asked where I had to quote examples from my past experiences where I had been in such situations. 
(2) The second round was mainly HR questions revolving around demonstration of leadership skill during my work experience, challenges faced and how I overcame them.
domain_questions: Domain related questions were specific to my work experience. My work experience revolved around Salesforce platform, and CRM tools, so I was asked about the out-of-box Salesforce tools, customisations and configurations that can be done.
hr_gk_questions:
(1) Have you ever proposed an innovative solution which you had to pitch to the senior management for its implementation?
(2) Did you ever give up a short term benefit for long-term aspirations? How did you make the decision and was it right?
(3) Tell me about a situation where you had an idea and it faced a lot of criticism from others in the team? How did you handle the situation? Was it implemented or rejected in the end?
(4) Your profile is very tech heavy and now you are making a shift to its management side. Do you think you will be able to do it? How would you approach your new role?
looking_for: Quality of past experiences, clarity of thought, leadership qualities, approach h to problem solving
right_wrong: Good part was that I was asked questions on my past projects and I had a vivid clarity in that. The interview was good overall, but I felt I rushed through some of my answers which could have been better.
tips: My clarity with respect to the work I have done in the past was a major help. My answers were very detailed and structured, and answered the questions in a logical manner.
dos_and_donts: Be thorough with your past experience and resume. Do not rush while answering the question. Maintain a calm composure and answer the question in a structure and logical manner.

pre_process_tips: No specific pre-process as such. Candidates were shortlisted on the basis of their resume.
interview_outline:
Interview #1 - Basic questions on the resume. The interview was just to gauge an understanding of the role and if you hold a prior experience in the domain offered. 
Interview #2 - Specific and targeted questions on the project (since I had a project on Cyber for Financial Institutions). Though the interview started with the panelist asking me about to introduce myself, she immediately jumped onto the project and asked questions specific to cyber security. 
Interview #3 - HR round. Basic NPAD questions.
domain_questions:
1. What is Data Breach Investigations Report
2. Current scenario and future prospects of Cyber Security
3. Laws and regulations governing Cyber Security
4. Personal Data Protection Bill
5. Who owns the "data" in India
hr_gk_questions:
1. Hometown
2. Why did you pursue MBA immediately after graduation (since I have an experience of only a year)
3. What are your learnings from the course or IIM Indore
4. Why do you think your inclination lies in Cyber Security (since I had certifications like CFA Level 1 and Business Finance - Actuarial Studies)
looking_for:
They were looking for specific domain experience in cyber security/cyber law. My entire interview revolved around the mini project that I undertook during my summer internship.
Qualities like confident body language and ability to communicate your work/internship experience efficiently is what they are focusing on.
right_wrong: As previously mentioned, both the technical interviews involved discussion about the project "Cyber for Financial Institutions" that I undertook during my summer internship. Any portion of your resume having significant work related to cyber law/cyber security will act in your favour as far as this specific role is concerned. This is what the role demands and the panelists are looking for. I didn't require to steer the interview anyway, since they were very specific with their questions. Fair understanding of the resume pointers and ability to effectively communicate across the table is what worked for me.
tips:
Preparatory Material that helped me the most
1. Company Decks
2. Sector Reports
3. Consulting and HR Preparation Material
dos_and_donts:
Do(s)
1. Complete understanding of all the resume pointers 
2. Work on any project related to cyber law or cyber security (If you wish to target this role. Though this may not be their criteria, it will be a great talking point in the interview)
3. Read about the cyber risk, cyber law and cyber security reports published by the different consulting firms and reputed agencies (government or statutory)

Don't(s)
1. Don't stress much!

pre_process_tips: There will be a Screening test on AMCAT. There will be general aptitude questions along with a email writing and a few decision based questions. Overall its a straight forward process.
interview_outline:
I got shortlisted for AI automation. The first interview primarily focused on analytical understanding. After a brief intro, we deep-dived into the Analytical concepts. The questions were based on Central Limit theorem, Principal of Heteroscedasticity, Diff between t-test and Z-test and the utility of the same, etc. Then we deep-dived into my AI project and associated concepts regarding the same. Superficial Knowledge about the project will not be enough as there will be a lot of cross-question on the concepts used in the project. 
Then there was a case on a credit risk company that had given loans to three customers and wanted to analyze in terms of public sentiments the reputation of these companies in the eyes of the customers thereby deducing the health of these loans. The interviewer wanted the solution to contain three parts 1> Data Sources, 2) Platform/Tech including Algorithms that can be used 3) Lastly the Analytics part & the representation of the same to the top bosses of the company who have no idea about the previous processes, so that they could take an informed decision.
The Second interview revolved around my work-ex. The interview asked me to suggest measures, so as to employ AI and automation in my previous companies and then questions followed on the type of solution I came up with.
The Third interview was a typical HR one.
domain_questions: The questions were very conceptual and related to my profile. The interviewer picked up one of my projects and questions were asked left, right, and center. So if there is some technical project(AI/automation) mentioned in your CV know it inside out.
situational_questions:
Question regarding when you used Automation to solve a problem in your work-ex was asked in the second interview.
They will look for the magnitude of the impact created.
looking_for: They look for people who have a knack of solving business problems which a clear understanding of technology in the hind-side.
right_wrong: Have a understanding of the projects, quoting instances from the work-ex is a big plus.
tips: Try to give mock-interviews. One will be a mandatory one arranged by prepcom, besides this try to utilize the Alum Mentorship Program for mocks, have interviews amongst your peers. Prepcom's consulting material is more than enough for cracking consulting interviews. Especially for consulting interviews use IIM A,C,L,I case books. That has an exhaustive list of cases and guesstimates.

pre_process_tips: Applied in both reculta and in TAS portal. All students are asked to take Aptitude and psychometric test. Shortlisted candidates are called for GD round.
gd_topics_tips:
TAS conduced corporate GD. Shortlisted candidates are segregated into groups of 8. Seperate GDs are conducted within each group. In a group totally 8 GDs are conducted. Each person will get a chance to be moderator. 
Topics : 
1) ABC is a joint venture company between government and indian conglomorate company. The employees are mix of generation (Baby boomers, Gen z, millennials). HR is facing problem in work culture. Discuss the issue with your team and come up with a solution. 
2) XYZ is a large mining company who involves in many CSR activities like planting trees etc.., But Government and NGOs feel that their efforts are minimilistic when compared to negative effects of their action. so discuss and provide some solution. 
3) unreasonable boss who is your direct report and a star performer what where were the possible reason for this behaviour and solutions
4) 50 year old car company who is slowing down and loosing revenue, considered an old company, how are we going to make the company's brand image and attract possible employees and customers
5) chairman of digital marketing of a company who's 50% revenue comes from search engines another company approached you for customer data available to you in exchange for better position of your company in search engine. Should we sell the data or not what are the solutions
6) chairman of beauty and hair product-make the customer experience engaging through digital solutions and across all divices and operating systems.
7) A mining facilities working for 100 years which is now barely useful and has no future, 5000 families are dependent on this mine for employment. What is the solutions.
8) Aluminium industry pioneer and projected steady growth the company has a new opportunities (polymer and other), however the company doest have any inherent advantage in new industry. Should the company diversify or focus on the core business.
9) An unaided private school brings a policy where 25% students were not privileged you see a sudden spark of parent withdrawing from the school. Is this a result of the new policy that other parent don't want thier wards to study with them. What are the other factors. discuss
looking_for: good leadership qualities
right_wrong: Individual GD duration will was less. So i cannot able to pitch many points. I cannot able to convert. So express your points quickly and concisely.
dos_and_donts: Have more mock corporate GDs.

pre_process_tips: After the Walmart PPT, there was an application form published on the Reculta portal. There were resume shortlists and the shortlisted candidates went through a GD round. Post the GD round, there was a technical interview (resume + case based). Subsequently there was an HR interview.
gd_topics_tips: You wish to design an app for electric vehicles owners to help them with electric charging ports. You are required to identify the key problems, decide the steps that need to be taken and the features of the app.
no_interviews_duration: Technical interview (resume + case based): 40-45 minutes; HR interview: 25-30 minutes
interview_outline:
For technical interview, the interview started with my introduction and a detailed summary of my work experience. Since I had an experience with retail, I was asked a few in depth questions about the same. Further, I was asked to give details of 2-3 major projects that I had undertaken in my work experience. Then there was a case discussion. The topic for case discussion was: "3rd party marketplaces are slowly reducing the online retail share of Walmart. How would you tackle this issue". Although the topic was slightly broad, I was given appropriate directional clues as the case discussion progressed.
The HR interview was a very relaxed interview. Mostly generic questions were asked. A thorough understanding of NPAD would go a long way in such interviews.
domain_questions: There were no domain specific questions as such.
hr_gk_questions:
In the technical interview, there were questions asked about my resume. I would recommend to have answers prepared for every figure that you put in your resume. 
For HR based questions, nothing was outside of NPAD. If NPAD is prepared well, then the HR interview would be a smooth one.
looking_for: They were looking for people with methodical approaches to problem solving. A relevant work experience would definitely help in the technical interview. Additionally, you should be able to answer the questions asked on your resume.
right_wrong: In the interview, from a soft skill perspective, it is recommended that you show a positive attitude and keep a decent smile. You can also think of a good relevant question to ask at the end of the interview. The questions asked aren't that complicated but definitely require you to think carefully before answering. I converted the Walmart product management role.
tips: In the interview, from a soft skill perspective, it is recommended that you show a positive attitude and keep a decent smile. You can also think of a good relevant question to ask at the end of the interview. The questions asked aren't that complicated but definitely require you to think carefully before answering.

pre_process_tips: CV Shortlisting
no_interviews_duration: Round 1&2 (1 hr.), Round 3 (45 mins), Round 4 ( HR- 20 mins)
interview_outline:
Round 1- Started with "Tell me about yourself" , then focussed on the work done in the previous company and during summers. Then question about how my previous experience makes me fit for this role. After that it went on to a guesstimate and then a case.
Round 2- Started with "Walk me through your resume", followed by HR questions on how am I suitable for the role, what do I get to the table, and subsequent questions based on my answer. Then a case related to my introduction was given followed by a guesstimate.
Round 3- Began with "Tell me about yourself", followed by the work done in my internship and work experience. It was then followed by a small case. After that HR questions and situational questions were asked ( eg- Have you faced a conflict while working in your organisation?, how did you resolve it?). Then another caselet was asked to check my approach.
Round 4- HR round
domain_questions: Questions like why consulting or why particularly this competancy and not any other competancy were asked. Also, questions like how are you fit for Strategy role when your work experience is related to DDV were asked. I had prepared concrete pointers on how my skills or experience is a fit for the role and how my previous work ex also helps me in the same. each point should also have a valid story. Be personalised in your answer, avoid general globing.
situational_questions: Share an instance where there was a conflict and you resolved it. , Have you ever faced a problem of keeping your point across in a team?, If you have a deadline already and a senior person calls you for an urgent task what willl you do?
hr_gk_questions: Why are you fit for this role, What do you bring to the table, How do your colleagues view you as - both positives and negatives
looking_for: The previous experience the candidate had in work ex & summers and how was that relevant to the role selected. Also, the way a person approaches a problem, how they justify their assumptions and how clearly the candidate puts across his thoughts was also given weight.
right_wrong:
Right- Confidence, knowledge about whatever is mentioned in the resume and backing up each answer with genuine and valid stories.
Converted
tips: Consistent case prep in groups, discussion on guesstimates to have different perspectives and ways of thinking, be prepared on industries that are linked to your CV as the case might be related to that.

pre_process_tips: The first round is an online test conducted by the company for the various roles. Post that, the shortlisted candidates had a GD. After that there were two rounds of interview.
gd_topics_tips:
Topic - In the time of recession, should a company focus on debt or equity
The panel gave us the topic and we had to just generally talk about the same. When the conversation was moving in a different direction, the panel members stepped in to steer the flow and asked people who had not spoken till then to give their opinions. They asked us to include any real time examples for the same.
no_interviews_duration: First Interview : 15-20 mins | Second Interview : 5-10 mins
interview_outline: In the first interview, it was more focused on our knowledge about finance, the economy and how different sectors can behave in times of recession and inflation. The first interview was technical. The second interview focused mainly on our interest in finance and why we would want to work at JPMC along with what we think we will be doing in the company in the given role.
domain_questions: Which sectors will not be affected during times of recession/inflation? What are the various ratios that will be checked before giving loan? There were many more questions asked on the ratios. In order to answer the question, even if you can't get to the final answer, just speak out loud your thought process and the interviewer would only help you to get the answer if your thought process is in the right direction.
hr_gk_questions: If I have analyzed any company's statements? Why JPMC? What is my understanding of the role? Why finance?
looking_for: They were looking for someone who had a good understanding of the ratios and has good logical abilities. Even if they do not know the correct answer, atleast the candidate should be able to have good logical abilities to analyse the options if given.
right_wrong: Yes I converted the interview, and the good part is that they were not actually focusing on the correct answer. They were more focusing on the approach to the answer. The bad part of the interview was that I did not have a clear backing as to why I want to do a finance internship when my whole profile was marketing.
tips: I read a lot on the ratios and the best trick was that I remembered the ratio they emphasized in their workshop conducted before. So I included that in my answers which helped a lot.
dos_and_donts: Don't focus on a lot of financial details if you do not have that profile.

pre_process_tips: Filled application forms and received PI shortlist.
no_interviews_duration: 3 interviews. Two 30 minute technical rounds and a HR round for about 15 minutes.
interview_outline:
Technical interview 1: Started with intro, work experience and a bit about engineering as it was my background. I was given a guesstimate in the last 10 minutes while some other interviewees got case study. Guesstimate: Guess how many oximeters were in 2020 to 2023.

Technical interview 2: Lasted for about 35 mins and was similar to the first round: Intro, work experience (asked in depth) and some current affairs about medical field. Was asked about what were the major differences between Indian and US health sector. Case study in the last 15 minutes. Case: You are one of the directors of a multi-speciality hospital. You are looking at the prospect of opening a new branch in a metropolitan city. What are all the factors you look into before deciding the capacity and size of the hospital staff before making a proposal for building the hospital. Also make a GTM strategy for the hospital. I was asked about my knowledge and past experience with Power BI and how proficient I am with it.

HR round: Lasted for about 15 minutes. It was very chill and interactive. Just asked about what I know about pwc, about the role and my interests. Asked about work experience.
domain_questions: Asked about the differences between US and Indian hospital sector.
prep_resources: Chatgpt and asked seniors who interned in the same role.
looking_for: Logical thinking, presentation skills, proficiency with Power BI and PowerPoint.
right_wrong: Was able to crack the guesstimate. Case was a bit difficult because I did not prepare any case that is based on hospital and health services. But I asked right questions and was in the right direction. The interviewer said you were in the right direction but needed a little more practice. I asked the interviewer where i went wrong and what could I have done differently. We talked for about 5 mins on the case analysis. It was a good experience.
tips: I always smiled even when I didnot know how to solve the case, i asked right questions. At the end I asked about how the case should have been solved and where did I go wrong without being defensive. I think that helped. Answered all questions about work experience ro the point. Being thorough with work experience helps a lot.
dos_and_donts:
Show interest in the company. Be prepared about its achievements and current affairs.

Practice lot of cases.

Always smiled in the interview, be genuine, show curiosity and willingness to learn more.

interview_outline:
Round 1 (With Consultant): He just wanted to see the fit and my expectations. Introduction, resume based questions such as work ex, internship, technical skills, why Optum, what does Optum do, why healthcare, what do you know about US healthcare, etc.

Round 2 (With Senior Consultant): Technical heavy. I was asked about my work experience and projects in detail. 3 reasons I want to join the company. US healthcare supply chain challenges (leaving pharma out) since I had worked on supply chain visibility projects during internship. Technical skills and how I have used those in the past during academics or in professional capacity

Round 3 (With Consulting leader): Balanced. US healthcare questions like Medicare, Medicaid, work experience details, technical skills, what is a sales cycle, was asked to describe my decision making process, what are the guestimates- explain with an example, importance of building client relationships and how to maintain them, Out of the box question if I believe in aliens and why? He asked me to talk about myself for 30 seconds straight at the end of the interview

Round 4 (VP from US team): HR heavy. Situation based questions like how have I dealt with conflict in the past, incident where client was dissatisfied, incident where I went out of the way for a client, again I was asked about work experience, internship project, why healthcare, etc.
domain_questions: US healthcare related questions, learn about what Optum does, learn few imp. terms like Medicare, Medicaid, Provider, Payor, etc.
situational_questions: Situation based questions like how have I dealt with conflict in the past, incident where client was dissatisfied, incident where I went out of the way for a client
hr_gk_questions: Why MBA, why Optum, why Healthcare, need to know these answers and their justification very properly since they were asked by every interviewer
looking_for: They were looking for someone who is interested in Techno-management consulting role, communication skills as well as SQL, Tableu, R, python, etc. can help- no questions based on that but they want to see if you have used those skills in the past
right_wrong: Could have been thorough with challenges in healthcare
tips: past work experience in US healthcare was very helpful, good communication skills and justification for interest in healthcare industry
dos_and_donts:
Be thorough with the resume and relate their questions with your past experiences or skills you have displayed during professional or personal life
Make it an interaction, especially the last round. Ask questions regarding the org, industry, their projects, etc. at the end to show your interest

pre_process_tips: The pre-process included a short video where the candidate had to give his/her introduction.
gd_topics_tips:

2. How India dealt with COVID-19
3. You are presenting to an important SF client but your presentation was very poor. What remedial actions will you take.

no_interviews_duration: Round 1: Video Submission, Round 2: GD, Round 3: Interview
interview_outline: Started with introduction, some questions from the resume, some HR questions (same as NPAD), and I was asked to give my opinion on India's foreign policy-TATA merging all steel entities, etc (basically current affairs)
hr_gk_questions:
HR- During the GD, I was posed with situational questions where you had to answer using the company values. 

Current affairs- During personal interview I was asked questions on India's foreign policy( I was following some IAS prep channels so I was up to date on current affairs, I quoted Mr. Jaishankar and some recent treaties), I was also asked whether Tata merging its steel business is good or bad (I did not have an answer for this question but I had some idea of the steel industry owing to IA course so I gave my views using that).

This goes to show that anything can be asked from your resume, make sure that you can back every word and every number with speaking points.

Good part- I was keeping up with current affairs so I could answer current affair questions during the interview. And I aligned my intro with company values (in every company interview) to show that I know about the company. 

(converted)
tips:
1. Mock GDs (It is important that you are confident while speaking. Use frameworks like STAR framework to have proper structure)
2. Company research
3. Mock GDs
