It is important to be yourself, keep smiling and look confident (right posture and less fillers in speaking)
interview_outline: Started with brief introduction. Then the interviewer went on to some HR questions and finally resume based questions. It ended with the him asking if I had questions for him.
domain_questions: No technical question was asked
hr_gk_questions:
Resume: 
1) Asked about which internship had the best learning experience for me
Answer: I had an offline internship with PwC and also one marketing internship. Since it was a marketing role, I didn't want to focus solely on my consulting internship so I mentioned both of them and stated my learnings from those internships.
2) I was also asked about my academic projects 

HR Questions:
1) A situation where you took initiative and led a project

right_wrong:
The interview went very smoothly. After 15 minutes of the interview he asked me if I had questions for him and then for the next 15 minutes, I asked him 3 questions which he answered in great detail. dos_and_donts: Be thorough with your NPAD. Don't do it in a rush, take time to fill it and be truthful. Always keep questions ready for the interviewer (based on the role and the company) and do ask if given a chance. This leaves a good impression on the interviewer.

pre_process_tips:
Application form - Asks for significant achievements - align them with role preference
Screening test - Excel based round (SMOD syllabus - sumifs, index, match, pivots, vlookup) - pay attention to the cell reference (use of $ in the formula)
Multiple Choice based on some short case descriptions

2nd - situation based (for eg. what are the cost synergies when two firms merge?), resume based (about internships)
3rd - short case/situation based to test knowledge of M&A
4th - HR round
domain_questions:
Why do companies engage in divestment?
What are positive and negative synergies?
What are the aspects to look for while doing IT due diligence?

Why is the role given first/second preference? Why this role?
looking_for:

right_wrong:

Provided real life example to possible questions (divestiture examples). Ask questions towards the end of interview that would intrigue them.

tips: Mock PI was a great opportunity to identify my strength areas for interview, and work on areas I as not prepared for. Case books of several campuses shared by PrepCom. M&A preparatory material - elective for PGP2 in Term 4 and 5. Refer to those readings and PPTs (specifically for this role).
dos_and_donts:
Keep a calm mind and think of having a memorable conversation
Prepare cases and guesstimates
Have knowledge about the role, the specific terms in the JD, understand the company back office functions like IT, HR, Finance, Marketing, SG&A, etc.

pre_process_tips: Applied on Reculta. All candidates had to take a psychometric test on the Amazon platform (a simulation case similar to what was done in OB-1). Shortlisted candidates were called for the PI round.
interview_outline:
FIRST PI WAS INCLINED TOWARDS THE TECHNICAL SIDE (OPS/APTITUDE). THE SECOND PI WAS MORE OF THE HR TYPE.
Both PIs started with the classic question, "Walk me through your resume". In that process, they would be taking notes on key points or spikes and would ask questions from those areas (achievement, internships, work-ex, PORs).
Basic HR questions on why Amazon, why the operations role, the latest innovations in Amazon, Amazon Leadership Principles, questions on favorite subjects, and questions on the Amazon delivery process and how it can be improved.
domain_questions: Not too tech-heavy, PI. Just emphasize Amazon's 16 leadership principles and the STAR approach in your every answer; they are more or less looking for that only!
hr_gk_questions:
1- Where do you see yourself in 5-10 years
2-  Why Amazon and how you align your goals according to the leadership program they have in place
3- What was the most challenging task you faced and how did you approached it (star approach)
4- Company's JD
looking_for:
Just emphasize Amazon's 16 leadership principles and the STAR approach in your every answer; they are more or less looking for that only!
Domain-specific work experience, internships, certifications, and PORs are add-ons.
right_wrong:
GOOD PARTS: I explicitly made them notice my domain-specific spikes: CLUB KAIZEN MEMBER (OPS CLUB of IIM-I) + EY's LEAN SIX SIGMA GREEN BELT + CII POC + NIT (EE) + IIM-L DATA ANALYTICS INTERNSHIP. I played along those lines during my entire PI, thus getting their attention.

BAD PARTS - I could have done  better in 1-2 NPAD questions.

Final result: Converted
tips:
Materials :
1. OPERATIONS DOMAIN SESSIONS ORGANIZED BY PREPCOM + STARTER DECKS
2. LEAN SIX SIGMA GREEN BELT MATERIAL (if you have any)
3. ECONOMIC TIMES NEW PAPER FOR CURRENT AFFAIRS
4. COMPANY'S JD
5. NPAD

MOCK PIs (DOMAIN + HR): GIVE THEM DILIGENTLY AND WORK UPON THE FEEDBACK GIVEN. THEY WILL SERVE AS STEPPING STONES FOR PERFORMING WELL IN FINAL PIs.
dos_and_donts:
Do(s):
1. Prepare the company, JD, very diligently.
2. Base your answers around Amazon's 16 leadership principles.
3. Situational answers are to be given in STAR format.
Don't(s):
1. Don't bluff. In front of seasoned HRs, politely accept your shortcomings and convince them that you will work on them.
2. Don't ask questions just for the sake of asking.

pre_process_tips: Resume Short Listing
gd_topics_tips: It wasn't the GD. Microsoft had written case interview. Topic of the written case was "Due to the pandemic many employees are forced to work from home. Considering their new work model, how can Microsoft help organizations ensure the well-being and success of their employees. As a Microsoft PM , think of ways in which you can leverage and innovate upon Microsoft products to meet the evolved needs."
gd_duration: 30 minutes for writing the case document. 15 minutes for review by 2 panel members
interview_outline: There were 3 rounds of interview. Each one of the round started with tell me about yourself. In the first round it started with my work ex project and then the cloud concepts as I had worked on AWS. Next was one case and then it revolved about the metrics which I would consider for success. The case asked in this round was " As a PM at netflix you are given the responsibility to increase the adaption of Netflix in the age group of 60+. How would you approach this problem." 2nd round was again a case based interview taken by Senior PM. This round had 2 PM case questions. First question was "Design an alarm clock for blind people" and 2nd was " As a PM of WhatsApp in the year 2018-19, you are given the responsibility to decide the timeout for the newly implemented "Stories" feature. What all things would you consider while arriving at the timeout value". 3rd round was again a case based round taken by the Director. One was a PM question "As a PM how would you approach solving the problem of out of memory problem in mobiles". Another question in this round was aptitude question similar to CAT question.
domain_questions: There were no specific technical questions in the interview. Everything was around my work experience and PM cases.
hr_gk_questions: There were no HR questions asked to me throughout the interview process for Microsoft
looking_for: Mostly they were always looking for product management case solutions and the approach to the solution rather than solutions.
right_wrong: I followed the CIRCLES framework for all the design questions. And my work experience was on cloud computing and was well versed with it. In the first round the interviewer tried to dig deep into my experience in cloud computing.
tips: Do check the youtube videos for PM interviews. They will be very much helpful for preparing for the interviews. Product School is one such channel which is helpful.
dos_and_donts: Follow the framework and do go through few of the PM interviews on youtube.

pre_process_tips: Mckinsey conducts an assessment game called "solve". The game consists of a tower defense mini game and an ecosystem building mini game. Both games require the candidate to work through large amounts of data. It is advisable for students to go through some YouTube demo's on what is expected in these games.
interview_outline:
First interview : Started with a case followed by a conversation around college life. Discussion was very short and focused on recommendations around the case.
Case: Netflix is facing a declining revenue, figure out why and diagnose

Second interview : Introduction followed by a case followed by some resume questions. Focus on structure and problem solving approach. 
Case: Develop a incentive strategy for grass root level marketing for a sanitary ware company
Partner round 1: Guesstimate followed by some HR questions. Interviewer was looking for the right approach for the guesstimate
Guestimate: Estimate the number of flights in the air at the moment.
Partner round 2: Case followed by discussion on Mckinsey culture. Focus on structure and recommendations.
Case: A large pharma player wants to become a top 5 player in india, how can they achieve the same ?
hr_gk_questions:
Q. What is your favorite pastime on campus ? 
- A general ice breaker question, where the interviewer was trying to understand more about me. I mentioned that I enjoy to socialize and described some fun experiences I had on campus. 
Q. Of the 2 PoRs you hold, which did you learn the most from ? 
- The interviewer was trying to understand the impact and leanings I had from the PoRs I held. I had a PoR from my undergrad Placecom and one from my undergrad Debating society. I described how the debating society PoR was very meaningful to me as I was able to make a significant impact.
looking_for: Problem solving skills and ability to communicate effectively. No prior experience was discussed.
right_wrong: What went right : Recommendations provided where highly appreciated as I had some unique solutions to the problems presented.
tips: For case prep I had gone through Victor Cheng's videos on youtube. Moreover, I had a case prep buddy and we practiced daily for about 15-20 days. It is also important that during the interview you stay genuine.
dos_and_donts: It is important to practice with someone who can help with your blindspots. The biggest mistake people make in solving a case is not understand the problem correctly. Make sure you have the practice which prevents that from happening

pre_process_tips: We were required to fill an application form on company website. The form asked for basic background details and also asked us to write about our prior work experience in brief. It would be beneficial to focus on the work-ex brief; work-ex brief can create a lot of difference in your profile.
no_interviews_duration: 2 interviews. 1st round - 30 mins and 2nd round- 45 mins
interview_outline: Round 1- The interview was focused on understanding if I was the right fit for the role. Questioned were around how my prior experience (work-ex and academic) would help me in the role I was applying for.  Questioned revolved around data analysis, domain preference, why consulting and whether a a specific division in consulting such as finance, marketing etc. The interview was more of a discussion format. Round 2- The interview was more focused on my prior work-ex in risk consulting and HR questions. There were two interviewers in the panel. The interview started with a quick discussion on the round-1 interview and then moved ahead into work-ex discussion. The interviewer was focused on understanding my roles and responsibilities in my previous organization. The interviewer wanted me to define my role in a case format- starting from defining the problem statement, the process to solve the problem and then after present the outcomes. More technical questions were asked pertaining to my work-ex and internship. The second interviewer focused on HR based questions. The questions involved strengths, weaknesses etc.
domain_questions: Since I was applying for a consulting role and my prior experience was in consulting as well, the questions revolved around my roles and responsibilities in my previous profile and what had been the approach to solve cases (or complete projects) in a real life scenario. I emphasized on both- team efforts and individual contribution. I made references to as many examples as I could in order to better explain the process.
hr_gk_questions: No current affair based questions were asked. HR questions were about how well I worked in team and individual scenario, my strengths and improvement areas etc.
looking_for: In my opinion I think they were looking for confident strong headed individuals who would be a good fit for the team. Also, work-ex is an added advantage.
right_wrong: I think giving real life examples and being confident and to the point helped me during the interview. Maintaining your calm during the interview would be of great help.
tips: Keep your cool and take your time before answering. Do not rush into answering the questions. Also do not forget to smile during the interview.

pre_process_tips: Post the application through reculta, some shortlisted students got to take the psychometric test, post the pyschometric test there was a video submission round and after that the final interview. All rounds were eliminatory
no_interviews_duration: One final interview, duration was about 20 mins
interview_outline:
Started with intro 
I was asked some questions based on my introduction, was asked why sales, then questions about why I as an engineer would want to do sales, if I was comfortable with tier 2 cities, then questions around situations that I would face in a tier 2 city and how would I deal with language barriers, I was asked some domain specific questions indirectly as well. 
The overall interview was slightly stressful though 
the interviewers were quite engaging.
domain_questions: I was asked about what all brands of chips exist in the market other than the ones by pepsico, then I was asked a question about how would I launch a Pepsico product in a village in Bihar, I was also asked a specific question- they asked me if I’m aware of any chips brand which is local, and then they asked me why was this chips selling/being sold by retailers when big brands like pepsico exist
hr_gk_questions: Tell me about yourself, why sales, why sales after doing BTech and having a technical background
looking_for:
There was no work ex expectation as such, I believe they were looking for people who can talk in an engaging manner, are spontaneous, creative and can think out of the box
Overall good communication and not getting nervous if they put you in a stressful situation helps.
right_wrong:
What went wrong would be my initial answer to why after BTech would I want to do sales, could’ve framed the answer better
There were some answers that I could’ve been better prepared for instance the answer about how I would launch a product in a village in Bihar

tips:

dos_and_donts:
Donts - don’t ignore NPAD

Work on your ability to communicate in an engaging manner and thinking on the spot

pre_process_tips:
1. 7-min quiz based on company's brands and recent initiatives

gd_topics_tips:

interview_outline: Started with introduction, delved into why MBA and why this particular role (a lot of cross questioning on this part), moved to questions about team skills, past experiences of working in/handling teams, challenges faced (team based questions mostly from NPAD), moved to questions about the role and my expectations from it (a lot of time spent on this), and some basic HR based questions. Lastly, opportunity to ask any question from the panel. HR heavy, almost no technical questions asked.
hr_gk_questions:
1. Why MBA? Why FMCG industry? Why this particular roles after a very different background? 
2. Short/medium term goals & how the present role helps in achieving them?
3. Challenges faced working in/leading teams during undergraduate? My learnings.
4. My expectations & understanding of the role? How do I future in it? Am I open for a different role like operations in the company?
5. Failures and learnings from them.

There were lot of cross questioning on every answer, so the correct approach is to answer honestly. Sticking to the points prepared for NPAD helped answering most of the questions. My approach is to answer from a learner's perspective looking to explore & understand the particular domain.
looking_for: Good at working in/leading/handling teams, open to learning, have clarity regarding the role and kind of work
right_wrong:
1. Good Part: Well prepared with the information about the role. Described well my past experiences of working in teams. Able to align my short/medium term goals with the offered role.

2. Bad Part: Hiccupped in explaining why I am switching from my UG background and opting for a S&M role. 

Converted.
tips:
1. Being thorough with the NPAD helped the most during the interview. Most of the questions were covered in NPAD.
2. Be very clear with the role and why do you want it.
3. Marketing Compendium and related material helped preparing for the case base GD.
4. Company knowledge gives one added advantage over others.
5. GD/PI were very helpful. Helped structure the preparation in the right direction.

pre_process_tips: Company asked to choose any startup and  analyse it. The objective was to write a 200-300 word thesis on why the firm should invest in that startup. I gave a ratios based analysis from the annual financial statement and also gave justifications on how the ratios translate to startup's day -to-day operations. The idea was to present as many angles of looking at a companies performance that can justify an investment. I also gave my own recommendation on which areas does the company need to improve in terms of operations and financials.
interview_outline: Introduce yourself, why mba as a fresher, why vc firm, any prior experience with startups, resume questions, describe internship, questions about Utsaha, Any questions for us
domain_questions: No technical questions. But we did talk about the firms current portfolio of investments and how they want to invest in companies which are solving problems of the future.
hr_gk_questions: Both interviews were mostly about my life story. Since it was about me, I did not have to prepare or fake any story. I think they were mostly looking at my way of communication and presentation.
looking_for: The JD was for Thesis writing where I have to submit detailed reports on the various avenues where the firm can invest. In that sense, clarity of thought and presentation were what they were looking for. I have no prior experience with startups and zero interest in entrepreneurship......so that was clearly not a parameter for their decision.
right_wrong: Interview converted. What went right was that I was comfortable and smiling throughout the interview. the questions were about my life story and interests so I was at ease during my interview.
tips: I had prepared basic finance and ratio analysis which were taught in class. I had one mock HR round( Thanks Humain_I). For HR round NPAD was a good help. I had completely changed my NPAD answers just a week before the interview. So Tip would be to keep updating your NPAD and add more personal and recent stories.
dos_and_donts:
Read about the companies portfolio. Whiteboard does not have a specific industry or a broad portfolio that it invests in. As a seed funding firm, there isn't a lot of number crunching. Your thinking process matters because you must provide good recommenations about where the firm should potentially invest.


There was also an Entrepreneur-in- residence role mentioned in the JD which involved making GTM strategies for the portfolio companies. Whiteboard did not conduct process for this role.

pre_process_tips: Case study submission on their latest product ( MG1 Mixer Grinder)

Then a guestimate was asked and followed by some HR questions. The first interview had very few HR questions whereas the Second interview was HR heavy. Many questions based on my resume were asked. The introduction of a product into the market and my ideas on it were asked. 
In both the interviews I was asked about how would I respond to various situations that might occur if I got the role.
domain_questions:
Guestimates and go-to-market strategy was asked. For guestimate i was asked to calculate the mixer grinder market in India and for go-to-market introduction of Flying cars was asked.

hr_gk_questions: No current affairs questions were asked, but many questions based on my resume were asked. I was asked about my gap year and my PORs. Questions based on my introduction were also asked. Basic HR qns like tough situations I faced during my work, I resolved them etc.
looking_for: Logical explanations for the ideas I submitted for my case study. How I would handle the situations that might come up and do I know about the company.
right_wrong:
My research on the company helped a lot. I tried to let them know that through various answers even though it was not directly asked. I had a couple of questions prepared to ask them which came in handy in both interviews.

 Being strong on basic marketing ideas will help a lot. That's a field I could have improved especially in the go-to-market question where I was cross-questioned a lot.
I did clear the interview.

pre_process_tips: Psychometric test - video interview in HirePro/Hireview platform. A question would appear with 30 secs to prepare and 3 mins to talk about. Total of 5 questions. domain_questions: series of questions related to finance academic project mentioned in resume -> asked about minority interest and its affects in valuation -> series of questions related to valuation
hr_gk_questions:
Where do you see yourself in 5 years from now?

Why Bank of America? it was connected to previous question

tips: Prepcom finance material for valuation and company decks to know about the culture of the company along with secondary research, notes of FAC, Fin-1, Fin-2, finance electives in 2nd year and Secret sauce of CFA lvl 1

role_offered: Risk & Financial Advisory Internship - Cyber Risk Services
pre_process_tips: Pre-processes included building of a customized resume in the format specified, which included a profile summary and reason to apply to Deloitte for that role. This resume should be uploaded to the Deloitte Careers Website, along with other details in their application form. No other screening tests conducted
interview_outline: The interviewer introduced herself first, then asked for my introduction. She then delved deeper into the Cyber Security Research Internship part of the resume, asked for details on it and also some questions on the concepts used. She then asked for details if and where Cyber Security risks were identified and resolved in my work experience and what more could have been done. Finally it ended with HR based questions. domain_questions: Most questions were based on the technical details based on the projects, internships and work experience part of the resume. I tried to follow the STAR approach in the form of a story in a chronological order mentioning the technical details wherever relevant. The interviewer showed curiosity and was pleased with most answers.

looking_for: Relevant work experience, internships and projects would give an edge in the interview. Else it would be helpful to find a relation between them and cyber risk. Enthusiasm towards the company and the role would be helpful.
right_wrong: I answered the questions asked from the resume well, I had prepared the technical details well. I answered the HR based questions about the company and the role were answered well. dos_and_donts: Although it was not asked to me specifically, but knowing about cyber threats and recent events on cyber security breaches and attacks would be helpful. Prepare NPAD and Resume well. Be enthusiastic about the company and the role.
