Further they were also looking if you fit there work culture. They were questions regarding which team i would want to join in GPS and what is the kind of work do we do under GPS.
right_wrong:
I had answer to almost all the answers in the interview. Further the JD matched my academic background. I could have handled the technical questions in the 2nd interview a little better as i fumbled a little in that. 
Converted
tips: Read the JD and prepare accordingly. I knew that the questions would be from economics and i prepared that. Further mock PI is important specially from HR question point of view (at least in my case). And do prepare HR questions, over and above NPAD and ask friends to review those answers
dos_and_donts: Do read about the company from their website and about the role as well. Try to align your answers not only to their values, but to the role as well.

pre_process_tips: Screening, 1 buddy round, 1 technical round, 1 hr round
no_interviews_duration: Buddy round- 20 mins group call followed by 45 mins of individual interview and individual interview.  Technical interview was around 40 mins. HR round was hardly a minute where HR just wanted confirmation on if I would be joining or not.
interview_outline: Buddy round (individual part) started with a problem involving affect of transaction on all three financial statements after various different durations and required in depth knowledge of all statement ( whatever was taught in FAC was enough) . Briefly touched on valuation portion and talked about company role and all. Technical round was again on same lines with questions on all financial statements but also asked questions from valuation portion including fcf and wacc and all. They also expected that you know what company actually does so read the jd properly and Google terms and know the basics of what project finance and corporate finance is.
domain_questions: All three financial statement (FAC level), Valuation (prepcom material was helpful with slight more google research and good to go), JD(google jd stuff and learn it's basics).
hr_gk_questions: Briefly talked about a current affair topic related to my past internship which was in finance so not much stress on current affairs.
looking_for: They wanted people with good understanding of accounting and someone who knew what company does and had basics of finance clear. FAC level is enough but what worked for me in both rounds was that I was talking to them whenever solving questions and was taking them through my approach so even if I was making mistakes (which I did plenty) they would point it out then and there only and they were aware of where I was going wrong and this way my silly mistakes weren't confused for conceptual errors. Know FAC thoroughly and then walk them through every answer.
right_wrong: Talking to them entire time and walking them through my approach really worked in my favour. I did commit few errors where I blurted answers without thinking but managed it by slowing down and telling them where I was going wrong. Also research properly what company does this surely gave me some brownie points when you know what you're supposed to do for company and for that go through jd and ppt shared and then connect it how it aligns with what you did and why you want the intern.
tips: Staying calm and don't be afraid of uncomfortable silences.
dos_and_donts: FAC is enough for three financial statements, For valuation FCF and WACC stuff read prepcomm shared material (super helpful) and Google for slight more depth. Google about JD stuff really helpful

pre_process_tips: Preliminary aptitude test covering mathematics, logical reasoning, accountancy, economics and finance.
gd_topics_tips:
1. How can one assess that an industry carries, can you give examples of risky and relatively risk free industries? 
The discussion mainly spoke about different sectors and industries and the risk they carry in terms of their interaction with different parts of the economy. At the end of the GD, each of the participants were handed a chit wherein they were supposed to write a financial ratio that would be the best to understand the risk a firm carries in an industry. 
2. The final GD was a case based GD wherein we were given the financial statements of a high net worth individual. We were supposed to discuss the various factors that go into the pricing decisions of the lease based on the risk analysis of the financial statements. The topics were thoroughly covered in the workshop held right before.
interview_outline: Asked for an introduction while the interviewer went through the resume. Process was centred around the work I had done in my internships (M&A profile internships, so highly technical questions around DCF model, valuations, etc) and certifications, primarily in the field of equity derivatives (covered trading strategies, black scholes merton pricing model). Was satisfied with my interest in finance based on this so ended the interview.
domain_questions: DCF Model, how are the three financial statements connected, valuations of financial securities, companies, and HNIs, options trading strategies, black and scholes model of options pricing.
hr_gk_questions: Only the intro, tried to end the intro on a hook (something you want the interviewer to pick up on and continue the discussion) so the interview started off by discussing the extracurricular activities section.
looking_for: Interest in finance, fact checking in terms of the knowledge I have as compared to the work mentioned in my resume.
right_wrong: I was able to convert the interview because even though I had quite a technical interview as compared to all the other candidates because of the past internships and certifications I had done, I was actually able to answer all the technical questions correctly, which went in my favour.
tips: Mock GD was not so helpful because the final GD was a case-based GD. In terms of prep material, the Red Book by Wallstreet Prep was very helpful. Prepare a sector regardless of the role, it would be helpful even if it seems irrelevant to the role.

no_interviews_duration: Round 1 (30 minutes), Round 2 ( 60 mins), Round 3 (30 mins), HR (20 mins)
interview_outline: All the interviews were balanced - Resume + HR  + Technical questions related to the role
domain_questions:
Round 1:
- Top 3 technology trends - Read Gartner reports
- As a scrum master what would you do if two of the critical resources have been infected with COVID during  (i). Start of the Sprint (ii). Middle of the sprint
- Assume Nokia is planning to divest a BU. What factors would you consider post closing the deal (My previous work ex was with Nokia networks)

Round 2:
- Walk me through the Mergers and Acquisitions course (elective)
- Case: Your client is a technology service provider and has 6 BUs. He is planning to divest 2 units - Healthcare and Telecom. The acquirer of HealthCare unit is a strategic buyer and Telecom is a PE buyer.
(i). How would your technology DD differ in either case?
(ii) What factors would you account for if the Healthcare unit is bought by a US acquirer vs a global acquirer?
(iii). How would you optimize cost for the client with only 4 BUs now?

Round 3:
- A bigger company divests a smaller unit. The divested unit wants to migrate to cloud. What factors would you consider ?
- Difference between the cloud migration strategies - pros and cons of each
- How would you choose a particular cloud service?
- How would you evaluate the run rate of the cloud?
situational_questions:
- Tell me about a complex problem that you solved
- Tell me about the most challenging job that you have done
- Why not Microsoft or Amazon? ( Depends on your profile)
- Have you liaised with global teams?
hr_gk_questions:
Walk through your resume
Why PwC?
Why Consulting?
Why M&A?
looking_for:
- Interviewers were trying to assess the impact of whatever is mentioned in the resume
- They were looking for points that were unique for a candidate ( try to highlight why you are a better choice for them - it could be from your work ex, POR, academic projects etc.,)
- Basic knowledge of M&A, Technology, Work ex- exposure to project management, stakeholder management
right_wrong:
- Resume preparation is important especially the work experience
- Try to build stories from your past to justify why do you fit the role.
tips: Please read about M&A, technology due diligence, TSAs, Day 0, Day 1 and Day 2, M&A lifecycle

pre_process_tips: Application on Reculta followed by resume based short listing for PI
interview_outline:
Both the interviews (Online) were a mix of questions related to my work-ex and HR. The first interview (Skill interview) was more about two-way interaction and the interviewer made it clear in the very start of the interview. He was frequently asking for queries and I asked many question mostly about the work culture, types of projects and his experiences so far with the company. 
I was not asked any case or guesstimate.
domain_questions: No company specific question was asked by the interviewers.
hr_gk_questions:
Some of the HR Questions asked in the interview 1- Tell me about yourself; What is consulting according to you; What are the skills required for consulting and how will you rate yourself; What are your career goals; What are your aspirations; Why MBA
Some of the HR Questions asked in interview 2- How do you relate with tech and digital and do you have and experience of that; How has been your experience till now at IIM Indore; What is your understanding of consulting

My approach to answer HR questions was to keep the answer very specific and the most important thing is that tried to back my answers (wherever possible) with real life experiences (mostly work-ex) also I tried to keep it as simple as possible (No jargons and wherever I used any technical term, I explained them in brief and then continued with my answer)

Apart from HR questions, some decision-making questions were also asked where a scenario was given and I had to tell what would be my approach. I was also asked about my roles and responsibilities during my work-experience.
looking_for: I believe they were looking  for people who are curious and passionate about the role and the company and were judging on the skills and cultural fit.
right_wrong: The Interview was more like an interaction so it was just like a formally talking to a person instead of giving an interview. I asked so many questions to the interviewer (perhaps more than he asked me). Converted
tips: NPAD is very important for such interviews. Mock PI was very helpful in assessing the level of preparation which helped in improving my performance in the company interview.
dos_and_donts: Be thorough with you NPAD and resume. Keep the interview as interactive as possible by asking questions, be calm and keep smiling.

pre_process_tips: They have a 250-word minimum written submission on a topic related to tech. The topic for us was "Will automation transform the job industry?". More than the stand, it is the approach, logic, and facts given that matters.
no_interviews_duration: Case round 1 (30), Case round 2 (45), Partner round (40)
interview_outline: Round 1 : Tell me about yourself, why Everest and what do you know about Everest, what do you know about the role, followed by a case. Round 2 : Tell me about yourself, why Everest and what do you know about Everest, what do you know about the role, followed by a case followed by a few Hr questions. Round 3: Hr questions with a small case (this was for me only). It is most case based and on your resume. Make sure it is a good conversation, stay pleasant.
domain_questions: On outsourcing in BPS and IT.
situational_questions: How I fit in with the role, how my previous work ex would help and how MBA will help.
hr_gk_questions: "Why not to hire you?", "Tell me about yourself", why everest, why role, mostly from NPAD
looking_for: Research oriented, hard worker, structured, analytical, and someone who have conversations with clients.
right_wrong: Right - Able to link my sales work experience and case competitions with the role, Held good conversation, kept a smile and pleasant demeanor, did the cases decently well. Wrong - Probably should have had more technical (domains the company operates in) questions and knowledge. Converted the interviews.
tips: I worked on my resume and HR questions well. I did very few cases from each type, and I would say I got lucky with easy cases. Guesstimates I learned the general approach and the key data points. Prepcom made casebooks available which was very useful. The HR questions guide was exemplary. The company deck came in handy in each interview, probably without which I wouldn't be placed. I didn't have a GD, but the interview was okay. Roy Charles sessions aren't as insightful as it can be.  Ananya R's sessions on consulting and prep were much more insightful.
dos_and_donts: Do - SMILE. Keep the conversation going. If you make a mistake, take it in your stride smoothly. Keep a structured approach for the cases. Generally it is simple. Read about the company, what the role is, why the company, how you will fit in. Donts - Don't freak out. Keep calm. It isn't do or die. Just give it your best.

pre_process_tips: CV uploading on their careers site besides reculta, psychomteric test, GD, interview
gd_topics_tips: Case based GD: We were given a small write-up on how technological advancements are inevitable now. In light of the same we had to discuss on "The future of work in 2025". Try to bring in new perspectives and do not center your answers around banking. Also, the moderator already mentioned that he wants a discussion so keep it civil.
interview_outline: General introduction about myself; what domains interest me followed by quite a few HR questions. It was HR heavy
hr_gk_questions:
No current affairs questions, only HR. Be thorough with your NPADs. They saw marketing in my core electives and asked the difference between sales and marketing. They also asked if I understand how FMCG related sales is different than a banking related sales. They asked me if I am comfortable with a sales role (this is not sales, but involves lots of client interaction). I told them how through my PORs I have had to talk to a host of people. They asked to elaborate on this point further so I told them the kinds of people I had to deal with in the three roles mentioned in my resume. I was asked if it was me who initiated the connection with all the stakeholders mentioned so I answered according to the PORs. Their questions were quite focused on my interactions with different kinds of people.
Besides this, I was asked about my background and if there are other colleges who are offering this course; how does my course help me in the role being offered. I also had an NCFM Investment Analysis certificate on my resume so they asked me if I am interested in finance and if I would like to persue this line further.
looking_for: Someone who is confident and good at communication
right_wrong: Converted the interview: I had a lot of experience relevant to the role and I made it a point to promulgate it in my answers. I did so by referring to my resume and pointing out that this is where I used the skills you want me to use during the role.
tips: Company deck to align your views and values with that of the company.
dos_and_donts: Be very throrough with your NPADs and relate NPADs with your answers which can be exemplified through points on your resume.

pre_process_tips: Resume based shortlisting followed by a psychometric test.
gd_topics_tips:
First : Case based GD, about 25 minutes allotted to read the case and discussion. My group was given a market entry case of an insurance firm.
Second : Guesstimate submission where 15 minutes were given for case read and solution submission. Case was about same insurance firm and it was asked to estimate the number of 4 wheelers sold every year for personal use in India.
no_interviews_duration: 1 interview (50 minutes, Technical + Behavioral + Situational + Guesstimate solving)
interview_outline:
Only 1 interview of 50 minutes was there. PI started with tell me about yourself followed by questions on internships and projects. Detailed description and reason behind choosing them was asked. After that some hypothetical situations were given where my perspective and plan of action was asked. Then company fit and role fit questions were asked.
A guesstimate extending the case given in the GD was asked where I was supposed to calculate the ROI if the same insurance company launches a website.
situational_questions:
Q1 : People, Deadline, Revenue - whom would you give preference and why ?
Q2 : Since your profile is very diverse and you like to try new things, how long would you stay in one role and if project is long enough would you leave & handover to someone else and switch?
hr_gk_questions:
Basic questions like : Why MBA, Why this role and company, How you are perfect fit for this role and Where do you see after xx years were asked.
In short, be thorough with NPAD questions and have basic understanding of the role(ELITE GM Program) and company.
looking_for: Good analytical, logical and problem solving skills and someone with appetite to learn and willing to explore new.
right_wrong: The answers revolving around their requirements which pretty much matched with my profile too. The way I presented each and every answer relating with any of my strengths or achievements in the past helped me to maintain my interviewer's interest throughout 50 minutes of interview. And structured answers and guesstimate solving was the key to crack the interview.
tips: Preparation of case interviews and guesstimates helped as GD was case based followed by guesstimate submission and one guesstimate was asked in the PI also. Additionally, structured answers keeping the role in mind helped.
dos_and_donts: Be confident, prepare structured answer for each line of your resume and try giving glimpses of your strengths indirectly while answering their questions.

pre_process_tips: Application form with personal and resume-based details
interview_outline:
1 - Introduction, Resume details, questions about why PwC, why Operations, guesstimate, HR questions.  (Balanced)
2 - Introduction, Resume details, questions about why Operations, Case, HR questions. (Technical Heavy)
3 - Introduction, why PwC, why Operations, questions about clarity of the role offered, HR questions. (HR Heavy)
4 - Introduction, HR questions. (HR heavy)
domain_questions: What is the value chain of an FMCG company like? (Spoke about only the primary activities, forgot about the support activities; no response)
hr_gk_questions:
Were you in a team when working on a task? What problems did you face in the team? (Freeriding a major problem, the opposite also very common - someone takes up a lot of tasks, spoke about importance of distributing tasks effectively and timely reviews to check progress ; positive response)

Problems faced as a team leader. (gave examples from internship where a member was not contributing, I spoke to the person, tried to understand his problem and redistributed tasks to help him cope, got high contribution and active participtation from him later in the project ; positive response)

Why should we select you? (spoke about my strengths and how they align with the role; positive response)

Why should we not select you? (spoke about weaknesses and how I am working on them; positive response)
looking_for:
Proactive nature when it comes to solving problems
Eagerness to learn
Workex is a plus, but is not necessary
Interest in the domain
right_wrong:
In my 1st interview, my approach to solving the guesstimate was incomplete. I feel like I could have taken other factors into account as well.

In the 2nd interview (Case interview), the case I had been given was a real case that the interviewer had worked on. I was able to give a few recommendations which were actually implemented and got a positive response for that.
I got stuck twice, where the interviewer wanted a certain answer from me but I was unable to come up with it. I took my time and reviewed the data I had. The interviewer was helpful and pointed out areas I should focus on. This helped me arrive at the desired answers.
tips: Company Deck was really helpful in answering questions about the company and the role. Mock PI helped in pointing out areas I needed improvement in, especially in regards to domain-specific topics.

pre_process_tips:
Initially, there was a resume shortlisting, followed by an online test. The test consists 2 RCs and 3 DI sets with an overall duration of 60 minutes. Difficulty level was moderate. RC questions were more like inference based. Prioritization of sets is a key (basic CAT strategy).
In JD/brochure, there was a mention of case workshop but they shared a video recording for the same (which was really good).
no_interviews_duration: Round 1 (30 min)   A few selected students sat for round 2 as well
interview_outline: Started with Interviewer introducing herself and then my introduction. Asked Why consulting. Then we moved to a Market sizing guesstimate (I mentioned about sports in my intro so she picked related topic)
domain_questions:
Why consulting? I gave a very crisp answer of around 1 minute where I tried to cover what consulting means for me by showcasing a few examples from my experience so far.
I mostly avoid using the cliche words associated with consulting and formed my answer in very simple and relevant way which i felt the interviewer liked.
looking_for: My interview was very straight forward. The interviewer cross-questioned me on my assumptions for the guesstimate. I defended them well. And I think they were mostly looking for how well you clear your thoughts are.
right_wrong:
The interviewer cross questioned me about my penetration rate assumption for the guesstimate. I defended it by stating my own experience with which she seemed very impressed. 
The interviewer also asked a ball park approach, for which i took a little time and still could not come up with a strong answer, where I think I could have worked better. I honestly accepted and shared whatever thoughts were there.
tips:
First of all, self confidence. Believe in yourself that you can make it. I tried to avoid any comparison with peers. 
I had very clear cut targets for each day. sorted my priorities in terms of what to prepare first on the basis of my experience of summers. 
My advice is to first of all have a look at all the available resources and then prioritize/select. I also referred to the case books of other B-schools. FMS & IIML were really beneficial. 
Must do P2P case solving sessions. Just reading them wont help.
dos_and_donts:
Be prepared with your resume. You should not only have explanation for any specific point but also think of cross questions and prepare accordingly. 
Have a good motivating self talk each and every day.

pre_process_tips: There was a gamified psychometric test, you download a game a play in on mobile. Fairly straightforward
interview_outline: The interview was mostly resume based with one case, there were two interviewers one from HR and one from business. They concentrated on the academic and live projects, and the learning gained while doing these. There were HR questions mixed in between which were asked as follow up to things that came up during the interview, try not to get thrown off if you get some unexpected questions. While solving the case, the interviewer kept telling me to go more in depth while I felt that I had more or less solved the case as per the initial requirements, I think this part was more about how I react when I feel a little out of my depth and requirements were not clear. The key here was to maintain composure, I got a little tensed and messed some calculations at this stage, but they pointed it out and I was able to rectify the error and move on while maintaining a confident demeanor.
situational_questions:
Tell me about a significant non academic challenge you faced and how you overcame it?
I did not have a prepared answer for a non-academic one, so I took a minute and gave them an answer.
While I did talk briefly about the ways I dealt with the challenge. They're next question was to give 3 concrete steps I took to deal with this issue. 
Since they do cross question like this, it would be best to talk about a genuine scenario even if not that significant.
looking_for: I think they were looking for individuals who could maintain composure in unexpected scenarios.
right_wrong: I messed up some calculations which was bad. The good part was they seemed to appreciate genuine answers and gave very positive feedback on especially my BTech project ,which they appeared to be genuinely interested in and impressed by.
tips: The most important material for this interview would be the NPAD in my opinion, I would even advice thinking of answers for variations of the NPAD questions. While they did not actively ask me anything about the company, going through the company deck and understanding the company values and what they are currently doing and integrating these into your answers will help in any interview and here also it did.

pre_process_tips: Application on Reculta --> Further info through PC forms --> Resume shortlist for Online Assessment ( Included aptitude and psychometric both)
interview_outline:
Panel had 1 HR(HR) person and 1 Senior Management(SM)
SM started the PI, asked for brief introduction; questions regarding under graduation details,
mostly CV based questions, wanted some nice insights about one of my Intern work. Where did I see myself(role wise) - why's and what's of why I wanted that role. Why Reliance ? There were some questions regarding my internship experiences also but 80% questions are already covered through NPAD
domain_questions: Gen Man roles are mostly looking for leadership qualities. Not so domain specific per se. Your POR's will be judged as well and important for that matter. Having 3-4 decent POR's are must to have good talking points during the interview.
hr_gk_questions: Small use case from the club POR cv point that I had. The HR quoted the first line I mentioned in my resume and gave a small situation based question that I had to analyze. Relatively simple if you know your CV in and out. Current affairs regarding the diverse businesses that RIL had.
looking_for: Previous intern and current full time contacts have mostly suggested that RIL looks if you are an organizational fit for them. It's as simple as that. The interview I had, I would definitely concur the same.
right_wrong: Mostly rights , almost no negative points during the PI(personal opinion) -- I could relate to the role as well and sending that message across during a PI is important. Need to be a jack of all trades for Gen Man - RIL looks for that.
tips: Tips from previous interns, current full time employees, NPAD preparation, Domain sessions by Prepcom and company decks are some of the must have hygiene factors.
dos_and_donts:
Do(s) -  1. Pay attention during the basic domain sessions
2. Try to take the maximum out of Senior's prep sessions(ask questions wherever necessary)
3. Read a lot about the company , any new upcoming M&A, projects, past history.
4. PLEASE PAY ATTENTION DURING COMPANY PPT. Some hints regarding how PI's are going to be will already be given during company PPT's.

Don't(s) - 1. Wait for starting your prep till you get a shortlist (Start now)
2. Overthink about getting an offer
3. Never hesitate to take your time to respond to situational questions.

role_offered: 9,9,7; Engineer with 2.5 year work-ex in IT
pre_process_tips: No specific pre-process
gd_topics_tips:
Topic: Is the Metaverse here to stay?
The panel discussed about the prominence of the term and why is it getting so much attention. The benefits (connecting, remote operations, etc.) and negative effects (costly technology, misuse, etc.) of the technology was discussed.
interview_outline:
The interview started with questions on my resume - “TMAY with all the important phases of your life and how you handled them as a product manager”. Further questions were on my work-experience like my role, experiences and learnings.
•	Then he asked about my most used applications and selected Spotify for discussion. Questions ranged from the revenue model to the current issues and suggested updates to the app. I suggested launch of a Summary feature for Spotify Podcast & introduction of exclusive BTS footage to garner user interest.
•	Then I was given a case on how I would go about launching Spotify if they decided to enter the video streaming business. I explained my solution assuming India launch and explained the target user segment, app features, USP, tracking KPIs and pricing.
•	At the end, I was asked a few questions about Walmart.
domain_questions: Asked about the Spotify launch case mentioned above.
hr_gk_questions: Resume based questions were asked as mentioned in the interview outline answer.
looking_for: Companies hiring for PM roles typically prefer work-experienced candidates, so relevant retail or IT work-ex is beneficial. Your critical thinking skills and understanding the customer needs are very crucial as they help in designing great products.
right_wrong:
I felt that I performed really well in my GD which probably helped me in my interview as well. I built a great rapport with my interviewer and displayed a keen interest in Walmart's business.
With respect to the Spotify launch question, my suggestion of branding Spotify as a one-stop shop for all things entertainment was also well received and appreciated.
tips:
* Diligently go through and prepare the Product Improvement and App Critique Sections in the casebook. You can expect a question from any of the commonly used applications.
* If you have a technical background, you could get asked some questions pertaining to the language used, especially SQL
* If you don't know the answer, politely communicate it to the interviewer. Do not beat around the bush
* Also read about the company, its business model and important news pertaining to the company

pre_process_tips: Application on Reculta
interview_outline:
1 panelist- from Credit Risk Dept.
1. Asked for introduction only on educational background and related achievements.
2. Asked how my workex (manufacturing) would be relevant to the role ? 
3. Asked about subjects I'm currently studying and how I can use them in the role.
4. Past experience in coding
5. Any questions that I had.
domain_questions:
1. Any financial ratios  I studied and their significance in my past employer's company
2. Explaining basics of distribution curves studied in IPS- Examples of normal distribution curve in real life . 
The panelist was super chill, he was supplementing my answers with examples of his own and encouraging me to refine my answer before moving to the next question.
hr_gk_questions:
Q. Why I wanted to work in Axis if my past experience was in manufacturing ?
A. On my resume every workex point has some financial relevance mentioned. While working I learnt to look at the business from a financial perspective and hence I want to change my domain.
looking_for:
They wanted candid answers. They were also checking how much I've learnt in the first term FAC and IPS courses and if I can relate it to real life situations. I have achievements in various math olympiads at school and college level which helped me justify some of my answers.
Knowledge of programming languages would have also helped. I replied that while I haven't used any of them since graduation, I can build the logic to solve a problem, and learn the syntax of whichever language the application needs.
right_wrong:
Converted
My interview was preponed by a few hours and it clashed with another process. The panelist had to wait a few minutes before I could come online. He mentioned that before asking for my introduction. I apologized in a very genuine manner (gave a good impression). After that he was pretty chilled out. 
He asked if I have any questions- I framed the Q using the exact words from some of the workex questions he had asked previously. ( I was not prepared with questions of my own so initially I said no, the panelist told me to think carefully and ask)
tips: Mock interview with prepcomm was quite helpful. In class discussions with FAC prof were also very useful for this interview.
dos_and_donts: Learn 1-2 topics from all term 1 subjects.

pre_process_tips: Only application form fill-up
interview_outline:
Round 1 (15 minutes, 1 panel member, Balanced interview)-
The interview started with "Tell me about yourself". It then moved on to my resume details on work experience and internship. Like I had an internship in a steel industry and work experience in IT so I was asked a question on how technology can be leveraged in the steel industry. I was also asked questions on the entire value chain of steel industry. Further questions were asked on my work experience and my roles, the challenges that I had faced during my work experience years. What were my other roles during my work ex duration other than the normal project responsibilities. 
Round 2 (20 minutes, 2 panel members, Balanced interview)-
The interview started with Why consulting domain and what makes you switch to consulting from technical domain. What are things you are aspiring to learn as well as contribute during this internship. Next the interview moved towards my work experience where I was asked to explain the end-to-end implementation of my project. I had follow up questions on my work experience and a situation based question which was again aligned to my work experience. Further questions on Master Data Management (MDM) was asked and why MDM is being adopted by industries. My work ex project was based on MDM.
domain_questions:
There was no specific company related questions but I had questions from Why consulting and reasons for switching from technical to consulting.
My approach was to bridge the gap between technical and consulting considering the prior client roles that I had already experienced.
hr_gk_questions:
No questions on current affairs.
HR- What challenges were faced by you during the work experience duration and how did I react to the same?
looking_for: In depth knowledge on what one has done prior to MBA which includes the work experience and internship and any other point mentioned in resume
right_wrong:
Right- My explanations on my work experience
Wrong - While explaining the value chain of steel industry, I considered that not up to the mark. That could have been better.
Interview - Converted
tips: Calm, presence of mind, knowing each and every point in resume
dos_and_donts: Do(s) -  Preparation on resume very well specially on work experience and internship. Even though my internship were done long back I was still asked questions from them.

pre_process_tips: Interview Directly
interview_outline: Started with Introduction, then went straight into a case which was followed by a guesstimate. Considering the case and guesstimate as technical topics for consulting, it was very technical heavy.
domain_questions:
CASE: Your client is a namkeen company operating in Western-India that has a revenue of 100 crore. They are looking to grow to have a revenue of 300 crore. What can you recommend to them?
GUESSTIMATE: Try to estimate India's yearly diaper consumption.
hr_gk_questions: 1. Walk me through your resume.
looking_for:
1. Creativity
2. Problem Solving
3. Communication
4. Attention to Detail
right_wrong:
What went right?
1. I was able to organize the case answer very well.
2. The solutions offered were fairly exhaustive by the end and the interviewer was asking for more ideas simply to see if I could keep coming up with more.
3. The interviewer was well satisfied by the approach to the guesstimate. I started by saying diapers are consumed by infants, the elderly and for those with medical circumstances such as confinement to the bed in hospitals, loss of bladder control due to medicines etc. In the end I asked if she wanted me to estimate to number for the 3rd group as well and she said that there was no need and that she was just glad I'd thought of it immediately. 
4. When asked if I had any questions for her, I brought up the split of EY consulting from the audit business which had happened just a couple of days prior. She said it was good that I was up to date on the company.
tips:
I started preparing just the night before when I saw that I had an interview in the morning. I called a friend who told me to go through the IIM Ahmedabad casebook as much as I could and took up a couple of cases just before the interview.
The mock GDs didn't help much because there was no GD round.
The mock PIs were useful at providing interview practice which I'm sure was instrumental.
dos_and_donts:
1. Stay updated on all the company news and know the company well.
2. I think the main selling point in the guesstimate and case wasn't the structure as much as the ability to think of different possibilities so maybe look at the cases in that way as well?

pre_process_tips: Shortlisting followed by Case Workshop and Buddy Round (both non-eliminative)
interview_outline:
Round 1: Started with basic HR questions about Deloitte and my profile followed by a guesstimate. Further conceptual questions were asked from within the guesstimate. Additional questions were asked based on my answers.

Questions:
Estimate the number of customer service employees required by a food delivery app for its Grievance redressal services for the customers in Indore.
How to reduce staffing costs.

Round 2: Began with a brief introduction about myself, based on which some questions were asked. An in-depth explanation of my summer internship experience and my takeaways from the same. An open-ended problem statement was given to find ways to increase margins and cut costs for a client. Further, detailed data about the company's expenses and revenue was shared, to draw insights.

Questions:
The client is an international B2B Pharma and Biotech producer. How to increase the profitability of the company and improve margins.
Insights were asked, along with recommendations based on the data provided about the company.
domain_questions: There was no direct technical question, but based on the problem statements, questions related to Supply Chain Optimisation were asked.
situational_questions: Weaknesses and how you overcame them?
hr_gk_questions:
Tell me something about yourself (Some questions were directly asked from the answer to this question)
Why Tech-consulting, Why Deloitte?- Had prepared the answers beforehand
Summer internship experience- More about the project, client, and my role in the team
Something not on your resume?- Talked about my role as the Junior Placement Coordinator in the first year
Strengths and Weaknesses
Where do you see yourself in 5/10 years
looking_for:
Ability to approach a Business problem, practically.
Clarity in the Value chain of the business.
Ability to comprehend financials of the company and draw insights from it.
right_wrong:
Good- Was able to analyse the Value Chain exhaustively, during the case interview
Bad- Forgot the name of the first interviewer, which was asked in the second round
tips:
The preparation for the consulting domain roles was mainly based on figuring out the most convenient framework for different cases and practicing cases.
Preparatory material used: CaseBooks of BLACKI IIMs and FMS; Past interview experiences.
dos_and_donts:
Do(s): 
Have a good look at the JD before the interview and have a clarity about the role
Be thorough with the basic HR answers
Don't(s):
Panic (the interviewers are pretty chill)

no_interviews_duration: 3 Interviews (R1: 20 mins, R2: 30 mins, R3: 20 mins)
interview_outline:
R1: Introduction, Understanding of JD, Resume based questions (Finance projects, case study competitions), Risks in futures contracts and how to mitigate them, Basics of Call & Put options
R2: Risks involved in lending to Financial Institutions (Hedge Funds, PSBs), What type of instruments we can use to mitigate such risks (think of derivative instruments as well as qualitative tools such as covenants, downgrade triggering etc.); Detailed discussion on Margins in futures contract, Basics on Option Greeks
R3: Categories of instances in which the firm can be exposed to credit risk, then HR & Behavioural questions (Be as conversational as you can), Soft offer handed : )
domain_questions:
--Margins of futures contracts (Take an example and explain it, that way the numbers tell the story)
--Derivatives (How they are a source of risk, and How they are a robust category of tools to mitigate the risk...Understand both the sides)
--Mix of stats and option contracts (If a portfolio contains 5 securities, and we have 1 call option on that portfolio whose payoff is decided according to some pre-defined relationship, how will it pan out if the correlations between the securities increase or decrease etc.)
--Opinions on current monetary policies (this was linked to my #1 interest, that is keenly following central banking and global economics)
--Current affair questions related to new types of risks emerging (e.g. Chinese macroeconomic policy changes, De-globalization, Tail risks such as climate change etc.)
situational_questions:
1. Instances of failure, and how I handled it
2. What did I like and dislike while I was an intern, while I was working etc...
3. How did interest for Finance shape up (Try to be honest...give instances such as following XYZ sectors, excelling in XYZ Finance case competitions or Finance electives)
hr_gk_questions: 1. Top 2 strengths
looking_for:
1. Keen & Honest interest in Finance
2. Sound knowledge on derivatives contracts, basic statistics
3. Ability to understand mistakes, own it and course-correct
right_wrong:
Good: Genuine interest in Finance & Economics, Good grasp over Derivatives and Markets, Resume
Could have done better: More practising of HR/Behavioural questions (to structure these answers properly)
tips:
--I was damn crazy about Finance and International Economics
--Followed certain sectors of my choice (esp. Indian Banking industry), and certain eminent professionals in the financial field of my choice (Global markets, Central banking)
--Positions in case study competitions

pre_process_tips: Resume on Reculta followed by a buddy call which was normal interaction about why consulting and why redseer
interview_outline:
1st Interview :- Introduction, Company related questions (What do we do, New progress), Case related to growth and M&A in the next 20-25 mins (Domain Heavy)
2nd Interview :- More HR questions, Why Redseer, Why Consulting, What did you like in the previous round case. (HR Heavy)
domain_questions:
Your Client is a Online Turf booking platform and they have seen stagnated growth in the past 2 years.
Approach was similar to the case framework, asked about organic growth and then inorganic growth. (Medium difficulty) The main idea was to cover each branch under the framework as the panel wanted to look for the approach.
At the end he gave me a scenario that let's say Amazon wanted to acquire your client would you go ahead with it or not take a measured guess.
My response was they should go for it as Amazon has the capacity to market our brand and since we have no resources left this is a logical method to save our business.
hr_gk_questions:
Why Consulting.
Why Redseer. ( Varied Domains, More collaborative work can learn from other teams as well)
Since Redseer has startups as major clients and there is a funding winter going on what do you think this means for the business? (Responded that in the long run this would subside as India's startup ecosystem is growing so it would in a way bring more opportunity to us)
looking_for: They were looking for detailed problem solving approach, My past experience in tech consulting worked in my favour too, they were looking for hardworking individuals as well because they mentioned that the working hours could be long as well.
right_wrong:
I think my approach to the case was detailed I covered most branches in the framework, My Past experience in tech consulting aligned with the things the panel were looking for.
Converted the Interview.
tips:
Be Prepared about the company, what they do, who are the major clients and news related to that. 
Make sure the things you said in the buddy call you stick to that as to why you want to join Redseer.
The mock PI was helpful because it helped me craft a better introduction and my approach to cases.

pre_process_tips:
1) Resume shortlisting (No form filling)
2) Aptitude test + Algorithm test: For algorithm test, a problem statement was given with tabular data and we were required to write an algorithm to create a loop and calculate something.
interview_outline:
1)1st interview with Project Manager: (Online) Tell me about yourself, few resume questions, one small case
2) 2nd interview with Associate Director: (Offline) TMAYS, went into resume details, gave 2 medium-length cases one after another
3) 3rd interview with Managing Director: (Online) TMAYS, one small case and few resume questions
domain_questions:
1) Asked whether I know any programming language- I said Python, so I asked to write a program to check palindrome. Next, told me that a company wanted to implement a fraud detection system and asked how I would do it using data analytics. The interviewer stressed a detailed answer, and the keywords he was looking for were big data, trend analysis, etc.
2) The first case was based on data analytics; the case had tables, and the task was to write an algorithm to process the data and get the required output. In the second case, they gave multiple tables and asked to write an SQL query/Python algorithm to fetch a specific combination of data.
3) Gave a small Quant-based case (similar to what is asked in the CAT exam) and asked to solve it manually and then write an algorithm for the same.
hr_gk_questions: Basic HR questions like where do you belong to, what family does, why do you want to join Sutra.
looking_for: They were looking for someone with strong algorithm-building skills and good knowledge of programming languages
right_wrong:
Interview status: Converted
What went well: I came up with my algorithm quickly compared to other candidates; others were asked only 1 case in an hour, but I was asked 2 cases in the same time frame.
What could've been better: At a few points during the interview, there was a long silence, so I could've engaged the interviewer better.
tips: Be thorough with big data analytics and know at least Python programming language and the libraries used in it for processing big data.
dos_and_donts: Always prepare one good question beforehand whenever the interviewer asks "Do you have any questions for us?" as it gives you an opportunity to express your interest in the company.

pre_process_tips: 1 Application form along with 1 form of HR based questions and 1 form which was given after the 1st interview which asked details of any project that you pursued till now
interview_outline:
1st interview had 5 panelist, 4 physically and 1 virtually, this interview had some technical questions. 
2nd interview had 3 panelist, 2 physically and 1 virtually, this interview was driven mostly by resume based (PORs) and HR questions.
domain_questions:
What frameworks do you know?
What is 4P and 7P in Marketing? How do you apply this framework? Give an example where you have used?
STP?
Market Entry Framework? 
Electives based questions like what did you learn in Social Marketing/Consumer Behaviour?
hr_gk_questions:
No Current Affairs.
HR questions-
Why BPCL?
Why Marketing after doing an internship in Investment Banking?
What were your learnings from the startup you tried to pursue? How would you do it differently? There was a lot of discussion on this in the 2nd interview like what was your investment? How much did you make? What methods of advertising did you choose and why?
Why are you a part of GMLC? How does it create value? What are the parameters that you judge the outcome on for any activities of GMLC?
prep_resources: Know every single thing on your resume. Go through the basics of Marketing and its applications. If you have an internship in Marketing they can grill you on that.
looking_for: Not technical heavy interviews, mostly tried to asses culture fit and why you did what you did till now on your resume. They were not looking for heavy technical knowledge as when I asked what can I read to prepare myself better for the job, they said you will have a training scheduled where you will be taught everything you need for the job. But yes, willingness to learn, someone who takes initiative, hardworking and commitment were some of the qualities they were looking for.
right_wrong: Me knowing my resume went right
tips: Know every single thing on your resume.
dos_and_donts: Do not argue with the panelist, Do not use heavy jargons to flaunt your knowledge, keep your answers simple and straight forward. Have topics that you can speak on in the interview, for me it was the startup that I worked on and IIM I PORs

pre_process_tips: Resume based shortlisting followed by a Buddy round & Case solving workshop
interview_outline:
Round 1 (Guesstimate) : The round started with HR questions related to hobbies and interests and projects mentioned on the resumes. They ended the round with a guesstimate(Number of microwave ovens in a tier 2 city)

Round 2 ( Case Interview) : A technical case based on prior work experience domain
Problem statement : Our client is planning to migrate their on-premise servers to a cloud based model. What all aspects will you consider while making a final decision regarding the cloud migration strategy to be recommended to the client.

Round 3 ( Director/Partner Round) : This was a generic conversation with the director/partner to judge whether the candidate would be a perfect fit for the team/company. Did not have any specific questions and the interview was an open ended conversation. Also judged the awareness and knowledge regarding the company and the work culture and why you would like to join for this position.
domain_questions: Technical questions included questions around Cloud computing and cloud migration strategies. What all aspects to consider while recommending cloud migration to a client. Benefits and tradeoffs of shifting to a cloud based model etc. . They asked technical questions based on the projects undertaken by me as part of work ex.
right_wrong:
I worked towards maintaining a conversational tone all throughout the interview. I was confident with the technical aspects of the questions asked to me which I feel went right for me.
I believe I failed at following a structured approach of solving the case. Although the technical aspects were correct, I lacked structure and flow while communicating my thoughts to the interviewer.
Result : Converted
tips:
Mock GDs/PIs did not play a major role in the interview process and were not very helpful.
NPAD is extremely important and helpful for all companies irrespective of domain/profile.
Be extremely thorough with all points mentioned on your resume.
dos_and_donts: Be confident and thorough with whatever you are saying during the interview. The interviewers were looking for how confident/firm you are with the ideas you are presenting. Be prepared with company background and work culture. If you have prior work experience have clarity regarding the projects undertaken and the impact/value delivered through your contributions to the project.

pre_process_tips: Application forms-PI
interview_outline:
Introdution
Went directly into the resume. I had experience in the Business Development and they dug very deep into the workex. 
S&M and Supply chain Case based questions. Changed the case parameters to make it difficult.
The questions on workex covered the domain of S&M as well as Supply Chain.
domain_questions: There were no academic focussed questions. But how you apply what you learnt in the case was the focus.
hr_gk_questions:
Explain about the product which you were dealing with?
What did you do in the job daily?
How did you plan the Business development?

Supply Chain focussed questions?
How did you do the vendor development for the product that you manufactured?
How did you plant the distribution of the machine? What all did you consider while planning the distribution?

S&M
There is a platform of LnT where B2B business is transacted. There are tile adhesive manufacturers which we want to tap. How would you approach the situation? 
There were a lot of follow up questions over this like 
How will you convince the adhesive manufacturers to come to the platform?
What could be the customer base for these manufacturers? How would you bring in the customer base for the adhesive manufacturers? How would you develop positive network externalities?
(I had worked in the adhesive industry hence the questions were focussed on this topic).
looking_for:
Planning, 
Problem solving,
 People with good amount of workex especially in the secondary sector.
Thorough knowledge about the workex
right_wrong:
I converted.
Good part was that I was well aware about my workex hence I was able to answer the questions satisfactorily.
Bad part was the case based problem. They dug deep and hence I got stuck at a point. So it would be better if you can go prepared with thorough knowledge of your workex and practice a few case based problems before appearing for the interview.
tips:
The prepcom decks
NPAD
IIM Indore Case book
Mock GD/PI gave good insights about the process and helped to gain confidence.
dos_and_donts: Very important for people who have good amount of workex to be aware about their role and responsiblities which they performed. Be well aware about the major projects which you had accomplished. Quantification of the result could help to give you an edge in the interview.

pre_process_tips: You have to fill the application form both on Reculta and company websites, then there is screening test, which is basically aptitude based on quant, VA, LRI and basic coding
no_interviews_duration: 2 round of interviews, 1st - around 30-40 mins, 2nd - 15 mins
interview_outline:
1st round - Started with Introduction, picked 2 specific project from work experience and the discussion went for 10 mins, then asked question about relevant quantitative and qualitative metrics used in PM, the 2 guesstimates
2nd round - Started with introduction and mostly HR question and some questions about Japanese culture and language as I have worked in Nomura
domain_questions: No technical question related to product management. But there were questions like why Prodman, why Amex, etc. They mostly talked about my workex and HR questions
hr_gk_questions: HR based questions - Prepare your NPAD questions (No questions were outside of NPAD) thoroughly, take it seriously and always use the STAR framework to answer your HR questions. No GK questions
looking_for: In my opinion they were looking for someone who is good at what they have done till now and have enthusiasm about the role and company. I didn't have any ertification related to coding or prodman, but I asked interesting questions related to company and role, which showed my interest toward the company and role.
right_wrong:
The good part was that they didn't asked me any questions related to prodman or coding, whole interview revolve around my workex and HR questions
Bad part was justifying how I am a better candidate that Computer science graduate who already have relevant workex and when they asked to solve one puzzle, I changed my anser 3 times even though I was correct in my first attempt
tips: Focusing on resume and NPAD really helped. Discussing with friends and seniors about the company and role also helped. Mock GD/PI helped but the quality of Mock GD/PI could be improved.
dos_and_donts:
Don't get disheartened if you are not getting shortlist or if you are getting shortlist but not able to appear for interviews. SIPs are totally random so prepare for 2-3 domains don't be so rigid on any specific role or companies. Talk to seniors, talk to your batchmates on how to improve your resumes and what to prepare. Take your resumes and NPAD seriously.
Just put your efforts and relax (its easier said than done :))

pre_process_tips: No pre-process
gd_topics_tips: The topic was "Work Life Balance Vs Work Life Inclusion".Time was 11 minutes(1 minute for preparation and 10 for speaking).It would be a good idea to jolt down your points, start the GD and try to bring structure into it .3-4 decent attempts with good points will surely help to convert GD.Try to bring new and relevant points while acknowledging others .Be confident.
interview_outline:
1st interview: Was asked to introduce myself,then there were mostly questions based from my resume , Hr and Summer Intern
2nd Interview:Was asked what is the differentiating factor about me and why should they hire me and other situational based question
The Interview was mostly HR and Resume based while having a thorough understanding of Job Description and how your past experiences is related to that role. Since I am a fresher I tried to connect all my internship experiences with this role.
domain_questions: Not really. At the end of interview I was asked if I had any question for them. I asked them about 5G technology that wipro was working on(researched their linkedin page) and asked them about Azim Premji foundation
hr_gk_questions: Mostly situation , Hr and Resume based question. It would be better if you can tell them stories about situations and your past experience(PORs, internship, work ex etc) and try to make the interview more of a conversation and engaging.
looking_for: Energetic, Passionate and proactive people who are willing to learn and deliver high quality results . A previous experience with the role or a fair idea about it will be a plus point.
right_wrong: I was as honest as possible with a constant smile on my face and telling them all the stories about me that made me the person I am today and how I will do justice to the role by having great passion for sales and marketing and showcasing that I worked in a startup and handled all kinds of  work assigned to me and delivered up to the mark while stating achievements at work(internship). Be confident, cheerful and approachable.
tips: Thorough with Resume, Hr and summer intern as well.Telling them stories while showing high level of energy and passion to work.
dos_and_donts: Having an idea about company's current affairs and showing genuine interest in working with the company.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlist by the company
interview_outline:
1st interview- Tech based and resume focussed. Started with 'tell me about yourself', 'Why DTDC', 'Do you have any tech background'. Then went into technical part, was asked about 'KPIs of warehouse management' and was also asked a guesstimate- 'How many parcels do you think Kolkata office of DTDC handles per day?' 
2nd interview- HR based and a proper testif you are fit for the role. Was asked if I have any proper idea of the role. Then asked basic HR questions like mention your strengths and weaknesses. Then I was asked suppose that you are currently working on that role, what breakthrough innovation would you suggest for DTDC in the tech domain. Was grilled on that part for a very long time.
domain_questions:
KPIs of warehouse management
Talked about inventory turnover, no. of shipments being handled per day, inventory management systems like ABC classification and all.
situational_questions:
I was asked suppose that you are currently working on that role, what breakthrough innovation would you suggest for DTDC in the tech domain?
 Had gone through DTDC company ppt and the company website, so I had a basic idea of the various tech products that DTDC currently employs and talked about it and gaps in the current system and how it can be improved
hr_gk_questions:
Q- Why DTDC
Align your answers with company values like customer centricity and innovation. How you identify yourself with the values and why the role perfectly suits you
Q- Strengths and weaknesses
Again align your strengths with company values. Don't mention any major weaknesses and talk about how you are dealing with them
looking_for: Person who knows about the current workings of the company inside out, basic tech background, can come up with new innovational ideas
right_wrong: Similar to the next question I think
tips: I had researched about the company properly, so was able to answer whatever they had asked me about the company and the role. Asked them a lot about the company and about anything which I hadn't understood from the JD and the ppt. That probably showed that I am interested in the company and the role
dos_and_donts: Just get a detailed description of the company and the role. Learn of possibilties to leverage of your tech background

pre_process_tips: Applying on Reculta - Resume based shortlist
interview_outline:
Round 1 - Started with guesstimate, then an M& A case based question, ending with HR and NPAD based questons. Balanced
Round 2 - One HR based question, then a guesstiamte. Guesstimate heavy.
Round 3 - HR based questions, then a case.
domain_questions: Cases and Guesstimates. I always tried to seek the inputs of the interviewer wherever I could to clarify the problem statement and the approach I was taking. The interviewer across all the 3 rounds were looking to cooperate and looking for an interaction based discussion.
hr_gk_questions:
The biggest challenge I faced in leading a team? What did I do about it?
What efforts did I take to improve my client interactions skills?
Why consulting? Why DDV? Why PwC?
Why should we consider you for the role?
What has been the most important constructive feedback you've received?
How good are you at MS Excel?
looking_for: I think they looked for people who were willing to hold a conversation, and able to think in a structured manner. During my interview guesstimates, I missed a few factors that I should have considered but my approach was logical and structured.
right_wrong:
Right - Conversational interview, structured approach to guesstimate and cases, well prepared HR answers, realizing my mistakes and utilizing the input of the interviewer during case solving
Wrong - Could have thought of factors that I missed out on for guesstimates/cases, assumed figures for easy calculation without providing any reason for them upfront, calculation mistakes, was rushing to answers without giving a deliberate thought at times
tips:
Firstly, the casebooks were of great help as they helped me practice cases with friends and also align my approach, and helped me understand what sort of questions to ask
Prepcom's introductory and advanced session on Consulting was great to understand how the interview experience might seem like and how to present your points
Mock PI was insightful, but can't say the same about Mock GDs
dos_and_donts:
DOs - Practice a variety of guesstimates and cases with friends, keep a smiling face throughout, try to keep the interview as conversational as you can, take time to think when the interviewer asks you to
DONTs - Don't rush, don't assume any numbers during guesstimate solving without clarifying

pre_process_tips: We filled the application form on their company portal along with applying on Reculta. After a few days 4-5 of us got shortlisted, where we attended the company presentation, where we also got to know of the interview dates. After a couple of days all of us had a brief group interaction session with a couple of seniors from IIM Indore working in Praxis where they provided us with valuable insights of the interview process.
interview_outline: Cases and guesstimates in both the interviews
domain_questions:
1. Market entry case of an apparel company into kids' category
2. Cost reduction case of Eureka Forbes
3. Growth strategy case of an EV charging infrastructure
prep_resources: Case practise with peers, with cases from multiple sources like IIM Indore Casebook, IIM Ahmedabad Casebook, IIM Bangalore Casebook and FMS Delhi Casebook
looking_for: First principles thinking, thorough knowledge of work experience, project and summer internship industries, and ability to structure thoughts in a MECE way while solving cases.
right_wrong: Thorough preparation of entire resume, and an updated knowledge of the industries worked in during prior work, projects and summer internship helped a lot. Also, 40-50 days of sincere case preparation with friends and taking a detailed feedback after each case improved case solving tremendously.
tips: For final placements, it is very necessary to prepare your resume entirely. For consulting preparation, you should have 4-5 friends with whom you should practise cases, 2 per day for a minimum 30-35 days.
dos_and_donts:
Dos:
1. Refer to multiple casebooks
2. Practise cases with different people to get different perspectives
3. If possible, contact seniors working in the company that you get shortlisted in to get some specific tips
4. Thoroughly prepare a short and long version of your introduction

Don't(s):
1. Make sure that you avoid taking very long pauses, but at the same time avoid using filler words. This will require practice.
2. For consulting avoid these 3 things during your case interviews: Long pauses while calculations (try to explain your thinking to the interviewer while doing so), not doing MECE (at least in the initial stages, only make a laundry list if very necessary), and taking assumptions without the buy-in of the interviewer (except the very obvious ones). Keep check of these during case preparation

pre_process_tips: Initially, there was an aptitude test. The test contained questions based on general awareness, finance (mainly accounting and corporate finance) etc.
gd_topics_tips: A telecom company based case study. It would handy to have calculators and use the information given in the financial statements to calculate solvency, profitability and liquidity ratios. Using economic concepts like elasticity, price sensitivity etc. could be helpful when discussing the industry as a whole. Sufficient arguments could be made just by using the information given in the case. Your points should be backed by some logic (e.g metric you have calculated, numbers given in the case, application of a concept you have studied etc.)
interview_outline: The interview started with an introduction. After that, most of the questions revolved around my resume. I was also asked why I wanted to apply for this role. The interview was mainly technical.
domain_questions:
Questions about my academic projects 
Questions on the impact of COVID-19 on various sectors (especially telecom sector since that was my sector of choice)  
Questions on my internships

Approach was to try and give as many examples as possible as well as discuss any latest development or research I come across on the topic. The panel looked satisfied with my answers.
hr_gk_questions:
Why this particular role?
I mainly focused on re-iterating what the Job Description contained and explaining that I found those responsibilities interesting. I discussed the dynamic and spontaneous nature of risk analysis and how I would enjoy the continuous challenges.
The panel looked satisfied with my answers
looking_for: Good Communication Skills, Knowledge about finance, Basic awareness regarding the role
right_wrong:
Good
I answered my internship and academic project questions well since I was comfortable with them.

Bad
Most of my answers related to telecom sector were based on me beating around the bush 

I was able to convert the interview
tips:
CFA Books
Sector Reports on TrendLyne
dos_and_donts:
Have a pre-written introduction that you have memorised.
Go through all your resume points (especially the top half) and ensure you can speak for at least 5 minutes about each point.
Have at least 2 questions prepared beforehand that you will ask your interviewer. Questions could be based on the impact of a recent industry wide phenomenon on the company or a particular initiative the company has taken.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlist followed by 2 Rounds, 1st round guesstimate and behavioral questions, 2nd round Partner Round
interview_outline:
1st Round: - 
-Started with introduction.
 -Asked to choose a sector, based on the sector asked about my view and insights moving ahead and initiatives taken by govt. Budget allocation on the sector by govt. 
- Guesstimate on number of volleyball coaches in Delhi NCR
- Asked HR question on what is my approach when problem is placed infront of me. Is it directly rush through it or directly move into research mode.
- What kind of person I am, project initiator, middle executive or finisher.
- Asked to rate on 1-10 with using Excel, Powerpoint and Doc.
- Why consulting?
2nd Round:- (Partner Round)
-  Started with introduction
- Reason behind persual of consulting 
- Dug into the CV,  and asked structural questions on previous internship in startup
domain_questions: Just had a guesstimate. Followed simple top to bottom narrowing down approach. Have GDP figures handy in case domain specific questions are asked. And try to have the references from where we are quoting those figures because they will cross question that figures are underestimated or vice-versa.
hr_gk_questions:
1) When a project is alloted to you, whats your approach either you directly start working or start with research of relevant matrix related to problem statement?
2) Which type of person are you, leader, path follower or one who finishes and submits at the end. At which point of time you enter a project alloted?
looking_for: They require person who has clear and structured thought process, confident while speaking and stays firm on the figures and data quoted even when stress interview is taken.
right_wrong:
Keep practicing guesstimates. Thats the only part of process which can make or break an interview. After quoting the figures on the sector of choice they try to emphasize that the figures are wrong, so prepare beforehand for all the justifications which might be required. Never stress out in interview even if its not going according to expectation. Good or bad interview is relative for both interviwer and interviewee.
- Converted the interview
tips: Staying Confident, Honest and having self belief is key here. Go thoroughly through the company deck, sector reports of prepcomm and the CV.

pre_process_tips: Resume based screening, followed by Creative submission in video or PPT, followed by PI
interview_outline: Resume focused, a lot of HR questions, some marketing concept explanations like ATL BTL strategies, and GTM case
domain_questions: 2 cases, one was a general problem solving case where I had to diagnose how coca cola can increase demand in a location, and whatbare possible barriers to entry. 2nd was GTM case for entering a new market, what are the retailer expectations etc.
hr_gk_questions: Very resume based, a lot of questions on the introduction as well. Spent a lot of time in discussing internships and the work I did there, and how it could be leveraged for coca cola. Also spent time on PORs as well as my co curriculars and how it helps me to be better in business
looking_for: They wanted super strong communication skills, critical thinking skills from all the cases I was asked, and some foundational knowledge of marketing jargon as well as concepts. Favorite brands of the company, marketing campaigns, also helpful.
right_wrong:
There was a component to the case when I started asking too many questions instead of analyzing, so I feel like the interviewers got lost there. The overall case solution in my opinion was good, and they acknowledged that. I had also brushed up on investor relation goals, their business model, and how their distribution works and I referenced it during answers if I could, which they appreciated. Lastly, good knowledge of marketing concepts, generally building a rapport as someone who is outgoing and engaging I think was good. It also helped to ask relevant and engaging questions at the end, about project details, their expectation, etc.
The bad things in my part could have also been not emphasizing on my PORs during my introduction, and also not having very set answers prepared for some HR questions.
tips: PI
dos_and_donts: Always know the company business model and the goals for that year(in terms of EPS, or growth  etc), and general marketing concepts from the prepcom deck. Keep it engaging and conversational, they appreciate a fun interview and it's essential to be as charismatic as you can. Also, make your intro perfect and super engaging, as well as keeping an answer for all questions in the npad.

pre_process_tips: Resume based shortlist, followed by group discussion and personal interview
gd_topics_tips: Topic: Digital platforms and social media: The impact on society and human behaviour. They did not want people talking over each other and no points were given to the person who spoke first or last.
interview_outline:
4 member panel, all of whom presided over the GD as well (online). They went directly into the details of my summer internship. I had done slot and constraint optimisation for a retailer during the pandemic, and they wanted to know the exact logic and process I applied. Then they asked me about my live project and the research techniques I used there. No questions on Kotak were asked. 

Case 1: Disruptors like PhonePe and Paytm are becoming common payment methods for daily transactions. How can Kotak position itself to appeal to these customers? What are the changes in buying behaviour since COVID-19 that we can leverage?

Case 2: FASTag will be compulsory for all 4 wheelers by the end of Jan, 2021. If 15% of our current customers have FASTag, how can we use our information database to analyse which of our current customers would be the best to target and increase this to 25%?
domain_questions: Asked about my strength in market research techniques and what kind of platforms I am comfortable with. S&M questions like marketing and sales channels, estimated costs etc were asked
hr_gk_questions: Not in particular. General HR questions would be expected.
looking_for: Working knowledge of every platform/software you mention in your resume. They can test you on what a line of code would mean if Python/R/C are mentioned. Lots of emphasis on exact technique of project execution (academic and internship)
right_wrong: Be calm and collected. Interviewers put pressure for complete explanations but were otherwise quite friendly. Focus hard when they present the case, and repeat it back to them for clarity.
tips: Reading PrepCom company deck and sector deck is a must. Live sheet with sector wise news was quite helpful. Specifically, read up IT, S&M and consulting material. For GD, keep up to date with current affairs.
dos_and_donts: Be cheerful and answer with clarity. The interviewers have had a long day as well. All cases need to be structured well so they understand your thought process.

pre_process_tips: A test containing 5 sections: Quant, LRDI, VARC, C language, SQL
interview_outline: Started out with intro, then questioned how would you fit in without Computer science background, a guestimate, 2 puzzles, case analysis, 3 questions on C language.
domain_questions:
Asked what kind of a new product or a new service could they introduce. I remembered something from their pre-placement talks that they help airlines to optimise their travel routes with the help of transaction histories of their customers. I couldn't come up with something, so I mentioned that. Her response was, "was this in one of your case studies in your college", to which I replied "no" to which she replied, "we actually do that". That was the end of it.

Another question was "you are not from CS background and the job might require skills like C++ and such, so what are you going to do about that?" to which I replied "we were introduced to C++ in our UG 1st year. Since it was a long time ago I forgot most of the basics but I did find it very interesting. I never had the need and time so I couldn't learn it in the past. But if it is essential, I am more than happy to learn it."
looking_for: Asked a few time how would I manage if I dont have an experience in computer languages and such. Mentioned that knowing this would be an added advantage. But the most important trait would be, be as confident as you can especially when guestimates and case analysis are involved. Even if one doesnt have a knowledge in the mentioned computer language based skills, show them that you are willing to learn it
right_wrong: Was very nervous. Haven't practiced guestimates, and lacked in Computer knowledge. While they weren't dead set on recruiting a CSE student, the other two were very important and might have been the deal breakers.
tips:

interview_outline:
Started with introduction, questions on projects within work experience. Large part was a case discussion to check general acumen and understanding of strategy concepts. Why consulting, and why this domain was an important aspect. The candidate was asked to create a matrix of the roles offered on campus and the parameters on which she would rate them (with weights assigned), and was then asked to rate each profile. The candidate was then asked to convince the interviewer that this was the best profile for their career. 
The partner round followed a similar format, minus the case discussion. 

Case problem statement: What changes do you foresee in the petroleum retail industry given the scenario of a recent change in government regulation, keeping the minimal criteria for a firm to enter into the petroleum retail space is to have a market cap of INR 250 Cr., from the previous mandatory investment of INR 2,000 Cr. in the O&G value chain to be able to retail.
looking_for: From my understanding, they were looking for a willingness to learn and adapt to situations. A proper understanding of what the role is about and whether the candidate is mentally prepared for the work coming their way was important. Domain specific knowledge was not a must, but at the same time an interest in the domain is important.
right_wrong: Keeping the interview conversational and setting the tone of the interview at the beginning by engaging in small talk helped. Reiterate the questions in your head before answering, ask if in doubt. Clarity and conciseness of answers is important, and keep a scope for exploring a little further if the interviewer wants.
tips: Case prep material shared by Prepcom and Consulting Club. Discussion on HR questions aligned with the NPAD.
dos_and_donts:
Do: Spend time on preparation for HR questions based on your resume, helps make your answers comprehensive and to the point by the time you actually interview. 
Don't: focus all your energy on revising subjects. While important, it is more likely that he interviewer is looking for a more general fit and a candidate that can be taught things as need be. 

Being conversant with your resume is extremely important, should have a story that flows.
