pre_process_tips: Aptitude Test >> Live Case Round >> Case-based Interview >> Founder's Interview
no_interviews_duration: 2 Interviews >> Interview #1: Approx. 45min-1hr & Interview #2: Approx. 25 mins
interview_outline:
The first interviews started with introduction and a brief background (interview panel had IIM Indore Alums), talked about IIM Indore to ease me into the interview. Then we moved onto the case analysis, wherein I was asked to explain my solution to the case, post which, probing was done into various assumptions, and my analysis. Heavy questioning was done on financial analysis and ratios, especially which ratio is applicable and best to judge a company from various perspectives. The interview was more like a conversation wherein you were allowed to use the internet and they also helped, and were looking to see if one could reach the logical conclusion. 

The second interview was a more relaxed, non-technical round taken by the Founder of the firm. The partner asked various HR questions in this round.
domain_questions: The panel asked various technical questions relating to topics such as Financial Statement Analysis, Ratios and basics of Valuation. Ratios was the most asked topic, with majority of the interview being driven by the same. They expected the candidate to know all the ratios he/she used in their model (case solution), and were expecting logical reasoning for the same.
hr_gk_questions: The second interview entailed the HR-based questions and was a much more relaxed round, wherein I was asked about my experience, my past internships, as well my hobbies and interest. A rapid fire round where he asked questions like strengths, weakness, why am I the best fit, as well as why should I not be hired.
looking_for: They were looking for students with strong basics in finance, as well as students who were able to formulate logical arguments, and hold their stance.
right_wrong: The interview went well in terms of justification of the solutions as well as probing questions. The interviews were appreciative of the confidence as well as honest responses in certain cases, as I was unaware of a term, which I asked them for the meaning of, the panel explained the same and appreciated that I let them know the same.
tips: Finance Mock PI as well as preparatory session in addition to the FAC course in term-1 helped a lot.

pre_process_tips: Initial shortlist based on resume followed by a test (both aptitude and psychometric). The further shortlisted students had to attend a case study workshop following which there was only 1 round of Personal Interview (guesstimate and case based)
interview_outline:
Interview started with the question : Tell me about yourself, followed by some preliminary questions such as 'Why consulting/research' , ' Why this vertical (my vertical was Middle East)'
Then there was a Guesstimate given to me, followed by a small case question.
The interview was majorly knowledge based and tilting towards technical heavy.
domain_questions:
Guesstimate: 'How many EVs (cars) were sold in India in 2020?'
My approach was to go top-down, determining the total no of cars bought in 2020 and then taking the EV cars as a small percentage of it. The interviewer liked my simple method and guided me wherever necessary.
Case : ' Declining revenues of Coal India'
There was no information as such given for the case. I just had to give 2-3 suggestions so as to improve the market position of Coal India.
The interviewer liked me long-term solution that ' coal india should move towards renewable sources of energy and as they have a great logistics and supply chain network they can leverage that as well to diversify'
Questions: 'Why the Middle East vertical?'
I had thoroughly gone through the job description and thus was able to answer this question.
hr_gk_questions: Tell me about yourself' and 'why consulting?'
looking_for:
I  was a fresher thus work ex wasn't necessary. They were looking for candidates who were quick on their feet and had a good understanding about Guesstimate.
Guesstimate forms an important part of the interview.
right_wrong:
It was crucial that I was able to communicate my assumptions clearly, and that it felt more like a conversation. 
Do not get too tensed up leading to long quiet phases in the interview. 
I converted the interview.
tips:
Go through your NPAD very well as they might ask questions from it.
Go through various guesstimate examples in Casebooks of various colleges.
Have a mock interview (especially case solving) with a senior/friends.
dos_and_donts:
Prepare your NPAD well. 
Dont take any assumption in the interview without confirming it with the interviewer.

pre_process_tips: Initially, there was an aptitude test. The test contained questions based on general awareness, finance (mainly accounting and corporate finance) etc. The next round was a case study-GD round. Finally, there were interviews.
gd_topics_tips: A telecom company based case study. It would handy to have calculators and use the information given in the financial statements to calculate solvency, profitability and liquidity ratios. Using economic concepts like elasticity, price sensitivity etc. could be helpful when discussing the industry as a whole. Sufficient arguments could be made just by using the information given in the case. Your points should be backed by some logic (e.g metric you have calculated, numbers given in the case, application of a concept you have studied etc.)
interview_outline: The interview started with an introduction. After that, most of the questions revolved around my resume. I was also asked why I wanted to apply for this role. The interview was mainly technical.
domain_questions:
Questions about my academic projects 
Questions on the impact of COVID-19 on various sectors (especially telecom sector since that was my sector of choice)  
Questions on my internships

Approach was to try and give as many examples as possible as well as discuss any latest development or research I come across on the topic

Why this particular role?
I mainly focused on re-iterating what the Job Description contained and explaining that I found those responsibilities interesting. I discussed the dynamic and spontaneous nature of risk analysis and how I would enjoy the continuous challenges.
looking_for: Good Communication Skills, Knowledge about finance, Basic awareness regarding the role
right_wrong:
Good
I answered my internship and academic project questions well since I was comfortable with them.

Bad
Most of my answers related to telecom sector were based on me beating around the bush

CFA Books
Sector Reports on TrendLyne
dos_and_donts:
Have a pre-written introduction that you have memorised.
Go through all your resume points (especially the top half) and ensure you can speak for at least 5 minutes about each point.
Have at least 2 questions prepared beforehand that you will ask your interviewer. Questions could be based on the impact of a recent industry wide phenomenon on the company or a particular initiative the company has taken.

pre_process_tips: Perform well in the aptitude test as it is most of the people get screened out in this round. The aptitude test consists of questions which are tougher that AMCAT but easier than CAT. Don't waste time doing lengthy questions (it is OK to leave one or two) and try to focus on accuracy.
interview_outline:

1st: Introduction, What was the most challenging thing you have done in MBA, biggest achievement, what is your biggest failure
2nd: Asked about the business model of Amex (after answering I asked him a counter question), guesstimate on revenue of youtube in a day, a very easy puzzle (which I was not able to solve but tried to say out loud on what I was thinking which worked), how do you manage conflict in a group
domain_questions: Do you know SQL (I answered no but I was learning)
situational_questions:
1st: What was the most challenging thing you have done in MBA, biggest achievement, what is your biggest failure
2nd:  how do you manage conflict in a group
hr_gk_questions: Answered above
looking_for: They were looking for someone with good communication skills and consistency. Taking CRM as an elective worked for me as I was able to show a lot of interest in their business model and was able to cross question them.
right_wrong: I treated the interview as a conversation and tried to understand how the company works (read intensively about the company's business model and why they are the market leader). I asked them a lot of questions.For eg,, where did they use the concepts of traditional marketing when almost all their targeting was based on CRM. I also asked if the credit card fraud detection was solely dependant on time (I had seen a database related to that while studying for tableau).
tips: Company deck of Prepcom, NPAD, previous interview experience by Prepcom and reading news on the company helped a lot in preparing beforehand on the questions being asked.
dos_and_donts: Do not get nervous as it will reflect on your communication skills. Take time to frame your answers even if the interviewer seems to be in hurry.

pre_process_tips:
Round 1: An application form that contains mostly NPAD kind of questions
Round 2: Recorded Video Interview having 3 caselets one after the other. 1 min to think for each question and 4 minutes to answer.
Round 3: Final Interview
interview_outline: Started with a question from my resume. All following questions were about the same topic which was social media, including a small strategy question. Very few questions were asked.
domain_questions: One question asked me to create a social media strategy for my favourite brand which was Coca-Cola. The answer I gave was based on the values of Coca-Cola. Although, I feel a better answer would have been to actually use an STP analysis as well.
hr_gk_questions: No HR questions were asked in the interview.
looking_for: I think all they are looking for are people with a particular skill and passion relating to marketing. For me this was Digital Marketing. But they expect you to know very well about this particular skill and it will be tested. For me, this was tested in my interview as all questions were about it only.
right_wrong: My interview went quite well just because I knew the topic I was asked about well enough. What actually did not go well was the second round involving recorded interview.  Time management in the recorded interview is where it can go wrong very unexpectedly and that's what I had really messed up. Plus the caselets ask for elaborate answers while giving very less time to think. Be most careful about time management and giving well structured answers.
tips: Although I had prepped myself for domain technicalities, these were not asked of me at all. I only had question about Social Media which was my area of strength (luckily). However the previous year, technical questions were also asked in the interview such as to create a Go-To Market strategy for a particular product for a particular area.
dos_and_donts: There is a question asking for your biggest passion in the first round application. Do this really well about one particular topic and be sure that you are well aware about everything in that area. Absolutely do not mention that you are knowledge in areas where you actually are not.

pre_process_tips: Aptitude test of 80 mins followed by a PPT submission

situational_questions: There were normal situational and behavioral based questions which can be found in NPAD like conflict resolution in workplace, and more questions were related to what I like to do in free time. The 2nd round was workex heavy as I had my workex in R&D and new product development. Also asked a case - to design a lift for 100 storeyed building. Answered it again using the CIRCLE framework. hr_gk_questions: How would you expect Paytm to be different from your previous organization?  What was the most challenging project I handled during my workex, how did I tackle different problems/challenges related to the project?
looking_for: They were looking for creative minds with a bit of technical knowledge, who can think out of the box.
right_wrong: The good part was I structured both the cases pretty well, also I could relate the role to my previous workex (NPD).
tips: I used to practice daily 2-3 prodman cases for one month before the laterals. The PrepCom material was really very helpful, specifically all the external case books including our own prodlab casebook. Also, the domain session decks for brushing up the concepts just before interview.
dos_and_donts: Stay confident and keep a smile on your face during the interview :)

gd_topics_tips: Some topic on "Growth of India vs China". Multiple questions asked in group interview setting post GD. Achievements relevant to Adani, what concepts each one of us know in Finance, in how much depth are we familiar with them, Workex company, etc
interview_outline:
Round1- Completely resume based interview. Asked about my work experience in depth. Also asked about my UG internship which was in Ops & Supply chain in depth. Questions on case comps listed on my resume. Favourite subject. 

Round2- Again resume + finance domain. Asked some basic fin concepts-DCF, CAPM, accounting terms, and portfolio management. Interviewers were very friendly. They asked what all topics I knew in how much depth and give examples of each of them. 

Round3- Short HR interview. Asked my CAT Quant %ile. some generic HR questions
domain_questions: If you work in Corporate Finance team of Adani, how will you contribute? I mentioned about all Corp fin concepts I have studied and how I will apply them- Capital budgeting, dividend principle and Accounting concepts
situational_questions:
They asked about my biggest failure in life. Mentioned my NPAD answer.
One thing I could have done different in MBA- I told I would have opted to specialise in 1 domain instead on having a generalised resume having subjects from all domains.
They were quite happy and delighted from my answer
hr_gk_questions: Why Adani?
looking_for: They were basically looking for confidence, motivation to work in the Fin domain and how clear I was in whatever I was mentioning them. They didn't grill me much in Fin concepts.
right_wrong: All the answers that revolved around my resume gave very positive impression to the panelist.
tips: I did Case prep and basic Fin prep. Prepcom basic domain sessions were very beneficial. Also prep decks are a must go-through. I almost completed IIMA and FMS casebook by doing case practices. That I feel was more than enough.
dos_and_donts: Prepare 1 domain in very detail (which is your preferred one). And prepare 1 domain with all the basics cleared. NPAD is must. Do 1-2 mock HR interviews with your friends who are preparing with you or are PPOed.

pre_process_tips:
1. We had a resume screening round. 
2. After shortlist, we had to answer a few questions in the form of a video interview. Here, I was given 3-4 questions based on my shortlisted domain (IT) and I had to record 2 min videos giving answers to the questions one by one. This video recording  was timed and you couldn't record the video again. Once the time is up, your video would be auto submitted. 
3. The people selected after this round had to appear for the PI.
no_interviews_duration: Video interview (4 questions, 2 mins each) and main 1 interview (25 mins)
interview_outline:
It started with introduction. 
Then my work experience in great details because I had the same domain experience. 
Next, a few company related questions.
Asked me about my hobbies as mentioned in resume. I mentioned that I write poems. Interviewer asked me to recite one. Asked about why I wrote it, inspiration behind it, etc.
Probed about my other interests as well.
domain_questions:
Interviewer asked me about how can HUL leverage IT, as it is an fmcg company.
_ I talked about how a house of brand like HUL can streamline its supply chain using IT.
What factors would you consider before implementing any IT strategy? 
- The scale of business, the usability of IT that would be implemented, costs, etc. 
How can cloud help HUL?
 - told basic advantages of cloud
Other emerging technologies that you see could be pf help for HUL?
- integrate generative AI for consumer complaints redressal (and others as well)
How can you streamline operations between our plethora of product lines and sub-brands using IT? 
I was aksed general questions about my experience at IIM Indore, my CAT journey. What one thing would you change about your college?
looking_for: Knowledge of emerging tech in IT and how will you integrate/use them at HUL. Work ex was expected in IT domain or at least UG in IT/CSE.
right_wrong: Converted the interview and accepted the offer.
tips: The main thing or resource one should rely on is the company website. Also, mock GD and PI were also helpful.
dos_and_donts: Past year experiences, company information from the website, tech news.

pre_process_tips: The pre-process was an assessment test. To ace this one, practice Decision Making questions similar to the ones asked in XAT and Data Interpretation (Graphs, Charts, etc.) This is followed by a case study workshop. Try to make an impact during the workshop by being participative.
interview_outline: Started with introduction, went into my resume, my entrepreneurship experience, and questions about my work experience. Then, moved into two riddles, one was how to measure 4l using a bucket of 3l and 5l and second one was on the river crossing problem. Next, moved into a guesstimate to measure the number of denims sold in a year in India, and a case of market entry by a telecom service provider in the Indian market.
domain_questions: Questions about why I want to join Bain, what do I know about the different COE's and so on.
hr_gk_questions: Questions about Why Consulting? How does my elaborate research experience fit into consulting and so on.
looking_for: They were looking for enthusiastic people who were good with numbers, clear idea about different sectors, and a clear idea of why they want to join consulting.
right_wrong: Could have done a better job in framing the case. The good parts of the interview was my relative ease with numbers and ideas about different industries and sectors. Additionally, I was well versed with the numbers such as smartphone penetration, gender divide, and all for guesstimates and was able to analyze the guesstimate comprehensively from multiple points of view
tips: Get well versed with numbers. Practice a ton of guesstimates. Look through the IIM A casebook and the FMS casebook on guesstimates. Read up on different sectors, especially the supply chain.
dos_and_donts: Do focus a lot on guesstimates. Do read your NPAD well and prepare well for questions from your resume. Don't try to rush it. Take your time to formulate a proper approach and aim for constant feedback and verification in the process of solving the case. Don't assume anything, get your assumptions verified in every step. Try to have a dialogue with the interviewer instead of rushing through the case.

role_offered: 9/9/8, B.Tech, Mechanical Engineering, NITK Surathkal, 3 years of work experience at Tata Motors(Operations)
pre_process_tips: Application through Reculta
gd_topics_tips: GD topic: Is MBA necessary to start a business?
interview_outline: I was asked to share any significant achievement that I have done at Tata Motors. I talked about how I took a Data driven approach to solve the Brake oil Leakage issue.There were a couple of cross questions. Then I was asked about my Internship at ISRO. There were a couple of cross questions on that as well.
domain_questions:
I told the interviewer that, after identifying the Vendor Quality issue, I talked to the Vendor and the issue was sorted out. The interviewer questioned me asking whether I came up with a control mechanism or not(because just talking to the Vendor doesn't help).
Me(agreeing): Yes Sir, you're right. I should have thought about it. However, the issue did not repeat after I talked to the Vendor.

After I talked about my internship at ISRO, I was asked what kind of Mathematical model did I build? Was it a Regression model?
Me: Sir, No. It was not a regression model. There were a couple of factors considered, like Law of conservation of Energy....and there were a couple of differential equations.
hr_gk_questions: No
looking_for: They were looking for candidates with 2+ years of experience in Operations Management. I guess they appreciated the honesty in me. I was calm and confident while speaking.
right_wrong: I was calm, confident and honest. I could have thought about the potential questions about my work experience and prepared for it. I was lucky they did not dig deep into it. Yes, I converted the interview. Out of 19 shortlisted candidates(for GD), 2 were selected.
tips:
The interview was fully resume based. Mock GDs were helpful because I realised that, even though I made valid points, I participated less. I talked 3 times in the 10 minute GD.

Know your resume in and out.

Get to know the concepts in Operations and Supply Chain Management.

Go through the website of Vector Consulting group and understand what 'Theory of constraints' is. Even though I wasn't asked anything about it, it might me asked in future.

pre_process_tips: Aptitude test that consisted of maths, english and accountancy
gd_topics_tips:
It was not a GD but a case discussion, they divided us into a group of 5 and allotted each member in a group with a company. One has calculate a list of accounting ratios. As a next we have rank the 5 companies based on both qualitative and quantitative risk factors based on the ratios. Then questions were asked based on our findings. 

Mainly they expecting that one should know what does each accounting ratios actually mean in the practical context of the company. And needless to say one needs to be through with basic accounts and accounting ratios.
no_interviews_duration: 3 rounds with last round being HR (20 mins)
interview_outline: The interview was mostly based on current affairs and how does the current situation affects the risk situation in banks. There were couple of basic HR questions. Also there were some questions from the workshop.
domain_questions: Since I said I analyzed a bank, there were many technical questions related to the terms and valuations  methods of banks.
hr_gk_questions:
They asked about how does the current macro economy situation is? How does the global macroeconomy affect India? How are banks affected due to this situation? Mention one of your strength. What is your biggest failure and the learning from it? Tell me something that is not there in your resume.

Reading newspaper is very important as it outlines most of the answers for the current affairs related questions and for HR NPAD was really helpful.
looking_for: NISM Securities Markets Foundation, NCFM Intermediate module: Investment analysis and portfolio management. No work-ex expectations.
right_wrong:
The good part was I was able to answer all the questions that the panel posted and no where in the interview I struggled or skipped any question. I think I could have handled my introduction better as it was pretty generic. 

Converted all the three interviews.
tips:
For finance interviews I prepared mostly from CFA books. Also reading newspapers were also really helpful. 

Mock GDs and PIs were very helpful as the mentors gave valuable feedback which gave actual results during the real PIs and GDs.

pre_process_tips: Application form - 2 Buddy rounds - Interaction/Networking dinner - 1 Personal interview
interview_outline:
The interview panel included 4 members 1 MD, 1 VP, 1 Associate and 1 HR
The MD started the interview with general question like introduction, questions about the role and company. 
A large set of questions based on my CV, which included many questions on work experience , clarity about the role and company, personal drive and motivation 
Interview ended with few questions from HR revolving around strengths, weakness and examples about the same.
domain_questions:
What is Corporate Banking
Types of skills required in CB
Which are the financial products Deutsche bank has to offer
Out of these products which area is a good fit for you and why
hr_gk_questions:
HR - 
Any event of failure and how did you overcome it
Situation which shows initiative or leadership skills 
Future goals in finance 

Resume -
Sports questions - Biggest achievement in Chess 
How has chess helped you

Interest - I had mentioned eSports 
eSports industry overview 
Difference in Industry in India as compared to globally 
Regulations and compliance related questions on eSports industry
looking_for: They were looking for candidate who is interested in finance and has strong communication skills
right_wrong:
My answers related to engineering, work experience, pors had a story which showed my deep interest in finance which I was able to justify to the panel. 
My work experience of managing various stakeholders helped me show strong communication skills points which were essentially the 2 important skills they were looking for
tips: Knowing your CV and building a story which helps in showing skills that are required for the role. Salesman experience can be useful in a Sales and Marketing job as well as Corporate Banking, it just depends on how well you use it.
dos_and_donts:
Dos - 
Be clear about the role, company and your CV
Buddy rounds are very important 
Keeping the 1st buddy round with associate informal and 2nd with VP formal worked for me to built good relationships which helped in the networking/interaction round
Ask questions in all rounds

pre_process_tips: Application form
gd_topics_tips: Product comparison of Swiggy and Zomato
interview_outline:
Interview 1: 1) Resume questions about details of the projects I did during my stint as a software developer 2) Create an application for E passport seva Kendra to make it easy for people 3) Asked to create features, prioritize them, Define KPIs 4) Brainstormed the ideas I suggested and gave their feedback 
Interview 2: 1) Resume based questions
2) Why Matrimony? 3) Suggest changes to make spotify better and imrove churn rate. 
4) If you are building a new matrimony or matchmaking app what do you think people will look for in a partner while choosing their partners? 5) Some HR questions like the most challenging situation you handled etc.
domain_questions:
1) Desgin question about passport seva app:- Approach was to think from user's point of view, think about their pain points first like document storage, commute time waste, inconvenience because of multiple visits to office . Then, come up with the features to tackle this.
2) Improve spotify: Suggested features which will make platform more collaborative like listen together, create music groups etc
hr_gk_questions:
Following HR questions were asked:
1) Why MBA after Barclays?
2) Why Matrimony? 
3) Most challenging situation faced? 
Approach was to be real and honest. Be clear about what has been asked and what is expected.  Prepare NPAD thoroughly.
looking_for:
Good understanding of products in general.
Leadership skills, Work experience in IT preferred. Strong fundamentals in product management case solving
right_wrong:
I started the GD and that gave me an edge. Since the GD was about product review I kept my approach very product oriented and avoided any generic inputs rather I kept it technical and from a product manager's perspective. 
In interviews I handled the difficult questions calmly but I felt I could have come up with better solutions if I had practiced more cases. 
I converted the interviews in the end
tips: ProdLab case book, prep com material, IIMA case book, exponent youtube channel
dos_and_donts: Prepare good number of cases , practice frameworks as it gives structure to your solutions

pre_process_tips: Application on Reculta
interview_outline: Started with an introduction. They asked questions on my Resume, they asked about a project I had done in undergrad, it was on IOT. Then asked about my work expereince at Sumasung. They asked questions about what makes me a suitable candidate for the role and what domain I would want to work in. What MBA subjects was I most interested in. The interview had more HR questions.
domain_questions: They asked about a project I had done in undergrad in IOT. Told them, they did not ask a lot of follow up questions. Asked which role I would like to work for, I answered that a role which involves strategy and planning would interest me.
hr_gk_questions:
Technical Projects, Work Experience at Samsung - Gave them clear and crisp answers, not many follow up questions. 
Favourite subjects- I was honest that I had no experience in these domains before and by what I experienced in my team at IIM I was interested in Finance and Marketing, explain what you liked, I said in Finance apart form the numbers the thought which goes behind decision making is what I found interesting. 
There asked some other questions as well which are covered in the NPAD document which you will make.
looking_for: They are looking for someone who knows about the company and role and what they have mentioned on their resume. There is nothing specific they are looking for.
right_wrong:
I was able to answer questions confidently. Maybe have better answers for things on my resume.
Converted the interview
tips: NPAD is the most important document for GenMan preparation. Resume is equally important. And know about the company. Practice HR PIs with seniors. And the PrepCom mock Pis were extremely helpful as they give constructive feedback.
dos_and_donts: What helped me was that I asked a question in the end of the interview even though I was not asked to. It was news I came across while reading about the company. I asked about their recent JVs and how they decided they should go ahead with them.

interview_outline:
Round 1 - Somewhat technical heavy, Started with introduction, resume based (focus on analytics projects completed), an analytics problem (approach to solve was important), some HR questions, and ended with an guestimate

Round 2 - Started with introduction, resume based ( was asked to explain analytics projects ), some HR questions, asked to show any presentation prepared for a project
domain_questions:
Was asked to explain 2 analytics projects completed (those were on resume ). I answered by stating the problem statement, methodology/approach used, actual analysis conducted, insights, conclusion. Projects I explained were in Marketing Research, Machine Learning & Text mining domains respectively.

Was given an analytics problem statement - if you are given a book in form of document, how will you generate the summary of the book. This question was asked following my explanation of machine learning & text mining project. The panelist wanted to know the approach

Guesstimate - Calculate the amount of tea consumed in India per day in kgs.
hr_gk_questions:
In both interviews, I was asked :why this company,why this domain
I answered with pointers : 
-Interest in the domain of digital transformation
-Company culture 
-Long term goals

This worked well for me.
looking_for:
The panelists wanted people who showed real interest in the digital transformation field, knowledge of analytics and ability to communicate
clearly.

 Story as to why you have interest in this domain, Live and academic projects in analytics, marketing research domains, positions of responsibilities were the points that justified the above expectations
right_wrong:
Analytics projects - ability to go in depth and explain, the why this company answer including story of how I generated interest in the domain, how my long term goals aligned with this company , these things went right.

Guesstimate could have been better, but they were looking for approach and details covered, instead of final number to be calculated. 

I converted the interview.
tips:
Being thorough with your resume, projects mentioned should be prepared in structured manner, prepcom material for consulting helped me practice guesstimates. 
Creating a story depicting interest in the field.

pre_process_tips:
There was a resume shortlisting, gamified cognitive test, and a psychometric test. They share a report of psychometric test, you can use it to prepare yourself for the interview, how your personality fits the organization. 

Google the description of gamified test before taking the time, saves time while making the attempt to understand the games. 

Company schedules a Job Description meeting for the candidates shortlisted for the interview on the day of final process. Make sure to be attentive while they explain the roles, note important points, comes in handy during the interview. It's a good thing to ask questions in this meeting.
no_interviews_duration: 2 interviews: Business interview (15-20 mins), HR interview (15 mins)
interview_outline:
Business Interview: Not very technical, they just want to know why you are interested in the role and company. 
1. Tell me something about yourself
2. Why do you think you are suited for this role, give example from any projects that you might have done
3.Since I did my engineering in IT, I was asked how that experience will help me in the job in question
4. What do you think a Business Analyst does
5. Where do you see yourself in the next five years if you get hired at Capgemini

HR interview: Very chill and basic questions.
situational_questions: 1. Sometimes client don't know what technology to adopt, or they are hesitant to make a change. How will you convince them to use the company offering?
hr_gk_questions:
1. Tell me something about yourself
2. What attracts you to Capgemini ( Talk about their values and culture) 
3. 3-4 questions were around the things I mentioned in my interest
4. Questions on the social work I did, what was my aim behind taking up those activities
5. Most challenging thing that I faced during summer internship
looking_for: Confident person who understands the role and is genuinely interested in it.
right_wrong: I was smiling throughout both the interviews. Related everything from my past experiences.
tips: Smile and treat interviews like a conversation. Read thoroughly about the company and role. Reading about the new trends in the industry is a plus.

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlisting prior to interviews
interview_outline:
The technical round started with the usual introduction and then was asked about my CAT percentile, JEE rank, MBA CGPA as well as graduation percentage. Subsequently, I was asked about my knowledge and experience in the field of data analytics (I had various courses, subjects and live projects in data analytics and this made the discussion easier). There was discussion on a case competition of which my team was National Finalist and it also included data analytics. I was asked about a use case of data analytics from any industry. I was asked what other areas or specialization that I had interest in and I told them operations since it was required for the role. After that the conversation moved on to my inclination towards Polestar and why Polestar. (35 minutes)
The HR round housed similar type of questions on my fit to the company, which factors will be negative if I join Polestar, why polestar not a brand and my background. There was also discussion on my role in an academic project. (10 minutes)
domain_questions: Knowledge of Qlik Sense, Tableau, Market Research concepts (Be clear with the projects that you have mentioned in your resume)
situational_questions: What can go wrong on your personal side if you join Polestar and not a brand?
hr_gk_questions: How can you contribute to Polestar and why Polestar ?
looking_for: Smart people, eager and fast to learn in a rapidly growing firm
right_wrong: The absolute right thing that happened was I had prior experience with Tableau and Qlik Sense which were the major tools used at Polestar. This gave me an advantage and various points in my resume were also targeted at data anaytics.
tips: I firmly believe that keeping a constant smile on your face and addressing each question with confidence lets you perform better in any interview. In interview, where the panel is looking for a particular skill (mentioned in JD), try to incorporate in the introduction itself so that further discussion becomes easier and flow is established.

pre_process_tips: Online test, relatively easy, with a coding section which could be skipped
interview_outline: I had to walk the interviewer through my resume in 2 minutes. Then there was a rapid fire set of 25 finance questions, mostly basic level 1 cfa questions. He asked me about 2 strength and 1 weakness. Finally he asked if I had any questions.
domain_questions: There was a rapid fire set of 25 questions he asked which had one word or one line answers, some of them being definitions of fin concepts and some being formulae expansions. CFA level 1 covers all of them.
hr_gk_questions: 2 strength and 1 weakness, interest rates in the US
looking_for: Dedication and team player, CFA seemed like important, as soon as i told him i had cleared CFA level 2, he seemed more interested
right_wrong: It was a very short interview and i think the fin questions were all known to me which was good. Telling him about the fact that i had clear L2 was a bonus.
tips: Mocks were really important. Helped me with the confidence. If you are a cfa, revise the content well. Also, know about the economy and things that are happening in the financial world, basic things like government policies, their impact etc. They might not always come in handy but the fact that you are prepared and can make conversations helps a lot with the confidence, and i think that's the most important in an interview
dos_and_donts:
Do work on HR questions, extremely important not just from the perspective of them getting asked but also they make you remember things about yourself which can well be used in the interviews and networking sessions.
Do revise each and every point in your resume. You should be absolutely confident and willing to speak for at least 2 minutes on every point there.
Don't miss mock interviews, mock gds.
Don't worry if you have lesser shortlists or don't get placed in the early phase, extremely good opportunities open up in the later days too

pre_process_tips: There was an online test of 1 hour consisting of 20 questions - 12 RC kind and 8 DI kind. Shortlisted ones had to sit in a Case workshop where they explained the right ways to solve Guesstimates and Cases.
interview_outline: The interview was divided into 2 parts - General questions for close to 25 mins and a guesstimate for around 20 mins. He started straight away by asking me to explain my academic projects and work-ex. As I was sitting for Data Excellence vertical, he specifically asked me to emphasize those aspects in my project/work-ex where I had done analysis/development work. The guesstimate was about finding the revenue of a Starbucks outlet in a day.
domain_questions: He didn't ask me anything which wasn't there on the CV. Only asked me to explain things in my projects and work-ex. Even when I was explaining a marketing project to him, he asked me if I had done any analysis work in it.
situational_questions: No situational questions were asked
hr_gk_questions: No HR/Current Affairs asked
looking_for: Mostly two things - relevant work done in the past in the areas of development and analysis, and structured way of solving a problem.
right_wrong: The general questions about work-ex/projects were simple conversational ones. For the guesstimate, he seemed pleased with the way I structured the problem and conversed each step. He asked me to reconsider a few numerical assumptions I had taken, which I corrected. I converted the interview.
tips: Need to be thorough with resume, and case study & guesstimates. I had prepared from the case books of other B-schools as provided by Prepcom, most importantly the IIM A casebook, apart from a few other materials commonly available.
dos_and_donts: During solving guesstimates in the interview, take a structured approach, and communicate every step and all the assumptions. Instead of making the calculation complex by incorporating every lever going into it, it's better to keep it simple and communicate frankly for small insignificant cases, that this particular scenario is averaged/left out to keep the calculation simple.

pre_process_tips: Pre-process involved applying on Reculta and filling out a google form in which an essay was to be written on my views on Working from home.
interview_outline: Started with an introduction, why I want to join Everest Group, then went into consulting cases straight away, and 2 cases were asked. The first case was about increased hiring time faced by a company, and what could be the reasons for this. Was asked to analyze it in a structured approach. The next case was about a Multinational Hospitality Chain in Europe, that wanted to expand into the Indian market, so I had to tell them how do I arrive at the best-fit city for opening the first hotel.
domain_questions: No just two consulting cases asked.
hr_gk_questions: None, just an introduction about me
looking_for: They were looking for a structured approach for the cases, they were not looking for the exact answers, but they wanted to see how much I can expand my thinking and how I can present my solution with confidence.
right_wrong: I was okay with the first case, but I could not handle well the second case related to the best-fit city. They were looking for how would someone think about which city to open the first hotel in, and what data you would use to do that, for example, no. of flights to a city, no. of tourists. I was more focused on giving the name of the city, whereas they wanted to me give an approach to how to find that city by asking questions about the chain and what they specialize in.
tips: Preparation Committee's domain sessions gave me a good understanding of how to go about solving cases, my own personal preparation of cases with friends helped, and mock PI conducted by Prepcom was a good confidence booster before the final SIP process.
dos_and_donts: Try to frame a good answer to why you want to join Everest Group and be good with consulting cases, specifically market entry, unconventional and HR cases.

pre_process_tips: CV shortlisting
gd_topics_tips: Flipkart vs Amazon ; everyone got a minute to present their views on the topic and then a 5 min GD ; try to cover as much as you can in the 1 minute given to you
interview_outline: Started with resume based questions, background, engineering branch, mathematical question, knowledge about product management ( very important) , guesstimate, describing yourself as a person towards the end, asking relevant questions to the interviewer ( clarifying questions about the role or the kind of projects or any news surrounding the company)
domain_questions:
1. Knowledge about product management
2. Details of customer journey in the booking process and knowing the most critical and difficult part of it
3. Favourite app and why that app is popular vis-a-vis others ( Eg : Whatsapp vs Google Hangouts)
4. Your favourite subject and 1/2 questions around that ( Eg : KANO model of BMOD) 
5. Technical projects mentioned in resume ( Eg : clustering, SEO , SEM)
6. Key word bidding
7. Suggesting improvements
hr_gk_questions: Describe yourself as a person out of your resume; if I ask the faculty members to describe you in 3 words- what would they say, how good are you as a team player, are you a fun person to be with
looking_for: Strong analystic skills, technical projects on resume is a plus, knowledge about the product management in the e-commerce space, behavioral fit ( team player)
right_wrong:
Wrong - Not clear knowledge about product management in the e-commerce space
Right - structured approach for solving guesstimates and puzzles ; thoroughly prepared for resume based question ( technical projects particularly - NPS, clustering, SEO/SEM , analysing revenue based and cost based synergies for a merger)
tips: Checking the company website thoroughly, PM interviews on YouTube, content needs to be developed for Product Management interviews hence relied on Google search for information
dos_and_donts: Be aware of the job role thoroughly and for MMT GD- speak as much as you can in the 1 minute assigned to you

pre_process_tips: Just one psychometric test which had questions revolving around the leadership principles of Amazon
interview_outline: Both the interviews started with introduction followed by questions which were customized according to my resume and majorly work experience. The focus was on how I took initiatives and I behaved in various situations during my work experience. Hardly 1 technical question and mostly HR questions.
domain_questions: Not really, I was not asked any technical questions or company related questions
hr_gk_questions: Both the panelists were very peculiar for looking the leadership and team building qualities which I have displayed in the past. Like there was question in which I was asked to tell about one instance when I came up with an innovative idea and what impact did this idea have on my team. In every answer I used the STAR framework which made it easy for the panel to comprehend. Panelists were very supportive and friendly.
looking_for: So I felt their focus was a lot if I fit the culture of Amazon and if I am having the Amazon leadership principles which are given on Amazon site. And I feel having a work experience played a crucial role in my interview because most of the questions were work experince related.
right_wrong: The good part of the interview was the supporting and friendly nature of the panelists. As I converted the interview I would not call it a bad part but the not so good part was I fumbled a lot, maybe it was because this was my first interview but I was energetic and confident so that was a plus point.
tips: I had went through all the domain sessions presentations and sessions so I was confident about any basic questions related to them. Mock interview was a very crucial part, though it might be my worst interview but it gave me an idea of the things I should focus on, it made me aware of my weaknesses and accordingly I prepared myself from the feedback I received.

pre_process_tips: Aptitude/Psychometric Test Post Resume Screening.
interview_outline:
Started With Introduction; Backed With Some HR Q Such As Why MSIL; Any Learnings From SIP & Challenges During SIP And How You Handle Those Challenges. 
Other Q Were Based Upon Resume - Started With Detailed Explanation About SIP Role & Project; Your Contribution & Impact (Ans - Based On STAR Framework).
Some More Q Asked Were On The Lines On Devising A Strategy To Launch A New Prod/Service. 
Go Through The Academic Projects Mentioned In The Resume. 
Some Other Situational Q Were Asked About The Industry & MSIL.
domain_questions: Devising A Strategy To Launch A Prod/Service - Used Comprehensive Market Entry Framework Including MKT Attractiveness, Viability Analysis; Modes Of Entry (GTM; STP; 4Ps), Growth & Exit Opportunities. Q Around Project Management; Lean Six Sigma Certification Were Asked.
hr_gk_questions:
Why MSIL ?
Why Digital Enterprise ?
Learnings From MBA ? (Could Be Related To Technical Or Soft Skills)
Learnings, Challenges From SIP ?
How You Would Manage Conflicting Personalities Within The Team ?
Q On The Lines Of Cross Functional Teams ?
prep_resources: PrepComm Dashboard Filled With Domain Materials & NPAD Prep.
looking_for: Candidate Having Clarity Of Their Resume & Ability To Express Their Future Expectations. (Confidence Is The Key Here).
right_wrong: Important Tip - Preparation WRT Domain & MSIL.
tips:
Being Confident About Your Ans.
Maintaining A Good Body Language. 
Have A Good Sense Of Humour For HR Specific Q.
Be Thorough With Your Resume.
dos_and_donts:
Do(s) - 
Go Through Your Resume; Candidates Should Know What All Are There In His/Her Resume & Be Prepared With Everything That You Could Be Asked On The Basis Of Your Resume. Go Through The NPAD Q Especially WRT SIP. 
Go Through The Basics Of Each Domain - You Never Know What All You Could Be Asked About. 
Go Through The JDs & What All The Expectations Are Around The Role.

Don’t(s)
Don’t Give Generic Answer.
Don’t Globe Around.
Don’t Give Unstructured Answer - It Looks Unprofessional During PI.

pre_process_tips:
There was an initial test which had logical reasoning questions and coding
Note: For IPM Students it wasn't open initially. They later did resume based shortlist and then asked IPMers to give the test
interview_outline:
1st interview: a very brief introduction and why BOFA. Very technical questions
2nd interview: More conversational, resume based but still technical
domain_questions: Very technical but only to the extent of CFA L1 and Fin1&II- asked about all types of valuation, fifo-lifo, EV, EBITDA, EV formula, P/E for two firms is x and y - where will you invest, Depreciation methods, growth vs value investing, Interest rates and effect on debt, Government bonds and various scenarios in which repo, reverse repo, OMO (all those instruments to control Money Suply) are affected
hr_gk_questions: Tell me something about yourself, do you know the role and why BOFA
looking_for:
1. Basic Technical knowledge
2. If you can identify the concepts properly - like the interviewer said "which depreciation method is better - LIFO or FIFO, or gave P/E of HUL and LIC, so he wanted me to point out that LIFO/FIFO is not a depreciation method or to tell him I can't compare P/E of two different sectors
3. Presentation skills (asked to explain a thing from interest section to a layman in 60 seconds)
right_wrong:
What went right: 1. A bit of technical knowledge
2. When the interviewer asked me to explain badminton in 60 seconds, I drew the badminton court, net and racket and used it for explanation, the interviewer didn't expect that I ll draw up to explain, so he liked it.   
3. There were way too many questions, so I kept on asking if i can think for a minute
What went wrong: I couldn't answer all the questions right so panicked a bit.
tips: CFA L1 summary notes and knowing what is EV (there were atleast 4-5 questions on EV)
dos_and_donts: For other set of people, interviews were pretty chill. Just this one division took slightly intense interviews

pre_process_tips:
Number of Processes: 2 (Aptitude Test + Psychometric)
Duration: 45 minutes for Aptitude and 35 for Psychometric
No specific tips, Just be yourself and some Apti prep shall help
interview_outline:
1. A generic PPT given by the HR rep
No introduction was asked
2. Questions about myself and my experiences
3. Questions from myside to them
situational_questions:
1. What was one time when I had to do something challenging? What did I do to go around it?
I gave him my own experience managing a team of 49 people. And asked me to explain it in deep details of how I approached the whole process. It took me some time to explain to him exactly what it was and how my team did it. My overall goals were set with a bit of conservative realism and revenue generation was not a priority. This might be one bad strike for me.
2. What was that one time when you had to work with a person who did not agree with your opinion? 
I explained 2 incidents, one from Sports while the other with an academic project. I might have come back as a person who always wanted to win the argument and can be a bad trait which they did not want. Hence a balanced personality would be better than forcing to win personality!
looking_for: They wanted people with Entrepreneurial experience and skill set. They want to have a person who can align with the organization's high growth prospects.
right_wrong:
My team managing and goal setting was certainly different from the company's overall prospect. They wanted people with similar approaches to their goals. I might have come across as a Safety first person.

Focus on the these things
1. Keep an Ownership Mindset
2. Understand the KPIs for a retail store
3. Know the history and Ops of the company
4. Show that profit matters (My conservative approach might have come altogether against this)
tips: I was not selected for the next round

pre_process_tips: Personal Interviews
interview_outline: Interview was balanced. It started with Tell me About yourself and other questions which are based on resume. Details about achievements were asked initially from resume and what did I learn from it. After that questions related internships and projects were asked. These questions were accompanied with domain specific questions at the same time. Few new domain specific questions were asked. At the end few HR questions were asked and interviewer asked me whether I have any questions. Overall Interview experience was really good.
domain_questions:
Technical related questions were asked which are related to my resume. Internships and Live projects were focused. 
Few marketing related questions:
Mini case study : How will you do STP for the particular product?
Other questions : What is CRM, activities in CRM, explain it with particular product.
Difference between traditional and current marketing
Few questions related Digital marketing.

I followed STAR approach wherever possible and tried to use frameworks wherever possible backing up with formula and got really positive response from panel.
situational_questions:
Few questions related Position of Responsibility and academic and extra curricular activities. What PORs I had, Major challenges and how did I overcame, How did I managed events etc. 

Here also I followed STAR approach for questions.
hr_gk_questions: No current Affair Questions Few HR questions like tell me about yourself were asked.
looking_for: Good Technical Knowledge and Cultural Fit.
right_wrong: I was able to answer most of the questions in a structured format and frameworks. I could have used more  quantitative data to back up my answers
tips: Prepare your resume thoroughly and really well, Be prepared for each and every line and term you mention in resume. Go through basic concepts, electives you have opted for. Do mock interviews with friends. The more you practice, more helpful it will be. Domain sessions and PrepCom preparatory material was really helpful and sufficient, you can refer that frequently.
dos_and_donts: Be calm during process, Don't stress out. Prepare well in advance. All the Best.

pre_process_tips: Application filled, shortlisted for GD, shortlisted for PI, offer roled
gd_topics_tips: Product VS Marketing (pros and cons)
interview_outline: Introduced myself, family background was one of the key areas of discussion. Mostly domain related questions, HR questions related to group handling skills. Interview was more or less balanced but slightly inclined towards technical questions.
domain_questions: Introduced myself, Majorly focused on roles of responsibilities in school and college, stressed on leadership capabilities, talked about the switch from finance to sales & marketing, talked about multiple events organised as a team leader, asked about any past experience connected to sales and marketing front (even if remotely related).
hr_gk_questions: No current affair question was asked. Panel was welcoming, they were actively listening but did not give me the satisfaction of them looking convinced. Panel was expecting more technical knowledge in S&M. Once the interview was over, they stated how the usage of technical concepts like distribution channel and STP could have been acknowledged more.
looking_for: Traits and overall character as a leader. They constantly pushed me to answer how I'd motivate my team members. Leadership traits is suggested to be touched upon by a candidate before the PI.
right_wrong: PI converted. Usage of more S&M concepts would be appreciated more.
tips: I figured that even though it is largely understood that interviewers are looking for confident candidates but a balance between humility and assertiveness would be the perfect sweet spot. Throughout the interview I tried to speak very politely and not just throw around words to impress. I also admitted not knowing few of the answers and apologized for trying to beat around the bush for a brief second or two. This was later on appreciated by the interviewers.
dos_and_donts: Please don't try to come out as a candidate that the interviewers find intimidating. Be self assuring but they need to know if you'll deliver output as per their instructions in a corporate setting. So, my biggest learning would be to regulate confidence as and when needed.

pre_process_tips: Direct application through placement portal
interview_outline: Interview started with 'tell me about yourself in 30 seconds' and they moved to a case immediately after. The case lasted for majority of the interview. The interview concluded with discussion about favourite domains during MBA and why.
domain_questions:
1. Since it was GRID Infra, I happened to mention about my internship with a highway design company in the tell me about yourself question. 
2. That seemed to have interested them and the case was based on the same topic. 
3. Case question : There is a plan of expanding a 2 lane highway into a 6 lane highway. Discuss. 
4. My approach:
    1. Asked preliminary questions like purpose of expansion, location, availability of alternate routes, traffic and funding model. 
    2. I was asked to estimate the traffic- both present and expected traffic on the highway(simple guestimate- looked only for approach and not the numbers) 
    3. I next moved to cost-benefit analysis. Estimating the revenue from tolls and comparing it to the costs incurred. It was a PPP model so spoke about that here. 
   4. Also asked what all aspects would motivate people to take this route- I split the traffic into commercial and other and answered based on cost savings vs time savings.
situational_questions: NA.
hr_gk_questions:
What were your electives in the second year and why.
Since it was a consulting role, I had mentioned about the strategy electives I had opted for in particular and spoke about having a balance of all domains as I was a generalist.
looking_for: Structured thinking and communication skills.
right_wrong: I was able to cover all the aspects of the case and answer all their questions concisely, this would have worked well for me. Based on my understanding, they judged based on quick thinking and structure of answers.
tips:
For consulting case and guestimate prep I referred to Case in point, IIM A and L casebooks. 
I started the preparation in advance and solved 2- 3 cases everyday.

pre_process_tips: There was an exam, pretty basic math english and logic questions
interview_outline: HR interview was on hirevue, Technical interview was over videocall for 30 minutes. Most of the questions were about the resume and there were a few puzzles.
domain_questions: Questions about the companies I interned at before: how they managed sustainability, what their biggest contributors to their carbon footprint are according to me, etc.
hr_gk_questions: Why this field, what made me apply to the job, am I interested in consulting, do I see myself working in consulting for long, etc. Would I prefer a tech company (since my resume was heavy on mathematical modelling and coding). I answered all the questions honestly, told them I want my work to be meaningful and that's why I'm choosing the sustainability division, long term plans include a PhD after a few years of work, wouldn't prefer tech because coding isn't what attracts me, solving problems is what I'm interested in, etc etc.
looking_for: Enthusiasm, willingness to tackle challenges, positive outlook, confidence
right_wrong: There weren't any bad parts as such. I think maintaining a positive attitude throughout the interview definitely helped. Even in cases where I wasn't able to think of an answer, I shared my thought process with the interviewers and openly admitted my weaknesses/where I was getting stuck.
tips: Consulting domain material was useful to build confidence in answering cases, though typical cases weren't finally asked in the interview. Mock PIs are important in giving you an idea of how you behave in interviews. I went through a lot of typical puzzles asked in interviews to understand how to approach puzzles. Although the one they asked me was not one I'd encountered before, the revision definitely helped me approach it the right way.
dos_and_donts: My advice is to remind yourself before the interview that you are qualified, intelligent, and definitely worthy of the role. Don't be afraid of the interviewer, be comfortable with them and remain calm, positive and honest throughout.

pre_process_tips: There wasn't any Application form. But yes, there was a psychometric test, then a GD and then an Interview. The psychometric test was not that tough and it was testing my personality, how I would react in some situations, etc.
gd_topics_tips:
The topic given to my group was "Can Indian start-ups survive the winter funding?". We were a group of 8 people for the GD. The key tips is to speak out loud relevant points. Do not cut other participants and not to just talk about your points. 
We kind of strayed from the topic during GD. But we got ourselves back on track and I believe the discussion was healthy.
interview_outline: It started with a brief introduction. Then they went through my resume and asked me numerous questions based on that. Then they went to domain based questions. It was a friendly interview conducted by 2 people. Overall, it was HR heavy along with some technical questions.
domain_questions: They asked me basic HR domain questions such as "The maslow's theory", and a marketing question as well, i.e. "How would I sell an IPAD pen to them?"
hr_gk_questions: HR Questions: Why I left CA, where my articleship was, Why HR consulting etc. They asked me about my career plans, since my life till now hasn't followed a particular path. Also asked me questions based on my previous Lawn tennis aspirations and tested my current Lawn Tennis knowledge. They also asked about the BYJUs financial issues.
looking_for: I think they were looking for a person who not only has book knowledge but overall knowledge too. They were interested in the personality of the interviewee and how well they can fit in the organization.
right_wrong: I could not answer the current affairs question as well as 1 tennis related question. Yes I converted the interview.
tips: The HR prep pack was extremely helpful. As well as the Mock GD/PI sessions conducted by prep committee.
dos_and_donts: I read extensively about the company.

pre_process_tips: After the initial shortlist (probably based on Resume), we had an Excel test. Since it was being conducted online, it was a MCQ test utilizing Excel formulae. A couple of caselets were given and we had to answer along the lines of what Excel formula would be used (Formula Name, $ Referencing etc) to achieve the desired result. It was fairly simple given that it was MCQ and there was ample time. Probably had some more criteria as well to shortlist for the next round which were not revealed
no_interviews_duration: 2 Rounds of Interview - one with Senior Associate (appx an Hour) and one with Senior Managers (2 senior managers took consecutive interviews of 30 minutes each)
interview_outline: The Senior Associate interview was almost entirely based on Cases and Guesstimates. The first Senior Manager interview had a couple of situations and Resume-based Qs whereas the second Senior Managers interview was more of a conversation about general stuff
domain_questions:
Senior Associate 
1. Case - Cab driver wants to increase his Revenues 
2. Guesstimate - market sizing of a magic veterinary drug
3. Mixed - estimating standalone costs of a company division which is being carved out

Senior Manager 1 
1. Situation - what all synergies might be there if 2 Auto companies are merging (I had mentioned M&A as an elective and I had worked on Auto sector during Summers)
right_wrong: I think the fact that I had done a live-consulting competition (Neetishashtra in Iris) really helped to boost my story as to why I want to do Consulting as a fresher since it was a unique point and I was able to relate DDV to my Finance knowledge and interest in IB and related topics
tips:
M&A course by Prof. Manish Popli -  I was able to utilize a lot of classroom learnings and I think they liked the fact that I had some knowledge about how M&As work, different kinds of synergies, post-merger integration etc, all of which was covered in this course

Prepcomm Navkiran Consulting session - the speaker shared a factsheet of information for Guesstimates which was really useful

pre_process_tips: Had to fill the application form on reculta itself, following which we had an online test which was a mix of aptitude questions and some software questions (primarily SQL)
no_interviews_duration: 2 interviews, duration of around 20-25 minutes each
interview_outline: First round of interview focused more on my understanding of what the company does and how is it different from its competitors. Also had to solve small problem statements relating to some use cases of the company. Second round of interview was more technical, with questions on statistics and probability
domain_questions: Most of the technical questions were based on statistics and probability like for example knowledge on different types of discrete and continuous distributions. One questions also asked related to joins in SQL
hr_gk_questions: Few questions like introduce yourself and why this role in particular. No current affairs based questions were asked
prep_resources: Previous transcripts of interview questions helped a lot in my preparation. Studying in depth about the company and what it does I believe was the key
looking_for: They were primarily looking for candidates who were genuinely interested in the company and the role and had done a thorough research on what it is exactly that the company does.
right_wrong: As I was well prepared with the company background, I was able to make a good impression early one and that set the tone for the rest of the interview as it helped made the interview more conversational and interactive.
tips: As mentioned earlier, I believe having a thorough knowledge of the company was the most critical aspect. Apart from that just putting on a confident front, even if you are feeling the nerves will go a long way in impressing the interviewer
dos_and_donts:
Be well versed with the company culture, values and offerings
Be confident, always maintain eye contact with the interviewer and have a warm face
If you do not know the answer, it is okay to say you are not aware of the particular topic instead of globing around.

pre_process_tips: We got direct shortlist
gd_topics_tips:
We had Chairman's GD, 8-9 different topics were given and it was case based !!
For each of the 8-9 rounds one leader was appointed and his role was to moderate the GD for other members and summarize the dicussion
no_interviews_duration: There were 5 different elements. 1. GD, 2. Written test (HR ), 3. Psychometric test, 4. Case Study round, 5. Final Interview
interview_outline:
1. GD - Chairman's GD took around 1.5 hr
2. Written ability test - In this there were a few HR questions for which we had to write the answers covering Why Lava, Long term - Short term goals
3. Psychometric test - takes around 30 - 45 mins
4. Case Study - We got problem statement related to Market entry and had to create solution ppt like we do for typical case comps, it also tests analytical and logical reasonings.
5. Final Interview - It took around 1 - 1.5 hrs, 5 panel members
domain_questions: For GenMan role focus more on the elements of your resume, panelists takes one of the pointers from each of the heads like academics, Work ex, POR etc and asks in depth questions from them.
hr_gk_questions: Basic NPAD questions like Biggest failure in life, Long term goals and vision, Why lava etc
prep_resources: Case prep helped a lot, End to end prep of resume is very important
looking_for: They look for good analytical + logical reasoning skills, they tend to look for good top of mind answers and how motivated the individual is for joining the leadership role.
right_wrong: Being confident and showing genuine interest for leadership role and paying lot of emphasis on learning !!
tips: Participating and podium finish in case competitions helped a lot, even consulting case prep helped in aspects related to structured thinking
dos_and_donts:
Do(s):
Resume prep to be done throughly
Show inclination towards learning and developing
Interviewer will give hints, refine your answers accodingly
Stay humble and respectful

Don't(s):
Don't answer spontaneously, think and answer, structure your thoughts well thats what they mostly look for.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlisting followed by 3 Case rounds and 1 Senior Partner round (to assess cultural fit)
no_interviews_duration: 4 interviews (3 case + 1 with Senior Partner). 3 case interviews were 45-60 mins long. The Senior Partner round was 5-7 mins long
interview_outline:
The 3 Case interviews started with a brief intro, both candidate and interviewer. Then "Why consulting? Why PwC? Why Strategy?" Followed by a full length Case to be solved. Was asked to solve on Excel and screen share in 1 interview as well, and walk the interviewer through the approach used, assumptions, etc. Case rounds did not ask much from CV either, just a brief discussion on 2-3 projects I did in my previous job as an Associate Consultant in management consulting firm. 
The final Senior Partner round was just to assess company fit and see if candidate was interested in joining the firm before PwC rolled out the offer. Was just 5-7 mins long, brief discussion.
domain_questions: Just cases were asked. One case required knowing financial statements - what information is available in which financial statement, etc. Case was related to Banking industry in US
looking_for: Logical thinking, business acumen, critical thinking and clarity in thought & communication. Cases were not straight forward. Some Excel modelling was also tested basis the cases.
right_wrong:
While solving the cases, ensured I was communicating with the interviewer at all times - conveying assumptions used, approach was conveyed in the beginning, asked relevant questions, etc. Kept interviewer in loop at all times, and ensured time was not breached either. Interview was not stressful either, so concentrated on the case completely.
Converted the interview.
tips: While solving the cases, ensured I was communicating with the interviewer at all times - conveying assumptions used, approach was conveyed in the beginning, asked relevant questions, etc. Kept interviewer in loop at all times, and ensured time was not breached either. Interview was not stressful either, so concentrated on the case completely.
dos_and_donts: Practice cases and guesstimates. Basic consulting prep should suffice. Ensure communication wit the interviewer at all times. Convey approach and assumptions beforehand.

pre_process_tips: Resume Based Shortlist
no_interviews_duration: 3 PI Rounds (50 mins, 35 mins, 20 mins) + HR Round (5 mins)
interview_outline:
The rounds were quite balanced. All the rounds started with basic Tell me about yourself, Why PwC, Why Ops/Consulting & resume based questions, followed by one or two Cases/guesstimates. In cases and guesstimates, they were more interested in the approach than reaching the final answer.
The rounds seemed like extensions of previous rounds. If you made an error or weren't aware of some concept in the earlier rounds, ensure to read up on it before the next round, as they are highly likely to ask the same thing again.
Prepare some questions to ask at the end of the interview & feedback on previous rounds.
domain_questions: Operating Model of a Retail firm (SCOR Model)
hr_gk_questions: As I was a fresher, why should they select me over someone with WorkEx. Showcasing genuine interest in joining the firm and the domain helped.
looking_for: They tried to gauge my interest in ops and how serious I was about the job role. Being well versed with JD and mentioning instances from the Pre-placement talk helped. Data analytics projects (SPSS, R etc.) was a focal point in 2/3 rounds.
right_wrong:
Good Parts - I was able to back all of my assumptions during cases and tried to keep the process engaging for the interviewer and take their inputs. Clarity of thought and composure was a plus.
Bad Parts - I wasn't well prepared for the technical part for round 1 and used generic terms.
tips:
IIMI Consulting casebook for interview experiences. Domain session PPTs for technical.
Victor Cheng and IIM-L consulting club YouTube channel for case interview preparations.
Basic research on the interviewer helped.
dos_and_donts:
Know about the company and the role. Talk to seniors and PPO'd friends in the firm and get clarity on what is expected of you.
Don't get nervous if you don't know something; ask clarifying questions. More often than not, the interviewer will guide you in the right direction.

pre_process_tips: Application, Resume Shortlisting, Online Test, Case+GD, Final Interviews (2-3)
gd_topics_tips: GD was an extension of the case study, where 5 leadings case questions had to be discussed
interview_outline: Both interviews were completely technical in nature. No introduction or HR based questions were asked.
domain_questions: Technical questions included areas like the 3 financial statements, valuation (absolute and relative), calculation of FCF, EV, Working Capital Changes etc. "Walk me through DCF" is a typical question. There were also some basic math questions like square root of 3 and 2.
hr_gk_questions: Some current affairs like present GDP figure, NIFTY, SENSEX, why the indices have shot up so much. Also about recent M&A deals with details about how the company being acquired was valued.
looking_for: They were mainly testing your knowledge of finance and accounting concepts, as well as your awareness of general market trends. In addition, a rapid-fire nature of the interviews tested how you react under pressure and handle questions you don't know.
right_wrong:
Try to build a rapport with the interviewer. For example, the lady taking my 2nd interview was the same one who had conducted the PPT, and I mentioned that I remembered her, which set a positive tone to the interview and showed that I had paid attention. Basically, LISTEN TO THE PPTs. 
As this is an IB profile, having a strong grip on Finance is but essential, so if you have not brushed up your concepts, things could take a bad turn.
tips: Corporate Finance Institute (CFI) website is a go-to for finance interview preparations, coupled with Investopedia. The session decks shared by Prepcom and Equit-i's material is also very helpful to skim through a few hours before the interview. The mock GD and PI are helpful to pinpoint your weak areas and it is best to take them seriously.
dos_and_donts: Read in detail about the role and the company, and have RELEVANT questions to ask at the end of the interview.

pre_process_tips: Resume shorlist, case based discussion round, Interview 1 and Interview 2
interview_outline:
No resume based questions in the first interview. Was given 2 cases - 1) Netflix wants to start D2C ecommerce website. Need to analyze and design. 2) List out Main problems with swiggy app and operations and provide solutions
The second interview was a little resume based - TMAY, why microsoft, why prodman, link between work ex and prodman, how would you explain servicenow to a 9 year old as a prodman
domain_questions:
Case 1 - Netflix wants to start D2C ecommerce website. Need to analyze and design.
Started by asking as many questions as possible to the panel. For eg, why does Netflix want to explore this domain, for customer engagement or to Inc revenue. Usually the panelists leave all the details upto you but it is highlight recommended to ask questions.
Started by analysing which customer age to target and listed their pain points. Sourcing methods were discussed where the panelist helped me a little by pointing out flaws in approach. Then priotised which pain points to address and designed the app by providing the customer journey.
hr_gk_questions: The interviews was completely case based with some work ex questions.
looking_for: They were looking for people who were genuininly interested in product mangement and were willing to learn. This can be portrayed by asked as many questions as possible to the panel while solving the case.
right_wrong: Converted. I could have learnt more frameworks to have a better understanding of which one to use and in which situation.
tips: I was genuininly interested in prodman and wanted to learn as much as possible with the interview. I was calm and smiling throughout which gave them the impression that I was prepared. It would help to watch some prodman related interview experiences on youtube to gain some confidence.
dos_and_donts: Need to have an answer to why prodman and why microsoft.

pre_process_tips:
1. Filling form on Reculta 
2. Psychometric test
gd_topics_tips:
Case based GD 
Case related to car rental service company whose customers were unsatisfied with the services due to wait time and some other issues. 
Just after GD, more information was given for the same case and we were asked to write a solution in A4 size paper. Question was based on cost analysis for the digitisation of the rental service.
gd_duration: 8 minutes for GD then 1 minute each was given to everyone to summarise their points
interview_outline:
Was first asked to give introduction but something which is not already written in resume. 
Then was asked some follow up questions related to it (all HR based). 
Further, the same case for GD was taken up, the company was now facing declining profit and we had to recommend solution.
Finally a guesstimate was given, which was again structured in a way that related it to the case but was basically a guesstimate on number of non residential passengers arriving in Bangalore airport daily.
domain_questions: Company related questions were minimal. While answering one of the question I had stated that Capgemini serves big clients so the panel asked me to name a few clients
hr_gk_questions: I had mentioned that I love to do social services, so I was cross questioned on the same. Some of the questions were - “How would you manage to work for corporate which focuses on profits while social services are non profit”
looking_for: Good confidence and answering with calmness when faced with unexpected questions.
right_wrong:
Bad parts - Messed up a little bit on the structure while solving the declining profit case. 
Couldn’t solve the guesstimate. 
Good parts - I knew I was messing it up but still held the smile and the confidence. Didn’t show a pinch of nervousness. I feel that’s what helped me convert it.
tips: Basic cases from consulting prep material provided by prepcom is sufficient. Mock GDs helped in building confidence and strategise when to enter, dos and don’ts, etc.

interview_outline:
1st round started with intro and a brief about the internship, followed by a case (profitability) and a guesstimate.
2nd round was a mix of technical and HR. Mostly grilled on the resume. 
Final Hr round was more of a formality to test basic communication skills.
domain_questions:
Case - Declining revenues of an edible oils company in India
