Guesstimate - Estimate the weekly revenue of a street vendor
Other questions were mostly resume based.
There were no questions from finance as such. Since my resume was tech heavy, I was asked to tell ways in which technology can be helpful during a merger/acquisition. 
Also, I was asked a few puzzles.

They were looking for a structured approach and comfort level with numbers. I was asked to calculate the final answer in the guesstimate. Try to round off as much as possible. Also, mention even the most basic reasons while solving cases, instead of jumping to sophisticated ones. Clearly communicate any assumptions that you take.
situational_questions: Nothing much
hr_gk_questions:
Why MBA? Why EY after a work ex in IT?
4 qualities that will help you while working at EY?
3 things in life that you want to improve?
Why didn't you get a PPO?
looking_for: Logical thinking and structured approach
right_wrong: 2nd interviewer was counter questioning all my answers. Being calm and taking his comments sportingly helped a lot. I should have mentioned a few finance electives and read about recent M&As cases, since they were trying to gauge my interest in the role.
tips: I started solving cases early. Casebooks of other IIMs shared by PrepCom helped a lot. Giving a mock initially is very important, since it makes you realise how much preparation needs to be done and what your weak areas are.
dos_and_donts: Write down all your basic answers for resume defence and HR stories (at least in bullet points). It is something that 99% interviewers will ask.

interview_outline:
Round 1: Started with introduction and asked about the projects in my resume. This round was technical heavy with in-depth questions about the tools and technologies used in my final year project. A case related to my project was asked.
Round 2: Fully HR based
domain_questions:
Round 1: A lot of technical questions about my final year on computational drug discovery and about the ML/AI, NN technologies used. 
Case: Say, a pharmaceutical company approaches EY to tap into the India market which is in it's R&D phase what are the bottlenecks or challenges expected specifically in India and what will be your strategy for them?
The case question interviewer gave was very vague at first, asked more questions to get clarity on the problem. When I asked him more questions, he responded well.
Round 2: Why EY? I did talk about the purpose and vision of EY as a company and how it relates to my vision in life.
hr_gk_questions:
Round 2: You are a fresher, why should we hire you for a consulting role? What's your biggest strength? Asked about my hobby(Gaming and cooking)
I was prepared for these questions and also with my NPAD
looking_for: Me being a fresher, they just tested my undergrad concepts and the projects I've worked on. How I approached a case was also tested.
right_wrong: I was strong with my projects and its IT part. I handled all the technology related questions well. As he asked a case related to one of my projects, it was comfortable to answer.
tips: I was not prepared for consulting. I just went through the consulting case books of some B-schools the previous night and did a good amount of research about the company.
dos_and_donts:
Dos:
Do a good research on the company
Prepare for guesstimates and cases(mostly beginner level if you are new) from B-school casebooks in the repository
Make your self introduction part interesting

pre_process_tips: Application on Reculta, Resume Shortlisting and 2 Buddy Rounds
no_interviews_duration: 2 Buddy Rounds- 15-20 min each, 1 Director Interview-40 mins, 1 Partner's Interview-30 mins
interview_outline:
Interview 1- Started with introduction, questions about resume points , FAC concepts, Guesstimate and Market entry combined case on Tesla's Market in India and should they enter or not. Good healthy discussion on various aspects of finance and resume points.

Interview 2- Some more discussion about myself and my resume , mostly evaluating my job fit for the company role. Some questions on Financial Accounting and costing. HR Heavy
domain_questions: Ratio analysis,  Flow of Income Income Statement and its pointers, What are the various financial statements and what are the objectives of it.
hr_gk_questions: Most questions were about my achievements in the domain of electric kart racing championship where I attained AIR-1. my POR's and my work ex .
looking_for: Good confident personnel ready to learn , ready to correct his mistakes.
right_wrong:
I feel what went good was my confidence and concept clarity. Also i dived into each and every aspect during case solving , went MECE which was appreciated for structured approach , I had clarity why I wanted to join this role which was a plus point. 
I feel that i was not able to crunch some numbers quickly, which I thought would've gone wrong, but fortunately I got in and the interviewer was impressed with my structure and approach.
Converted both interviews
tips: The started decks on finance and consulting, also the case book helped me a lot during the preparation. The mock PI conducted by PrepCom helped me gain a clarity on how to attend interviews and what I should work on before sitting for the company interviews.
dos_and_donts: Just be yourself and confident , Summers can be a bit exhaustive but at the end its all worth it. Focus more on having a structured approach towards the cases you are given and try to have a good idea about the various domains of interviews.

pre_process_tips: Got shortlisted for Buddy Round, had one call with my Buddy and then shortlisted for the Final Interview
interview_outline: The buddy call was quite technical and the interviewer wanted to grasp my understanding of what Synergy does as a firm and what Project Finance is. Then questioned about some Finance and Accounting basics followed by some questions about the projects that Synergy has taken up recently and also how to approach Valuation when it comes to Project Finance.
domain_questions:
Valuation
3 Financial Statements
Project Finance Basics- CFADS and other terms
hr_gk_questions: My views about the national policy affairs that were going on during the time of my interview( Delhi Govt's order against Stray Dogs). They were mainly trying to assess my personality and whether I'd be able to fit in the firm and have opinions about things or not.
looking_for: I think they were looking for candidates who had an aptitude and willingness to learn with an open-mind, given the fact that Project Finance is a very niche industry, they don't expect you to know the intricacies of it. Just strong basics and clarity of basic finance concepts.
right_wrong: I think my introduction and conversational questions during my final interview went right for me as the interviewer was interested to know more about my answers and spikes that I was laying in my answer and it wasn't monotonous or a one-way conversation at any point.
tips: Along with the required theoretical knowledge, focus on your NPAD and situational questions so that you are able to build a story and thus have a conversation with the interviewer.
dos_and_donts: Be inquisitive about the field of Project Finance and the type of work Synergy does.
additional_remarks: I was asked a lot of puzzles and also some questions related to our Term 1 subjects (Financial Accounting, Probability and Economics), so brushing up on your basics would help as well.

pre_process_tips: After resume shortlisting a form was forwarded from ITC containing some general NPAD questions.
gd_topics_tips: It was a case based GD. And the case was "Air crash". GD composed of 8 candidates and there was 1 moderator. We all were asked to discuss about the case and then speak one by one for 1 minute each on question from the case given by the moderator.
interview_outline: Introduction, background, Resume based questions on internships, convincing the moderators why marketing, a case was given on how will you launch a new product( masala) in your local area. In 2nd interview I was asked to choose an ITC product and had to convince people so that its market share increases. ( products- Ashirvaad  aata, Lays vs Bingo).
domain_questions: Won't say technical, actually in the case they were looking in logical aspects, and frameworks like porter's 5 forces, 4P's used if required.
hr_gk_questions: Which is your dream company other than ITC. I initially picked apple which was safe bet considering it doesn't competes with ITC as well as its not possible for me to join that but later they forced me to pick one that comes in campus. I chose one of the consulting companies. Later they asked me why not marketing and not consulting?
looking_for: One thing they were looking was speed, you cannot take much time and they even told me FMCG employee has to be fast. Other than that it was logic and communication.
right_wrong: Don't answer anything about which you don't know and in analytical questions try to bring creativity. Research about 1 or 2 of its product.
tips: The marketing compendium or the Kotler Summary. It'll take 3-4 days to go through properly, but as I was constantly questioned on academic concepts, I think it was very important to know that. And what they asked was usually beyond the scope of Marketing-I, so the Kotler summary helps.

pre_process_tips: ICICI form to be filled on the website. Pretty simple form, just normal Resume facts and basic HR facts
gd_topics_tips: Small case study - not finance related - TOPIC: Role of social media at workplace
interview_outline: 2 panelists(both male) - Introduction, Balance sheet and income statement of a bank, some basic accounting treatments of financial transactions, financial results of ICICI, Why ICICI, Comfortable with hindi? (P.S:- I am from Chennai), recent trends in the banking sector, what are my roles and the tasks performed in the finance club I am a part of, what was the GDP growth in the previous quarter?, Comfortable with sales also?, Family background, any relatives in ICICI?, any live project or internship with ICICI? (don't know why the last 2 questions were meant for).
domain_questions: I managed to answer most of the technical questions, except the financials of ICICI. I don't think they expect students to go through the annual reports, both the interviewers were very friendly, kept smiling all through the process, expected detailed answers especially for the financial implication technical questions (the question was what would be the changes if depreciation of $100 has been omitted on the 3 statements at a tax rate of 40%), I was working on an article for my club and asked me in detail about the article, since my father is into automobile industry, asked about the industry overview, Vehicle scrappage policy.
hr_gk_questions: GDP, growth of automobile, and banking sector
looking_for: They were looking for thoroughness with finance related questions and the passion of the candidate for the role.
right_wrong: Verdict - Converted. Good things - was confident and thorough with most of the basic questions. Bad things - couldn't answer the ICICI financials question.
tips: Learn about the banking industry thoroughly and be well-versed with the CV. Also, go through recent finance related news. Glancing through their annual report can also be considered.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlisting
interview_outline: Both interviews started with basic introduction, some questions on FAC (subject in 1st term) and then a guesstimate
domain_questions:
Interview 1:
What is P&L statement? What is its utility?
What is inventory turnover? What happens if it is high/low? Interviewer needed detailed and well structured explanations
Guesstimate: Estimate the number of televisions sold in india in a year

Interview 2:
1 guesstimate on- "Estimate the number of mobile phone users in Bangalore"
How will u vaildate the answers?- I  mentioned about 2 hypothesis testing we had learnt in IPS. Interviewer was fine with it but also wanted non-statistical way how validating.
hr_gk_questions: No HR questions
looking_for: The interviewers were looking for concept clarity and approach. They never expected the final answers in any guesstimate. They were also looking at how clear you are with what you have learnt so far.
right_wrong:
Some times in guesstimates I missed out a few cases but always checked with the interviewer and was quick to take his cues and come up with the answers. Interviewer was happy with that. 
I was asked to validate my answers I came up with in guesstimates. I went with complex statistical solutions. Interviewers wanted simple solutions as well. Always look for simple approaches first

Got rejected in final round
tips:
Had practiced a lot of cases and guesstimates from various case books. So these guesstimates were very simple compared to that and I could solve it easily. Mentorship sessions conducted by consulting club in collaboration with seniors was really helpful,

Paying attention in academic classes also was helpful.
dos_and_donts:
Practice as many cases as possible and utilize the various sessions organized by consulting and other clubs effectively.
Do not give less weightage to classes as compared to placements. A couple of questions feature from academics as well and a lot of things discussed in classes can actually be used in the interviews.

pre_process_tips: Application on Reculta followed by online test (Aptitude test+ Questions from Finance+ Questions from happenings in Financial Market)
gd_topics_tips: JAM round where two candidates chosen by the coordinator spoke on each topic. The first candidate was given 90 minutes to speak and the second one was given 60 minutes to add on. Topics included: Localization or Globalization, Improvement of standard of Sports in India, Bank Mergers- Boon or Bane, Harmful Effects of Covid 19 in the long run etc.
interview_outline:
1. Technical Interview- Started with walking them through the CV, asked why I was applying to 
Finance role, asked few finance questions, asked if I understood the job role and explained it for me, asked what all was taught in Finance in Term 1 and what topics other than that I had looked into, questions from topics I said I looked into, few more general questions from finance
2. HR Interview- focused on trying to understand if I would stay in the company in the long run if given the internship and PPO. Asked to elaborate on  extracurricular activities mentioned in the CV. Again asked why Finance.
domain_questions: Difference between bank's balance sheet and a manufacturing company's balance sheet, liquidity ratios, what is a bank and what are its different verticals?
hr_gk_questions: Focused on trying to understand if I would stay in the company in the long run if given the internship and PPO. Asked to elaborate on  extracurricular activities mentioned in the CV. Again asked why Finance.
looking_for: Effort that was given in preparing for the job role and whether I would stay in the company in the long run.
right_wrong: Converted. Weren't really any good or bad parts. Interview went on like a discussion.
tips: Reading the JD and preparing accordingly (knowing the terms, what they meant and how they are calculated), listening to the Pre-Placement talk, knowing the points in the resume well

pre_process_tips: Assessment - basic accounting, corporate finance, Quantitative aptitude and market awareness
gd_topics_tips: Case discussion - taken in 2 parts - 1 part 80 min assessment had MCQ questions with followed by a case related to basic financial concepts like CAGR, multiples, etc. 2 part was a GD where some qualitative questions with respect to the same case were discussed. For GD part try to put different points and try giving suggestions related to the domain things like buy back and stuff.
no_interviews_duration: 3 of approximately 20 min each (back to back)
interview_outline: Basic intro, technical questions, Industry awareness, basic 1-2 HR ques like why Investment banking, why MBA, mental math. Heavy on the technical and industry part. Be through with accounting and extras (if mentioned in the resume of are aware of). Follow a sector, recent trends in the industry, recent news (at least 3-4), basic economic variables GDP, repo rate, nifty index, etc.
domain_questions: Basic accounting questions walk through the 3 financial statements, impact of depreciation on all three, minority interest.
hr_gk_questions: Recent news you have heard, numbers if any.
looking_for: Typical finance interview heavy on technical and industry. Basically you need to be through with your concepts and having some background in finance would definitely help
right_wrong: Though I converted it but I did messed my industry awareness part, it was mainly compensated by my string technical but do read up on the industry trends.
tips: The 400 Investment Banking Interview Questions & Answers You Need to Know - Breaking into Wall Street really helped me. For finance domain PI would help more
dos_and_donts: Do not try to globe if you don't know the answer simply say you are not aware of. Be through with your resume in and out and not just in terms of what you have done but the external factors like about the industry you have worked or interned in, current trends of what you did or what you have mentioned.

pre_process_tips:
The process started with applying on portal and choosing the preference of roles. Next a workshop was conducted where people were divided in breakout rooms. 

After which a small case was discussed, which was a decline in revenue problem, and the second part included guesstimates.

The next case that was discussed was the Mergers and Acquisition case. It was very detailed and included both qualitative and quantitative analysis.
gd_topics_tips: No GD
interview_outline:
The first interview started with an introduction of myself, followed by a small case which was qualitative and based on reasons behind employee attrition rates.

The second interview had 2 panelists, this was a longer interview and went for more than 40  mins. It was a case discussion on GTM strategy and had two parts qualitative and quantitative.

The last round was a one on one conversation with the Director, it was mostly an HR round and just was about the expectations.
domain_questions:
Case 1: Recent times have seen employee attrition rates go up. What could be the reasons and provide recommendations

Case 2: A foreign financial company is looking to open up its services in India, for it citizens in the US. How should they go about it?

Cases like M&A and GTM mostly asked
hr_gk_questions: Introduction, PoRs and overall why consulting
looking_for: They were looking for someone who was eager to learn and could think on his feet. I remember not understanding a lot of terms in the case asked but it is important to be confident and ask questions, show the learning nature and then work around it
right_wrong: I asked questions and understood things that were beyond my prior knowledge. More than knowing a lot of concepts, it becomes important how to apply those concepts.
tips: Solving casebooks, in groups and alone helped. Reading about various industries. Talking to seniors and getting to know how to go about interviews help

pre_process_tips: The Application for CDD role was quite simplistic, I just had to fill in some basic details.
no_interviews_duration: 2 buddy calls(30 mins each), 1 Director Round(30 mins), 4 interview rounds(30-40 mins each)
interview_outline: Most of the interviews started with an introduction, a case or a guesstimate, some basic HR questions (about the firm, role, my aspirations) etc. In one of the interviews on the final day, I was thoroughly asked about the Indian Economy, CPI, WPI, RBI's Stance etc.
domain_questions:
I was asked 5 guesstimates and 2 cases overall.
Case 1: Your client is an ice cream manufacturer who has been facing decline in profits, find out the reason why and recommend solutions. (Applied the basic profitability framework)
Case 2: You own a b&b chain of 10 restaurants, one of the hotels has low efficiency and occupancy, find out why.

Guesstimate 1: The number of high end salons in A city like Mumbai (Gave both supply side and demand side solutions) 
Guesstimate 2: The number of pencils used in Bangalore in a year.
Guesstimate 3: Estimate the market size of online education in India.
Guesstimate 4: Number of two wheelers sold in India in a year.
hr_gk_questions: Why Deloitte, Why this role, Tell me about yourself and basic conversation that took place with the interviewers.
looking_for: A logical problem solving approach, ability to take as many things into consideration, and being able to communicate effectively without getting nervous.
right_wrong:
Converted
Positives: Being able to clearly list down my thoughts during the cases and guesstimates. Able to talk to the interviewers freely and confidently.
tips: Case Prep with my group definitely help improve approach towards cases. Mock PI was helpful and helped me to focus on HR questions better. Basic session material from Prep Com was helpful and finally the current affairs sheet brought all the news together in one place.
dos_and_donts: Trust your instincts and communicate freely. Work on Case prep and solve minimum of 15 cases on your own.

pre_process_tips:
It was a two-part process. Aptitude+Domain knowledge test and the second was a 15 second long "Why me" video submission. 

There were two sections in the test. First was an aptitude test which is simple but you'll have to keep an eye on the timer. The second section tested your domain knowledge, since I am a Civil Engineering graduate I was asked basic and intermediate level domain specific questions. It will help if you brush up some basic concepts. Expect numericals too.

The video submission expected you to tell why you are a good candidate for the internship and how well you fit into the organization. It helps to pay attention in the PPT as they tell you what kind of candidate they are looking for.
interview_outline: They asked me to introduce myself and run them through my resume. It was an HR based interview and basically a best fit check. They asked me if I have a preference for the kind of projects that I would like to work on and if I have an issue with relocation.
domain_questions: Nope
hr_gk_questions:
I was asked to elaborate on some projects that I worked on at the my previous company. It was a 15 min long interview, so it was pretty brief. 

Just be confident about what you are saying and project yourself as someone who is willing to learn and perform.
looking_for: A confident person who has reasonable knowledge and is flexible.
right_wrong: I converted the interview. All went well and the right answer to the question - "Would you have an issue with relocation?" is - No.
tips: The company decks, sector reports and the current-affairs live sheet. The mock GDs/PIs were important to boost confidence and identify areas for improvement.
dos_and_donts: Prepare a question or two that you to would want to ask them at the end of the interview. Very important.

interview_outline:
No intro, asked my name and whether I was comfortable with accounting. Started with accounting, shifted to finance, macroeconomics, microeconomics, behavioural economics, back again to macroeconomics, & then finally accounting. The last question was what did I knew about the company. Surprisingly, the interviewer was friendly; we had a few jokes in between.
Was too technical heavy.
domain_questions: The first question in economics was Quantitative Easing and Quantitative Tightening. The interviewer was looking for three things: concept understanding & how well I can relate it to other concepts of fin or eco, past occurrences and current or future possibilities, data to support the concept.
hr_gk_questions: For almost each technical question, the interviewer asked for any data for supporting my answer. Detailed discussion over a lot of current affairs happened: how much is the drop in fed reserves in India (exact data with timeline) & the probable causes, detailed explanation of crude oil prices (exact data with timeline) & how is that linked to the PFCE of US vis-a-vis India vis-a-vis Russia, Russia-Ukraine war effects, US economy, Sri-Lankan Crisis reasons & effects, US Fed & RBI new regulations, monetary & fiscal policies, etc.
looking_for: Knowledge of economics, finance and global economy to back the answers.
right_wrong:
The interviewer confused me in a discussion over a simple topic of inflation by linking it to a few other concepts, and at the end I wasn't able to give the correct answer. I didn't give much focus to economics for summers prep, could've improved my answers a lot. 
Financial concepts along with economics and current affairs on the US Fed & RBI actions in the past helped a lot. I did convert the interview.
tips: The best help was the current affairs sheet, especially the BFSI, Indian Economy and the RBI actions worksheets. Would be really great if the committee adds another worksheet for Global economy.

pre_process_tips: A submission on the topic 'Is India Ready for Digital Payments' was asked
interview_outline:
2 Case interviews and 1 HR interview with Partner

Interview 1: Started with introduction, then case was given to find out causes of attrition in XYZ consulting firm and solutions for the same if I were a senior consultant there and members from my team were leaving.

Interview 2: It was a mix of case and HR. Case asked was to find out market size of robotic cleaners in India. HR questions about Everest Group and prior workex were asked

Interview 3: Entirely HR , with questions similar to that of NPAD
domain_questions: No technical or domain specific questions were asked
hr_gk_questions:
1. Why consulting 
2. Why Everest
3. Strengths and weaknesses 
4. Learnings from MBA and internship
5. Biggest failure
6. Subjects that I liked and subjects I didn't do well in MBA, and my academic performance 
7. Question about prior workex and  change of industry- from construction to supply chain to consulting
8.Your profile looks ops/scm heavy,why don't you want to pursue that, aren’t you interested in it anymore, why
9. Walk me through any of your case competitions, your approach and framework
looking_for: My guess is that they wanted someone with credible workex or intern in a strategy based role
right_wrong:
In the case interviews, asking questions and granularity helped. Could have handled a few HR questions better- like describe a situation where you exhibited xyz characteristics, so better examples could have been thought of there, NPAD should be thoroughly revised and rewritten
For me, sounding candid and sincere worked, so HR questions need preparation
tips: Casebooks provided by Prepcom and Consulting club
dos_and_donts:
Understanding Everest's work and the domains they operate, their website and prepcom deck should suffice
Also to be able to relate prior workex with current profile and justify your interest in Everest

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlisting
no_interviews_duration: 2 interviews. 1st lasted for an hour. 2nd was for 45 minutes
interview_outline: First interview started with introduction, went into resume details specifically workex questions, workex projects and their details. Then moved into a case which also involved guesstimate. After the case there was some discussion revolving the case. Overall the interview was quite balanced. For the 2nd interview, the interviewer directly jumped into technical questions related to the industry I had previously worked in. The interview was completely technical and more of a stress interview
domain_questions: The 2nd interviewer asked me if I knew what the company exactly did. I had researched about accenture strategy and was familiar with the kind of projects they took up and their approach towards the implementation side. The interviewer was happy with the answer
hr_gk_questions: The first question was about the introduction.  Prepare a well rounded introduction. Also be sure to mention cues in the direction which you want to take the interview. You can drive your interview from the introduction. Also be thorough with the NPAD questions and try to create detailed answers for all the questions in NPAD.
looking_for: In terms of technical aspects they were looking at structured case solving and also number crunching abilities. Be sure to solve guesstimates as well. Also they were looking at knowledge of the industry you have previously worked in. Be thorough with your previous projects and also with the industry you have previously worked/interned in
right_wrong: Having a structure to the case and being confident helped. Also taking the cues given by the interviewer helped. Being well versed with my workex also helped. Converted
tips: Case and guesstimate prep helped. Being prepared with NPAD questions also helped. Mock PIs helped in understanding what was lacking in the overall preparation.
dos_and_donts: Be thorough with the case and guesstimate prep. Be confident and structured with your answers. Also be thorough with your past work ex internships and projects

pre_process_tips: First, resume shortlisting. Second, an excel test (elimination round). The excel test comprised of 13 MCQ questions based on 3 short cases. The topics covered included functions like VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, INDEX, MATCH, and pivot tables (topics covered in the course SMOD)
no_interviews_duration: 3 interviews (30 minutes each) and 1 HR interview (10 minutes)
interview_outline: All interviews started with "Tell me about yourself" or "Walk me through your resume." Questions like "Why PwC", "Why DDV", "Why consulting", "What do you understand by the role DDV" were a part of all the interviews. Then there was one case or guesstimate in every interview.
domain_questions: For the question "Why PwC", research well on the company and don't give generic answers. The interviewers wanted to know how well I understand the role, hence the question "Why DDV?" I structured the answer on the basis of the inputs I received from my buddy and the company website.
hr_gk_questions: The HR interviewer asked me that I have a finance heavy resume so why do I want to enter in a consulting role. I responded by telling how my interest in Finance was a result of my subjects in undergrad. However, exposure to subjects like Strategy in first year of MBA and my summer internship in a 'Data Consultant' role has shaped my inclination towards consulting roles.
looking_for:
In-depth research on the company and role.
Very clear answer on "Why consulting?" and "Why DDV?"
MECE Approach to Cases and Guesstimates.
right_wrong:
Went wrong: I made a few unrealistic assumptions during the first guesstimate. I could have done it better by remaining calm.
Went right: I solved the cases very calmly in the subsequent cases with the senior managers of the company. Even when I got stuck in between, I didn't show the tension on my face, and asked them for 30 seconds to think about it and respond.
tips: Guesstimates and case preparation (particularly M&A cases) are a must.

pre_process_tips:
Resume based shortlisting.
No written/psychometric assessment. No GDs.
interview_outline:
Both interviews had similar type of questions. Introduction was asked only in Round 2 and NOT Round 1. There were questions based on my work ex and also internship.  Be ready with in depth knowledge of whatever resume points you have mentioned under any heading.
There were multiple questions around Marketing domain. 
There was only 1 HR Question - How will you motivate team in a high pressure environment? 
At last they asked - Why Paytm?
domain_questions:
Marketing domain questions - 
1) Frame a marketing plan for an app through which users can invest in mutual funds. I started with customer segments, then their needs, how to solve those needs, ATL and BTL activities, ROI to measure them. The interviewer was pretty satisfied with the answer.
2) How an airline company can increase its profits? Give 10 new ideas which not have been implemented by any existing airline. Go whacky. Brainstorm hard. I started with the problems which I had faced while travelling through air and gave suggestions to solve those.
situational_questions:
How will you motivate team in a high pressure environment? 
I answered - I will help my peers to realize how important their contribution is. How it will have a big impact on the company.
looking_for: An interactive person who is good storyteller. Frame any answer based on your personal experiences. It will be more relatable for you as well as them. Domain knowledge must be strong. Keep it as a discussion rather than an interview.
right_wrong:
Personal touch to all the answers went great. Be funny if possible. The interviewer will enjoy the discussion. 
I converted the interview.
tips: PrepCom material - go through each and everything. Go through NPAD. Have stories around each resume point.
dos_and_donts: Do NOT mug up the introduction and why this company. Be spontaneous.

pre_process_tips: Case Submission (Online)
interview_outline:
Round 1 of interview :- Guesstimate :- How many litres of water is used at IIM Indore in a day? I followed a bottom up approach number of people in one hostel * number of hostel * average daily consumption of an individual (including drinking water too) + faculty housing + gardening etc (I took an average number for this)
RCA :- Amazon after sales return has increased by 10% find out why?
(Followed the structure of Internal, external factors as a start point)
Case based discussion on the case submitted.

Round 2 :- Case :- Google is trying to add new features of parking in maps, what all things would you add?
2. How do news recommendations come on in-shorts, name a few key parameters for recommendations (eg location, age, interest etc.)
HR questions (Why PM? Why media net?)
domain_questions:
Guesstimate :- How many litres of water is used at IIM Indore in a day? I followed a bottom up approach number of people in one hostel * number of hostel * average daily consumption of an individual (including drinking water too) + faculty housing + gardening etc (I took an average number for this)
RCA :- Amazon after sales return has increased by 10% find out why?
(Followed the structure of Internal, external factors as a start point)
Case based discussion on the case submitted.

Case :- Google is trying to add new features of parking in maps, what all things would you add?
2. How do news recommendations come on in-shorts, name a few key parameters for recommendations (eg location, age, interest etc.)
hr_gk_questions: HR questions (Why PM? Why media net?)
looking_for: Structured Approach to solve RCA and PM Cases.
right_wrong: Case solution could have been more detailed. Features should be prompt while designing a new product
tips: PM case books would help.

pre_process_tips:
Test which included Aptitude, English, Management Decisions, etc.
(Test was easy to crack, no need to study for that given you know how to solve basic aptitude questions)
Application form in which we had to submit our mark sheets, proofs about our work experience, etc.
no_interviews_duration: 4 (15 min each, last was HR round)
interview_outline: 3 technical interviews and 1 HR interview.

pre_process_tips: Application on portal only
interview_outline: First round there were 3 panelists, it was a general HR round asked basic information about yourself, strengths, weaknesses etc. In second round there were 6 panelists and this round was case interview, gave a profitability case and asked to think of new business strategy (any kind of idea such as marketing, operations or new product) to double the revenue in the next five year.
domain_questions: No technical questions.
hr_gk_questions:
From resume asked about internships only. Other HR questions were 
1. Introduction and Why MBA?
2. Why marketing and 7Ps? (first asked domain preference)
3. Future goals? (long and short)
4. Strengths, weaknesses, achievements and biggest failure.
5. Why Menon and Menon?
I prepared NPAD very well thanks to the PCom. I answered all questions honestly and tried to explain in detail.

right_wrong:

role_offered: BE Mechanical, Work ex 20 months in Automotive sector
pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlisting
interview_outline: Started off with introduction. First round was a case round with technical heavy questions. Second round was balanced involving HR questions and resume based questions
domain_questions: I was asked if I knew about Accenture strategy and the roles offered by them. The interviewer seemed keen on skills related to my previous experience and other skills like analytics. I could answer the questions related to the company and roles. Since I am not well versed with analytics I demonstrated keenness to learn it in the near future. The panel seemed convinced.
hr_gk_questions: I was asked about my projects in the previous organization that I worked at. I elaborately described the nature of my work and the skills acquired during the experience. The case framed by the panelist was related to my answers. No questions based on current affairs were asked.
looking_for: The most important trait that I thought they were looking for was my eagerness towards the role and the willingness to learn new relevant skills. They were particularly impressed by my way of communication. Maintaining a smile and answering positively created a good impression during the interview. They made sure to offer roles which were relevant to some skill/experience mentioned in the resume.
right_wrong: I could solve the case well, but I could have answered in a more structured manner. Not being nervous during the interview and asking the interviewers about their work and experience was something that enhanced our conversation.
tips: Solving multiple cases from the case books and developing my own frameworks helped me a lot. NPAD helped the most to answer HR questions. Mock PI helped me structure my answers to the resume-based questions.
dos_and_donts: Be thorough with your resume and prepare your NPAD answers. Practising multiple cases for consulting interviews is a must. Try finding cases relevant to your past work-ex/projects.

pre_process_tips: Aptitude test
interview_outline:
Started with introduction, got cut across at several points in between, dug really deep into various projects they saw on my resume. 
First interview lasted 45-50 minutes, had two guesstimates and a case on Luxury Retail- market entry (since I had taken this elective). 
Second interview lasted an hour- had two cases - one on choice and implementation of ERP in an M&A scenario. The other was a relatively simple profitability case . 
HR interview lasted 20 minutes- resume verification, asked me to walk her through my LinkedIn profile, etc
domain_questions: Questions on Telecom and digital marketing since I had worked as  a business analyst at Verizon. Questioned me about Agile Scrum and certifications they saw on my resume. Asked me why Agile was better than Waterfall, artifacts and roles in Scrum. Differences between Agile and Scrum etc.
hr_gk_questions: Why I left my job after two years;whether I would go back, given a choice; why consulting ( went on for 10 minutes) why Infosys, location preferences, whether I was open to traveling.
looking_for:
Confidence, Strong english vocabulary, Use of jargons( not too extensively), logic driven approaches to cases ( they will help you out if you're headed the right way), Back your answers up with facts and data wherever possible. Most important- maintain eye contact. 
Also, read up on digitalization versus digital transformation- very important.
right_wrong:
Good parts- once you set the tone well initially, the interview will proceed smoothly. 
Bad parts- can't recall anything
tips: Extensive preparation on resume, industries in general and specifically what industry you've worked in previously. Prepare for generic cases ( profitability, market entry and expansion, M&A), guesstimates. Stay I  touch with your company folks, keep in touch with what they're doing.
dos_and_donts: Be confident and calm. Maintain eye contact. Don't fidget and use a lot of hand gestures.

role_offered: Senior, Climate Change and Sustainability Services-Financial Advisory and Accounting Services (CCaSS-FAAS Professional)
pre_process_tips: An aptitude screening test was held initially.
no_interviews_duration: 2 interviews. A HirePro virtual HR interview (lasting roughly 20 minutes), and the final technical interview (lasting 30 minutes).
interview_outline:
The HirePro virtual interview tackled 8 curated questions (same for everyone)related to past working experience, basic introduction and background, expectations and situation handling.
The final technical interview, in my case, tackled mainly introduction, and lot of questions were asked regarding my summer internship at Mumbai International Airport Limited, and a few questions regarding an Environmental Economics project.
domain_questions: Not in my case. Although, hearing from others who had appeared, most of the technical interviews by EY for Senior-CCaSS FAAS were very domain heavy (especially economics and various ESG frameworks, plus logical reasoning and situational questions; it is a very good idea read up the frameworks mentioned in the JD).
situational_questions: Not in my case. Although, this was the trend observed in most of the EY interviews.
hr_gk_questions: We did discuss a point on the recent COP26 conference, and India's stand on climate change.
looking_for: I think the interviewers were actively looking for someone with projects and internship experience that dealt in fields directly related to environment, sustainability and climate change. Accordingly, the interview direction was determined by this. If the candidate did not have a the relevant experience, he/she were asked a lot of technical questions. If yes, then the disucssion mainly would've centred around the internships and projects.
right_wrong:
Interview went according to my best expectations. I had extensively prepared according to my recent summer internship and the environmental economics project, as I felt these two would be the most relevant points of discussion for the position at hand. 
The interviewers were very patient and very chill. They had enabled a very friendly and relaxed vibe, which definitely might have helped in my case.
tips: I basically focused on brushing up my resume points, especially my internship and academic projects. I practiced mock interviews from an external resources.

pre_process_tips: 1 MCQ test- 10 questions on logical reasoning and critical thinking, 10 on data interpretation, 10 on finance and account. Followed by a 6 min video round- 1 question about managing conflict and another on whether startups are fairly valued
interview_outline: First two were technical rounds, the third round was with head of talent acquisition. First two rounds were mostly resume based. Focus was on my internship projects. A few questions HR questions like which role interests you. Didn't ask a lot of fin, very basic questions on options.
domain_questions: Very basics questions on options. Which industry do I follow and my opinions on it
situational_questions: multiple scenario based questions like, how would I go about dealing with a situation where I have two deadlines and I can't meet both of them, what if my manager isn't available and a report needs to go out to the head of the team. The time I managed a conflict in a team
hr_gk_questions: Weakness, a follow up scenario based question on that, what role was I interested in within Financial Ops
looking_for: Communication skills, how in depth my knowledge was about the stuff I had done, were looking for a fin profile (cfa, summers at Edelweiss)
right_wrong: had researched the organisation well, asked smart questions in each interview and they appreciated that. Apart from that, was able to answer fin questions, and they were interested in my summer project so was able to build a long conversation on that. Talk about the work culture and company values. They are proud of it.
tips: Company Deck, went through the entire finance domain folder (Very very very useful), The HR document was also very helpful. For HR, prep 4-5 incidents/ situations, use those as examples in answers.
dos_and_donts: Follow your sector thoroughly, make sure you're well prepared with your resume and NPAD

pre_process_tips: Reculta
interview_outline: Started with Introduction, went into questions based on what I said, then some small situation basis question related to finance.
domain_questions: Mention 3 decisions that you would take to improve cash flow situation on the company and then how to approach a distributors association of a particular state who are not willing to sell your product. Take your time and have a structured idea. Even if your answer is not to enter the market, give a structured and proper justification
hr_gk_questions: Why Medtronics, and which segment do you prefer in Medtronics as a finance intern. Learn about the values of company and drive with that.
looking_for: No certifications required, should have some financial knowledge. FAC is enough. We should be able to take decision based on the situation what the panelist said. I think they were also looking for people who aligns with their values, culture and who are willing to learn more.
right_wrong: I was unaware of the duties of a finance intern, my answer was not that satisfactory. I thought I lost his interest in me. At the end he gave me an opportunity to ask questions to him, I asked a question that was very interesting to him as a CFO. He enthusiastically replied to my answer in a detailed way. dos_and_donts: Prepare a question to ask him. Try to include some current events that has happened in the firm into the question. That final question can also be really helpful to convert. This suggestion applies for all companies

Second interview: HR related questions, technical questions, questions about company

certifications: CFA L1, Lean Six Sigma Belt (Green)

Interview revolved around discussions on valuations, enterprise value, financial statements, etc. The interviewer nudged at places I got stuck, it was really important to be calm and think thoroughly before answering.
domain_questions:
1) How do you account for a joint venture and an investment (subsidiary) into the financual statements?
2) What is enterprise value? What are minority interests? Why do we account for them?
3) What are the various valuation methods?
4) Walk me through a DCF. 
5) What is the difference between comparables method and gordon growth model in determining terminal value?
6) Why is the denominator WACC-g in gordon growth model?
7) Basics on option? Asked if I know about exotic options
8) What will be the impact on financial statements if bonus shares are issues to employees. Some more questions on impact on the financial statements.

10) What will be the impact on reserves and currency (appreciation/ depreciation)

right_wrong: I answered almost everything on the technical side. I accepted whatever I didnt know instead of making wild guesses. The most important thing was to carefully listen to the nudges and think accordingly which showcases your critical thinking skills
tips: Be clear with your answers
dos_and_donts: Just keep your basics strong

gd_topics_tips:

The discussion started with different criteria for reservation, i.e., caste, geographical region, gender, etc, and which of them should be given more importance and why. The group put forward points to support economic criteria as well as points in support of other parameters as well.
interview_outline: Started with basic introduction, past internships and project, why MBA, why marketing, favorite subjects in graduation and questions on that, basic marketing concepts, why Wipro, what is your understanding of Wipro
domain_questions: What all concepts did you study in marketing? What is the product life cycle? How can consumer behavior be influenced? 7ps of marketing? looking_for: The panel was looking for someone genuinely interested in marketing and someone who is able to relate theoretical knowledge with practical experiences. Internships in marketing and insights on that should help.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlist was followed by an Online Psychometric test (also contained how you would tackle operation problems in Amazon and respond to them). Then 2 online interviews.
interview_outline:
Round 1 was CV based - know your CV in and out, and try to align the work that you have done with what Amazon requires- like how you analysed data to come up with actionable insights, led a project/ownership, etc. Be clear on "Why Program Manager?" and "Why Amazon?". 
Round 2 started with a puzzle (from GeeksforGeeks). Could not solve it, but approach conveyed to the interviewer. Interviewer was also pretty chill, and interview felt like a normal conversation. Then interviewer asked a basic guesstimate - "Suppose there's only 1 meat vendor delivering meat to all Pizza shops in Indore. How much meat should he stock on any day?"  Shared screen and solved the guesstimate on Excel, conveying all assumptions I used like % non-vegetarians, % pizza preference etc. Interviewer liked the bit about including Safety Stock in calculations. In end, asked Top 3 company preferences.
domain_questions: Asked Why Program Manager role, and not consulting (as I had front-end \consulting background)
hr_gk_questions: Basic introduction
looking_for: Amazon has clearly outlined traits/values they look for in hires, some of which I outlined in my interview using my CV/work-ex - Ownership, data-based decision making, growth mindset, etc.
right_wrong: Interview went very well. But rejected basis the last answer (had to purposely tank the last answer of "Top 3 company preferences" as was already placed). But overall, interview still went very well
tips: Consult seniors who appeared in the interviews and gauge their experiences. Overall, know resume inside-out
dos_and_donts: Be clear on JDs, Amazon principles, resume should be on tips, each and every project and its impact. Relate to the values and traits Amazon looks for in hires

pre_process_tips: Pre process - Buddy and Mentor Round
interview_outline:
Round 1 - Case on Profitability - Zomato is burning cash with negative profits, how can we improve?
Followed the profitability framework (Revenues andCosts), laid out the business model in revenue and all the cost heads. The interviewer asked me to calculate how much revenue zomato makes in one day and gave some data (mini guesstimate). 

Round 2 - Case on banking - Client is a retail bank, how can we diversify the retail loan portfolio
Asked preliminary questions. Followed the Growth framework and worked out details on expanding existing loan portfolio (increase ticket size, increase number of clients ) and looking into newer avenues (rural, insurance etc)

Round 3 - Your client is preparing a pitch deck for investors. It is a pharma company heavily focussed into RnD and used 3rd party for sales. It needs funds to set up its own sales network for a new drug. What will you include in the pitch deck.
I divided the ppt into 5 parts - The history about the company, the benefits of the new drug (why it needs to reach the market), flaw with the current system and why the need for change, sales plan for the new drug, financials for the new plan. I then dived deeper into the rationale behind each of the 5 buckets and explained the details.
hr_gk_questions: Tell me about yourself, Why Consulting, Why BCG, Questions on resume (projects, achievements)
looking_for: All 3 rounds were case based. They were looking for the structure - how detailed it is, the kind of questions asked to the interviwer and the suggestions given
right_wrong:
Couldnt convert.
Parts that could have been improved- Obviously improved on the structure and recommendations given, could have added more details and depth.
