Proove that data can predict things. Interview was somewhat balanced but more hr questions.
domain_questions: I mostly focused on answering questions regarding how being from biochem and biotech background I can relate to the products and the company. The info of co.pany was well researched so I kept my answers towards that area. Other hr questions I answered the same way as the preparations committe suggested and the panel members were happy with my responses and were supportive throughout the interview even if I didn't know some answers.
hr_gk_questions:
1)Define what academic projects you did
2) define leadership in your por roles
3) tell me somethinv about data
4) proove that data can predict
5) how you add value to the role
looking_for: Someone with decent amount of understanding about finance and knew somewhat about data and numbers(stats etc)
right_wrong: All the hr questions and info related to the company was well researched by me so I converted interview based on that only. Also I knew about ml models and stats which I used as an example towards number heavy roles could suit me
tips: Adsociation towards a number heavy finance role and how I can add to the company. Answers to these questions were already prepared by me
dos_and_donts: Keep it interactive as the panel members were supportive and were expecting a big conversation from the candidate side.

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlist, 3 Rounds of Interviews
interview_outline:
First Round: Tell me about yourself, internship experience and approach to the project, theoretical questions(basics of operations), work-ex takeaways
Case- What are the aspects you would consider if you want to reduce the logistics cost of an FMCG firm?
Guesstimate- Estimate the number of trees shed to meet the annual demand of paper.
Second Round: Extensive questions on work-ex, understanding of Industry 4.0(JD), analytics based questions, sourcing strategy, HR based questions
Case: How to reduce the catering cost incurred by a low cost aircraft carrier?
Third Round: Conversation-based, explain internship experience, favourite subject and concepts, rapid-fire questions
domain_questions:
What is Lean six sigma? Difference between TQM and Lean Six Sigma?
Favourite subject? Explain a concept from the subject to a layman.(Cross-questions)
situational_questions: No direct behavioural questions as such.
hr_gk_questions:
Tell me about yourself, Why consulting, Why PwC, strengths - the interviewer was attentive, asked for clarifications and cross-questioned at every step
No current affairs.
looking_for: Structured, open-to-learn, easily adaptable, relevant work-ex/projects(cross-mapped JD with resume before the interview)
right_wrong:
Good part: Clear understanding of HR, could connect theoretical questions with work-experience, structured approach to answering all questions, had practiced all kinds of HR questions, guesstimate approach was very well appreciated, covered all aspects of the case
Bad part: No experience with any data analytics software. Didn't know what poka-yoke was. But could answer the questions when prompted. 
Verdict: Converted
tips:
Extensive case prep- VC videos, CIC, CIP, IIMA & IIML casebook.
Having a case-buddy is a huge help. 
The consulting domain session was very useful.
dos_and_donts:
General: Be very clear with guesstimates, case preparation and HR questions.
Maintain your calm throughout the interview slot. 
Do not bring up hazy concepts in the interview. 
Expect thorough cross-questioning at every step.
Company-specific: Interact extensively with your buddy.

pre_process_tips:
The primary step involves making a customised resume, format for the same is provided by Deloitte USI and it needs to be uploaded on theur website. 
Once this is done we received our shortlists and we had an interview which had one round of 40-45 minutes and we were done.
interview_outline: It started with a brief introduction then it moved towards my work-ex and it's implementation in the field of Cyber Risk and then some questions were asked to check if I can provide innovative solutions to existing problems based on my knowledge. Then I had a situational round, where I was asked about conflict resolution and after that
domain_questions:
Q1. Difference between AI, Data Science, ML.
Q2. Existing applications of these three in Cyber Risk.
Q3. New and innovative applications that are possible in the future. 
Q4. Name a few cheaper ways of protecting data and softwares from ransomwares where we do not use AI/Data Science.
hr_gk_questions:
Q1. Why do you want to pick Deloitte? 
Q2. What is the one thing that actually taught you something that changed your life constructively?
looking_for: They were looking for Technical Knowledge based on what I have done and how much of it I can apply in the future, and they were looking for someone who can handle different different situations well enough.
right_wrong: Nothing went wrong throughout the interview, my technical knowledge and the situations that I used from my life in different questions about pushed the interview in the right direction.
tips: Mock PI helped a lot, I also did an HR round separately which helped a lot and to prepare for the interview I used the documents available on their website and I also used their press releases to understand current trends about yhe company which helped a lot.

role_offered: 19 months of work ex. in a CA firm
pre_process_tips: First it was filling application form then GD and last was interview.
gd_topics_tips: Diversity and inclusion - Whether it is needed or hyped ?
interview_outline: Started with introduction, then moved towards work ex. , internship, school, sports, and Domain specific. It was for an HR role hence most of the questions were related to HRM.
domain_questions: Asked me about my previous work, the roles performed and the different projects I was part of.
hr_gk_questions: Roles during interview and my learnings that will help during internship, about the sports that I play and 3 things it taught me, also asked me to give examples for everything. Asked me about my family background, also since I have been to many cities, they wanted to know what all things I learnt and how places were culturally different. Asked about outsourcing. They wanted me to relate everything with HRM and how would I react as an HR. Asked about recent HRM trend - Moonlighting. And if I were the HR how would I respond to it and what steps I'll be taking.
looking_for: Whether I knew things I have mentioned in CV or not. Also, they wanted me to link everything with the domain I am getting into and the job role that I will be performing.
right_wrong: I messed up a bit with the introduction part, tho they laughed and brushed it off. Rest I wasnt that prepared with connecting everything with HRM as my previous role involved more of audit work.
tips: Prepare your CV well. Try making atleast 7-8 probable questions from every single point written. Give as many mock GD/PI as possible. Cover latest trends in the industry.
dos_and_donts: Dont put your worth on any particular interview or company. It's more about having a good/bad day and nothing more than that.

pre_process_tips:
The pre-process was based on the following:
1. Memory based & chronology based puzzles 
2. Brain teaser games 
3. 100 Pyschometric questions 

There were no Quant or DI-LR based questions
interview_outline:
The first interview in essence was a formal conversation. At any point in time, it never felt that they were looking for a particular set of answers. They wanted to know me as a person and my perspective on various scenarios. They were looking for how well I would fit for the role. They heavily focused on ethics and values. 

The second interview was very fast-paced but only heavily focused on my resume. I was questioned on all the sections of my resume starting from my educational qualification, summer internship, co-curricular achievements, academic projects, research papers, PORs, extracurriculars, and interests.
domain_questions: In layman's terms what is Supply Chain Management?
situational_questions: In case a situation arises that a person who is designated to do a job fails to do the job and not available to resolve the problem. How will you handle this situation. What is the one critical aspect of this situation that would lessen the consequence of the problem?
hr_gk_questions:
I am a Chemical Engineer

Did you always want to be a Chemical Engineer?
Why did you choose a career in management after Chemical Engineering?
Can you mention few critical learnings from your Internship?
looking_for: The firm is an IT Consulting firm but the role did not require any technical expertise. A good business acumen and good aptitude was required. Knowledge or affinity towards finance was a perk.
right_wrong:
1. Ability to elaboarte on every word on resume
2. Knowlege of the mission, vision and goal of the firm
tips: Always try to align/ justify your answers with the job description or the firm in general.

pre_process_tips: Application on Reculta, Resume shortlisting
gd_topics_tips:
Topic: Distribution Strategy, More distributors vs Less.
-2min were given for thinking about the topic
-Every one got 2 min to speak on the topic unlike a traditional GD setting.
-Order of speaking was based on timing of hand raise by participants.
interview_outline: Started with introduction, Question about the challenges faced by TATA Steel, Few technical questions. It was balanced not too technical.
domain_questions:
Question on 3PL vs 5PL logistics: I told the panel i wasn't familiar with the terms, changed the question to "As a CEO of the firm, Will you recommend doing every work inhouse". I explained that few activities can be allocated to 3rd party so that our production output is not effected. Provided an example relating it.
Question on Six sigma( mentioned white belt in resume): Talked about DMAIC approach and tools like Pareto principle, fishbone diagram, etc.  
Panel composed of a HR and two technical panelists, all questions were asked by one of the technical panelist and he seemed satisfied with my answers.
looking_for: There were looking for cultural fit, knowledge of basics of operations and steel industry as a whole.
right_wrong:
Good: Introduction went well, i could give examples to back up my knowledge in operations
Could have handled better: I should have went through basic differences and terms like 3PL&5PL.
Converted.
tips: Steel industry deck and live news related to Tata steel by prepcom were useful to understand the current scenario and revise things in a short interval of time. Mock PI helped me understand a few must know questions like about company and industry to tailor my answers as per the company interview i was attending
dos_and_donts: Do's: Prepare basics of supply chain and operations, Lean six sigma green belt certification would be helpful.

pre_process_tips: Application on portal followed by resume shortlist
no_interviews_duration: 2 buddy calls (5 mins & 20 mins) and 2 offline interviews (both 20-25 mins)
interview_outline: Both the buddy calls started with some recent news related to global markets. First interviews was technical and second was HR. Asked about a few technical questions about derivatives, bonds. Then asked a few details about a recent project I did in finance about portfolio management. After that went on to ask why finance after engineering and why GS. Ended by asking expectations from the internship.
domain_questions: Futures and Options and difference between them, Equity swaps, Relation between bonds and interest rates, Libor vs Sofr and difference between them, If given $1 million which assets would you invest, which sector would you short, technical analysis (related to my project), current repo rate, pros and cons of OTC products over exchange traded, Why GS, why global markets.
hr_gk_questions: Questions about metrics related to my internship, certifications I did and why I did, why finance after engineering, why GS and why this role, what would you bring to the table, what role in finance are you aiming
looking_for: Basic knowledge of financial concepts, someone who had genuine interest in finance and would continue to work in finance. No expectations work-ex wise.
right_wrong: Good - Had a good understanding of the financial concepts and about the role, answered almost all the questions. Possible improvements - Should've prepped for current affairs and recent happenings in global markets well. Converted in the end.
tips: Know everything about the role. Prepare for NPAD and company specific questions like Why GS. Following recent news is very important. Read about derivatives, ratios(analysis), valuation and all the financial assets. Follow domain prep material shared by prep com and Equit-I.
dos_and_donts: Prepare a good question to be asked at the end of the interview. Be interactive and don't panic.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlist, followed by GD and two rounds of interviews (technical and HR)
gd_topics_tips: Risk Management - How can banks/financial institutions manage their AUMs under crises situations. Should have an understanding of different macroeconomic variables, their impact, basic understanding of market and credit risk
interview_outline: Started with resume questions, discussed PoRs, projects. Explained my understanding of risk management, small caselet on risk of exposure of an intl bank
domain_questions: Basics of risk management, understanding of the exposure that Credit Suisse has. Requires an understanding of type of assets, instruments held by fin. institutions. Following a cause and effect relation of macroeconomic variables on company performance will help.  Should be able to identify the different risks that they face and how they can minimise them. Projects (related to finance) on resume can be discussed
hr_gk_questions: Questions on PoRs held, discussion on what difficulties were faced in the same. Should be able to justify the work done and how it relates to your growth as an individual. Motivation to join the company, understanding of the company and its operations. Should be able to relate to short term goals
looking_for: HR- Confidence in abilities to perform, how you can relate past achievements to your potential internship and expected work. No additional qualifications were explicitly required
right_wrong:
Good - Was confident throughout, resume was thorough and displayed a strong understanding of stats, economics
Bad - Took a while to get the right answers for the case. Should keep answers brief while covering all related variables in the given context
tips: Read up on financial risk, risk management. Should be able to highlight key cause and effect relations during GDs, use economic/fin. knowledge to tackle cases if any
dos_and_donts: The role involves modelling, knowledge of R/Python is useful, however not a prerequisite

pre_process_tips: Online test that had to be done from mobile. Basic aptitude questions, had English oral and aural tests, English reading test and one audio submission about the company. Total time 30 mins.
interview_outline:
First interview: Online pre-recorded 9 questions. Had 4-5 mins to answer each question, keep camera on from laptop. Behavioral questions and company specific questions. Total time 40-45 mins.
Second interview: Interview in person. Questions were asked on general topics - resume, work ex, company specific, behavioral. Overall chill panel with slight grilling. Total time 45 mins.
hr_gk_questions:
Who are you?
How do you deal with conflict in your team?
How can you, being from technical background, think yourself suitable for a Genman role?
Strengths and weaknesses.
One instance where you showed demonstrated your strengths.
Which company under CKB you want to join and why?
looking_for: Clarity and consistency of thought in the answers. Sincerity, the interviewers were extremely smart and could catch any bluffs.
right_wrong:
Good: Well prepared about the HR questions. Was able to talk and keep conversation about the various companies under CK Birla, their values and the challenges they are facing. Knowledge of current affairs helped in keeping the two-way communication going. 
Bad: Fumbled a bit about the "Who are you?" question. They didn't want to hear about the standard Tell me about yourself answer. But the panelists helped me in getting the answer they wanted.
tips: Almost all HR questions were from NPAD. Company specific preparation helps a lot.
dos_and_donts: Know the company and the role - Basic qualitative understanding. If you don't know something in detail, admit you have a lot to learn - steep learning curve. Do not be intimidated by a 5-member panel with a lot of senior executives - be honest, sincere and polite.

pre_process_tips: First was a resume shortlist and after that a case based interview round. we were given a case and the solution need to be submitted in 30 mins and after that interviewer will question on the interview
interview_outline:
Round - 1
	Started with TMAY and he was interested in my work experience. So he talked about my work experience fully and asked some basic technical questions about servers, DNS, etc..
Overall interview went well and got selected to next round

Round - 2
	What is computer related supply chain? and all NPAD basic HR Questions but he grilled each answer and I was confident in every answer which I spoke, He seemed interested at the end of interview
domain_questions: What is a cloud based server? What is DNS? For both the questions interviewer  expected basic answers and since I worked in the same industry I was able to tell more about my work experience as well
hr_gk_questions: Both the interviewers seemed very interested about my work experience and constantly asking questions about my work experience related HR questions. Everything was covered in NPAD questions
looking_for: A person with relevant work experience who was very expressive and interested in joining the form. I would urge my juniors to construct a TMAY very coherently and be strong with the resume and HR questions
right_wrong: There was no bad parts significantly. I converted the interview and if it is an online interview make sure the mic and internet connection is good
tips: I used p casebooks from Lucknow, Bangalore and Indore. More than the preparation the interviewee must very expressive and very confident in the interview irrespective of the preparation
dos_and_donts:
Be very strong in HR questions and TMAY should be constructed very interestingly.
Be very proactive and confident

interview_outline:
Technical and HR questions in the first round
HR questions only in the second round
domain_questions:
What do you understand by risk and control? 
Can all types of risks be mitigated?
How would you explain the law of diminishing marginal utility to your younger brother?
hr_gk_questions:
NO Current Affairs Questions

Round 1:
Why do you want to do internal audit given that people join this function after they have explored a lot of different options and then they come to internal audit?
Why do you want to do internal audit given that people join this function after they have explored a lot of different options and then they come to internal audit?
What are your goals in life personal or professional? Not how do you see yourself five years down the lane, 10 years down the lane but more like what do you want out of your life?
What are your expectations from the role? 
Tell me two things about Indore that you think I would not know. 
Who is the famous comedian from Indore?

Round 2:
Why internal audit? 
Give an overview of the projects during internship. A cross question on that.
What is a challenge that you’ve faced during your internship and how did you go about it?
(Building on previous question about internship) Do you work better alone or in teams?
How have you added value to any of your internship after the eight week or two months period? 
Give an example of a situation where you managed conflict, say in clubs, committees, or group assignments?
looking_for: Fit and clarity
right_wrong: Right- Knowledge about the role, confidence in answering the questions
tips: clarity of thought
dos_and_donts: Understand what Internal audit is and why do you want to get the role

pre_process_tips: Initially we were needed to fill an application form on the company's portal. Next there was a   30 minute test testing cognitive abilities.
interview_outline: Both the interviews started with general introduction. Since I had prior work experience with Analytics, they asked about my work experience in detail. There were many questions about American Express like why I wanted to join the company, what I knew and liked about the company etc. Both interviewers asked 1 case study, 1 guess estimate and a couple of probability/puzzle questions each. There were less of HR questions.
domain_questions: What are the different segments in which AmEx works in India? What work I specifically did on Python? Tell me the uses of Linear and Logistic regression and what types of data they are used for ? Have you worked on any data visualization tools? The case studies were also related to the work AmEx did and how will I go about it.
hr_gk_questions: Why do you want to join AmEx? How can you contribute for the growth of AmEx? Tell me 2 of your strengths?
looking_for: They were looking for individuals who think logically and can look at a problem from various perspectives. Getting the exact solution was not what they were looking for. Secondly, they wanted individuals who genuinely wanted to work for AmEx and showed interest in the company's work.
right_wrong: Having prior knowledge about the company and going through the company's website proved critical. I tried to bring a logical approach to each question answered by me which I think they liked. I did convert the interview !
tips: (1) Company Website (2) Prepcom Company decks (do look at recent news about the company) (3) GeeksforGeeks Puzzles (1 puzzle was asked from here) (4) Practicing guesstimates

role_offered: Associate at Investment Banking & Private Equity Division
pre_process_tips: No forms or pre-process. Resume shortlisting & then personal interviews
interview_outline: After tell me about yourself, only technical questions were asked in both rounds except for just  1 HR qn at the end of 2nd round. There were some 10-12 technical qns asked in each round, 1st round set of questions revolved around testing basic fundaments of finance & and the 2nd round had a lot a situation based questions created from my internship section about investment baning and equity research.
domain_questions: First round started off with simple questions like what's freefloat, different valuation methods & kept increasing level of difficulty. Second round had questions had a lot of scenario based questions created from my internship column in Investment Banking like If there's a PE investor looking to invest how would you narrow list of firms. And kept asking for more criteria to narrow down the list further.
hr_gk_questions:
Only one HR qn was asked, where do you see yourself in 3 yrs.
CA questions like acquisitions that happened last year, indicators to check for economic state of country were asked
looking_for: Good understanding of finance concepts & investment banking domain & also articulating it confidently with clarity. Clearing cfa/frm wasn't used as a hygiene criteria.
right_wrong: It was like a rapid fire round and lot of time wasn't given to think of the answers. So staying relaxed during the interview & having the presence of mind to think through answers fast and present it in a structured way proved vital to clearing the interview
tips: Resume based preparation along with basic fin concepts& understanding valuations, fundamental analysis & investment banking
dos_and_donts: Prepare fin related resume points & basic fin concepts well & keep smiling a lot (a lot) during the interview.

pre_process_tips: Reculta Application and a buddy call
interview_outline: Started with a brief introduction, then onto cricket related hobby based question, after that questions about company and finance domain questions. Gave a logical puzzle to solve and finished it with some HR questions. Interview was quite balanced.
domain_questions:
1. What synergy does?
2. Questions about project finance vs corporate finance.
3. 3 financial statements relation with each other.
4. Valuation of a company.
5. Important ratios in project finance and their application(Read DuPont).
hr_gk_questions:
1. Hobbies based question on cricket and its current news.
2. Questions on academic project based on WTO.
3. Hometown and UG college related questions.
4. Future Career path?
looking_for: Basics regarding finance, interest in the job profile, ability to think on your feet, confidence in your opinion or views and ability to remain calm under stress. There is no certification or work ex expectation.
right_wrong:
Bad Part
1. Wasn't able to recall DuPont analysis? 
2. Got stuck for a while in solving puzzle due to a doubt? Ask questions to clarify the path forward.
Good Part
1. Interview was quite engaging and flew in a conversational manner as the start was with hobby based question and a dive into it.
2. Asked questions that was very logical and could be derived from basics of finance.
3. Solved the puzzle there itself although it took some time.
tips: Preparation Committees Domain session material, FAQs and company decks, online sources to revise basic finance and Equit-I finance material. HR mock was quite useful as it taught how to try to get an interview into conversation mode.
dos_and_donts: Read Company Decks thoroughly and complement it with internet surfing into projects of Synergy, read a bit about geopolitics, focus especially on project finance.

gd_topics_tips: How do you see the world in 2050?
gd_duration: Total duration: 15 minutes. 10 participants in 1 GD. Each participant given 1 minute each to express their opinion in the beginning. After 10 mins, 30 seconds to each participant to argue against/support the opinions expressed.
interview_outline:
Started with a brief introduction. Then it moved to why I wanted the role, why the firm. They asked me about my plans to continue with CFA Level 2 & 3 and if so, why want a role with not much core-fin knowledge requirement (Have a good answer prepared for that in case you have a fin-heavy profile). 

This was followed by resume based questions, they picked up a valuation based competition and asked related questions: How do you value intangible assets? What are the main aspects that you would consider while valuing intangibles? Do you think value stocks are influenced by the intangibles of the firm?
This was followed by questions on my internship. What was the project and the final recommendations you made. Some cross questions on the same.

Then they moved to my interest in the role. How long do I plan to stay in the role (they mentioned they were looking for someone who stay for long term) and my thought process behind the same.

The final segment included a few HR questions. If I have ever worked in big teams before, where's am I based out of and some basic details of my family members.
domain_questions: Try and relate more with examples. In the question pertaining to value stocks relationship with intangibles, I talked about the case of Amazon and how the market discounts all the information. Giving examples makes the answer more relevant and interesting.
hr_gk_questions: Why Nomura? Why this role?
looking_for: CFA Level 1 comes handy as the role requires basic knowledge about the different products from fixed income and derivatives.
right_wrong: Try to be confident. Smile if possible, that comes in handy.

pre_process_tips:
Candidates have to fill up an application form with the following questions:

1. What are your career aspirations. How do you propose to accomplish your career goals?
2. Why do you want to join ICICI Bank?
3. Which of the following possibilities appeal to you more and why? Kindly explain with reasons. a) Joining an organisation which gives you role and locations as per your choice. b) Joining an organisation which will rotate you in different role and location based on organisation needs.
4. Are you willing to move to any part of the country, away from your hometown? Why/why not? If the answer to above question is Yes, how would you overcome any challenges which you perceive you may encounter while working in a city away from your hometown?
5. Would you be open to take up a Sales role with ICICI Bank? Kindly provide the reason for the same?
6. Any other information about your candidature which you want to share with us.
interview_outline: Introduction, Role in the internship (in depth), Idea about the role interviewing for, How would I adapt in an on-field role, Why banking.
looking_for: They were looking for flexibility, willingness to learn and adapt, enthusiastic mindset and alignment of future goals of the candidate with the organization.
right_wrong: The whole interview felt just like a casual conversation between two colleagues. The intro went well and everything followed by was smooth.
tips:
1. Crafting a structured introduction of my journey like a story.
2. Keeping answers natural and to-the-point.
3. Confidently communicated and convinced them on why I am a good fit for the role.
dos_and_donts: Research about the workplace, culture and values as they were looking for a culture fit.

pre_process_tips: Aptitide test and a form with basic NPAD questions, mainly related to internship. This was followed by a case based interview and an HR based interview
interview_outline:
The first round of interview was based on a case provided there itself. 20 mins were given to read and analyse the case(pretty open ended) then the interviewer took a guided interview, basically to understand the approach I would take.
The second interview was situational as well as based on the resume.
domain_questions:
A few team management related questions like:
1) Do you think a diverse team is desirable? How would you manage conflict within the data experts and the client facing team?
2) What determines the outcome in (a certain situation)- stats based
3) Asked about my understanding of what the company does
4) Told me to form a hypothesis statement for a hypothetical question related to my social internship experience, asking me to repeatedly improvise until I crisped it down to the basics
hr_gk_questions: Questions were mainly based on internships. They expected me to relate it to how it's going to help me in the future. Asked me to introduce myself (expected a longer answer than usual). Asked follow up questions on my hobbies and interests. Asked which subject was my favourite throughout college and asked me to summarize why.
looking_for: Great communication skills, ability to perform under pressure, thorough knowledge of past professional experience(s), consideration of multiple facets while answering technical/case based questions
right_wrong: The fact that they saw me to be a good communicator and my ability to stay calm despite them throwing multiple questions at me simultaneously turned out to be a great plus.
tips: A few subjects related to the job profile, like IOTB and SAR

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlisting, Case Study Workshop and Buddy Round (Non-evaluative), Personal Interview-3 rounds (1 guesstimate, 1 case study, 1 HR)
no_interviews_duration: 1st : PI : 25 mins, 2nd : PI : 30 mins, 3rd : HR : 15 mins
interview_outline:
Round 1 : Introduction, Went through the resumes, picked up a project and asked a guesstimate related to it - Estimate the market size of Zomato in Delhi
Round 2 : Basic Introduction and a data-intensive case study where a new product (colour changing labels for milk bottles) had to be launched in two geographies - US and UK with an objective of achieving a turnover of 1B$ in 5 years. Data like price of the product, mobile penetration, population, technology adoption, price of bottle, margin was provided. Had to calculate which market is profitable
Round 3 : HR - Asked my expectations from the role, introduced the role, be sure you have questions to ask in this round
domain_questions: Why Consulting after BTech?
hr_gk_questions:
What are your expectations from the role? 
Why did you leave your previous job?
looking_for: Structured approach in case and guesstimates and clarity of thought
right_wrong:
1. I had practiced ~50 cases and ~15 guesstimates which made me comfortable with the case solving approach. It's important to practice cases and guesstimates for Consulting. 
2. Stayed calm and didn't panic
3. Took my time to understand the case and situation
tips:
1. I had practiced ~50 cases and ~15 guesstimates which made me comfortable with the case solving approach. It's important to practice cases and guesstimates for Consulting. 
2. Stayed calm and didn't panic
3. Took my time to understand the case and situation
dos_and_donts: Practice cases and guesstimates well in advance. During cases, don't stick to frameworks but be structures. During guesstimates, make sure your calculations are correct and you dive deep into the problem.

pre_process_tips: No pre-process direct shortlist for GD based on the resume
gd_topics_tips: Sectors which are positively and negatively affected by Covid
interview_outline: Started with the introduction, Went into the resume and questions based on POR which I held on my resume right from Cofounding a startup to being a part of Voyage capital and markets, HR based question in the end for few minutes in the end.
domain_questions: So being a Cofounder and member of Voyage Capital they asked me to analyze any sector of my choice of which I selected Automobile. They asked me how the sector is performing. my outlook and recent news. Further they asked me about the startup which I cofounded and what all things which I learnt during my MBA till now which I think will be useful in expanding it, some questions related to valuations of a company and especially valuation of a startup how would you approach towards it.
hr_gk_questions: Current affairs questions based on the sector, HR based questions on why gap year and what was your experience during National Defence Examination and it SSB.

pre_process_tips: Shortlisting from resumes (no application form)
interview_outline: Started with intro for the first interview, then a case, and sometimes they gave space to ask questions at the end. No HR questions, almost entirely case-based
looking_for: Structured approach, clear thought process and direction; how effectively can you communicate what you need and why you need it. The metrics were Problem Solving (highest weightage), Communication and Recommendations.
right_wrong:
Converted. 

Kept cool and moved on quickly if I got something wrong, stayed focused, if I was asking a question I tried to explain exactly why I was asking it so they knew it wasn't just for the sake of it. Tried to be detailed and creative when warranted. 

Could have clarified more aspects of the cases, could have gone slightly faster through the case.
tips: Material and guidance from seniors, case prep with friends from casebooks, Victor Cheng videos, domain sessions (live case solving), past years' feedback (FAQ sheet supplied by PrepCom) from seniors who had gone through the process (helped for a reality check)
dos_and_donts:
Start early. Don't overprepare frameworks - once they're clear and you notice little value add from each new case, move on to a new type. Unconventional cases are really good practice for thinking exercises and making your own structures. Definitely watch a few of the Victor Cheng videos and do thorough post-case analysis (helps in learning about industries) and listen to feedback from friends, seniors and buddies. Don't be afraid to ask seniors for help. 

It's okay to be burned out after doing a lot of case prep, and it's okay to take a couple days off here and there. Use that time to flip through old cases and revise what you learned.

domain_questions: None- just cases
hr_gk_questions:
1) Tell me about yourself
2) Why did you choose CA? Why MBA after CA?
3) Describe the projects worked on by you at your job (and follow up questions on the same)
4) What do you think is the key difference between working in a team and leading a team? What were your key learnings while leading a team?
5) What was the biggest challenge you encountered while leading a team?

right_wrong:
My background from a Big 4 firm helped me a lot through the interview, since they were interested in my work experience at that firm.
In the initial interviews (including 1 partner round), I rushed through the case unnecessarily, rather than taking my time and asking relevant questions. This led to the case going in the wrong direction, and loss of time.
tips: Victor Cheng videos, Case Interviews Cracked (Book and 4-part video series), Casebooks (IIMA, FMS, IIMI). Lots of case preparation with seniors and batchmates

pre_process_tips: Applied on Reculta, got direct interview shortlist
interview_outline: Started with introduction, one question about company. This went went on for 8-10 min. Then, one case for 30 min.
domain_questions:
Case - 
(Interviewer showed a product on Amazon) This is from a digital door lock company called Dorset. It entered in Indian market 2-3 years back when awareness about digital door locks started increasing and captured good market share. But slowly, the company started losing its market share with the entrance of Godrej and other small startups. Find out the reason and determine whether it should look for growth in India or should it exit from India.

I did not go with any framework. But used MECE approach, and asked questions basis the information being shared. I tried to keep the interview engaging during the whole time. The interviewer was also responding to my solutions in a positive manner that boosted my confidence.
hr_gk_questions: My introduction. What do you know about Everest group? He was not satisfied with my explanation so he explained about Everest. Then, the case started.
looking_for: They were looking the clarity on how you structure your questions and recommendations.
right_wrong: I could have had better understanding of the company. But because the case part went great, I was able to convert it. In the last, the interviewer gave one recommendation after my recommendations, I politely pointed out a possible drawback on that and provided a workaround.
tips: Keep the conversation engaging. Avoid redundant questions while solving a case. Keep on asking questions and if you are assuming something, inform the same to the interviewer first.
dos_and_donts: Case preparation is a must.

interview_outline:
Round 1 (40 minutes): Resume-Based Discussion
Resume based and basic discussion over company and role. Expect questions on workex, intership and projects.
Round 2 (25 minutes): Case Presentation
A case was provided during the first round and I was given 30 minutes to prepare a 3–4 slide presentation deck. 
Round 3 (70 minutes): VP / Leadership Round
Disuccsed about the role in detail and consulting nature of the job followed by domain specific questions. Discussion on the reflections from the previous interview rounds. Situational questions on experience during summer internships and workex. Strength and weaknesses were discussed thoroughly, with emphasis on learning mindset and cultural fit.

interview_outline: Interview was very technical. Started with introduction and detailed walkover my resume. A lot of cross questions with respect to work experience(Had worked as software developer in security domain). Then asked to discuss about any security framework and was given a case to solve using the framework.
domain_questions: The technical questions was mainly to discuss about the NIST cybersecurity framework and the various subpoints under it. I was also asked to develop a cybersecurity scheme for Zomato application using the NIST framework.
hr_gk_questions: Not much of HR questions. Just asked about myself and why I wanted to work in the organization
looking_for: They seemed to prefer someone who had work experience in software domain.
right_wrong: I had a decent knowledge on cybersecurity and frameworks but I couldn't make the cut probably because my answers for the case discussion was not quite structured.  I immediately jumped into the solution. I feel after the case was thrown at me, I should have taken a couple of minutes to structure myself. Could have helped.
tips: After getting the shortlist I read through basic cybersecurity stuff and the frameworks like NIST framework online. Mock PI's provided more confidence.

interview_outline: Started with TMAY, then jumped into my summer internship where they spent about 20-25 minutes. They then asked a case based question. Then went into HR based questions.
domain_questions: Tried to grasp my understanding on the Sales and Marketing domain through cross questioning on my internship experience. Questions like, what kind of sales strategies did you use. What was the process followed for lead generation and conversion. etc. Other than that, they gave a case based question: Titan is planning to enter the audio devices segment. Do you think it should? why/ why not? Solve this using the Porter's five forces perspective.
situational_questions:
Did you face any failures/difficulties in your internship? How did you deal with them? 
What were your learnings from the internship?
What could you have done better?
What were some of your ideas/contributions? How did your manager react to those? What was the feedback? Were any of them implemented?
hr_gk_questions: Long term, short term goals? What do you expect from Titan? Why Titan?
looking_for: Strong basics. Good understanding of the fundamentals. Communication skills. Clarity of thought and speech.
right_wrong: I was calm during the interview, despite the flood of questions and cross questions. I could have answered the case based question in a more structured way.
tips: Being thorough with the minute details of the summer internship and preparing HR questions well helped me.
dos_and_donts: Start your preparation well in advance. Be thorough with the subject and practice TMAY and other HR questions. Try to practice a few mock interviews with your friends. Smile brightly and stay calm during the interview.

Once the facts were established, I followed a 5C approach for giving suggestions. At the end I summarized the entire case in 3-4 lines.

looking_for: Good communication skills, confidence and someone who has researched about Consulting and Accenture.

tips: The mock PI arranged by Prep Com was helpful. Introductory sessions were also helpful for the case analysis approach.

looking_for: Read the "What went wrong/right?" section
right_wrong:
I did not convert the interview. Here are the details - Coca-cola came with the operations role as part of their Mantra intern. There was no JD, no description in the email, no ppt. The official site of Coca-cola nowhere mentioned any details about this role. In previous years they had always offered the Sales and marketing role. When I went to give the interview, they asked me about the operations at Coca-cola. I talked about supply chain management, production, quality control etc. The interview then anchored around supply chain related case problems and other questions. 
After my interview (I was first), we all were informed that they were not here for supply chain or any traditional operation related role. For Coca-cola, operations means sales (yes, I had the same expression). So they were basically here for a sales role. I was immediately rejected from the interview, because according to HR I did not even know the role for the company I was interviewing for (which is true because there was no way I could have known).
tips: Nothing could have prepared me for this.
dos_and_donts: Read the JD! If there is no JD, and if there is even slight suspicion about what the role concerns, ask someone (Last resort, ask PC). Get your idea about the role very very clear.

pre_process_tips:
1. Technical Interview
2. Partner Call
3. HR Round
interview_outline:
Interview 1:
1. Tell us about yourself question
2. Resume based questions from my internships and academic projects
3. Asked why I want to become a consultant rather than an investment banker given a lot of quants and finance on my resume
4. Why should they hire me despite my not coming from a background in Energy sector
domain_questions: None since they were aware that I did not have a background in the industry
hr_gk_questions:
Why PWC India?
Why should we hire you?
looking_for:
1. Knowing what you have on your resume
2. Well structured answers
right_wrong:
I knew my resume thoroughly (came in handy since they were digging deep into it)
Had a variety of topics in the variant submitted and mentioned about the consulting preparation I had done (to showcase that I was actually interested in Consulting)
tips:
Well articulated answers (must for consulting roles)
Honesty about the things you don't know (It was 'Why hire you' in my case!)
Reasons you'll stay in this role for a long time to come
dos_and_donts:
1. Know very well the JDs, but you might get a shortlist despite you not matching the criteria. They are fully aware of it. Be willing to learn, it always helps.
2. Your style of answers should match the profile you have applied for. The way you frame your resume-based questions should also give a sense that you think and act like a consultant (eg: They liked that my answers were well articulated)

pre_process_tips:
Pre-process has an online psychometric test where they test basic behavioral skills, make sure you are consistent in your answers and think like an ideal employee 
Another part in the same pre-process where they see how you behave in certain scenarios
interview_outline:
Started with introduction, asked me why Amazon,then told he will be asking me situational questions based on leadership principles, but before that asked me 2 technical questions related to Amazon (not operations)
The questions asked where

-Third Party delivery carriers (e.g. Blue dart, Delhivery) vs Amazon In house delivery
-Challenges for the same
-How should amazon ensure the customer experience should be same irrespective of the delivery
hr_gk_questions:
Why Amazon? Why Operations role?

Situational Questions
-A situation where you didn't meet your goals
-A situation where you had fewer resources
-A situation where you exceeded targets and what were the challenges
-A SItuation where you had a conflict with a member at work
-A situation where you took a decision without asking a senior or manager
-A SItuation where you showed leadership skills
looking_for:
How you are a cultural fit and align with their leadership principles
Checking if you know deep about what youve done in the past
right_wrong: Keeping situations well prepared and thinking 2 minutes to frame my answer before answering
tips: Have a situation for each of the 14 principles, prepare situations and you can use the same answer for different HR questions
dos_and_donts: Deep dive your resume, Use STAR framework for answering your questions (Situation, Tasks, Actions taken, Results), Leadership principles

pre_process_tips: No pre-process, only resume shortlisting
no_interviews_duration: 2 rounds- One technical and one HR. Each PI lasted roughly for about 25 minutes
interview_outline: The first round was an HR interview. The HR wanted to know more about me, my learnings, facts about me other than those mentioned in the resume, and why I wanted to join Shopee. It was just like any typical HR interview- but more conversational and warm. The HR was constantly smiling and it made me feel comfortable while answering questions.
domain_questions: 2nd round was technical- I was asked about marketing and data analysis. I was also given two small case studies to solve that required the application of marketing and data analysis knowledge. I was constantly asked to deep dive into my answers- the interviewers seemed not to be satisfied with whatever I spoke!
hr_gk_questions: Why Shopee? Why marketing?
looking_for: Confidence, crisp articulation and good domain knowledge.
right_wrong:
I think my confidence while delivering answers and good grasp of S&M concepts helped me clear the interview.

The analysis of one of the case studies could have been more crisp and in-depth:  the interviewer told me which all areas and ideas I could have explored.
tips: Prepcom material, Mock PIs and being updated with all latest happenings related to the domain of interest( Shopee is an e-commerce company, so my knowledge related to ecommerce also helped me answer many technical questions)
dos_and_donts: Be thorough with NPADs and behavioural questions. No matter you know the answer or not, be confident! And never be afraid to say NO if you don't know the answer to any question- beating around the bush is even worse!

pre_process_tips: Application form- preference order between three roles.
interview_outline: First interview:- Started with introduction, then why marketing field, asked me about my branch from engineering. It was technical more on my branch as they were looking for interest in the manufacturing field. Asked me about preference between MNC and startup.
domain_questions:
New technological development in textile. Project and Internship related questions. 
I tried to explain with example as the interviewer might not understand the technical terms of the domain. He asked me to elaborate my process and asked questions from my answers.
hr_gk_questions:
1. Why do you want to join a startup: explained him startup's importance, the learnings it provides.
2. Where do you see yourself in the next 5 years: I explained him that i will work with this startup to make it into an MNC.

There were some basic questions related to my city, branch and why engineering.
They also asked me about my hobbies and interests and why they are unique.
looking_for: They were looking for an outgoing personality and someone who is eager to learn and face challenges.
right_wrong:
I was unaware of the fact that Ofbusiness just turned into a unicorn. 
But I accepted that i might have missed the news and showed interest when he was explaining about it. 
I converted it.
tips:
Know your resume in and out. The undergraduate branch is very important especially the projects and internships.
Some basic understanding of sales and marketing helped.
dos_and_donts: Don't be overconfident and don't be fake, they can see through it very easily.

pre_process_tips: Psychometric test and aptitude test
interview_outline: The interview started with an introduction. Questions were actually very random in nature. From picking questions within the resume including work exp, hobbies, projects etc, then the interview went into domain related questions.
domain_questions: Asked on the PLC of the Pulsar bike in India, questions on different stages of a sales and marketing cycle, ideate on introducing a new product in India, famous brand and why
hr_gk_questions: Mostly questions were asked on what was listed as hobbies in the resume and whatever was listed as extracurriculars.
looking_for: I think they were looking for an organizational fit very much. They also checked the depth in which we knew our work-ex and the projects in which we were a part of.
right_wrong: I think the good part was that I was able to communicate with my interviewer in a pleasing manner and by maintaining a confident tone all the time. He was also engrossed in the interview for the whole part of it which resulted in the conversion.
tips: I think knowledge on the company helped a lot. I went through some of the advertisement campaigns of the firm, the recent news of the company etc to help with my prep. I think these greatly aided in the interview process.
dos_and_donts: Maintaining a calm is a must. I think prior to the interview, one must take some time off and relax rather than overprepare. Most interviews go in a dynamic fashion and i think overprepping just before the interview only adds to the stress.

pre_process_tips: Aptitude Test, followed by GD and 2 interviews
gd_topics_tips: We were given a case during our aptitude test. The GD was based on our analysis of what we had written in the test. This was followed by individual questions pertaining to industries as well as some financial terms and models
interview_outline:
The first interview was HR based. It was just to gauge my interest in the role as well as my interest in the company.
The second interview was technical
The questions were about the DCFS and other valuation methods as well as questions about the impact of recession and inflation on macroeconomic factors etc. It ended with a puzzle
domain_questions: The questions mostly were about methods of valuation and didn't get too much into detail. I was just asked to loosely explain the model
hr_gk_questions: Questions about which role I preferred in the JD, my core competencies as well as some questions about the real estate sector since I had done internships in that industry
looking_for: They were looking for someone who was a self-starter and confident but at the same time was already quite well-versed in finance
right_wrong: My knowledge of finance was not as sharp as my peers and I was also informed to show up for the interview on very short notice which may have given me the nerves due to which I could not think clearly. I didn't clear the interview
tips: Prepare well and be so well prepared to be able to give an interview even 30 minutes after waking up
dos_and_donts: N.A.

pre_process_tips: The pre-process involved applying the role on the company portal, following which 2 rounds of buddy calls were conducted. The telephonic rounds we done to check fit for the role and basics of finance such as ratios were asked.
interview_outline:
The interview began with a basic introduction. I was questioned on why the role and why finance. Later, every point on the resume was discussed. I was asked to give a detailed explanation on my academic projects since they were related to the role. I was also given a small puzzle to solve. 
Since, I had relevant project work I was asked a lot of technical questions on machine learning model and how they worked.
looking_for: They are looking for candidates who are interested in the role and display an inquisitive front. You should be willing to learn even if you are new to the domain. Candidates were expected to show their interest in the role during the interviews. Good preparation and communication skills were also expected.
right_wrong:
What went right - I displayed a confident front and was able to convince them of my interest in finance and how the particular role interested me over the other roles offered. I was able to link my interests and my project experiences with the role offered. 
Result - Converted
tips: Finance Starter deck. The mock PI helped me understand where I lacked in terms of explaining the contents of my resume. I was able to prepare and explain my resume pointers better post the mock PI.

pre_process_tips: The first step of the process was a screening test with 4 sections; Quant, English, Financial Ratios and Marketability, at the end of which 80 people were selected for further rounds. Next, there was a workshop on different Financial Account Statements and a bit of Firm Value and Valuation. The workshop was evaluative and followed by a quiz on the contents 0f the workshop. Finally 30 people were selected for the interviews.
no_interviews_duration: 3 (First Interview- 15 mins, Second (HR) Interview- 15 mins, Third (Technical) Interview-20-25 mins)
interview_outline:
First Round-
Started with an introduction, went into resume details, questions about the company. Mainly the questions revolved around the role and the company. They wanted to know whether I was really interested in the firm and the role.
Second Round-
Started with my strengths and weaknesses but was basically around my interests and turned into a discussion on our favourite novel series.
Third Round-
Was split into two parts; the first part was more technical and based on the content of the workshop, and the second part was mental maths. Technical questions included questions on firm value, conglomerate discount etc, while the mental maths questions were basic quant stuff.
domain_questions: Answered above
hr_gk_questions: Answered above
looking_for: I believe the team came here for a person with more of an academic background, and since has taken 3-4 freshers' work-ex was not a decision criterion.
right_wrong: Converted. I think the most important part was looking confident even when you were not.
tips: I read the Finance PPT of PrepCom before the workshop and that helped me a lot with my participation in the workshop.

pre_process_tips: Shortlist was based on Resume
no_interviews_duration: Two Interviews. One Technical and One HR (20 min each)
interview_outline:
Started with introduction. Prepare this part extremely well the interview will be driven by this. Try to include numbers if possible. Asked me about the impact of Saudi Arabia in manipulating football( my interest was football). Guesstimate and talked about atomberg a bit.

The HR interview was more Npad based. Try to provide as many examples as possible and relate with your life. Be honest.
domain_questions: Do you know what atomberg does. What can be the problems faced by our suppliers at the ground level.  Try to think on your feet and again give honest answers. I had gone through the websit so I knew some things.
hr_gk_questions: Do you think you will be able to work continuously in the field as a salesperson. Told them I won't be able to that I wanted to learn in different verticals and not just stick to SnM.
looking_for: They were looking for a practical and genuine person who could think on their feet. I faced lost of issues during the interview like net connectivity or background noises. I asked them multiple times to excuse me so that I can change my position and things. Yet that didn't affect my interview
right_wrong: I had prepared introduce yourself extremely well. I feel that is the most crucial part of the interview
tips:
It's important to give the GD/PIs organised by prep com. I would also suggest you to conduct your own interviews with your friends once u get the specific shortlist
All the best

pre_process_tips: Form filling (Basic stuff) followed by direct interview.

2. Background (UG)
3. Workex (In depth)
4. Domain related

Questions around steel industry like-

HR-
1. What qualities do think a manager must have.

right_wrong: What went right was having an explanation to all the CV points mentioned.

tech_skills: Finance and Accounting questions given my background.

pre_process_tips: None - extremely relevant profile based shortlist
no_interviews_duration: 2. Interview was of 2 parts. Technical and Hr. 40,30 min respectively
interview_outline: It was balanced.
domain_questions: Many domain specific questions were asked. Mostly about product management.
situational_questions: HR interview was completely based up on behavioural aspects. Main focus was up on strengths and its coherence with the role offered.
hr_gk_questions: Current affairs were asked mostly about popular global affairs and technology. I was asked about the role model and Why was he/she my role model etc.
looking_for: They were looking for relevance and were keen on finding whether i was very much interested in the company and role in particular. I had 2 product management certifications and my summer intern was at NPCI in prod man role. So I builded up on it and have shown my interests and shared many experiences.
right_wrong: I should say that nothing went wrong in the interview. I was very much confident while answering and wasn’t nervous even a bit. And   I cleared the interview.

dos_and_donts: Just don’t be nervous. Be confident with the answers. Never fumble while answering, no one like it, it shows that u might be lying or extremely nervous which is implies that u aren’t fit to be a manger. Just be confident with whatever you have and don’t compare with ur peers.

pre_process_tips: Application form- Had to fill a google form with generic details.

interview_outline:
Tell me about yourself.
Tell about internship and work experience, the projects i have been part of.
Any hobbies.

Profitability case- generic wanted to know heads that would affect the revenue and cost side.

Right-

Practice Case Frameworks extensively. 
Ask relevant questions.

pre_process_tips:
Pre-process:1.5 hours Aptitude test
Verbal, Logical, Quant,
interview_outline: Started with resume introduction and cross questioning on details from my resume. Most questions were HR based, like challenges faced and lessons from previous internships. One question about prevalence of data and how can we use that, relating to a project i had taken up. One question on how I would fit well in the company and expectations from the internship.
domain_questions: One company related question on 'why RIL'. I connected company values to my personal values, saying these are the reason why I think I would fit well in the company. I mentioned my internship and course as an advantage which makes me better suitable for the role.
hr_gk_questions:
HR questions based on my resume, How was your experience leading a team, what challenges did you face during that time. I 
explain a little about my experience and what different problems I managed with my team.
2.What does positive reinforcement(in giving feedback) mean to you? I explained how I believe constructive feedback should be given along with positive appraisal so that the person doesn't feel dejected rather motivated to correct their mistakes.
looking_for: Working well with a team, ability to learn from challenges, company knowledge, previous responsibility positions were a good talking point.
right_wrong: The HR questions were good, i could manage to relatenmy experiences and answer. A few questions about my resume I could have elaborated in better manner.(Converted the interview)
tips: Company Deck and GenMan FAQs were helpful in quick preparation for the interview.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlisting for 2 rounds of interviews
gd_topics_tips: No
interview_outline: Both interviews were technical, started with small caselets of how can zomato go about increasing the average order value, what steps can be taken, more of a conversational aspect
domain_questions:
Both rounds were technical, based on cases, growth in round 1 and market entry in round 2. For round 2 there whole interview was on "How can we launch online ordering in Jammu", Jammu being the place I come from. 
It started with a rough estimation of how zomato can collate data on restaurants, not by an on ground fleet of people but by collating data from resturatns, the hyperpure vertical, pan india restuarant dataset. 
It then went on for a guesstimate of how many riders would be needed for the operaion, which started with an order number of 20,000 for the first month, giving is 220 odd riders. '
I had corrections in my number which the interviewer gladly accomodated.
The interview then ended with a couple of questions I had for them, viz, How much exposure would I have with the CEO amd towads the clients.
hr_gk_questions: NO
looking_for: A maverick, as their JD mentioned. A problem solver, who can analyze a problem. My cv was POR heavy , with a lot of experiences during my UG years in terms if different events.
right_wrong: I converted the interview. Answering the questions, showcasing my analytical skills, communication skills and a cultural fit were the things that worked for me.
tips: Prepcom PPt and mercuri compedium

pre_process_tips: Apply in the Placement Portal. Need to give preference in the given profiles. After the resume shortlist, Personal interviews happened
no_interviews_duration: 4, ( 3 Technical Interview, 1 HR) First 3 are eliminative rounds ( 45 minutes to 1.25 hours). 4th round - 10 minutes.
interview_outline:
The first two rounds were done in phases on different days. After every round, there will be an elimination and subsequent rounds were carried out. 40-45 minutes were Resume  basedin each round and followed by a case/guesstimate. 
Every round some default questions like
Why consulting?
Why Ops consulting?
Why PwC and why not Amazon, Flipkart?
What you know about PwC and role?
How PwC will help in achieving your goal?
domain_questions: Inventory Management, Production methods - All were from internships or work. What did you do in the project and why? Is it possible to do the same in all industries?
situational_questions: No situational based question
hr_gk_questions: HR round was not an elimination round. Just casual conversation. All three rounds has some HR questions as well.
looking_for: Confidence, Communication, Logical approach in all answers not only with cases. I have conveyed the ops part from my internship and Work Experience. They did not expect you to say right answers for all the questions. I made many mistakes, and the partner explained the concept.
right_wrong: Explaining in detail all the concepts. My confidence and thinking before each answers.
tips: Be confident with your resume. What to say and not to say? Be thorough with subjects as well. Even though, questions would be basic, you will be very confident during an interview.
dos_and_donts: Read about the company. What are some recent works. What are they basically into.

pre_process_tips:
Video Interview on Talview. Basic HR and situational based questions- 
Tell me about yourself, Why cognizant,
A time where you had take in different perspectives to come up with a solution,
How a negative behavior of your teammate impacted your productivity,
Describe a situation where you had resolve a conflict, 
Describe a situation where you has to complete a task without taking feedback or submitting reports
interview_outline: Started with "Tell me about yourself" and delved deep into resume. A well balanced interview with a mix of technical and HR questions
domain_questions:
Softwares/Languages worked on during work ex.
My approach was to tell them about the task at hand, software used and what impact had been created by using that particular software.

As for the internship, my approach was to tell them about the sector in brief, the task assigned and my approach for work for accomplishing the task and creating an impact
hr_gk_questions:
Why cognizant? How do you align yourself with this role? ( Aligned my answers with the culture and values of the organization )
Any location constraint? 
How do you explain conflict and collaboration? ( Defined what both the terms mean to me and substantiated with an example)
looking_for: Someone who is confident, knows his/her resume in and out
right_wrong:
Right - Could create a story of my strengths

Wrong - Nothing as such
tips: Knowing your resume well. Prepcomm material and regular practice makes you frame your answers well during the interview
dos_and_donts: Staying calm and drive the interview towards your strengths

pre_process_tips: Application form followed by Aptitude test
gd_topics_tips: AI in beer brewing- The panel specified no brownie points for starting or concluding the GD. many candidates came up with innovative points. Align the points with the working style and role offered by the company that you're interviewing for. panel looked for unique points, it wasn't important to give too many points but to give appropriate points.
interview_outline: Introduction, Why this company, if given an opportunity would you like to work in Finance team, operations question,  It was a balanced interview.
domain_questions: What things do you know about finance or accounting because both the panelist were working in finance team. hr_gk_questions: why not automobiles because I'm from Nagpur city which has many automobile companies, why not PepsiCo or fmcg because I have a chemical background. Gave me two minutes to convince them that why should they select me .
looking_for: Confidence and broad knowledge of every domain.
right_wrong: I knew about the company very well and I took the interview in my direction of knowledge. Could have answered the HR questions and domain specific questions better. Converted the interview
tips: NPAD, prepcomm material and mock GD helped me a lot.
dos_and_donts: Very open to every opportunity they offer during the interview and just be confident in whatever you answer. Have certain knowledge of every domain like finance, marketing,etc.

pre_process_tips: Resume Based Shortlist
gd_topics_tips:
Can AI replace the humans entirely 
( There was no elimination here, some weightage was given for this round)

pre_process_tips: Application form, applying on reculta, skills interview and HR and M/D interview
no_interviews_duration: 2 interview. 1st of around 20 min. 2nd was of 40 mins
interview_outline:
The first interview started with introduction, next went into internships. He was particularly interested in one of my internship and we had a long discussion on that. Then a case analysis and interpretation. Then current affairs and question if I had any to  ask them.

Second interview started with HR question, and case analysis(M/D round).
domain_questions: I was asked lots of questions from my internship that was based on building an end to end B2B Cloud Application. I just explained my internship in as much brief as possible. Told how and what concepts we worked on. Also mentioned the technical tools that I had used and the purpose of the project itself.
hr_gk_questions:
HR questions
I was asked questions related to how was the first interview. I was asked to give feedbacks to the first interviewer. And also why I want to be in Consulting. Why this firm is suitable for me. What do I expect out of it.
looking_for: They were looking for someone who has full knowledge of  AI and ML. Since I being a CS engineer and having 3 internships and 3 academic projects on that itself, I guess I was a good candidate
right_wrong: Yes I converted the interview. Good parts of the interview was that I was frequently asking question to clarify myself. So the interviewer was able to understand my thoughts.
tips: Be thorough with your resume
dos_and_donts: Do read about the company a bit

gd_topics_tips: Tinder Vs Jeevansathi
interview_outline: I believe the line of questioning will be entirely based on where your prior experience lies and what you have mentioned on the resume. The description mentioned is given the fact that I had mentioned a lot of research work in the marketing domain and performance marketing work.
domain_questions:
Interview 1: Introduction, why marketing, explanation of research papers, in-depth explanation of internships, case on bisleri- if there are fake competitors cropping up, what kind of losses will the company face and as a marketing manager, how will you deal with it, which company under InfoEdge's portfolio would you like to work under, a brief about the performance marketing work done
Interview 2: Introduction, heavy grilling on performance marketing work done and related internships and results, performance marketing metrics- their formulae and meanings, a numerical based on calculation of CTR, CTA and CTC, grilling on Principles of Management academic project- individual contribution and application of Porter's Five Forces in the company that the case was based on

They don't expect you to know everything and won't penalise you for wrong answers, they would rather appreciate sincere efforts in answering the questions and whether you are able to justify the knowledge and skills mentioned on the resume.

dos_and_donts: Have thorough knowledge about whatever you mention in the resume

pre_process_tips: Registration on PWC US portal and google form

Introduction
Resume based questions
Small case
Questions for the interviewer

Introduction
NPAD questions
Puzzle
Questions for the interviewer

NPAD questions. I followed the suggestions given by NPAD iterator and had prepared well for the questions. The interviewer seemed satisfied with my answers.

The best way to tackle this round is to work on your NPAD as extensively as possible, as all the possible questions are covered here. In my HR round - after my introduction, we had a discussion on long-term and short-term goals, how I handle tight deadlines and how I see myself after 10 years. The interview ended with my knowledge of EV sector and how OLA is performing.
looking_for: They were looking for a person, well informed about his work-ex and have a structured thought process and good communication skills.
right_wrong: Guesstimate went well, I managed to take care of minute details. Moreover, research on EV sector helped a lot.   --Converted
tips: NPAD is the best resource to prepare for HR round. Please work on the feedback given in MOCK GD/PI.
dos_and_donts: Be confident even when things are not going well in the interview.

pre_process_tips:
1. You dont even apply to it. Your resumes are sent before they are freezed on Reculta. 
2. You will get a mail from PlaceCom once you are shortlisted.
3. Post that, you will be assigned a buddy (Senior Associate) and a mentor (Consultant) to help you in preparing for and solving cases. 
4. You will then have a workshop with other BCG IIM Indore Alums who will give tips on how to solve a case and demonstrate solving a live case. Post that you will have 2 mock cases with different buddies and mentors. Make sure you perform well in these.
5. Then, you will have a Networking dinner where you interact with other people and alums. Make sure that they remember your name when you talk to them,
6. Finally, the most important part - Case Interview. 2/3/4 rounds of Cases over 2 days with Project Leader on the first day and then with Principal/MDP

domain_questions: Nothing as such - just the case.
hr_gk_questions: Nothing as such - just the case.

tips: Casebooks of IIM A, FMS and ISB

interview_outline:

pre_process_tips: Applied on reculta, there were 2 telephonic interviews, introductory HR interviews first with a senior from IIM Indore working in DB, second with a senior manager. Try to ask a lot of questions about the work, the role it shows where your interest lies. They will ask for your interest in CB in the first call, if you show your interest then only you will get second call. Both calls were evaluated.
no_interviews_duration: Total 3 interviews, 2 taken by senior managers and 1 by the HR. Interviewers ask basic HR type questions, nothing about finance. But more about how your past will help you in the role. Try to convince them that you are good enough for this role.
interview_outline: HR heavy interview. Started with Introduction, background, why CB, Why DB. They asked me about cricket as I have played it at district level. It was purely HR based. In the second interview I solely had to convince the interviewer why I want this particular role.
domain_questions: They asked me about my academic projects. That's it
hr_gk_questions: Asked a lot about past experiences. how I was able to crack CAT without coaching etc.
looking_for: They were looking for enthusiasm while talking, you should be able to have a good talk with them throughout the interview. They aren't looking for core finance knowledge. Tell them everything that you have done in Mba in UG, how it has helped you to become the person that you are.
right_wrong: I come from a small town, they were shocked when they got to know that I cracked CAT without coaching, even when I come from a small town.
tips: Prepare HR questions by heart
dos_and_donts: Be yourself, be enthusiastic, keep smiling throughout the interview.

pre_process_tips: Filled the application form, 1 round of HR/Resume based interviews followed by a report-writing

right_wrong: General Awareness, NPAD questions and Genuine interest in the role worked in my favour. Could have written the report better.

dos_and_donts: Give your best in each of the tasks assigned(it was report-writing in my case).

pre_process_tips: Resume based, personal interviews. Be thorough with resume.

hr_gk_questions: Was asked about conflict situations I had faced and my resolution. If Manager was non-cooperative or did not accommodate my views how would I deal with it? If I couldn't deliver a project on time, what steps would I take and how would I communicate communicate the client? In every case I followed the STAR approach and substantiated with a story.
looking_for: They were looking for people skills and how well I could hold a conversation. This could be a way to judge the way I communicate. Secondly they judged the approaches I took to solve the guesstimate and case.
right_wrong: The good parts were that I was thorough about my resume and my work experience details. I was also prepared with the consulting interview scenarios therefor I had a fair idea how to approach the problems. What went wrong was that in the case interview in round 2, I should have exhausted the number of clarifying questions to get a clear picture before I dove into the solution.

dos_and_donts: Prepare for the consulting case interview by practicing with people.

pre_process_tips: Resume based shortlisting
no_interviews_duration: 2 interviews - 1st Interview of 30 min duration & 2nd interview of 10 min
interview_outline: The interviewer asked about summer internship in detail. The questions were how did you convince the management for your idea, how did you implement your idea, etc. Then he asked about work experience in detail. Questions were what was your role, what work did you do, which computer language have you worked on, who were your clients, etc. He asked if you can build a product from scratch. How will you understand the requirements when the customer can't convey it clearly? Why should a client listen to you when you have no experience in his field? How would you convey the value proposition?

How will you convince an architect to listen to your idea even if you have no experience in his field? Suppose a paper factory is facing the issue of discolouration of paper, how will you solve this problem?
looking_for: People who can understand requirements well and have some technical knowledge. They wanted people who can get the work done.
right_wrong: I had summer internship in product management. This helped me in answering questions related to building products.
tips: Be thorough with your resume. Mock interviews helped in that. For product management preparation, I referred  mock interview videos in YouTube. Although no case was asked in the interview, case preparation helped in answering situational questions.
