pre_process_tips: Aptitude test - Verbal ability, Data interpretation and Quant
interview_outline: It started with an introduction then went into the company and role-related questions like why BCN, why consulting etc and finally 2 guesstimates.
domain_questions:
1. Why BCN?
2. Why Consulting?
3. Why incubation? ( I was shortlisted for Incubation CoE)

Go through the company profile. Prepare an answer for why consulting and why the specific CoE (Listen to the pre-placement talk). For case study or guesstimate they are looking for a Structured approach, strong analytics and good communication skills.

Guesstimate questions
1. Number of band-aids sold in India in 1 year. 
2. Apple is launching a new phone (cost 1.2 lakh) in India. Estimate the number of phones that will be sold in the next 2 months.

I took the top-down approach for both guesstimates. Started with the total population and then went down to get an approximate number. 
For band-aids:- Population - gender - rural/urban - age - the type of work (physical or other types)... etc.
Took the similar approach for 2nd guesstimate too
hr_gk_questions: Some Resume related questions
looking_for:
Structured approach 
Strong analytical skills
Good communication
right_wrong:
Good:- 
- a good structure for the guesstimates
- Communication
- The final answer

Bad:-
- could have researched more about the company
- HR questions

pre_process_tips: Three step process. First step had basic questions. Second step had locations preference type questions. Third step was video interview round. You had to record yourself in response to the questions that were displayed. Three questions were there for this round.

interview_outline: Resume and HR based. Definitely know why you want to do sales. And basics of sales and marketing. Know your resume word by word. There were 6 people in the room.
domain_questions: Difference between sales and marketing. Why sales. What parameters are important for social media platform selection. Gave the definitions and real life examples. Gave in detail explainations. Other questions related to marketing. One case based question, very short.

looking_for: Genuine, fun and energetic people. I am a fresher, no additional certificates. Just did an online certificate on digital marketing.
right_wrong: Converted. I think don't take it as a quiz where you are just answering questions. Try to engage them. Humor them. Keep smiling.

pre_process_tips:
The first process is a google form majorly based on NPAD questions. Stay true to yourself here.
The next round is online video submission. 3 questions relating to the company( its brands and apps) and general marketing strategies were asked. You will be given some time to think about it, after which you have to record the answer. You will have only one chance to record the answers. 
The final process will be the interview.

Questions were based on the answers of 2nd preprocess (video submission). No HR questions asked. Strong knowledge about each and every brand of the company is essential.
Questions related to marketing strategies, wherein you will have to use models like STP/ 5P, were also covered.
domain_questions:
Situation based question which generally involves:
Strategy to introduce a new product to the market- use marketing model, structure the answer.
Importance of branding, branding strategies, business and consumer impact of the same.
hr_gk_questions: No HR questions/ current affairs was asked.
looking_for: Have a good idea about marketing and branding strategies. Deep knowledge about the company and its brands.
right_wrong:
Yes, converted.
The answers to questions regarding marketing strategies needs to be very structured and well backed up. Rather than the rightness/ feasibility the focus should be more on the logic and the thought process for your pitch.
tips: The industry reports and company deck sent by Prepcomm,  and the HUL website.

no_interviews_duration: Three rounds of interview of 30-45 mins each

domain_questions: Case specific question
situational_questions: Every single pointer from the resume, specially the academic projects and POR points
hr_gk_questions: In the last round, I was asked to play a game where first I had to ask 10 questions to the interviewer and then the interviewer would ask me 10 questions. I went for very honest personal and professional questions such as lowest point of his life, what makes him want to wake up everyday and work, if he could give a piece of advice to his 23 year self who is sitting on the opposite side of the table what advice would he give and so on.

Bad: Initial jitters in the first interview, not being prepared for why SCMO as I did not apply for it but they allocated it directly to me

General questions from marketing & sales - usual frameworks and how they can be implemented on fashion brands.

What do you want to do in life?
Why arvind fashions?

pre_process_tips: No Pre-process
interview_outline:
It was a group selection process. All the applicants were put in a single zoom room for further processes. 
In the first round, the applicants were asked to introduce themselves to the whole room in an innovative and unique way, while also answering some basic questions given by the interviewer. Applicants who were selected advanced to further rounds while the rest were asked to leave the zoom call.
In the second round, applicants were asked to choose any company of their own choice, and were asked to explain how the marketing strategy of the company can be changed all over India to make further profits. Some counter questions were also asked by the interviewers to some of the interviewees. Again, the applicants who were not selected were asked to leave the call.
In the third round, the remaining applicants were asked why they should they be selected and what strengths they have. An additional interviewer also took a kind of stress test of the applicants.
looking_for: They were looking for confident, innovative individuals who stood out from the crowd.
right_wrong:
Confidence was key in the interview, and only those who were not afraid of speaking to a room full of other people progressed.
I converted the interview, as I believe i was able to stand out from the rest.
tips: The mock GI/PI were extremely beneficial.

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlisting followed by Aptitude test. The test consisted of VARC and DI basaed questions. Not very easy, not very difficult.
interview_outline: The interviewer was the head of the Incubation CoE. He introduced himself and then asked me to introduce myself. He went on to ask questions about my hometown and current location. Then asked questions on my WorkEx which was based on Analytics and Summer Internship. Then he gave me a guesstimate (No of band aids used in India in a year). Asked all the clarifying questions and laid down my approach and arrived at the number. right_wrong: I tried to maintain a good friendly vibe which was possible due to the friendly nature of the interviewer. Laid down my approach and justified every number before proceeding to solve it.

dos_and_donts: Even if you know the entire solution of the guesstimate or case, don't solve it alone. Keep communicating and solve together.

role_offered: Retail Lending- Wealth and personal banking

I could make only 2 entries but made sure to make distinctive points and not the general ones

domain_questions: Qs related to revenue generation by credit card companies and what factors are looked while lending to an individual.
hr_gk_questions: Some current affairs relating to banking sector
looking_for: They were looking for willingness to learn and contribute and in general overall knowledge about banking sector
right_wrong: Confidence was they key. I could not answer all the Qs but i made them sure that i am a good learner

pre_process_tips: Applying on a separate portal ( provided by HDFC) with all the relevant details of previous academics and work experience (if any)

needed to be thorough with the FAC curriculum.
domain_questions: Questions based on the different financial statements and how they are different from each other, what to interpret from each of the statements. Also gave a simple exercise to test the understanding.
hr_gk_questions: Questions based on my work experience. I had 4 years of experience in the power sector and hence  there were questions about my job and responsibilities. It is recommended to know your responsibilities thoroughly and not get into too much technicalities while explaining the role.
looking_for: Probably they were looking for someone with diligence and interest in finance.
right_wrong: I felt being able to answer the questions based on the FAC course helped. However I felt I could have done better on the self introduction and "walk us through your resume" question. Finally converted the interview.
tips: Being thorough with the FAC course helped the most for this interview.
dos_and_donts: Definitely know about the role you're interviewing for.

What does a product manager do?

Guesstimates for number of casinos (playing cards was given as interest in the resume as well as spoken in the introduction) & calculating number of mails circulating in the campus in a given week. Mock PI: be thorough with NPAD

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlist - buddy round - workshop- two interview round

domain_questions: 2 case questions : 1. About food processing industry - a company like blinkit has been facing increased wastages in fruits and vegetables. Approach: 3CP, duration. Wrote down the supply chain of a food processing industry. Asked to analyse storage and warehousing. Possible problems were divided as : labour, machine, and other factors. Labour : chain of steps. Issue with inventory : Lifo / fifo problem. 2nd case question : guesstimate the fire extinguisher market in india. Approach : rural/urban - household/commercial- col further divided and estimated
looking_for: - good preliminary questions - communication skills - confidence - ability to handle numbers
right_wrong: good parts : preliminary questions , turned the interview into a conversation and kept my calm . Bad parts : more out of the box thinking and quicker calculation. Yes, converted the interview

dos_and_donts: Practicing cases with peers was the most important part because often our questions are understood in ways different than how we have asked. Case practice helped me understand how to frame my questions to ensure MECE always.

Good : interviewers were very encouraging and responsive to my answers.

Round 3 - HR based. Offer was announced in the interview itself.

current affairs - as in general awareness who are the competitors or substitute of the product application discussed by me during case based interviews.
Why product management?
Why PharmEasy?

pre_process_tips: CV shortlisting, PI (case interviews)
interview_outline: Introduction followed by case interview for both rounds.
domain_questions:
Two rounds of case interviews:
1. Unconventional: Your client is DC movies and sitting in 2008, they want to analyse whether they should continue with the Batman franchise after the release of The Dark Knight. Find the Brand value of Batman and help the client in deciding.
2. Profitability and growth: Your client is a steel player with EBITDA margins lower than industry benchmark, how should they improve their position

Follow a structured approach, ask good preliminary questions, be in constant conversation with panelists.
hr_gk_questions: About myself and my internship. Generally in MBB interviews, HR questions are icebreakers, case interviews are primarily evaluative. So be interactive and conversational. It should feel like two people discussing rather than an interview.
looking_for: Problem solving skills, effective communication, structured thinking.
right_wrong:
Bad : Lacked structured approach in first interview as the case question was a bit unconventional, so it's important to keep calm and proceed with confidence.
Good : Never lost confidence, course corrected as per interviewer's inputs.
tips: Consulting Primers, Casebooks by IIM A, FMS, IIM Indore. Sessions by Consulting Club and PrepCom.
dos_and_donts: Consulting preparation specially for MBB, Kearney etc is all about practicing cases and analysing them. Practice atleast 1 case daily for the 3-4 weeks window between shortlist and interview.

pre_process_tips: Filled a form and submitted resume on their portal.
interview_outline: Started with a brief introduction. Many HR questions were asked in both the rounds. Questions related to work ex were asked in 1st round. Questions were also asked to check my understanding of trends in BlockChain, Crypto, Cybersecurity etc. The questions were not very technical but they expected the candidate to have a basic understanding. Ended both my interviews by asking questions about the role and company.
domain_questions: Questions about company's CSR activities were asked. I went through their website an hour before the interview and that was sufficient research.

looking_for: Gauging the way of our thinking ability more than knowledge. Hints were provided in the interview in excess to know how we think and handle situations. Technical knowledge of whatever work is there on resume.
right_wrong: Handle the stress better. Do not let way for interviewer's expression demotivate you

dos_and_donts: Trust in yourself!!

pre_process_tips:
Only application form.
There was a workshop relating to financial statements, ratio analysis and valuation. Post which a test was taken on what was taught there.
interview_outline: Started with introduction and covered a little about the resume. Picked a topic from the resume and discussion started with that. Mental maths questions. Questions about company like ceo, headquarters location.
domain_questions: Mergers and acquisitions (because mentioned in resume).  Questions on stock market like value of sensex, any recent ipos. Valuation dcf questions and also questions from what was taught in the workshop.
hr_gk_questions: Why jpmc and why this role. Why mba. And otherwise it was a general conversation.
looking_for: Willingness to learn , attention to detail and quick thinking.
right_wrong:
They had asked mental maths questions and on one question I was unable to provide the correct answer however I explained my approach to the question and that was exactly what they were expecting. I was also well prepared with the topics mentioned in my resume. 
Result - Converted

dos_and_donts: For the workshop, remember to take as much detailed notes as possible because the test was based on that only and you could refer to those notes. Try to participate as much possible.

pre_process_tips:
Online GD (topic -memes are a legitimate form of art)
Interview - given a printed one pager case to solve in under 7-8 mins, later asked to formally present the solution to a panel, simulating a client meeting. Later asked to solve a riddle/ mini case verbally which was about FMCG industry.
Also briefly asked about work ex.
gd_topics_tips: Memes are a legitimate form of art
interview_outline: Case solution presentation (on the spot, verbally)

FMCG mini case/riddle

Work ex
Hobby - books - which book - why do you like it
looking_for:
Being able to articulate and present the solution in a succinct and impactful way, clarity of thought, structured way of solving the problem.
 Riddle/mini case to test on the spot velocity of thought (right direction and eventually right answer)
Soft skills for client presentations
right_wrong:
Impactful case solution presentation.
Having clarity and faith on the solution you’re presenting.
tips:
Confidence
Clear and well articulated thinking
dos_and_donts:
Accept when you don’t know the approach or nudge for a hint at the right time.
Be clear and confident about your approach

pre_process_tips:
Applying on Reculta
Online video submission
PI

hr_gk_questions: Questions on sports related current affairs like Olympics and IPL

right_wrong:
Goods- clear about marketing basics and was aware about current affairs, good conversation for the entire PI
Bad- Nothing as i was selected

pre_process_tips: Amex had a CV shortlisted round, an online test and 2 rounds of interview
interview_outline: TMAY. Then, it began with basic introduction and understanding of functioning of American Express card. They asked about how its income statement and balance sheets will look like. Why join Amex? How do you handle conflicts? Tell me about your weaknesses. Some cross questioning on PORs. What do you like and not like about IIM Indore? Why MBA?

Balance Sheets of Amex - which would be the major current assets and current liabilities in a credit card company.
Financial ratios
hr_gk_questions:
Tariff and AI effects on economy as whole.
TMAY
Weaknesses and strengths 
Why MBA? 
Where do you see yourself 5 years down the line?
looking_for: A person whom they can work with ease. A person who has understanding of how systems work and would be willing to learn and grow in the system.
right_wrong: Being amicable, honest and humble was the key
tips: Practicing domain interviews and specifically your HR questions
dos_and_donts: Don't lie or project yourself as a person with no fault. Be honest (as much as possible)
additional_remarks: Understanding a company's functioning shows intent of joining, do not miss on that.

pre_process_tips: Application form, Aptitude test then shortlisted candidates received behavioural test
gd_topics_tips: Case based GD relating to a sales issue, case was given one day before the GD, in the gd, each candidate was asked to give opening statement of about 1 minute on the case and then discussion was started, they appreciated peaceful discussion and points in which needs of different stakeholders were mentioned.
interview_outline: In the interview they had a pitch round for which scenario was given, we had to make a ppt and then give a sales pitch to the panel. After the pitch they asked few questions based on resume and some HR questions to check the culture fit.
prep_resources: Deep research about the company and its projects
looking_for: Good communication and convincing skills as it was a sales role
right_wrong: In the pitch round I was mostly giving the presentation about the company and what it is doing, instead the focus should be on convincing the client why they should buy the apartment and how it will fulfill their needs and demands.
tips: They liked interactive interview, having good communication skills and confidence would really help.
dos_and_donts: Be confident and ask questions to the interviewer in case of any doubt, don’t just assume anything.

pre_process_tips: Aptitude Test (Accounts, Maths, DI LR, English)
interview_outline:
Round 1 (Introduction, Resume Based, Generic Questions about your interests and job profile, HR heavy)
Round 2 (HR, Weird Random questions like most relatable animal, definition of failure, adverse situations)
domain_questions:
Why State Street? 
Most interesting part?
Difference between B2B and B2C marketing?
Which company is doing good in using Analytics?

tips:

Asking relevant questions

pre_process_tips: Application Form(Personal details+SOP) followed by a video submission(HR based)
interview_outline:
Resume based interview. 
1. Walk me through your resume?
2. Why do you want to enter an IT domain after having a non tech background?
3. Questions on electives (Concepts of Pricing and revenue management, Strategy management)
4. What skills from your MBA and graduation helped while working for the MP Govt (live project)
5. Walk me through the responsibilities of Infrastructure committee(Explained how responsibilities of Infra revolves around IT) 
6.Asked to explain the POR (Infrastructure committee, Enactus) , questions about Quora.
Be thorough with your resume.
domain_questions:
Not very technical heavy but was asked about how my profile aligned with the role that I was offered. Questions on certification.
Read JD properly.
situational_questions:
Question on how you handled a conflict in your internship, how WFH impacted your internship.
Rather than giving a straight answer focus more on what you learned from these experiences and how it had an impact on you.
hr_gk_questions: Why Cognizant? (Be thorough about the company and its latest projects)
looking_for: Confidence. They were looking for fit more than anything.
right_wrong: Was thorough with the resume. Be very confident in how you handle questions.(Converted)
tips: Read preparatory material for IT and Product Management.

pre_process_tips: Buddy and mentor just help prepare for cases - said to be evaluative, but it is not an "evaluation round" as such. You can seek any advice or help regarding preparation from them
interview_outline: Started with a quick introduction, asked to walk them through resume or give a brief introduction, asked about work-ex overview and what the company does and then started off with the case.
looking_for: Structured thought process, clarity about work-ex, good communication
right_wrong: Interview was highly conversational, case analysis was handled well and asked a lot of questions about the company and its values as well as the interviewer's personal experience. Could have handled some parts of the cases better - got stuck into one line of thought; helps to keep an open mind and be prepared to think on your feet.
tips: Mock GD/PIs boosted my confidence. IIMA casebook helped me the most in terms of preparatory material for case solving. Practicing with friends and more importantly structuring unconventional cases added maximum value during the prep.
dos_and_donts: Do not take a break - momentum loss impacts the prep majorly. Do not give up during case practice, even if the case is extremely challenging go through with it, and seek wholistic feedback.

pre_process_tips: No tests, CV shortlist
gd_topics_tips: Ethical Case based GD. Should a plastic making company continue with it or move to sustainable alternatives which may cause them to fire multiple people
interview_outline: First introduction, moved to CV started discussing about interests, deep dive into workex then work done during college, extracurriculars, all cv points was covered, also serious NPAD questions. Very balanced.
domain_questions: Question about work ex which was IT domain. Team and situations handling question. Balanced NPAD and technical details about software development processes like Agile and waterfall.
hr_gk_questions: No current affairs. Situation based questions like if a team member is not contributing and how would you handle it. Followed a structured way of answering what is the issue and what I would do and why.
looking_for: They were looking for someone who can keep calm under stress and knows the work ex domain very well. Good idea about the company and the profile one is applying to is a must.
right_wrong: Mostly deep diving into CV caused me to falter in answering some questions based on my hobbies and why I enjoyed them. But they we're good enough to let it go
tips: PrepComm decks of previous years interview experiences. And NPAD questions was the Bible

pre_process_tips: Applied on Reculta,GD round and 1 interview
gd_topics_tips:
Green Economy
All of us were given 1 minute to speak on the topic first and then 5 minutes for open discussion.
interview_outline: Started by asking me to introduce myself then discussed about a point I mentioned in the introduction. Asked me questions based on marketing integrating points from my resume. One/two hr questions. It was a balanced interview.
domain_questions: Asked me to formulate a Social media marketing strategy. Asked me to do a GTM for one of their products.
hr_gk_questions: How would I manage if I had multiple tasks/work alloted in a day? If I don't like a few tasks how will I plan to do them effectively?
looking_for: They were looking for a genuine person who is also a culture fit and eager to learn.
right_wrong: Kept smiling throughout even when they were grilling me for having multiple PORs and when I made a mistake in one of the answers. Also talked about things in my intro in which I was genuinely invested.
tips:
GTM strategies although they didn't expect me to know everything (they said).
Gd practices and mock hr interview helped a lot.
dos_and_donts: Know about the company (that gives you brownie points) also be authentic.

pre_process_tips: Psychometric
interview_outline: Started with introduction,  then every line of resume, some in very detail , talked about what I learnt at IIM Indore ( at a personal level apart from academics) ,about marketing cases, asked to pick up any 2 favorite cases of mm from term 1 and summarize them and tell 3 top learnings of marketing from each of those 2 cases
domain_questions: Asked what I learnt in pharmaceuticals as it was one of the subjects in my ug
looking_for: Clarity of thought as in why did I choose to do whatever I did, was I anyhow relevant to the company and was I capable of answering every tiny bit of detail in the things that I have done so far ( as they happened to ask questions exhaustively on randomly one the academic project and one internship)
right_wrong: Good- answered every question with a smile and was able to portray that I know and am sure what I'm doing and have done so far.     Converted
tips: Knowing every part of your resume helps and the domain for which you are applying know the term 1 subject well of it
dos_and_donts: Be clear as in why this happened to be the trajectory of your life

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlist-Workshop-3 Interviews
no_interviews_duration: 3. Interview 1-25 mins, Interview 2-50 mins, Interview 3-25 mins
interview_outline: Interview 1&2 HR & Case Based; Interview 3- HR and conversation with upper mgmt
domain_questions: Related to Financial Transformations (the vertical I was shortlisted for)
hr_gk_questions: How do you copmare to someone with consulting experience/profile? Why you? Take on AI booming today? What value can you add with AI advancing especially in our vertical? Situations on how you would tackle markets/clients? Resume based questions. Why consulting? Why not finance? What sets consulting and your interests apart and what makes it a good fit for our vertical?
prep_resources: Case Prep from IIM A,B,C Casebooks
looking_for: Aware about general affairs, someone who can survive in that environment, Clarity on basic concepts on Finance & AI
right_wrong: Questions on use cases of AI. Round 3 interview was conversational, lacked market knowledge on a few things, which might have made the difference.
tips: Stay calm, trust yourself in being able to tackle anything thrown at you. Take pauses to control the flow of the interview.
tech_skills: Breaking down a Problem to identify possible sources and solutions
dos_and_donts: Know as much as you can on the current hype in the market, whether AI or anything else relevant at the specific period of time. Don't overexplain. Keep it simple and clear.

pre_process_tips: 4 rounds of Interview. Resume preparation is a must.
no_interviews_duration: 4 (2 - 1hr interviews, 1-45 min interview, 10 mins HR interviews
interview_outline: Started with introduction. Also, in tell me about yourself other than the resume was one question which was asked. The first two interviews were based entirely on the resume. Interview with the director was more of getting to know you as a person.  HR heavy .
domain_questions: Was asked tk write a business case
hr_gk_questions: A question asked to me was , did you ever find a bad situation and you jumped in to save the day but made it worse ? What learning did you get and why do you think you failed .
looking_for: They were looking for a person with clear headspace who wants to learn and also be interested in the role and the company.
right_wrong: Converted the interview. Good parts were HR and Resume based question. With the through prep I was able to handle those questions. Also , asking the interviewer is a very important part of the interview shows your interest.
tips: Resume prep. Consulting deck came in handy also. Got insights from the past experience sheet shared by prep com. Mock PI helped gain confidence.
dos_and_donts: Don't stress too much about the technical part. Prepare your resume well

interview_outline: The interview started with the question Why are you interested in Finance ? Then it went into the resume where they asked me about my academic projects. They asked me about why HDFC, they asked about my hobbies, my family details. They asked me about which sector I followed and then asked me about what the current ARPU of the telecom industry. They asked me to talk about any bank at length.
domain_questions: It was very heavy on Economics questions which included Fiscal Deficit, Interest Rate, Repo Rate, SLR, CRR. The approach that I followed was that I first explained the definition and then supported it with an example. The important trick was that I took a minute to gather my thoughts before answering which the interviewer was okay with.
hr_gk_questions: What is the current ARPU of the telecom industry. Why HDFC? Family details.
looking_for: They were looking for people who had a solid basic understanding of Economics, were sure about the role and were confident.
right_wrong: I was able to answer all the questions with confidence.
tips: Basic Macroeconomics revision, Finance material of Prepcom, awareness and ability of atleast 2 sectors which you can talk about.
dos_and_donts: Macroeconomics and atleast 2 sector preparation

pre_process_tips:
AMCAT test : 
Aptitude - below CAT level - you can easily crack,
Situational and behavioral questions pertaining,
Resume writing in the same test link

situational_questions: Direct questions on where you have experienced leadership and team player
hr_gk_questions: Why this company and why this role

tips:
PrepCom material, Big 4 reports on digital transformation
Good to practice cases with friends.

interview_outline:
Interview 1 : Introduction, Discussed current stock market situation, Outlook on Stock Market, Would you invest in the market now, where if not the market
Interview 2 : Introduction, Why IPM? Why Equity Research? How is Equity Research done?
Interview 3 (HR Based) - Introduction, Why Equity Research, Where do you see yourself in 5 years
domain_questions: The technical questions were based on my Equity Research internship. How to analyse the financials of a company, what were the factors used in analysing a stock during my internship and a discussion the same.
hr_gk_questions: HR based questions were basic like where do you see yourself in 5 years, what are your strengths?
looking_for: I think they were looking for dedication, a keen interest for equity research, and willingness to stay in this domain for a long time.
right_wrong: I tried to convince the interviewer intermittently that I am interested in equity research by giving examples from my life. My preparation included reading up the latest news, finance and FAC. This was reflected in my answers and the interviewer may have been impressed by that part.
tips: Prepare basic finance topics from the CFA Curriculum, Know FAC in and out, try to understand financial statements.

interview_outline:
1. Introduction
2. About the company, and why I wanted to join.
3. why mba
4. How to make 4 litres with 3 and 5L jugs
5. How to transport a wolf, sheep & grain across a river.
6. selfish pirate problem
7. favorite subjects in undergrad(finance & programming)
8. questions on basic finance like balance sheet, accrual accounting, etc.
9. where do you see yourself long term?
10. why not pursue a career in software engineering?
11. favorite sports

13. anything you want to ask us?
domain_questions: No
hr_gk_questions:
why mba
where do you see yourself long term? why not pursue a career in software engineering?
looking_for: I think they were looking for people who could think on the spot and had decent reasoning ability.
right_wrong: I think I got lucky with the questions as I had covered them before. I was really frank regarding my long term goals (said I didn't have any lol), and I think they liked my honesty. Converted.
tips: Mock PIs were really important as they helped get acquainted with the interview process, so I wasn't really nervous before the interview
dos_and_donts: Just be yourself

pre_process_tips: Workshop was conducted by team BCG for two days to teach us more about the case solving strategy. They conducted both one on one session as well as a group discussion where in we raised our queries.
interview_outline: First interview started with quick intro and then it proceeded towards the case. Overall it was more focussed on case - to set the price for lunar trip
domain_questions: NO company related questions were asked
hr_gk_questions: No such questions, it was specifically related to the case
looking_for: They were looking for a structured approached and wanted to check whether we are to think out of box to come to innovative solutions and they also looked for communication skills.
right_wrong: Good part of interview was the structure was good and was able to implement basic structure required but when it came to decide the upper limit for a ticket for lunar trip, couldn't think of it as a tool to set it.
tips: the most helpful material was the fact figures sheet share related to guesstimates that helped me to easily solve the guesstimate in the case given
dos_and_donts: There can be more sessions on consulting related to different types of cases like M&A cases, unconventional cases.

pre_process_tips: Screening test and video submission on Unstop, psychometric test, called to Godrej HQ in Mumbai, they held workshops just before the GD/interviews to get us acquainted with the company and culture
gd_topics_tips:
GD was based on a caselet about whether they should invest in loyalty programs or social media to increase Godrej's reach - 4-5 panel members (some offline, some online)

Some members can be overactive, try to bring a new perspective and don't have one-on-one conversations. Try to bring in structure and moderate, if you can. Don't be afraid to use the data and numbers given.
interview_outline: Entirely HR questions - started with intro, resume-based for initial questions, then based on my answers they gave situation-handling questions. Easily handled if you know your NPAD well.
domain_questions: No technical questions
hr_gk_questions: Resume based, situation-handling (no real situations, just simulations based on my answers).
looking_for: Culture fit and clarity of thought - they already had our resumes and checked if anything was overblown.
right_wrong:
Not converted.

Was nervous, and answered passively without going into much detail. Was quiet in the GD.
tips: NPAD and mock HR interviews would be the most helpful, pay attention in workshops and don't be afraid to participate in GDs

pre_process_tips:
1) Filling Application
2) Psychometric Test
gd_topics_tips: Case based GD involving a case establishing a bank branch in a semi urban area where mostly elderly/ retired people live and construction projects happening
interview_outline:
1) introduction
2) resume based questions
3) banking questions
4) Situational questions

25%technical, 25%profile, 50%HR questions
domain_questions:
Q: Why do you want to join ICICI? What do you know about it?
Ans : I answered by my willingness to join, associating my skills to it. Told some facts about the bank
hr_gk_questions: Full form of ICICI
looking_for: They were looking for good communication skills, interest in banking, willingness to relocate.
right_wrong:
Bad part - I missed "I" part of ICICI while telling full form
Good part - HR herself hinted me to some questions and completed the full form of ICICI
tips: Company website, Common GD Topics with recent happenings, GD Session conducted by prep com and external vendor
dos_and_donts:

pre_process_tips: There were three rounds. The first round was a small case study and a guesstimate which was taken by a senior manager. He just asked me to tell how would I approach the problem. Second round was again taken by senior managers. It was a full-fledged case study which I had to solve on excel and share my screen with them. Third round was interview with partner. He asked me resume based questions, felt more like an informal conversation. Make sure that you have a lot of questions to ask from the interviewer.
interview_outline: The interview started with the introduction. Then, I was asked to tell something interesting about myself that was not written in the resume. There were some questions about workex as well.
looking_for: I think they were looking for someone who can think on their feet, is smart and is able to make good conversations/ networking
right_wrong: Approach to the problem. All they (recruiters) were looking for is how holistically you can think. Practicing guesstimates and case studies helped a lot. Also, the domain sessions shared by the prepcom were quite useful.
tips: Be thorough with your resume. Also, prepare multiple questions to ask the recruiter.

pre_process_tips: Application form (on Amazon's portal) --> Online Assessment (eliminatory) --> Round 1 Interview --> Round 2 Interview
interview_outline:
Round 1 --> Tested on all the 16 Amazon Leadership Principles' pertaining to my previous Work ex in detail 
Round 2 --> Behavioral assessment, kind of stress interview, guesstimates given to understand the logical thought process
domain_questions: Mostly pertaining to my previous work ex. I would suggest to be thorough with your work ex and each point should reflect contribution done by you in quantitative figures & its larger implication for the organization
hr_gk_questions:
Q1- Why do you think you are good fit for Amazon?
Q2- Guesstimate- If Amazon increase the price of Amazon Prime by X%, estimate the number of customer calls received by Amazon customer service center.
looking_for: The candidate should have shown most of the 16 Amazon Leadership Principles' in his/her previous work experience or in college in order to be a cultural fit for Amazon
right_wrong: Round 2 was kind of stress interview, don't get intimidated by cross questioning and answer the questions with confidence.
tips: Be thorough with CV, NPAD & the 16 Amazon Leadership Principles'
dos_and_donts: Be confident & try to keep a smiling face throughout the interview

gd_topics_tips: Privatisation of PSU: Good or Bad
no_interviews_duration: 2 interviews (1 offline and 1 virtual) - 10/15 mins each
interview_outline:
Tell Me About Yourself 
Personal background questions 
Basic idea of the company’s products and services 
Discussion on how AI could help in marketing 
Why MBA after computer engineering 
Long term ambition 
!!A demo sales pitch for one of their products!!

hr_gk_questions:
Tell Me about yourself 
Why MBA after computer engineering
Long term ambition

looking_for: Someone who dint just want to be an intern, but demonstrated a long term commitment to the company, alongside a hunger & willingness to learn
right_wrong: Almost everything went right in GD-PI, selected by the company
tips:

Being calm while answering and backing your strengths to help you cross the line..
dos_and_donts:

Go through the domain compendium at-least once 
Thoroughly read company profile 
Talk to yourself in mirror to improve communication 
Peer interviews 
Written and oral practice of HR questions 

Don’t(s):

Budging away from your initial answers/thoughts

Why consulting?
What business development you can do for a consulting company such as smarthead in a period of 8 weeks?
How will you impress a girl with all the skills you have as a consultant?
Any changes you can suggest for our website?
Which is your favourite subject here at IIM

Strength and weakness
Your biggest failure
Why startup?

How do you approach a problem
Understanding of your ug subject (your fav)
Hardworking
Adaptability

Try to read recent news related to their current project

Going through the website,
Reading about their ongoing projects,
Practice on how to approach a problem

pre_process_tips: Shortlist,GD, Interview
gd_topics_tips: How UPI has changed the payment landscape in India
interview_outline: One guesstimate, few behavioral questions , Favourite subject and questions related to it . Overall a balanced interview with equal HR and academic questions
domain_questions: Clarification regarding whether the person would like a market based hectic job or not .
hr_gk_questions:
Your biggest Achievement ,why getting into an IIM does not make to the top of your list of achievements . 
How would you handle a group conflict if one person does not work properly . Would your approach change of they were your friend.

I converted

Company's vision and highlights of last year .Answering honestly in behavioral questions even though it might not be the most conventionally desirable answer of that question.

pre_process_tips: Only Application on Reculta

Psychometric test was untimed and quite a lengthy test.

dos_and_donts: In general if one doesn't stress too much, they would be easily able to crack their interview.

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlist, Buddy round (eliminatory in nature), technical interview, hr (more of offer confirmation)
no_interviews_duration: Buddy round- 30 mins of group call followed by 40-50 mins of individual round where a case study similar to fac case studies was discussed thoroughly and discussion on company culture and requirements. domain_questions: A case study similar to done in fac where different statements were to be written taking into account depreciation and interest payments after various durations for a company.
hr_gk_questions: Brief 5 mins of questioning on my internship which was fin based.

I made a lot of errors but because I was talking them through my approach they knew that I was making silly calculation errors and no conceptual errors. This way I was able to showcase everything I knew and interview were kept engaging throughout the duration.
tips: Talk them through what you're doing and thoroughly read the company JD.
dos_and_donts: Read prep comm material along with FAC concepts properly.No case studies or guesstimate were asked so don't waste time over there.

pre_process_tips: Resume based shortlisting
interview_outline: Started with introduction, went deep into work experience and internship project. There was also a brief discussion on my academic/live projects. A couple of brief case scenarios and guesstimates related to the BU.
domain_questions: The panel sought our areas of interest in the particular domain and asked questions based on that. Be clear on the fundamentals and it helps if you've done a project in that space.
hr_gk_questions: Why consulting as a career, why Infosys Consulting and why the specific business unit. Try to steer clear of generic answers.
looking_for: A proper understanding of the projects executed while at work or during internship, along with a good overall knowledge of the industry in general.
right_wrong: Being thorough about my CV - on the various aspects of work-ex, internship and academic/live projects. Also helps if you have a genuine interest in the field.
tips: A proper explanation of the projects I had worked on.
dos_and_donts: Stay humble and frame your answers in a simple manner. Ask for a few seconds to note down and streamline your thoughts before answering. Though easier said than done, remain calm and try not to let the stress get to you.
