gd_topics_tips: 1 GD - They asked us to suggest some topics, I suggested how Agro Tech doesn't believe in celebrity endorsements and ads, panel member liked it and went ahead with this topic
interview_outline: Started with HR, asked about internships, then asked to analyse the Instagram account of ACT II popcorn, one of their brands, also had a good conversation about how the GD panned out - he was intrigued by my suggestion and we talked about celeb endorsements, he explained his stance - good convo
domain_questions: Analysis of the Instagram account of ACT II popcorn, one of their brands was asked to be done - I did a holistic analysis and suggested ways to increase their follower count
hr_gk_questions: Intro, Internship, Courses done related to Marketing in UG
looking_for: They were looking for someone who had a good understanding of the company and the brands under its umbrella
right_wrong: GD and PI both went great - Interviewer praised me a lot for my oratory skills - really don't know what went wrong - couldn't convert
tips: NPAD and Marketing concepts from Compedium

pre_process_tips: An online interview where you'll have to record the video of answers displayed on the screen. The time permitted was 2-3 minutes per answer.
interview_outline:
Started with introduction, went into resume details. 
Questions about self and HR based. 
One guesstimate on calculating how many Maruti Swift Dzires are there in Indore. Interview was balanced. 
Later on, asked about applications of AI from customer and company focus separately.
domain_questions: Asked if I can code. And if I can learn to code if they provide training.
hr_gk_questions:
Walk me through your resume
Asked about 1-2 questions on sports (hobby)
How a normal day at IIT was like
Counter questions on the work I did during my internship
Most interesting incident happened at my previous company
Invited questions from me about the company/role
looking_for: Basic tech knowledge, personality, ability to handle and manage a team
right_wrong: I didn't try hard at anything. They probably just look for the fit more than anything else.
tips: Zero nervousness
dos_and_donts: Nothing as such. They will take you if they feel you're the right fit for the company anyway.

pre_process_tips: Pre process involved a test which had a mix of quantative and LRDI questions (50 minutes test)
interview_outline: Started with introduction and a few questions about the resume. Asked about American Express revenue model. 2 cases + 1 guesstimate + 2 puzzles ( short puzzles). The interviewer was just interested in understanding the approach.
domain_questions: Why analytics and about SPSS ( since it was mentioned in my resume)
situational_questions: When did you learn something in a short period of time or were able to meet a deadline with tight constraints
hr_gk_questions: Why analytics, Why MBA, Why Amex, What was the best part about your internship. Why shifting from consulting to analytics?
looking_for: Someone who was confident and showed deep interest in what they do. They were not necessarily looking for someone who had experience in analytics. Just showing deep interest and justifying the interest worked.
right_wrong: Being confident about my skills and abilities and knowing well about the company
tips:
1) Read about the company’s business model
2) Practise guesstimates 
3) Have a good answer to why you want to enter analytics

pre_process_tips: CV screening and prioritisation in different roles
interview_outline:
1. Started with introduction, went into hobby and any other activity you do in free time apart from hobby, current affairs of the activity, Revenue increase case, Any questions for me?
2. Started with introduction, next 10 mins we had light conversation of how MBA was when the interviewer was pursuing MBA, why consulting?, Why MBA not M.Tech?, Guesstimate, Any questions for me?
3. Introduce yourself, Why EY?
hr_gk_questions: Gold medals won by India in Olympics
looking_for: Relevant background as per the role, Structured approach.
right_wrong: The interview rounds were very conversational. The bad part was that while solving the case based questions I was following the traditional approach while the interviewer was looking for recommendation. While solving the guesstimate, I missed on some clarification questions. The approach for sanity check could have been better. ( Converted the interview )
tips: Practice with your peers, referring to different consulting case books, sessions form Prepcomm
dos_and_donts: While solving guesstimate, make sure to solve it with different approach. It will help in doing sanity check.

pre_process_tips:
1. Aptitude Test
2. Behavioural Test
3. Group Discussion
4. PPT Presentation Round
5. Personal Interview Round
gd_topics_tips:
A particular real estate case given by the company based on their real issue with their apartments in South Bombay.

Tips -
1. Research about the industry before proceeding with the case.
2. Look out for recent innovative developments done by the competitors.
no_interviews_duration: 1 ( Started with PPT round followed by PI) (Around 1 hour)
interview_outline:
1. About myself
2. About the real estate sector
3. About the company and their latest projects
4. Basic finance questions based on NPV, IRR
5. How did we prepare for the GD
6. Family background
7. Interest based questions in the sector
domain_questions: 1. Asked basic questions based on how to calculate NPV and IRR and how these concepts are used in real estate projects.
prep_resources: Crisil reports on the real estate sector and company website
looking_for: Interet in sticking with their company and the real estate sector
right_wrong: I wasn’t well versed with the latest and ongoing projects of the company
tips: Genuineness
tech_skills: They didn’t test deep technical skills in the interview
dos_and_donts: Do(s) - Read about the company

pre_process_tips: Reculta and company Portal Application
interview_outline: all the interviews are Cases and Guesstimate
domain_questions: NIL
hr_gk_questions: NIL
prep_resources: IIM A, B and FMS Case Books
looking_for: Clarity of thought and speech, Structured thinking
right_wrong:
Structured Thinking, Clear Communication, Confidence and guesstimate's mathematical part -went right,

Not mentioning my assumption - went wrong
tips: Practice as much as cases, and guesstimates, observe others who does the cases let it be good or bad, and teach others how to do cases and try to apply MECE structure in day today life where ever possible
dos_and_donts:
Do
- Ask only Relevant questions
- Sayout loud your calculation in guesstimate
-Make it Interactive (Assume your interviewer as your colleague and speak, this releases out your stress)
-In MECEs list out your buckets first and confirm is it exhaustive,  ask the interviewer do they have any preference to focus on any of them
- Ask for minute breaks (from my experience - max 5 times) to structure your thoughts

Don'ts
-Trying to force fit case structure
-Asking toomany questions
- Asking permission to use calculator for guesstimate

pre_process_tips: Applied on Reculta, then PPT happened for the shortlisted people only. It was a pooled PPT for colleges across country (IIMA, IIML, etc).
interview_outline: Cases
hr_gk_questions: Why Praxis? Why do you want to do Consulting? What's your view on WLB?
prep_resources: P2P case practice, Guesstimate practice, Industry Knowledge
looking_for: Clarity of thought and structure in approach. Exhaustive details as well
right_wrong: I could have been more structured when the interviewer was asking for the cost headers in an industry. It was kind of stress interview because he was repeating everything I was saying and questioning. But I somehow managed through it. If was more structured, I could have been more confident.
tips: Preparation
dos_and_donts: Don't get married to your frameworks during interviews. I usually prioritize being MECE and structured, but in one of the interviews, the lead specifically asked for a raw laundry list of ideas. By pivoting quickly and engaging in a back-and-forth dialogue, I was able to satisfy his request. It goes to show: always be ready to adapt to the interviewer’s style rather than forcing your own.

pre_process_tips: There were no pre-processes except for applying to the company
no_interviews_duration: One round which was a panel interview consisting of 2 people from strategy and marketing team, a HR and some other person. Duration: 30-40mins
interview_outline: Started with "tell me about yourself" then it was completely about Resume and especially my internship projects. They deep dived into each point I mentioned while explaining about my Summer internship. Business model of my internship company. A few technical questions. About how my experience was working in the corporate out of academics. Also why Biocon, about Biocon, about the JD. In the end questions about trends in Pharma Industry.
hr_gk_questions: What is the industry you are looking to get into and Why?
looking_for: Interest to learn and grow, ability to work, interest towards the company and the role.
right_wrong: I showed immense interest towards the company. That was a plus point. But I believe the major point was that they were impressed with how thorough I was with what I did during my internship and how willing I was to learn.
tips: Always know what you are doing and why you are doing. Connect everything that you do in your work life with what you have learnt.

no_interviews_duration: 3 Rounds; First (30 min), Second (45 min), Third-HR (20 min)
interview_outline: Profile based- resume based- every point in the CV was asked in detail. Followed by a case based round.
domain_questions: What is your favorite technology? Give a brief of how it can be leveraged?
situational_questions: Consultants are often thrown into a corner - how will you handle when you face such a situation?  Why do you want get into a management domain in spite of a strong technical/engineering profile?
hr_gk_questions: Why do you think you are fit for a consulting role?
looking_for: Honest and structured answers. Relevant skills - impressed with the club activities and live projects majorly oriented around data interpretation.
right_wrong:
Connecting every answer with a personal story/experience was something that helped immensely in every round.
In the first round - my answers constantly revolved around tech - AI/ML .. this made the interviewer rethink on if I am an overly tech person -- I should have handled this better.
tips:
Consulting case books (IIM A, IIM Indore, IIM L), reherasing NPAD answers;
Mock PI was very helpful - candid feedback was given, GD was not that great/useful

pre_process_tips: An application form was asked to be filled and then resume shortlist according to role preference.
interview_outline:
1st interview was resume based followed by some technical ques and main focus was on the internship and algorithms in tech related to machine learning that could be applied in the summer internship projects.
2 nd was hr based regarding why cognizant, understanding of role and why should we hire you.
domain_questions: Just basic technical part mentioned in resume
hr_gk_questions: Why this company, this role, your understanding about the Role. Also why should we hire you.
looking_for: Mostly the technical knowledge mentioned in the resume should be properly prepared. They were not looking at the theory aspect but how can you put the knowledge in the real life scenario.
right_wrong: The good part was that it was interactive session. Going through with the resume greatly helped.
tips: The domain session deck and the npad helped a lot. The mocks gave an idea about what to look at exactly and gave a structured approach to the preparation.
dos_and_donts: Be thorough with the roles and responsibilities.

pre_process_tips: Case Study based Discussion (case was sent the night before discussion), 2 Interviews
gd_topics_tips: It was a 45 minutes GD. Be prepared with a lot of points to make several entries. Try to give the group an approach rather than everyone discussing different thing. Push in your points, no one cares if you gave someone a chance to speak or not (or at least I felt so)
no_interviews_duration: 2 interviews. For me first one was a 15 minute interview, the second one was not an interview but for people it went for 15-20 minutes.
interview_outline:
First Interview - Introduce yourself, Why Investment Banking? Summarise your Summers project? whom did your summers mentor report to ? Greatest achievement? No technical question.
Second Interview - They just pitched Equity Research role and it was not an interview.
domain_questions: No domain specific question
situational_questions: Already covered in earlier
hr_gk_questions: Already covered in earlier
looking_for: Someone who have done equity research earlier.
right_wrong: I described my internship project in a manner to suit with the job profile the firm was offering to me. That worked a lot.
dos_and_donts: In case you know who is the interviewer read about him on linkedin. And try to talk about the industry they are more interested in.

pre_process_tips: Aptitude test with questions of DI-LR and Verbal
interview_outline: Started with my introduction, moved on to quick mental math questions like 400% of 35, a question on probability (Permutation and combination concept), a logical question on determining output of an assembly line, a guesstimate and some clarifying questions on that
domain_questions: Guesstimates and mathematical questions
looking_for: I think they were looking for candidates who have good data interpretation and analysis skills. They will also ask questions which you might probably not know where they test if you are comfortable in accepting and asking for help
right_wrong: Maintained confidence throughout the interview, asked a lot of questions, did not shy away from asking for help. Could have solved the guesstimate better.
tips: Prepared cases and guesstimates beforehand with different set of people; Referred to case books of all top B-schools, Case-in-point; attended mock PIs for consulting
dos_and_donts: Try and step out of your comfort zone, do not practice cases with just one person; Practice all 4 types of cases along with their structures; Keep updated with latest news and trends

pre_process_tips: Just go through the JD properly as interviews are based on that.
interview_outline: It was based on work experience as I included that in tell me abou t yourself section and what do I bring to the table with my experience at work and summer internship. Finance based cases and usual guesstimates, plus basics of accounting.
domain_questions: Characteristics of the three kinds of financial statements, relationship between them, how to optimise CFO's work, how to reduce the costs of the finance function, why should assets and liabilities be matched.
situational_questions: Will you be able to manage doing backend work in the initial phases? Is online (wfh) comfortable with you? How did you handle any issues during your work in the PORs
hr_gk_questions: Why Finance? Why PwC? Why consulting?
looking_for: Confident indiviuals with good knowledge of basics of finance and consulting
right_wrong: Confidence was the most important thing that helped me amintain my composure
tips: Talk to the interviewers like a candid conversation in an official setting
dos_and_donts: Don't fret even if there's a moment where you think you may get stuck

pre_process_tips: Buddy round after shortlist: 3 calls, 2 cases solved in detail, (40 mins each)
interview_outline: Started with introduction, followed by a puzzle, then jumped into a case, and concluded with HR questions like why consulting and why Accenture. Second interview was majorly HR based, Tell me about yourself, one thing you could do differently in your work ex or college in hindsight, and why consulting, why Accenture.
domain_questions: Case solved in first interview: new product/service strategy: covered market attractiveness, financial viability, operational feasibility, and competitive landscaping to evaluate the opportunity.
hr_gk_questions: Tell me about yourself, one thing you could do differently in your work ex or college in hindsight, and why consulting, why Accenture.
looking_for: Problem solving, logical explanations for recommendations, no specific background or technical skills tested in interview but insights from prior experience help.
right_wrong: Getting the puzzle right in the first few minutes left a positive impression, take time to think and then answer, don’t rush into answering.
tips: Try to answer with structure and clarity don’t contradict your own words. Casebooks help a lot.

pre_process_tips: Buddy process
no_interviews_duration: 4. The first 3 interviews went for 30-45 mins each. And the last one went for 15 mins.
interview_outline:
I have a work experience. So, there were questions on my work-ex and internship in every interview round. If you don't have a work-ex, you can expect more questions from your internships. 

first round (Sr Consultant) - Guesstimate and Resume
second round (Manager) - Case solving, Resume and a mini case
third round (Director) - Case solving, more questions about the role and resume
fourth round (Partner) - resume and HR
domain_questions: Know more about your role. If it is DDV, have a prior knowledge about Mergers and Acquisitions. You can get more details about your role from your buddy.
hr_gk_questions: One challenging incident, Why do think you are a best fit as a consultant
looking_for: Your way of analysing a problem and the structure.
right_wrong: Be crisp while solving a case, especially when it is a mini case
tips: Know completely about the role and how it functions. Have few questions prepared to be asked after every interview. Practise cases and guesstimates well. If your role is DDV, you can expect an M&A case

pre_process_tips: Resume Submission
interview_outline: Started with asking what is with linear regression - what are dummy variables - Have i made any forecasting models-then a case based on metrics - HR based - what true Indira is beyond her resume
domain_questions: Started with asking what is with linear regression - what are dummy variables - Have i made any forecasting models-then a case based on metrics - HR based - what true Indira is beyond her resume
hr_gk_questions: HR based - what true Indira is beyond her resume - I gave a generic answer about my family interests and connected my childhood with star tv and how I have been influenced by it. I mentioned my strengths.
looking_for: work-ex - someone good with product strategy or comfortable with making models (metrics).
right_wrong: I think the HR questions where I connected star with my childhood and mentioning my strengths helped me to get through the interview.
tips: Bit of prod lab based metrics analysis
dos_and_donts: Just be yourself and if your profile fits in with the company you'll get through it

pre_process_tips: Application via Eeculta, psychometric test, PPT submission regarding "Real Magic", favourite product of cocacola, etc.
interview_outline:
Started with Introduction, talked about my interests, why switch in stream of education, projects I worked on. Technical question. 
Balanced.
domain_questions:
How do we analyse a company's financials for investment? - Talked about there current financial positions, P/E ratio, diversification of risk, future growth prospects, etc. Told them 5 stocks whose financials I had gone through including Cocacola.
Asked what was interesting about their financials - Change in there debt equity and them moving toward debt free company or trying to reduce their interest obligation.
hr_gk_questions:
Asked to explain Project related with analysis of financial statement of a listed company- Accepted explanation provided and then was asked about the technical questions
Why finance?
looking_for: Dedicated and loyal to the organisation and genuinely interested to work with them
right_wrong:
Good- Discussion on mythological fiction the interviewer and I had read .
Bad- Required more clarity wrt the stock recommendation made.
tips: Equit-I material and go through the company website and financials if possible.

pre_process_tips: Aptitude test
interview_outline: Balanced interview- Introduction, questions related to internships, logical reasoning and probability questions, one question related to Excel formula, small market entry cases,
domain_questions:
Why Amex
What do you know about Amex
How’s Amex different from others and how’s it able to charge premium from merchants
CEO of Amex
How and when Hlookup is used 
Questions on logical reasoning and probability
hr_gk_questions:
1. Why internships in different domains
2. Detail explanation of one of the internships
3. Cases:
-Market entry: opening something like Choki Dhani in Delhi
-How will you decide if Amex should collaborate with a company like Big Bazaar 
-How will you make a merchant pay a higher margin to you than your competitors
looking_for: Willingness to learn and interest in the domain
right_wrong:
Converted the interview
Good: had researched about the company and had spoken to past interns- mentioned their good experiences in my answers 
Bad: Couldn’t solve probability questions and didn’t know who the CEO of Amex is
tips:
No technical questions, just company related and general logical reasoning 
Case prep helped

pre_process_tips: GD round, Pitch Round, Group Interview
gd_topics_tips: Topics: Strategy over Culture, Culture over Strategy, Ideas to increase the women customers for beer
interview_outline: HR and Resume Based mainly (asked me 1 situation based question on a market entry case)
hr_gk_questions:
Introduction, Why AB InBev, Your dream, Strengths and Weakness, Market entry case, Pitch yourself 
Pitch Round: They will give you a brand and will ask you to pitch that brand to them in a way that they have 1 million dollars and want to invest so why they should invest in your brand (dont focus only on numbers, make it personalised, storytelling)
prep_resources: Company Website, GD prep, HR questions
looking_for: Culture fit, Curiosity, Ambitious, Personalization and storytelling in answers
tips: Know about the company in detail and these people are very much focused on their culture in general so majorly try to pitch yourself as an open, curious and ambitious person.
dos_and_donts: Practice GD topics related to beer market, know some facts about the market, answers should align with their 10 company values in general

pre_process_tips: An assignment on making a sales pitch to a prospective lead (details about the lead were given). Didn’t take up much time - could be done within 2 hours
no_interviews_duration: 4 (5-10 minutes each, only the first one lasted around 15 minutes)
interview_outline: All started with introduction. Why sales. Why this company. A lot about work experience, since same industry (software). A little about internship, and life at IIM Indore.
domain_questions: What kind of questions would you ask your lead before making a sales pitch. What kind of problems faced in work exp in which the product offered by the company could help. What is the USP of the product offered by BrowserStack.
hr_gk_questions: Basic introduction
looking_for: Someone aware about how software development and testing tools and processes, who also has good communication skills.
right_wrong: Could relate my work experience very well with why I’ll be a good fit - because I understand the product need and how it would fit into the market
tips: Knowing about the latest developments in the company and seeming genuinely interested
dos_and_donts: If it’s a startup, know enough about the company and how it’s doing

pre_process_tips:
1. Aptitude test of 1 hour comprising 20 questions on basic Quant with data interpretation ones slightly time consuming
2. Consulting Case workshop(1.5 hrs): Discussion on one guesstimate then two seperate cases as per your alloted breakout room
3. Personal Interview (25 mins)
interview_outline:
Questions:
1. Walk me through your resume and few cross questions on that
2. Basic maths questions like square of 35 but the answer is expected in very short time
3. Square root of 13 and convince me of your answer by 2-3 different logics
4. Operations based question where total output in a time, highest waiting time and machine no. etc. Was asked
domain_questions: Few questions about data analytics etc., for this particular Coe the consulting Case was not asked
looking_for: Someone who can think fast, defend the argument in the most logical way
right_wrong: Converted the interview, everything went very smooth
tips: Since I read all the basic knowledge sessions of Prepcom, when unexpectedly the operations question was there I was able to manage
dos_and_donts: No such special preparation is required

pre_process_tips:
Step 1: Resume Shortlist 
Step 2: Aptitude+ Domain Test
Step 3: Workshop(This round is eliminatory in nature , roughly half of the students were rejected
Step 4: GD 
Step 5 Interview Round 1
Step 6: Interview Round 2
gd_topics_tips:
The GD was NUMERICAL CASE BASED GD related to what they taught in the workshop and we need to apply the learnings in the workshop. The panel was looking who are proactive, giving relevant point, unlike marketing GDs, this GD was really smooth, 
Focus on proving relevant point
They were asking random person to conclude , however anyone can start the GD
interview_outline:
Started with Introduction, 
Some finance related question
Ratios
Resume related question, HR question

NOTE: It was a group Interview with 3 person and two panel
domain_questions: CASE was given to solve in the interview
hr_gk_questions: Why finance? Why JPMC?
looking_for: Interested students in finance with some background
right_wrong: Not sure, but definitely lack of preparation on my behalf
tips: PrepComm Material is best resources
dos_and_donts: Prepare in Advance, even if you think you would not get shortlist

pre_process_tips: Filling application/registration and then Interview
no_interviews_duration: Usually 2 rounds of interview but for me only one interview of 30 mins
interview_outline: Technical interview with focus on valuation and financial modelling
domain_questions: how to do valuation, different methods of valuation, explain how to do DCF from start to end with formulas, how to calculate WACC, what is CAPM, how to value a bank, how it is different from other companies’ valuation, what is dividend discount model, what is financial modelling, impact of selling an asset of Rs 80 for Rs 100 in all the three financial statements, how to evaluate a bank, what are the different ratios for a bank’s performance, difference between GNPA and NNPA, and if there is a new company with a new technology coming up, which valuation method to use.
looking_for: Finance technical knowledge with specific focus on valuation and financial modelling
right_wrong: In depth knowledge and confidence about financial concepts
tips: confidence plus Conceptual Clarity
dos_and_donts: Do's-In depth valuation knowledge, conceptual clarity, take time before answering,   Don'ts- incomplete knowledge, answering like you have only read it somewhere and have not done it practically.

pre_process_tips: Buddy rounds (4), Case Workshop and Networking Dinner
interview_outline: Introduction + Case/Guesstimate
domain_questions:
1st Interview - Case was asked (Your client is a Spanish Church and they have witnessed decline in revenue. Investigate why.) 
2nd Interview - Guesstimate the no.of petrol pumps in Kolkata and their growth rate
hr_gk_questions:
None in Interviews.
Buddy calls - Why consulting, Why BCG, What are your key strengths and weaknesses
looking_for: Work-ex is not important as I was never asked about the same. Were looking for motivated individuals with structured approach to problem solving and excellent communication skill
right_wrong:
Good - Was able to crack all the cases in buddy rounds, workshops and interviews
Bad - Was not able to properly guesstimate growth rate of petrol pumps in the last interview, Mentor connect did not happen despite multiple attempts to connect with mentor
tips: Case Books - IIM A, B, FMS and I. Industry reports.
dos_and_donts: Practice cases with batchmates and seniors, expect unconventional cases, assume all buddy rounds to be evaluative, Be proactive in workshop and networking dinners, Be Confident!!

pre_process_tips: Offline MCQ Test
no_interviews_duration: 4(3 technical and 1 HR) and approx 20 minutes per technical and 15 mins for HR
interview_outline: Technical interviews were heavily focused on subjects like Macroeconomics, Fixed Income and Derivatives; inside out conceptual knowledge of these subjects was expected. Confidence
domain_questions: Macroeconomics, Fixed Income and Derivatives(at least till L1 syllabus and everything covered in college academics)
hr_gk_questions: Tarrifs impact on Fixed Income securities and Derivative contracts(also Greeks)
looking_for: Conceptually strong candidates with an acumen and passion for finance and especially risk management
right_wrong: Being confident in my answers helped. Showing strong interest towards the role and organisation is very helpful. If one does not know some answer there is no shame in saying that. The interviewers very ready to hand hold and help reach the answers. Mainly the grasping and conceptual understanding of the topics was checked
tips: Finance focused preparation is very crucial and a strong wish to pursue a career in the specified role
dos_and_donts: Be confident and prepared. Not one of those roles where you can globe your way out. Long term knowledge of finance, macros and current affairs will be tested.

pre_process_tips: None. Direct ppra world from resume
gd_topics_tips: 2 rounds. Each person was given a chance to speak. First round current affairs or general.eg. Can startup’s make money, bitcoin. Second abstract. Eg. values for future generation. Need to raise valid points once or twice. No need to dominate or Scream. That’s negative.
no_interviews_duration: 1: 15-20 mins. Resume based. Strong fin requirement.
interview_outline: Completely resume based. Know every term and task done. 3 people each responsible for  finance , hr and operations questions. Finance given heavy weight. Atleast cfa and frm level 1 preparation. No need of certifications but need to show knowledge
domain_questions: Swaps, efficient market hypothesis and what is your view, difference between interest rate swaps and cross currency swap value , sharpe ratio. The more you answer the higher the level gets. They expect high knowledge
hr_gk_questions: What’s Ipm, why Ipm, why Nomura, what’s our role
looking_for: Communication skills in gd. Fin knowledge in interview. Fit for company
right_wrong: Knowledge of heavy fin concepts
tips: Prepare finance cfa and frm
dos_and_donts: Don’t shout in gd. Put points firmly and good ones. Be confident in Interview

pre_process_tips: GD and PI
gd_topics_tips: Future of general retail (brick and mortar) stores. The GD proceeded normally. Everyone presented points supporting the traditional stores or aiding them with online stores. everyone was asked to summarize the discussion at the end. The panel mostly looked for clarity of thought and presentation. The candidates with multiple useful entries were shortlisted for PI.
interview_outline: The interview was resume based with an emphasis on questions related to work experience. The panel asked various questions about how I dealt with the different problems during the job and what was my special contributions.
domain_questions: No technical questions were asked
hr_gk_questions: Resume and work experience-related questions. The panel was largely happy with my answers.
looking_for: The panel was looking for confident candidates who were good at problem solving.
right_wrong: The questions were largely based on what I had done in my job and it was important that the answers were straight to the point and without hesitation. Converted.
tips: Repository and Mock PI helped in the preparation.
dos_and_donts: Being thorough with your resume is important.

pre_process_tips: Psychometric Test, video based assessment, interview
interview_outline: Introduction, resume based HR questions, general HR questions, conclusion. Was completely HR heavy with no technical questions asked
hr_gk_questions: Introduction, why the company, why the role, how to prioritise deadlines/ time management and resume based questions.  My approach was too tailor fit my resume based questions in order to appeal to the values of the company. I was energetic and friendly throughout my interview and confidence was one factor which helped me stand out
looking_for: Energy and confidence in my opinion were key to cracking the interview and helped me gain favour of the interviewers
right_wrong: Mine was a short interview and it went really well. I was interacting well with the panelists despite the questions they asked and kept a cool head throughout. I was able to connect experiences in my life with their brand and their values to help crack the interview
tips: Mock PI's are important. Not much technical to know but get a background of sales and how it is different from marketing

pre_process_tips:
1-Resume shortlist
2-Online aptitude test of 45 min and a 10 min video test in which there were 3 qs about yourself, a financial question ( say on a topic like capitalism in India) and another one about renewable sector, simple qs-extempore type, have to record yourself answering in 3 min per question
no_interviews_duration: 2 buddy calls- 15 to 20 min each and interview of 30 min
interview_outline:
Revolved a lot around what the role was about
So basic intro+ some finance technical+ lot about role- regulations wrt to it in US, what factors to be considered while valuing a renewable projects, what factors to be sensitive of, types of renewable investments they were into etc.
domain_questions: Mostly revolved around capital budgeting and valuation
hr_gk_questions: About Trump Tariffs, One big beautiful Bill, Climate change agreement
prep_resources: Investment Prep Red book, About the Company+Role from official website, UG notes
looking_for: Enthusiastic about finance+ renewable space
right_wrong: Thinking on my feet, General Awareness, Knowledge of Role
tips: Same as above
dos_and_donts: Know about company/ role very well, have q chains ready so as to answer follow up qs quickly

pre_process_tips: No Pre Process. CV shortlisting
no_interviews_duration: 3 Rounds- Round 1(35 mins), Round 2 ( 20 mins) and Round 3 (15 mins)
interview_outline: Started out with resume(only the work ex and internship points were focussed upon). Know your resume points thoroughly.
domain_questions: Round 1 is based entirely on operations and supply chain management. The questions were both basic and a bit advanced. Go through the JD to understand what the role entails and try to read all the concepts mentioned therein.
situational_questions: Round 2 and 3 focusse on the fit into the role. Questions like why supply chain, why this role,basic HR, etc. were asked.
looking_for: Fit for the role and knowledge about the domain
right_wrong: Most of the questions that were asked were domain knowledge based. I was able to answer most so it was a smooth process.
tips:
1. Read the Prep com material for Supply chain and operations.
2. If possible prepare from the term 4 Supply Chain course material.
3. Read about the company and prepare 2-3 good questions.
dos_and_donts:
1. Resume points should be prepared THOROUGHLY.
2. Try to answer all the questions in the STAR  format.

pre_process_tips: CV shortlist
interview_outline:
It was case based and technical heavy. The interviewer asked for a brief introduction and favourite subject. I mentioned pricing. So, in the next 5-10 mins, several questions were asked on concepts in pricing.
Then there was a case on pricing. I had to suggest a pricing strategy for a mature B2B product before it is finally withdrawn from market.
domain_questions: Fundamentals of pricing. Types of pricing. What are the pricing strategies used in different stages of life cycle of the product.
situational_questions: No
hr_gk_questions: Introduce yourself. Future plan for 5 years.
looking_for: They were mostly looking for someone with strong fundamentals and ability to communicate properly.
right_wrong: What went right would be I was thorough in that one paper which they asked. What went wrong was during the case I lost the direction once, however, they helped me get back on track.
tips: Learn every point in CV thoroughly. Questions can be asked even on the point that seems to be insignificant.
dos_and_donts: Prepare the CV thoroughly. Don't panick in the process.

pre_process_tips: Aptitude and Psychometric test. Further a form to be filled before the GD
gd_topics_tips: Are space missions a waste of money for a resource starving country like India.
interview_outline: Started with an introduction. No technical questions were asked. Asked a question related to the psychometric test results. Questioned and cross questioned about the ability to handle a team. Asked about the expectations of the location and nature of the job. 'Where do you see yourself in five years?'
situational_questions: Multiple scenarios of handling a team with older men. I answered by talking about my PoR and how I handled the team there. Explain a scenario where I was assertive.
looking_for: They wanted to know whether I will be able to manage a team which comprises mostly of adult men.
right_wrong: I talked confidently about my abilities. I was honest about the expectations of the job and stated that I am willing to accept the job conditions.
tips: Prepared NPAD questions thoroughly with the help of placed friends. Mock PI with Roy Charles was helpfull.

pre_process_tips: First there was a google form with a lot of NPAD questions to understand us. After that the second round was a HireVue Virtual interview where 3 random Qs appeared and we had to answer them in designated time (1-2mins). Then I had a virtual interview
interview_outline: It started with my introduction then there were core finance Qs from beginner to advance level. Anyone who throughly prepares the material provided by prepcom, equiti and the FAC class could answer them easily. Also have through info about fmcg industry and company. Lastly I was asked ‘why finance’
domain_questions:
Leasing - operational, financial 
What supply side and marketing side finance cost an fmcg faces?
What are the industry benchmarks for fmcg industry 
Npv
Dcf modeling
Comparables transactions
Depreciation 
3 statements
hr_gk_questions:
Intro
Why finance
looking_for: Thorough knowledge of finance and interest in fmcg industry
right_wrong: Converted. I couldn’t answer few acad Qs but i tried to cover it up by including industry knowledge in my answers
tips: Prepcom and equiti material. Fac class notes and news

certifications: Lean Six Sigma Belt (Green), CSCA from ISCEA
pre_process_tips: Superset registration
no_interviews_duration: 3 interviews , first interview 20 min , second interview 20 min, final interview 10 min
interview_outline: First interview was a chill interview with a duration of about 10 min. Then next stage happened parallely while others were have round 1. Then R2 with a senior manager who asked technical and hr questions.Then R3 was a hr round that primarily was like a confirmation round specifying the terms of offer letter and other similar policies and not really an interview
domain_questions: It was a Salesforce consultant role (SFDC). Both first and second interview was based on resume, knowledge on CRM functioning, sales funnel, wheather I have used Salesforce prior, subjects I liked in mba, why this role,
hr_gk_questions: challenges I faced with teammates and questions along those similiar lines.
looking_for: They were looking whether I have knowledge in CRM and sales
right_wrong: I have worked with SAP hence my answers regarding CRM questions were based on that
tips: If you attempt the interview without actually caring u would convert or not will help you mentally give the best shot
dos_and_donts: Casebooks

pre_process_tips:
1. Resume shortlisting followed by 
2. Asynchronous or Automated Video Interviews ( questions : Introduce yourself , Why Cognizant over others , Describe a situation wherein you dealt with people with different perspectives,
Describe a situation where you managed a crisis,
Describe a situation wherein you persuaded someone,
Describe a situation wherein you used data to make a informed decision)
interview_outline:
Introduction and followed by work I did . Most questions were resume based and focused on internship work.
Second interview was mostly around my vertical ( BFSI) in my work Experience. Questions on concept of insurance and process flow and claims( because I was in insurance domain) .
This was followed by questions to understand if I understood the role they were offering.
domain_questions: Some questions were based on my vertical in my previous organisations.
situational_questions: Questions on team management ( because i had mentioned it in CV) . How did you handle the conflicts
looking_for: Panel was friendly and looking for profile match and willingness to join

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlisting
gd_topics_tips: Impacts of covid on Business. Do no repeat points, lead the group with new ones. Speak atleast 5-7 times. Give chance to others.
interview_outline: Introduction, then resume based. Based on resume asked domain specific questions. Like if there is a social media internship, then questions based on how to increase reach, which platforms to use. Asked about the methodology of my research paper. Why J&J?
domain_questions: Basics of Marketing
hr_gk_questions: No current Affairs.
looking_for: I was fresher. No certifications except digital marketing online course. I think during GD they looked at people who brought different view points, and spoke more. During PI it was more of a good conversation. They were looking in knowing if you are interested in Sales, J&J Products.
right_wrong: Converted another company before result. Being confident and relaxed helped me throughout.
tips: Studied based on the things I wrote on resume. Just follow all the steps mock GD,PI, domain sessions properly, they covered 70% things. Read business newspapers a little bit. Just be aware of current happenings.

pre_process_tips: Shortlisting from resume
interview_outline:
Round 1 : Asked to walk me through my resume. i explained him all the project that i did throughout my work experience. questions related to work experience were asked - i used big data technologies in my project so he asked about the same.

Round 2 : HR based round , why OLA ? , what do you know about the organization , recent news about the company
domain_questions: No specific questions , but it will be related to work prior work ex / internships only.
hr_gk_questions: NO Current affairs questions
looking_for: company fit
right_wrong: I converted the interview , so i believe nothing gone wrong
tips: Mock Prepcomm GDs and Interviews helped me a lot , please don't miss those mock interviews. also the prepcomm starter deck for IT / Consulting helped me as well
dos_and_donts:
Don't lose hope if you didn't get selected early in the season, eventually everybody will be going to get placed.
study hard and take sleep ( 4 hours at least) before interview

pre_process_tips: There was a GD followed by three interviews
gd_topics_tips: We were price chart of Bitcoin and asked to discuss on 4-5 questions
interview_outline: Questions were mostly technical but were focused on basics of the skills required mentioned in JD. Very few HR questions with no question asked about company
domain_questions: Technical questions were based on derivatives and bond pricing. There were general aptitude questions as well.
hr_gk_questions: There were couple of questions asked from the resume. HR round was short and focused on company's culture
looking_for: There were not looking for people who had very knowledge about financial concepts. They just wanted a person who would come and provide a different point of view which matters significantly in a risk role.
right_wrong: Even I didn't know the answer to a question, I didn't globe and was humble enough to accept that I needed to do further reading about them. I could have handled aptitude questions better
tips: The material from Team Navkiran was extremely useful. Mock GDs/PIs removed all the inhibitions we had

pre_process_tips:
1. Comprehensive form including SOP

2. Talview video interview (had to record answers to 5-7 questions like brief introduction, strengths, why cognizant, most challenging project etc.

"What are 3 most important things to you in a job? If you have to compromise on one , which one will it be and why?"
"What would make you chose cognizant over others?")
interview_outline:
-Introduction
-About summer internship organization and projects undertaken there (quite in-depth)
-Development economics (I mentioned it as my area of interest)
-Economics' concepts and discussions eg my opinions regarding the recovery path followed by India's GDP growth, analysis of the Indian economy pre, during, post covid (sector-wise analysis), India's trade patterns and its composition, concept of seigniorage-its impact and feasibility
-About the role
looking_for: Confidence, fit for the role/company, willingness to adapt and learn
right_wrong: Kept the interview more conversational in nature
tips:
-Prep-com consulting material
-Focused on an area of interest that I could have an in-depth conversation about
-Brushed up basic concepts of the mentioned subjects

pre_process_tips: Apply on reculta
interview_outline: Started with self introduction, then about my final year project in college (which was part of my resume and self intro),  then the panel talked a bit about what I could expect, that interns would be assigned to projects based on their availability. When they were describing the various verticals that projects could be assigned to interns from, they talked about digital transformation. I mentioned that I believe I would be a right fit for it owing to my background in engineering. They said okay.
domain_questions: none.
hr_gk_questions: I was asked about my final year project which I had mentioned in my resume. I described what I did in detail, walked through the basic technical steps, and the outcome. The panel acknowledged my answer and did not question me further regarding it.
looking_for: Someone with analytical skills who was a quick learner. Able to adapt to whatever project they assigned.
right_wrong: Converted.
tips: Mock gd/pi were helpful in providing a glimpse on what to expect during placements.

pre_process_tips: After applying on the portal, I gave a psychometric test which was the elimination round.
interview_outline:
Started with Intro
Went too deep into resume (specially work-ex) - almost grilled
Also questioned deeply about IIM-I PORs
NPAD HR Questions were asked too

PI was balanced.
domain_questions: They will indirectly ask. (specifically focussed on Amazon Leadership Principles)
hr_gk_questions:
They asked about almost every point from Work-ex.
From NPAD - situation when you went out of your way, biggest problem solved
CV - Asked to justify gap years

Approach of Answer - Using STAR framework along with combining Amazon Leadership Principles
looking_for:
- Genuine Candidate who complies with what they have mentioned in the CV
- Profile in sync with Amazon Leadership Principles
right_wrong:
They were going too deep in work-ex and PORs. 

Suggestion- Keep calm, take time & answer it in STAR framework
Be aware o                                                                                                                     f Amazon Chime platform where PI will happen
tips:
Amazon Leadership Principles
CV Prep
NPADs
dos_and_donts: Learn about Amazon Leadership Principles and use it indirectly in your answers.

pre_process_tips:
Workshop followed by assignment of buddy
One buddy round, one round with senior associate, followed by interview with the director
interview_outline: Interview was technical heavy and resume based, introduction was not asked
domain_questions: Majorly valuation and accounts based interview, basic concepts of statistics also need to be brushed up.
hr_gk_questions: I was asked in depth questions about my internships and academic projects, both of which were in the finance domain. My approach was to prepare a well formulated answer for each cv point prior to the interview which included introduction, the outline of what I did and any conclusion/ learning that I gained from that project/ internship.
looking_for: Majorly looking for people well versed with the basics of finance, apart from that having strong internships will help you.
right_wrong: The technical parts were handled well. However somewhere the in depth aspects of resume could have been dealt with better. I went till the director round, but didn't convert that.
tips: Prepcom and Equit-i material was majorly used to revise the concepts.

pre_process_tips:
Round 1: Aptitude test with 20 questions (2X4 RC, 4 quant, 4 DI, 4 LR)
Round 2: Case workshop of 1 hour where 1 case and 1 guesstimate were discussed (participants are expected to participate in the discussion process, and my experience was that more you participate in giving quality points, better your chances)
interview_outline:
50 minute interview starting with Tell my something about yourself and then-
a) 2-3 questions on statistics (what is clustering, p-value, etc) and basic probability 
b) 1 case (create a business case for a carbon consulting firm- which provides consulting for carbon footprint)
c) 1 guesstimate (estimate amt of money collected on a typical toll booth in India)
looking_for: Someone with good quantitative abilities fluent in statistics and probability concepts and able to solve guesstimates and cases with good recommendations
right_wrong:
Good parts: my prompt problem solving for probability questions, taking appropriate assumptions when necessary for case, constantly validating them with the interviewer
Bad parts: could have been quicker with the guesstimate

pre_process_tips: A Case based on one of their product was given, and ideal customer profile (ICP) and corresponding gym strategy was asked.
no_interviews_duration: 1st round of PI: 45-50 mins; 2nd round of PI: 25-30 mins
interview_outline:
1st PI was focused on the case submission and some discussion over it followed by a role play (me as their sales representative, the panel as their target customer)
2nd PI started with an introduction (past journey and experiences), then a short discussion on the product, challanges and possible solutions, followed by few NPAD questions (strengths, weakness and what I bring to the table)
domain_questions:
What should be the target customer profile? 
What should be the GTM and business model?
hr_gk_questions: No current affairs questions.
looking_for: Relevant past experience, SnM basics and intent to work on the project
right_wrong:
I am not sure, maybe the roleplay went good. 
Also, I had an internship in the industry.
tips: Straight and simple answers works.
dos_and_donts:
Do some homework on the company and industry.
Attempt few Case Competitions, few placement processes may have case submission for screening

pre_process_tips: No pre-process. Resume based shortlist.
gd_topics_tips:
Case based GD. Case was about how to deal with credit card in a shop using big data. 

They value unique points a lot. There is ample time for everyone to think. So don't cut anyone. Use the time someone's speaking to come up with unique perspectives and a comprehensive solution rather than redundantly agreeing to people.
no_interviews_duration: 2. First one 40-45 minutes and Second one 20 minutes.
interview_outline:
Completely resume based. Asked a sorta case/guesstimate but that was created from resume as well. 

Try and show that you have interest in analytics and willingness and ability to learn quickly. I think that worked for me.
domain_questions: Knowing how payments and credit card industry works and how to use ML/AI in this field is extremely important.
hr_gk_questions: HR based questions such as strength, weakness, why Amex were asked.
looking_for: Knowledge or interest in analytics.
right_wrong: My internship project aligned with the GD topic quite well and I leveraged that by trying to use the solution I created there.
tips: Mock PIs were very helpful.

pre_process_tips: Single line live case was given to be solved after round 1 interview
interview_outline:
1st round Interview was on video call. Started with introduction, went into my internship, talked about the subjects I liked, HR questions were there, finally a case guesstimate.
2nd interview was on a single line live case that was given to us 12 hrs before the interview, mostly cross questioned in that and a lot of hr questions. Answers don't need to be concrete numbers but the method used has to be clear and rational
domain_questions: No. But I didn't hesitate to show my knowledge where ever possible
hr_gk_questions: All NPAD questions and questions on the company. Be thorough with recent ads, insta fb page, etc
looking_for: Motivated individuals
right_wrong: I had done proper research on the company, and was able to improvise on my answers in the spot.
dos_and_donts: Focus on company motives goals vission etc and tune answers accordingly. Don't need concrete numbers for answers...rough estimate with normal guesstimate approach is enough

pre_process_tips: Video Resume
gd_topics_tips: GD topic: Is software valuable? and one situational leadership question. It was a friendly discussion, well moderated. There were two employees from Salesforce present, who intervened to play devil's advocate.
no_interviews_duration: 1 interview with HR and a senior leader (30minutes)
interview_outline: Introduction, Why Salesforce?, Why not Marketing?, Why this role specifically?, What values did you learn from your parents?, Describe your leadership stint
situational_questions: Describe a time you managed a conflict?, Have you ever been a leader?
looking_for: Confident that this role is what they're aiming for, Honest, Friendly, Open-minded
right_wrong: I couldn't convince them why I wanted to work in the company, Make sure that your answer is personal and not copypasta
tips: Prepcomm material, especially the current affairs excel sheet was helpful for the GDs. Read everything in the news about the company, their CEO's values and approaches, social responsibilities etc.
dos_and_donts: Do try to figure out instances where you've shown the values that they believe in, blend it into your responses. Be straightforward and if you don't know an answer, just say so.

pre_process_tips: Initial profile based shortlist
gd_topics_tips: Impact of e-commerce in India
interview_outline: Resume based questions- about family, why B.Tech, why MBA, choice of subjects mostly conversational interview around Summer Internship project -asked in details and cross-questioned extensively, why S&M (being a girl, why I wanted to have a field based job)
domain_questions: Summer Internship related technical questions, interviewers were trying to cross question every thing that was said
situational_questions: Nothing as such
hr_gk_questions: Nothing as such
looking_for: Looking for good communication, outspoken personality, ability to convince the panel that you are the best fit for the job
right_wrong:
Good part: Being well-versed and confident with answers
Bad part: Could have answered more precisely instead of going into detailed explanation (in some questions)
tips: A thorough study of the Prepcom materials will be more than sufficient. Apart from that, reading 2-3 business articles (not in-shorts) daily will help in getting talking points in the GD/PI
dos_and_donts: Know the summer project inside out, especially if it's in the same domain/industry you are interviewing for.

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlist>GD>2 rounds of technical interviews
gd_topics_tips: A business case was given about offering loan to company. 5 minutes were given to write down points, followed by10-15mins discussion
interview_outline:
Interview started with short introduction and resume discussion. This was followed by finance questions mostly from first term FAC , stock markets, basics about derivatives.
In last company specific role discussed . Prepare some good questions to ask
domain_questions:
FAC term -1  syllabus 
1. what is depriciation. How it is shown in three financial statements
2. types of ratios . Important ratios to look for valuation
3. Enterprise value
4. valuation of  selected industry
5.General awareness about economy and markets is plus
6. difference between book value and face value of shares
hr_gk_questions: HR interview was part of 2 interview only. It was light and mainly involved conversation about family background, role expectations, flexibility for relocation and long working hours
looking_for: technical knowledge was something they gave maximum weightage. Moreover right attitude   about working in investment banking domain

pre_process_tips: Resume Based Shortlisting, Psychometric Test and then PI
interview_outline: It was a stress and grilling type interview. He asked questions on everything which I said.
domain_questions: Asked about my Marketing internship at Reliance Industries and grilled me over that. Gave me a scenario and asked to implement my PORs' experience in that. Asked about Porter's 5 forces and apply to Bajaj auto.
hr_gk_questions:
Asked me to introduce myself then asked questions about my hometown. Why MBA? Why Marketing after Chemical Engineering?
What is the purpose of your life? What is the main motivation of your life?
looking_for: They were looking for a person who can handle extreme stressful situations. Testing everything which was written in your resume and your introduction.
right_wrong: I think handling the pressure situation and keeping a smiling face even after heavy grilling helped me. I was clear and confident in my answers and did not deviate from what I said earlier.
tips: Prepare from Prepcom deck and Kotler summary
dos_and_donts: Don't panic in any case.

pre_process_tips: 1 Buddy Round and an On-Campus Case Workshop
interview_outline: Started with tell me something not in your resume, delved into a guesstimate - estimating the size of plant based meat india. second case was - Your client is a fire can extinguisher manufacturer. You need to identify top 3 customer segments for them. Also, they are looking to grow by 3x in topline, how can they do so?
looking_for: how confident you are and how much structure your thoughts have
right_wrong:
What do you think went right for you in the interview?	-	Thinking out loud helped.
-	Was able to think on my feet. - Was able to communicate my thoughts properly. Even when not given time to think, justified my approach by putting the parameters used to evaluate those options
Any tips for the future batch based on the interview -	Stay calm during the interview
tips: IIM Indore's prepcom and consulting books helped a lot along with case practices with seniors and batchmates

pre_process_tips: Application on reculta, resume shortlist by the company, followed by direct PI call. Only on PI round was taken
interview_outline: Resume based interview - Started with introduction, followed by questions on my undergrad academic project, HR questions like why MBA, why not MBA in power, they asked me why you want to join power industry again, the interview ended with do you have any questions for us.
domain_questions: why MBA, why not power mba, why you want to join power industry again
hr_gk_questions: undergrad project was Flexible Operation of thermal power plant for integration of renewable energy resources. so they asked questions such as what was your project about, tell us in detail what did you do, how did you do that, overall my background based questions
right_wrong: What acted as an add on could be my work ex in power plant and my engineering in power engg.
tips: asking appropriate questions at the end shows your interest in the company and being confident about your resume

interview_outline: Started with Introduction and resume based questions. Asked a lot about my internship and my academic projects. Asked about if I knew any of the new technologies like AI and Machine Learning but I didn't know much and that was fine. Also gave a guesstimate to calculate the no. Of calories in a supermarket but then started to ask about if I was a consultant to a supermarket, how would I go about it
domain_questions: How would you be a consultant to a supermarket? I used the pestel framework to analyse the situation
hr_gk_questions: Basic HR questions like why consulting.
looking_for: Can talk like a consultant and use frameworks and jargon. Basic knowledge about the tech industry helped a lot.
right_wrong: Was well read about what's happening in the tech industry and was able to apply frameworks to a real life problem.
tips: Read up a little about what's happening with the big companies like Amazon and Google and what they're eyeing for in the future.

pre_process_tips: PAN verification
interview_outline: Resume based, Case based
domain_questions: Work experience based
hr_gk_questions: HR questions asked in HR round
looking_for: Confidence on domain knowledge, Star performer in college and previous job roles
right_wrong: Everything went right but final case Presentation went wrong. They asked me to give presentation like a story telling, but i went for structured technical approach.
tips: My NPAD preparation in which every answer portrayed me like a hero of my life.
tech_skills: AI knowledge, structured framework approach of answering questions
dos_and_donts: Practice NPAD till you are confident and heroic in your mind with your answers. Learn to answer point wise. Revise what is taught in PGP1 and PGP2
additional_remarks: Anyone with 3+ years work experience will be asked about his relevant work ex. Frame story in mind, practice with chatGPT. Interview checks your listening and comprehending skills rather than reading or writing skills. If you are a bad listener, practice active listening in class. If you are a bad reader, does not matter in interview.

pre_process_tips: Direct PI after applying on reculta
interview_outline: The interview started with an introduction, and there were some questions on my role and learnings in the internship. After that, I was given a simple case regarding increasing the company's profits and further discussions based on go-to-market strategy, STP, and why S&M? It was a balanced interview though the role was of general management but the interview was mainly focused on marketing.
domain_questions: It was a case based interview nothing technical as such but knowledge of some basic marketing concepts will definitely help.
hr_gk_questions: just Why S&M?
looking_for: Critical thinking and basic knowledge of Marketing ( No Work-ex expectations and certifications)
right_wrong: It went like perfect as I was able to solve the case in the structured manner so the interviewer was happy and I converted.
tips: Solving some cases of all types and preparing the NPAD. Feedback from mock GD was good  but mock PI's were average
dos_and_donts: Read a little bit about steel industry and the company

pre_process_tips:
1. CV shortlisting
2. Aptitude test (duration 1.5 hrs, Sections: English, Quants, logical reasoning, domain specific questions)
3. 15 sec video interview round (Question: Why me?)
interview_outline: The interview was more heavily bordered on HR questions. Started with tell me about yourself and went on into generic questions like why MBA after having work experience. Questions like what do you know about the company and why are you interested to work with us were also asked
domain_questions: An overview about the group was asked
hr_gk_questions:
Only very basic HR questions were asked like
1. Tell me about yourself
2. Why did you pursue the specific engineering branch
3. Why shift onto MBA later
4. Why do you want to work for us
looking_for: They were looking for honest answers. Domain knowledge related to their job role if available is better.
right_wrong:
Overall the interview was a good experience.
Converted the interview
tips: NPAD questions were extremely helpful; mock PIs helped in handling the interview pressure well

pre_process_tips: No pre process. Just had to apply on reculta and company portal
no_interviews_duration: 1 + 2(In the first round, had to make a design document for a problem statement followed by discussion on the same. 30 mins for making the document followed by a 20 mins discussion. Subsequent two interviews were case based interviews which lasted for approximately 50 mins to 1 hour) .
interview_outline: Was completely focused on the case. Had a small discussion on work experience and how the previous interview process had been so far.
domain_questions: Asked about a challenging project/time during work ex. Was then asked to describe approach to overcome it and key takeaways
looking_for: Ability to think out of the box. Ability to accept mistakes made during the interviews and correct them. Humility and ability to understand what the interviewer is hinting at during the case interview rounds.
right_wrong:
Went right: Being confident but at the same time being humble. 
Went wrong: Could have been more structured in the case interview rounds
tips: Online resources about product management and previous work ex. Practice a few cases with friends. But avoid overdoing it as then one will get stuck to conventional solutions and won't be able to think out of the box.
dos_and_donts: Sounds difficult at that moment of interview but relax.

role_offered: BCOM Graduate; 44 Months Work Experience in Audit (At Deloitte).
pre_process_tips: Only 2 Personal Interview rounds
interview_outline:
1st Round - Started with Introduction, talked about previous work experience. Moved on to a Growth related case. Interviewer guided throughout the case. Interview was balanced between HR and case based.
2nd round - Basic Profile questions. Had 2 rounds of Extempore post that. Basic questions related to profile.
domain_questions:
Not many technical questions asked. Discussed a very basic Growth related case. 
Ask ‘What would an Investor look for before investing in the market’. Difference between call and put options.
hr_gk_questions:
No current affairs questions. Only 2 extempores based on general knowledge. 
“Situation of World Economy in General and Indian Economy in Specific.
“Role of Generative AI in Short, Medium and Long Term.”
looking_for: I think they were looking for general awareness. Awareness about past work experience. Oratory skills and confidence.
right_wrong:
I think the fact that I was calm and composed throughout the interview, worked for me. 
Yes, converted
tips: Prepcom Dashboard for case preparation helped the most.

gd_topics_tips: Is quick-commerce a boon or a bane?
interview_outline: First interview included resume + technical + HR questions, second one had a quick business case (relevant to company's industry)
domain_questions: Questions on company's business model, impact on various financial statements, company and industry awareness
hr_gk_questions: HR - motivation for the role, strengths which map to the role, whether okay with heavy workload
prep_resources: Consulting case book, Marketing compendium, thoroughness with resume
looking_for: Candidates with well-rounded skills across areas and sound logic, with a clear motivation to join the specific role and industry, and confident communication skills

pre_process_tips: None - Resume Shortlist
interview_outline: Started with introduction. Most of the questions were based on my resume - particularly from my workex  (in project planning) and internships. Last few minutes were HR questions similar to NPADs. They also dropped some random questions like Design thinking.
domain_questions:
How will you analysis a power generation project from a creditors perspective? Give quantitative and qualitative parameters. 
How is electricity tariff decided? Who decides that? Overview & problems of Indian electricity sector, etc
situational_questions:
What is your greatest achievement so far? 
Learning from your last job & some questions from hobbies & interests
