looking_for: Some workex in core industry, basics of project finance & awareness about the power sector
right_wrong: Being composed & confident.
tips: Read about the power sector, PFC news & economics.
dos_and_donts: Be brief and to the point - panelists are highly experienced

pre_process_tips: Resume Shortlisting
gd_topics_tips: Is MBA necessary to be Successful in Business?
interview_outline: Started with initial briefing about the role , introduction,detailed questions on work ex,major learnings from work ex,HR questions
domain_questions: they were more interested about process like how whole process works for project  for e.g they asked me about how procurement process works in different industries,what are the role of  different dept. like finance,QCS etc in the process.I tried to connect answer with work ex also talked about challenges and learning during the whole process.
hr_gk_questions: what is your greatest strength,why mba,what are your future aspirations,what if your future aspirations doesn't come true
looking_for: they were looking for someone who know how to deal with different situation,ability to learn on our own,decision making skills
right_wrong: yes,converted.I was sincere with my answers and i related all answers with different experiences right from early childhood to work ex,
tips: Be genuine and confident.Go through JDs that will give some idea how to frame technical  answers

pre_process_tips: Reculta process, no forms
no_interviews_duration: Buddy rounds 2 (15 mins each), interview (30 mins), Networking dinner
interview_outline: Interview was revolves around the resume and questions related to each line on the resume. And then a few HR questions
domain_questions: Not very domain related but asked about resume and finance related projects on the resume
hr_gk_questions:
About yourself?
Work experience questions back and forth and then a few situations related at work?
How to tackle a difficult situation at work?
How do you take Criticism?
looking_for: They were looking for passion, confidence and someone who is outright when they don’t know anything. Not to globe at all. Also, post interview in the networking dinner they mentioned on how body language is equally important and some candidates didn’t meet that
right_wrong: Yes I converted the interview, I was vocal on what I didn’t know and was through about my work experience and projects which they liked. Also my interests was something they found unique and discussed about
tips: NPAD for HR questions and going through company Jd

pre_process_tips:
1) Resume Shortlist.
2) 2 Buddy call (1st - Introduce Yourself, Why Consulting, Financial Models & 2nd - Introduction & I was given brief about the interview process).
interview_outline:
1st Interview (Introduce Yourself, Why Finance, About my previous job, Two Guesstimates).
2nd Interview (Introduce Yourself, HR Based on questions about my work ex., Domain-specific (Finance)).
3rd Interview (Introduce Yourself, Domain Specific Questions).
domain_questions: Case-based questions (Given situations about a firm and need to answer about the growth of the company), Marketable ratios, About 3 financial statements.
hr_gk_questions: About my work experience, Any initiative that I have taken, Any challenges you had faced.
looking_for: Give examples as much as you can they were looking for more practicality in your answers, Communication skills, Be concise and to the point about all the points of your work experience.
right_wrong: Right - Examples, Use of various concepts of the FAC.
tips: NPAD, FAC Classes covered most of the topics, Domain interviews.
dos_and_donts: Be relax while giving the interview.

pre_process_tips: No preprocess
gd_topics_tips: A case related to a comparison of 3 E-mail marketing campaigns of a credit card company. They were looking for unique points and not the common ones.
interview_outline: 1 Technical, 1 HR
domain_questions:
1st Round: Technical heavy
Q1. Difference between RandomForest and Decision tree
Q2. A case on linear regression
Q3. What impact do credit rating agencies have on investment decisions (Because I had a certification in Commercial Credit)
Q4. When do you apply regression and when decision tree?
Q5. Questions on my Academic project related to Network Analysis and Sentiment Analysis
Q6. Linear vs Logistic Regression
hr_gk_questions:
Describe a weakness of yours.
Why Analytics?
Why Amex?
looking_for: Clarity of thoughts and enthusiasm
right_wrong: Structured approach. Try to give them some unique answers rather than the common ones both in GD and Interview.
tips: ISLR book, SAR course, Youtube videos on R
dos_and_donts: Have something good related to analytics on your resume about which you can talk well in the Interview.

pre_process_tips: None, Shortlisting was done based on resume
interview_outline: Introduction and resume based questions (for around 5-6 minutes) followed by a case for 20 minutes
domain_questions: None.
hr_gk_questions: Questions based on current developments in a company (Bajaj Auto) mentioned in my resume were asked. I mentioned about the current developments in the EV space and the new vehicle launches by the company which boosted their topline.
looking_for: Communication, clarity and structure in thought, ability to incorporate real world happenings in the cases
right_wrong: Overall, the interview was smooth but there's always scope of improvement in the structure and clarity of thoughts while solving cases. Regular practice is the key to polish that. Yes, converted.
tips: Practicing atleast 2-3 cases everyday from a variety of sources and with different interviewers (you can schedule case interviews with your seniors, peers and friends but don't stick just one group of people). Sources- Case books (IIM A, IIM L, IIM I, FMS), Case Interviews Cracked, Victor cheng

interview_outline: Brief Introduction followed by a case interview. High emphasis was on the case only. There was a general follow-up discussion with respect to role and consulting in general.
looking_for: Rather than personal traits, I believe they were looking for individuals showing a willingness to learn, and more importantly, who think on first principles.
right_wrong:
Structured Case flow and engaging the interviewer by giving necessary hypotheses and real-life examples based on personal experiences helped a lot. 
Yes, I have converted both rounds of interviews.
tips:
Consulting Domain Sessions, Videos and Case books provided by PrepCom helped me the most. 
Mock PI with the external vendor gave important insights with regards to framing of initial discussion as well as introduction.
dos_and_donts: It is important to practice a good number of all sorts of cases and analyse them properly. Sticking to and learning the frameworks is not necessary. Also, Regular guidance and feedback from PGP-2 seniors serve as a great performance check metric.

pre_process_tips: Form Filling, Case Competition
interview_outline:
1st - Case round: given a product design case introducing elements from Microsoft 365
2nd - Introduction, Product design Case Interview, Complete end to end design of product
3rd - Introduction, grilled on my startup, redesign the whole startup, system design
domain_questions: The panel was interested in depth knowledge of Resume and wanted technical system design to be included in case interviews
looking_for: Work Ex in software, structured thought process, innovative ideas, taking hints from the directions given, thinking out of the box, creation of customer friendly products
right_wrong:
Good : My interviews were elaborate and I created a rapport with both my interviewers. They also appreciated my structured approach and creative feature building

Bad: Nothing as such but was mentioned to gain more experience in the last part of the last round

Did not convert the last round
tips: Exploring Youtube channels like Exponent and PM School. Product casebooks and experiences from various colleges

pre_process_tips: Workshop related to "How to solve cases" was conducted by company, where they discussed examples to cases and how to approach in it
no_interviews_duration: 3 Interviews, first-25 min, Second-25 min, Third-20 min
interview_outline: First Interview was a case related to Supply Chain, Second Interview was a case related to growth and it was data driven (Data tables were flashed on screen)., Third Interview was conversation with MD of Organization and It was Basic Interview Conversation
domain_questions: case related to Supply Chain (Operation)
hr_gk_questions: Few Questions related to "Why I Changed Jobs ?", Your Strengths, and How you can be asset for Deloitte
looking_for: Straight to point, Quality Answers, Valid Explanation and Justification.
right_wrong: Directly coming to good Quality points, Giving accurate answers with valid reason, Always be under control (Do not be too much over enthusiastic)
tips: past knowledge, preparation
dos_and_donts: Just don't say anything just for sake of saying, you must have valid explanation. If interview is going well then, please don't be over confidence and lose your control.

no_interviews_duration: 2- One technical and One HR (20 min each)
interview_outline: Started with basic introduction and what was there in the CV. Then, questions related to investment and questions related to job.
domain_questions:
Asked about investment decisions and NPV and IRR concepts. So I explained them using examples, that's gives more clarity. 
Asked about specific questions related to job to check whether I am thorough with the work that needs to be done.
Few mini caselets related to investment.
hr_gk_questions:
Why should we hire you as a fresher over work-ex?
Your biggest learning in these two years of MBA life.
Asked about a case competition that was mentioned in my resume.
looking_for: Confidence, clarity about the concepts/subjects mentioned on your resume and clarity about the role offered.
right_wrong: Since I was very thorough with my basic concepts, it helped me to tackle investment related questions.
tips: Reading newspaper, prepcom material and sector specific reports
dos_and_donts:
Be confident and try to have a conversation. 
Ask relevant questions to the interviewers.

pre_process_tips: Test designed for Project management
interview_outline: Started with introduction and little about resume as well as past work ex. However major focus of all the interviews is on Amazon leadership principals. Different situations justifying the leadership principals.
domain_questions: Few project Scheduling questions as well as resource allocation.
hr_gk_questions:
1. Introduction
2. What is your leadership style : Read a bit about different leadership styles and be prepared to delve into it.
looking_for: People who have taken initiatives in the past and are ready to work in pressure situations.
right_wrong: First interview went really well however I was unable to convince the interviewer in second round about the leadership style and Why no one else initiated what I did.
tips: Be confident. Amazon Interviews in generally mot stressful. Whatever you speak, be prepared to back it with examples.
dos_and_donts: Do not fabricate a story there. If you are not really confident, tell them that you have never been in such situation.

pre_process_tips: Was asked to write about 300 words ona given topic during application.
interview_outline: First two rounds were case interviews with a few question from resume.They focused on approach and structure more in the case interviews. Last round was with a partner which was mostly from NPAD and Resume.
domain_questions: NA.
hr_gk_questions:
What do you know about Everest?
Why consulting?
Why Everest Group?
looking_for: They wanted to see if the candidate was aware about Everest Group and was genuinely interested in the company and the role.
right_wrong: Case interviews went good since it was an unconventional case and they see how you try to structure it.Always have suggestions in mind when you identiify root causes and have it properly on paper to summarize.
tips: Case interview preparation in groups would help for first two rounds and try to stay calm during the entire course of process.Casebook and past year interview experiences helped. Alums in the company were approachhable and helpful

pre_process_tips: There was a pre-assessment test. It's called AMCAT.
gd_topics_tips: GD was a question based on e-commerce. If you cannot start or summarize - at least pivot the discussion to something else.
no_interviews_duration: There were 2 interviews. I sat for only one.
interview_outline: The interview felt more HR oriented, and I was asked why e-commerce, and then a situation. It was general. Situation based question - there has been a theft at a hub and you're the manager. What will be the logical steps you will take in dealing with this measure?
domain_questions: I made a few mistakes in my logic with the supply chain, but they just wanted the thought process.
hr_gk_questions: Why this industry at least. Have an idea about what happened post-covid.
looking_for: They were more into understanding your thinking process than the correctness of your answer. They didn't really ask me technica questions.
right_wrong: Did not convert.
tips: Thorough understanding of why you want to get into the field is important. My answer here was not solid.

pre_process_tips: Post the release of the short list, the company has a 2 day interview process with Day 1 processes being eliminating in nature. An average of 2 interviews per candidate took place on day 1 and 1 interview on day 2. The numbers totally depend and vary as per candidate since I had 3 interviews on Day 1 and 2 interviews on Day 2.
no_interviews_duration: Day 1 - 3 interviews- 20 mins to 30 mins; Day 2 - 2 interviews- 20 mins and 10 mins respectively
interview_outline: Started with a short HR question to break the ice and make you feel more comfortable and relaxed. Then straight deep dive into the problem statement and case discussion. In the end you can ask any questions to the interviewer which part is usually underrated but had great inpacts on my interviews personally. Do read and prepare about the company well.
looking_for: Communication is the key, even when the case is not going in the right direction, understand your mistakes, communicate them well and then move towards your final conclusion.

role_offered: Full time analyst in CRG CIB
pre_process_tips: JPMC "The Deal" case competition: Resume shortlisting, Aptitude test, Workshop+ case based test, another case PPT+Financial Model submission, Final presentation cum interview
no_interviews_duration: 1 (25 minutes including 12 minutes of case presentation)
interview_outline: Apart from questions on case assumptions, 5 more questions were asked which were not related to the case competition. Questions were of mental maths, Covid related, minority interest and about summer internship.
domain_questions: What is minority interest?
hr_gk_questions: Which company except pharma companies performed good during covid? What feedback did you get from your summer Internship work? I told them that my mentors were happy with my work but senior management said I could have done better.
right_wrong: I was honest throughout and said "no" when I didn't know the answer
tips: The Workshop round conducted by JPMC was very important. The test immediately after the workshop and case study given to prepare PPT and financial model were directly from the topic explained in the workshop.
dos_and_donts: Note each and every point of the workshop!

pre_process_tips: A thesis submission on any startup that the candidate deemed fit for investment and reasons for such

Second Interview purely HR focussed.

hr_gk_questions:
Walk me through your resume?
follow up question on hobbies
looking_for: Looking for enthusiastic participants for the field who were decently interested in the field of entrepreneurship.
right_wrong: Went well since the interview became very conversational and like a discussion going to and fro when discussing the thesis and their companies for example, where the interviewer also shared their own experiences in the industry
tips: None, for the kind of interview I had. Perhaps being prepared for the HR questions was the biggest contribution from the prep process.
dos_and_donts: Know the startup ecosystem decently well

"Tell us about one strength of yours that distinguishes you."

"How have you grown as a person in the last 2 or 3 years?"

"What is your favourite marketing campaign and why?"
"You are a luxury skin care brand selling offline and online, troubles in online. [Profitability case]"

pre_process_tips: Normal application form then direct interview
no_interviews_duration: 2 rounds for me: both around 30 to 40 mins. (3rd round was also there but i got placed before that)
interview_outline:
1. Introduction
2. Extensive questions on resume primarily on my work on PowerBI during summer internship
3. One question on agentic AI as I worked on it in one of my case competition. 
4. Guesstimate
5. How proficient are you in Excel, SQL, Python
Both interviews revolved around the resume.

hr_gk_questions: Why PwC, Why deal Analytics, Why Consulting, Why did you leave UPSC? - too much grilling on it
looking_for:
1. Clarity of thought
2. As i worked on PowerBI during my internship & it was mentioned in the desired skills in JD, so they questioned alot on that
right_wrong: I was thorough with my resume & internship project
tips: Documenting my internship project & whatever I did during my internship. It helped in preparing about internship, countering all the cross questioning & numbers mentioned

pre_process_tips: Resume shortlist, aptitude and psychometric test, final interview
interview_outline: Introduction, questions based on resume not very technical but should know everything about resume and company values.
domain_questions: What do you expect from this internship and reliance in general? I mentioned how it was spread across various domains and sectors giving me an opportunity to learn.
hr_gk_questions: When asked about resume questions try to inculcate the companies values and ethics.
looking_for: Good communication, leadership skills and someone who doesn't bluff.
right_wrong: Converted. I was calm and did not fidget, I took pauses to answer questions and waited for them to finish whatever they wanted to say or ask.
tips: Good sleep!! It's really important to be fresh. Go through the company decks they have all the details.
dos_and_donts: Be ready with a question for the company. Don't forget to smile even if it's a stress interview. For freshers they understand you don't have experience so it's okay be calm.

pre_process_tips: Interview shortlist after filling application form

In the next round, I was asked about a case related to SAP and SAP S4 HANA Migration. Overall my entire interview was highly dependent on my workex, situation based caselets, frameworks and interests.
domain_questions: I was asked about why consulting, which I related to my previous work ex. I was also asked about a mini case related to approaching a client for S4 Hana Migration, the benefits and analysis of all aspects.
hr_gk_questions: I was asked typical HR questions related to workex, CV, PORs and extracurriculars.
looking_for: They were more interested in the approach, thinking ability and problem solving skills of the candidate.
right_wrong: The good part about the interview was that I was confident and passionate about my answers which showed my interest for the company and the role.

Why I want to join AB InBev / How can I relate to company?
Asked me if I had any questions.

right_wrong:
The best part of the interview was when they asked me if I have any questions.
I asked them 3 questions and the interviewer explained each answer in detail.
tips:
Going through company website. Looking at their recent innovations and strategies.
This helped me in asking Qs regarding company.
dos_and_donts: Same as above

pre_process_tips:

-HR round

hr_gk_questions: Questions on projects and relevant courseworks that I had mentioned in my resume. Current affairs entailed questions related to the company, why is it in news,etc.

right_wrong: I converted the internship.

pre_process_tips: Had applied on Reculta, filled application form on their website, got shortlisted for direct interview. Had 2 rounds of interview

The 1st round was HR heavy. He asked me to introduce myself, give example of when I solved conflict, why Amex. He gave me 2 cases-and asked to identify parameters-one retailing, one on jet fuel consumption

hr_gk_questions: No

right_wrong:
Bad part->    I was unprepared for cases
Good part-> I asked time from the 2nd interviewer and when she gave, could actually come up with 1 or 2 novel ideas
I could have smiled more
Yes I did
tips: I slept early the previous night and talked to only my mom and dad before the interview

pre_process_tips: There was no pre process
gd_topics_tips: No GD

hr_gk_questions: None was asked

pre_process_tips:
Application form on the website
Reculta application
Shortlist for the interview
2 rounds of interview

Round 2- Case and conversation around the case and work experience

Why MBA after Engineering? Why not take few years of work experience before MBA?
Your core values?

pre_process_tips: Application form to be filled, followed by Resume shortlisting

hr_gk_questions: N.A.

tips: N.A.

pre_process_tips: CV shortlist, aptitude test

Balanced interview

Having structured flow in HR questions
Able to keep up an engaging conversation

pre_process_tips: Aptitude test
